title: The Expert Who Helped Lamar Jackson Negotiate His Last Ravens Contract Believes End Could Be Near
full_text:
Almost no one was privy to the inner-workings of the Ravens’ long-and-arduous contract negotiations with Lamar Jackson, dating back to 2020, with an MVP already to his name, once eligible for his first contract extension.
General manager Eric DeCosta, now having quite a miserable time building a sustained winner, led the charge on a process that would take years to complete and was unlike any other first-time QB extension for a superstar in NFL history. It would include a non-exclusive franchise tag and trade demand and collusion case along the way. DeCosta was aided by cap chief Nick Matteo – who has authored some of the ugliest contract structures in the NFL in recent years ( hence the worst cap situation in the NFL ) and team president Sashi Brown, once he took over for legendary steward Dick Cass after he retired.
As for the other side of the table, it was and still is just Lamar Jackson and his mom.
No agent. No marketing guru. No other voice.
And Jackson was seeking counsel from DeMaurice Smith, head of the NFLPA at the time, and Mark Levin, who for roughly 25 years oversaw the Salary Cap and Agent Administration department of the union, in charge of regulating agents and helping them negotiate deals and serving as the PA’s foremost expert on the Collective Bargaining Agreement that governs economic engagement between labor and management.
Levin was Team Jackson’s de-facto agent in the process and a beacon available to them to discuss comparable contracts around the league and structures and guarantees and intricate language. He was available on the other end of the Zoom when they wanted to mull no-trade clauses and no-franchise tag clauses (both of which they successfully obtained) and when they got an $84M poison pill cap charge for 2027 (with a $75M dead cap) that effectively makes Jackson a free-agent after the 2026 season.
Levin was as plugged in on cap and contract matters are anyone on the planet for a generation, and even after retiring from the NFLPA last year, top agents seek his counsel regularly and he assists many more formally as head of Pro Football Consulting. Before taking over the salary cap department at the NFLPA, he oversaw the salary cap and contract negotiations for the Washington Commanders and understands these matters from all perspectives.
He’s continued to follow Jackson’s ongoing saga with the Ravens closely , and their inability to make even a modicum of headway on getting him extended to a new deal back in March of 2025, when it was imperative on the heels of Josh Allen’s extension in Buffalo. Levin predicted basically everything that was to come this summer and fall when he joined me on “The Daily Flock Show” in May to analyze Jackson’s stalemate with the Ravens.
So, with Jackson injured again and the Ravens noncompetitive without him, with a bloated roster that should have been purged before the trade deadline and one of the worst offensive lines and some of the least-proven overall offensive talent in the NFL looking forward, Levin has a strong feeling about what’s next between this two-time MVP, and the Ravens.
Levin knows these individuals quite well and how they operate and was inside these talks and how personal it got at times, unlike almost anyone else on the planet. Like other experts who have discussed this matter with us, it seems obvious to Levin that Jackson will command $70M a season or more, with massive guarantees (even despite his injuries; didn’t impede Dak Prescott, for instance), and Jackson can and will call his own shot in regard to where he plays.
“I would be surprised if he's on the team next year,” Levin told me on “The Daily Flock” this week. “I'd be surprised … Unless the Ravens change their course and agree to make him the highest paid or the second highest paid quarterback on a on a legit structure, legit deal - not with a lot of fluff and window dressing - I just don't see him on the roster next year.
“I think they're just going to have to, you know, for the Ravens’ sake, hopefully trade him and get some good compensation for him, as opposed to just outright cutting him and not getting anything. But I just don't see him on the roster this year. And I think that, based on what's happened this year, you know, it might be time for the Ravens fans to buckle up … and look at a rebuild. They're in a bit of a pickle.”
I’d put Levin’s assessment of the situation up against anyone’s.
Jackson has simply smiled and check-mated the Ravens all along, DeCosta reverted to a trite talking point about being “optimistic” about signing Jackson before the season even as the QB spurned him again, and if the Ravens haven’t paid him what it would take to secure his services by now, it’s beyond fair to suspect they might never again.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Cap Bizarre Deadline By Trading For A Starting Center, For The Second Time In A Month
full_text:
Executives around the NFL strongly suggested the Ravens would not do the obvious and logical thing and start shedding bloated veteran contracts at the trade deadline.
The front office was viewed as too stubborn, full of far too much hubris , to be a seller, and they were correct. But few could have predicted – even as bizarre as things are now in Baltimore – that they would give away their starting kicker to the Falcons, in essence, Tuesday and then trade for a starting center for the second time in a month, this time Atlanta’s Ryan Neuzil. This after trading what could end up being a top 40 pick in 2028 as part of a baffling package for concussed Eagles offensive lineman Cam Jurgens, whose time at center for Baltimore has coincided with an already terrible line hitting new lows with three QBs hurt on about 12 snaps in Week 8.
Yeah, this ain’t the Ozzie Newsome Ravens, not by a long shot.
The Ravens (losers of four straight) have allowed 33 points or more in three straight games for the second time in franchise history (2025) and have failed to score 14 points in four-straight games for the first time ever. And this is what they come up at the deadline.
Numerous NFL executives suggested to us this month that teams had interest in 32-year-old running back Derrick Henry. He's being hung out to dry by the offensive line with no chance to gain yards without Lamar Jackson at QB – and Jackson is most certainly done for the season on IR . Left tackle Ronnie Stanley, receiver Rashod Bateman and defensive lineman Calais Campbell were also identified as prime candidates to be dealt with Baltimore failing to look like a professional operation under overmatched rookie head coach Jesse Minter and facing sweeping roster questions with the worst salary-cap situation in the NFL.
The decision not to have already added kicker Jake Moody to their active roster had no reasonable justification , and after a desperate deal for Jurgens – who is effectively locked in for 2027 at a $17M salary – adding another center, this one a pending free agent, is odd.
Neuzil, 29, is a late bloomer who has strong ties to Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford and is a former Falcons undrafted free agent who has managed to hang around on futures deals and low-level contracts before getting an extension prior to 2025. The Ravens tried this already with former Falcons fringe lineman Jovaughn Gwyn at center, which struck evaluators around the NFL as a stretch, and he was lost for the season in Week 3.
Center has been a massive issue since the Ravens let stalwart Tyler Linderbaum leave as a free agent. The Ravens have had a new offensive line combo almost every week, the signing of free agent guard John Simpson has been tragic, and they do have first-round pick guard Vega Ioane back from injury (he remains the best center on this roster) and have also looked at youngster Emery Jones at guard.
There is a strong case to be made to bench Simpson (guaranteed at least $5.5M in 2027); but one would think Jones and Ioane would be the starting guards in that scenario. As bad as Jurgens has been adopting to Baltimore’s run fits and with all their communication issues up front, it would still be remarkable, even by this front office’s pathetically-low recent standards, to do that. Of course, with Jurgens’ deep medical history, having cover at center is quite important, too.
Neuzil has started every game at center this season and ddi the same in 2025, making about $4M. (They could have saved a bunch of money and a bunch of draft picks - and maybe had a decent OL - had they executed this trade, oh, I don't know, in May?)
He has 38 career starts. The Ravens shipped out failed offensive lineman Andrew Vorhees and a sixth-round pick in 2028 for him. They think loading up on comp picks is cute and figure someone will sign Neuzil to a decent free-agent deal this winter that will bring back a pick in 2028 that is higher than the sixth they parted with.
The Ravens also released blocking tight end Nick Vannett on Tuesday – the loss of TE Durham Smythe has been significant – and brought back fullback Lucas Scott, with it obvious for weeks more of a true lead blocker was needed for Henry. They let All Pro fullback Pat Ricard, who told me how badly he wanted to stay in Baltimore on "The Daily Flock Show," leave for the Giants in March, where he reunited with former coach John Harbaugh and is in first place in the NFC East.
Meanwhile the Ravens' playoff odds continue to sink and none of Tuesday's transactions are going to help much with that.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Failure To Secure Kicker Jake Moody To Active Roster Baffles NFL Execs
full_text:
The Ravens losing kicker Jake Moody – who they had been grooming as a possible replacement for struggling youngster Tyler Loop - is the latest roster blight and bizarre decision for a front office that is making it their brand lately.
Whether or not Moody solidifies himself in the league remains to be seen, but getting the chance to kick in Atlanta, a dome team, in a division in which weather isn’t nearly as big of a problem this time of year (NFC South) will certainly help his chances. The fact that the Ravens made zero effort to add Moody to their active roster not only at the time they signed him to the practice squad to replace Loop, who was struggling mightily before his groin injury last month, but at any point since, is difficult to fathom.
Moody booted a 50-yard field goal in the rain in Thursday’s latest debacle, a 33-10 loss to the Jags (their fourth straight). He is someone Ravens kicking guru Randy Brown identified back in the summer as a potential replacement for Loop if the youngster could not get more consistent in his second season. Baltimore originally brought in Moody to serve as competition before the season began and then signed him back to the practice squad in-season as Loop began to miss chip-shot field goals and struggled with clutch kicks (though he did hit a game-winner Week 3 in Brazil).
Loop could still return from injury to kick this season, but it was strongly implied that Moody could be preferred to him prior to the groin situation emerging after a loss to Cleveland in Week 6. Loop continued to struggle with kickoffs, too, and rookie head coach Jesse Minter – looking totally overmatched so far – expressed serious frustration with Loop prior to him being placed on Injured Reserve.
“We'll continue to work with him and continue to try to put him in position, but we need to make second-half kicks,” Minter said after his miss at Cleveland. “You could argue that second-half missed field goals are no different than turning the ball over in those situations. So, [that's] definitely something we want to keep striving to be better at."
The move to Moody was about performance more than anything else. And now they have neither kicker, and may have to turn to someone like aging Nick Folk, who the Falcons just cut.
According to multiple personnel executives we’ve chatted with in recent weeks, the state of kicking is bleak and there are few options on the street. Moody looked good in Washington to finish last year, kickers can be late bloomers, he has a pedigree as someone the 49ers invested a Day Two draft pick in, he had a nice preseason, and there are limited options. So the fact that other teams were watching him closely shouldn’t have been lost on the Ravens, but then again they seem to be a fog since last season.
“Atlanta is kind of rebuilding, they want to go with a younger guy with more upside,” one NFL personnel exec said, explaining the dynamic. “And the Ravens have to know there isn’t anything out there. They were just looking at the options before they brought Moody in. There aren’t enough good kickers right now. So if you have one, you need to protect yourself.”
By that he means, keep him signed to the active roster.
The Ravens merely elevated Moody from the practice squad to the active roster for last week’s game, but his roster spot remains on the PS. There was nothing stopping them from just giving him a 53-man roster spot once they knew he was taking over for Loop (most likely for the duration of the season if he was any good). Instead, they abstained and any team could contract Moody at any time with an offer on their active roster, and the Falcons pounced.
“It’s an unforced error,” said another longtime NFL personnel exec who acquired multiple kickers from various means over his career. “No other way you can put it. What the (heck) is going on over there? How does that happen in the NFL? He makes that kick Thursday, just sign him to the active roster …
“If you are this kid (Moody), would you rather be going out there to kick in Baltimore and Pittsburgh and Cincinnati in November and December, out in all of that (weather), or in Atlanta? DeCosta never thought about that? Maybe the other kid comes back (Loop) and he can do the job, but there aren’t enough kickers out there to be giving them away.”
Executives around the NFL have been calling out the Ravens implosions in real-time going back to pulling out of the Maxx Crosby trade in March for alleged health concerns, and with their lack of traction getting MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson signed to contract extensions, putting them in a perilous spot in 2027 . DeCosta has had nothing short of a failure 2025/2026, it seems obvious to other NFL GMs they should have been marketing veterans for sale well ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, in a robust way, and serious questions are being asked about the stewardship and direction of the franchise.
They have massive potential roster questions looming at QB (pending where Jackson wants to be next season), as well as left tackle, center, cornerback and safety - for starters - and an untenable salary cap situation to boot. Probably safe to add kicker to that mix, as well.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The One Contract-Extension Candidate The Ravens Must Approach Now Amid A Lost Season
full_text:
The Ravens have fallen far short of their goals thus far in 2027, hence rookie head coach Jesse Minter, looking largely overmatched thus far, vowing to take corrective measures with his defense ahead of Monday night’s game.
They have not met their overarching goals on offense or defense or special teams. They are the worst second-half team in the NFL, where coaching staffs are measures, resulting in poor results across the board . They prizes generating explosive plays and not surrendering them almost above all else, and rank 25th on passes allowed over 25 yards and have a -3 explosive play differential. They have allowed four more touchdowns than they have scored.
General manager Eric DeCosta built a failure offensive line that played no small role in three quarterbacks getting hurt and Lamar Jackson has suffered two critical injuries already. As we have been pointing out, the player-development fails are pretty sweeping as well (again, the Orioles and Ravens are so stubborn and similar it’s galling), with very few breakout players and the bulk of the team not performing to the level of how they are being paid, and or where they were draft, part of why they should be sellers at Tuesday’s trade deadline .
Minter and his novice staff were supposed to relate better to players and help develop a draft class that all made the team (except for the final pick) plus two undrafted free agent rookies. The inability to not choke away leads – Minter has made it worse – and get more from the roster were the underlying reasons John Harbaugh was cast aside ; he looks like the NFL Coach of the Year with the Giants.
And there is one other way to measure this failed campaign. DeCosta has just three blue-chip players, not on their rookie contracts, signed beyond 2027 – Nnamdi Madubuike, Zay Flowers and Kyle Hamilton. After letting a host of impact youngsters depart as free agents last year, it’s also a terrible sign how few players are making the case for contract extensions this offseason. Yeah, it really is that bleak.
There appear to be only three potential candidates, and there’s only one that I’d be actively trying to approach now, with some of the savings from Madubuike’s contract restructure, to invest in right now:
He is the breakthrough player, and he’s the only breakthrough player.
Especially among those who will have three or more accrued seasons come 2027, making them eligible for a new deal. Mike Green shows some flashes but DeCosta’s horrid record with edge players draws natural skepticism. Devontez Walker has gone backwards and injuries have also hurt others and Nate Wiggins has yet to flash even a modicum of ball-skills at corner and might not fit this scheme ( Marvin Lewis pointed some things out ) and even buying low on him, at that position, ain’t cheap.
Simpson should get a chance to replace Roquan Smith as this becomes more of a lost season and wear the green dot. They need to find out as much about everything he can do. The athleticism has always been there, there’s more pass rush to explore and he brings energy and thump. He should be the priority and seeing how he and Teddye Buchanan fit together the best has to become an overarching goal for Minter.
DeCosta loves to keep throwing money at his first-round picks hoping they eventually make him look good, so beware Wiggins after year three. Might make more sense to finally bench Marlon Humphrey or relegate him to slot-only and see if TJ Tampa can stay healthy and play outside and try to pay him sooner rather than later.
Roger Rosengarten has become more erratic and vulnerable and the overall quality of the offensive line has sunk dramatically since he entered the league. The Ravens have a long history of letting offensive linemen walk in free agency – just happened again with Tyler Linderbaum in March – and if he wants to take a team-friendly, league average deal, great, but starting tackles rarely want to do that because they can get vastly overpaid on the open market.
I would be more inclined to make the rest of this group play it out and prove it. But Simpson would be a priority, now.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: 5 Winners and 6 Losers From Ravens' Primetime Loss To Jaguars
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens dropped their fourth straight game this season in Week 9 on Thursday night because they weren't able to upset the visiting red-hot Jacksonville Jaguars, who pulled away from them late in the first half and never looked back as they handed their host a humbling 33-10 home loss.
They came into this game as heavy underdogs after placing their top two quarterbacks on injured reserve with physical ailments they suffered four days prior. It was going to be an uphill battle anyway; they tried to slice it, and pulling off an upset would've required tremendous discipline and playing complementary football in all three phases, and they did anything but.
With the loss, they fell to 4-5 and remain in last place in the division, where they rightfully belong given how they've played the past month and how banged up they've been on offense.
Here are several Ravens players and coaches who stepped up and showed out, and others who made some costly mistakes from coaching and execution standpoints.
The eighth-year veteran had his most productive game on offense of the season thus far and the second in which he recorded 70-plus rushing yards. He led the Ravens with 85 yards on nine carries, with the bulk of it coming on a 65-yard scoring sprint in the fourth quarter. Hill also caught all three of his targets for seven receiving yards and had some impressive reps in pass protection, picking up blitzers.
65-yard touchdown for Justice Hill! Tune in on Prime. pic.twitter.com/kvYH0fyt7X
In his first appearance as a Raven in place of injured second-year pro Tyler Loop, the more experienced fourth-year pro had a confidence-inspiring performance. He drilled his lone field goal attempt from 53 yards with room to spare and, right down the middle, did the same on his extra point attempt and didn't have any kickoff infractions.
Jake Moody from 53 yards in his first game as a Raven... JAXvsBAL on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TRegHRPfdk
For the fourth week in a row, the Ravens held the opposing team's rushing attack in check to under four yards per carry and didn't give up 100 yards on the ground collectively for the fifth time this season. They had three different players record a tackle for loss and did a great job of setting the edges and flying to the ball.
KYLE HAMILTON IN THE BACKFIELD. 😤 Tune in on Prime. pic.twitter.com/zVAwmOhArG
The rookie specialist was a reliable weapon for the Ravens in the battle for field position, pinning the Jaguars' offense inside their own 20-yard line on three of his five punts, with a long of 55 and an average of 48.2 yards per punt.
The second-year pro gave up a big play in the first half of this game and made one in the second half that gave the team life. On the one he allowed, he got beat inside for a 53-yard touchdown by Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington, who was playing in the slot when the Ravens dialed up a blitz. With the Ravens trailing by 17 points late in the third quarter, he not only made a tackle for loss by blowing up a wide receiver screen, but he also forced a fumble that gave the offense the ball back at midfield.
FORCED FUMBLE!!! RAVENS RECOVER!! Tune in on Prime. pic.twitter.com/Wmg8gj76dO
In more ways than one, it felt like the undrafted rookie never really had a chance to succeed in his first career start for a myriad of reasons, including his ankle injury, weather conditions, poor pass protection, pre-snap penalties that put him behind the sticks, and the players around him not making plays. Nonetheless, he didn't play well in his own right, by his admission, going 10-of-18 for 60 passing yards and two interceptions.
Although the four-time Pro Bowler finished the game stronger than he started it, by blowing a coverage on the Jaguars' opening offensive drive of the game, that sprung a blocking tight end for a 52-yard gain, set the wrong kind of tone for the type of game it'd wind up being. Humphrey earned Pro Football Focus' highest coverage grade on the Ravens' defense with a 68.9, had the fourth-highest overall grade with a 70.1 and had two pass breakups.
The three-time Pro Bowler led the team with 19 receiving yards on a pair of catches, but it was what he did before the snap and when lined up under center that landed him on this list. He was one of two veteran leaders on offense who committed one of two back-to-back false starts that derailed the Ravens' second possession of the game. Andrews also fumbled a fourth-and-1 snap on a failed quarterback sneak late in the third that resulted in a turnover on downs.
The Ravens got virtually little to no pressure on the Jaguars' quarterback, Trevor Lawrence, who wasn't sacked at all and was hit just once. Far too often, he was allowed to survey the field and launch bombs over their heads for chunk gains, completing 8 of 10 passes of 10-plus yards for 193 yards and a touchdown. The one good thing they were able to do up front to disrupt Jacksonville's passing attack was bat down three passes at the line of scrimmage, with two coming from two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and the other from fellow seventh-year veteran Broderick Washington.
While no quarterbacks were hurt during this game, compared to all three getting banged up the week prior, this blocking unit struggled to consistently execute once again. Even though the Ravens recorded their fourth-highest rushing yardage total of the season (172), the bulk of that production came late in garbage time, with the Jaguars up by 30 points and conceding anything that let them bleed the clock.
Pass protection continues to be a struggle for this unit, as they allowed an already physically compromised quarterback to get sacked three times and hit four times. The viral crash-out from offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford on the sideline that was caught on camera was completely warranted given how poorly his unit performed at home in primetime.
Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford is not happy 😳 (📺 PRIME) pic.twitter.com/KwgRWOSgDM
The second-year specialist continues to not provide much juice as a returner, and he fumbled the ball deep in Baltimore territory on a kickoff that set up the Jaguars' third touchdown drive of the game in the fourth quarter.

title: Final Ravens NFL Trade Deadline Big Board
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens have every reason to be as motivated to sell at the NFL trade deadline as any team in the league.
Okay, not as much as the Chargers or Colts or the Titans … but certainly as much as the Eagles as a team with Super Bowl aspirations that has never looked the part this year. The Ravens are the dregs whether they want to admit it or not – they have lost four in row being outscored by 70 points, they have allowed 33 points or more in three straight games and failed to score 14 in four straight and it’s far more likely than not that Lamar Jackson doesn’t see the field again this season no matter what the scoop jockeys peddle.
They are the worst second-half team in the NFL, the coaching staff has been totally overwhelmed thus far, and if you are looking for individual success stories from a player-development standpoint, well, there is first-round pick Vega Ioane and, pending unrestricted free agent linebacker Trenton Simpson, and Zay Flowers has had halves of football with Jackson that have been otherworldly and been largely invisible otherwise.
If you are looking at critical tiebreakers – the isn’t going to be an AFC North title, sorry – well a .286 strength of victory is third-worst on the AFC and Baltimore has just two AFC wins (lowly Colts and Titans) and their -47 scoring differential is better than only the Colts, Titans, Dolphins and Chargers. And they are 7-15 playing games that Jackson doesn’t start since he became their starter. They get whipped in the trenches with regularity and this offensive line – the “construction“ of which is a fire-able offense in and of itself – is probably not done getting QBs hurt.
But none of that matters in Owings Mills (that’s what the access merchants are saying ), where they talk a big game and hype-up an alleged winning culture that died years ago. So what does that mean as the trade deadline looms Tuesday afternoon? Here’s where things stand:
Cam Jurgens – Not nearly as good at center as Ioane, and will command $17M next season anyway. Dealing a potential top 40 pick for him in 2028 – while he was concussed, by the way – would get you fired soon enough in an organization that was serious about winning.
Jacoby Brissett – Giving up essentially fourth-round value for him may also blow up in their face. His ability to stay upright behind this offensive line could be a real issue and lacks the legs to help unlock Derrick Henry in a broken run game.
None - Yeah, this is over. The payroll is bloated beyond belief already, this was supposedly an elite roster all along and, while desperately needing all the picks they can muster to try to get out of an ugly salary-cap crunch (explained in detail in “The Daily Flock” below), they have already mortgaged future drafts. Even trying to make the case for a cheap veteran kicker like Joey Slye doesn’t make sense anymore and Jake Moody did boom one from 50-plus Thursday.
None – To this point, hubris and stubborn remain the rule for a front office that has been unable to steward this sinking ship anywhere but down – consistently – since the 2023 AFC Championship Game.
Henry – Longtime NFL general manager Marty Hurney explained on “The Daily Flock” how open he would be to moving the future Hall of Famer (“I’m not calling but I sure am listening,” is how he framed it). We have talked to execs around the NFL who believe Henry is cooked in Baltimore behind this line (3.4 yards/carry the last four weeks) and needs to go. Mark Levin, former Commanders salary cap guru who oversaw salary cap and agent administration for the NFLPA for roughly 25 years, also believes the team should try to get a fourth-round pick for him. He's 32, where RB careers expire, and being run into the ground.
Ronnie Stanley – His cap situation is ugly no matter what with $28M in dead cap hoveering in 2027. Now would be the perfect time to see what Carson Vinson could do and as a former Pro Bowl left tackle, in a shallow OL market, execs tell me he could fetch a decent return.
Rashod Bateman – Hasn’t cracked 300 receiving yards this season is still good for catching less than two of every three balls he sees and has never living up to his draft billing outside of what was really one 10-game stretch in 2024. With a $13M salary next year, he’s gone one way or the other in the spring.
Calais Campbell – At age 40, this is his last hurrah. Being a part of a rotation with the Lions or Chiefs would seem to make a lot of sense, for starters, or even a return to Jacksonville where he spent his best seasons after they just lost a dominant defensive tackle for the season.
Others – No one I talk to thinks any winning team would want anything to do with the contracts Roquan Smith or Mark Andrews, though the Ravens should be highly motivated to jettison both by any means possible.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Jesse Minter Asked About Dropping Play-Calling Duties Monday, Vows Changes To Ravens Defense
full_text:
Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter hinted at potentially significant changes coming to his failing defense – more personnel than schematic – at his Monday press conference, while not ruling out moves at the trade deadline and steering as far as possible from any clarifications about injured superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson.
Minter and his novice staff are reeling after four straight losses, and they have not looked good against middling competition this season let alone quality opponents. There was a lot of talk about “resets” and changes coming after Thursday’s flogging by the Jaguars and with this team not playing again until next Monday against the winless Chargers. Minter worked hard not to reveal too much about what he has planned or what he thought general manager Eric DeCosta might do by Tuesday’s deadline ( this is what they should do ) but was emphatic about one topic - defensive play-calling duties.
Minter was criticized for handling Jackson’s previous high-ankle sprain, calling it a “day-to-day” situation for nearly three weeks, and has been far more guarded about saying anything about his injuries since. He refused to acknowledge reports indicating Jackson had his thumb operated on, or disclose anything close to a timetable for return ( we doubt he plays again this season ).
“I’m going to keep most of the conversations between Lamar and I, between Lamar and I,” Minter said. As for any updates on his health – “that will come from him” the coach said. Minter was enthusiastic about what journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who will start in week 10, can bring to the team, in another piece of Ravens news from this afternoon.
“I think he’ll operate our offense at a level required to be successful,” Minter said.
When asked about giving up defensive play-calling duties with that unit allowing 33 points or more in three straight games, exhibiting no real strengths and with the secondary (their alleged superpower) getting shredded, Minter delivered a stern response: “No.”
Minter seemed a bit perturbed by the question but it’s being talked about all over the league . The lack of a former NFL head coach on his staff to help him has been a big issue, and former Ravens highly-successful defensive coordinators like Marvin Lewis and Wink Martindale, who installed a version of the defense Minter runs , have been quite critical of the 2026 Ravens defense (explained in detail here) .
“Lineup changes, those are all on an individual basis,” Minter said, “but certain things we have to have a really high standard for, so we'll see how it all shakes out … I take as much pride in not giving up explosives as any coach in the league, and that’s not showing up… it’s all lip-service right now.”
The Ravens have allowed 18 passes of 25 yards or more – 25th in the NFL – despite Minter flooding the field with defensive backs and being averse to blitzing or playing man coverage with two-deep looks predicated on taking away big plays. He has the worst second-half defense in the NFL, arguably, an they are 20th in opposer passing and do not have an interception fro a defensive back all season.
Minter was asked specifically about $19.3M corner Marlon Humphrey (highest cap hit in the NFL who has been in steep decline for years ) as benching him for TJ Tampa should be in order. “There's a consistency level in the secondary in particular that we need to find,” Minter said, “and we’ll keep looking for it.”
The Ravens should be robust sellers at the deadline given a brutal salary-cap situation right now and for 2027 ( worst in the NFL by some margin ), with the uncertainty of Jackson’s future hanging over it all. Minter didn’t signify much one way or the other about other additions, conceding this is a team to evaluate “the team now and the team in the future,” speaking to DeCosta “about what’s best for the team.”
Overall, he continued to give this group a nominal vote of confidence: “I like our team now, we just need to play better and do things better.” Other NFL execs see an unavoidable rebuild/roster purge, ( as explained further here ).
Hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton left Thursday’s game with a hip injury but Minter indicated he looks to be on a good path for the next game, along with starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins and corner Nate Wiggins. Minter was non-committal on rookie fifth-round pick Adam Randall (running back/Joker) making his season debut this week from IR.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Usual Suspects Are Up To Their Usual Antics Reporting On Lamar Jackson's Latest Injury. Beware
full_text:
Lamar Jackson does an incredible job of not letting people into his private thoughts or inner circle.
Through years of the highest-profile contract negotiations in modern US sports and for nearly a decade in the NFL, he has managed to keep access merchants and national-media types at bay regarding details and timetables and ongoing machinations of all sorts. And it drives them mad and drives them to extremes to the point that whenever he suffers an injury or reaches another inflection point in his contract, the misinformation and guessing or quasi-information that they peddle for others hoping to influence Jackson in some way or another reaches critical mass.
It never takes long for them to come out telling you when Jackson should be back and will be back; and if you are paying attention, the results speak for themselves. History has a way of repeating and I'd expect more of the same here. I doubt he throws a pass this season and might never again in Baltimore without massive capitulation from owner Steve Bisciotti this offseason.
Of course, many of the very same people who told you there was a “realistic chance” he’d play a week after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 4, are up to their usual tricks. The same people who said he would be back for the Packers game last year or who said he would be back for Week 17 two years before that – or certainly the playoff game with the Bengals – now want you to believe they have the scoop on what comes next for Jackson before he has even really begun any sort of recovery from the thumb surgery he just underwent.
Of course, this reporting always frames things like Jackson has every chance to swoop in and save the day. Somehow, it always seems to come from a perspective that would sell hope and expectations to fans, and put that all on one individual. In this case, it's made to seem like the QB has given some sort of explicit promise to his teammates to save them from the front office and coaching staff that is under intense scrutiny for the serious miscalculations they continue to make , and rescue them all.
Meantime, Zay Flowers, one of the players closest to him, wouldn't dare make a public projection about where he would ever catch a pass from Jackson again after he suffered the thumb injury in Week 8: "That's not really anything I can comment on, and that's not anything I can really control in my situation. So, that's something I can't really comment on for you."
And all of this comes at a time when the Ravens are hitting new lows with a young coaching staff during this four game losing streak, while former coach John Harbaugh is the leader for NFL Coach of the Year with the upstart Giants. And with the Ravens pushing back on the obvious notion they should be shedding salary with a bloated roster and terrible cap situation through these same media types,. Al the while successful exec on other NFL teams know what really makes sense for the Ravens by Tuesday afternoon ( selling at the deadline).
The loud truths about the realities of this roster are being shouted by those in the media not constrained by having to protect sources ( and former Ravens players and coaches at that ).  And with all attention being paid on team president Sashi Brown and general manager Eric DeCosta as they assumed even more power and control of the entire organization after replacing a super-established coach with a big voice with a rookie struggling to find his, we get always-ambitious "reporting" about Jackson's ankle injury. The another wave after his thumb was crushed by a pass rusher as soon as he dropped back for the first time upon returning from the significant ankle absence.
As we discussed at length with Bomani Jones on “The Daily Flock” the number of people Jackson actually confides in seems to grow smaller by the years (link to the show is below),. He is going make the decision he needs to make, at the appropriate time, in the best interest of his health and career based on the information available whenever he is close to being cleared to play again.
That's a good six weeks down the line; what all logic and stats and game film is telling you is a Ravens season far more lost than last year’s. Jackson has not played a full game since Brazil in Week 3, which is also conveniently left out of the "reporting" on him. And he reached a point where his future is in no way guaranteed given the poison pills he adroitly negotiated into his contract (no-tag clause, no-trade clause, $84M cap hit) coming to pass while this front office is under scrutiny and this roster is under scrutiny like never before.
He worked long and hard for the right to get to this point where he controls his own destiny through arduous negotiations going back to the conclusion of his third season in the NFL. The idea that he is telling people right now he will be back in December to save the season - and his teammates are taking it as fact - is preposterous. (Watch Flowers's expression when they ask him about Jackson's future last week - I'd trust that.
The idea he is making those decisions now given all the variables laid out above paints him as far less shrewd than he is, and if this feels a lot like the same ‘ol pressure trying to be applied on him from the same ‘ol places playing the same ‘ol games,, you aren't alone. It was just a few weeks ago that Ravens rookie coach Jesse Minter, was facing pointed questions after calling a high-ankle sprain “day-to-day” for nearly three weeks before changing his tune only after Jackson met the media to talk about it.
There has been a different sort of standard that has applied to this quarterback all along.
And it has much to do with the fact he employs no agent, and not even a marketing guy or business manager. Jackson doesn't play the PR game and at this I suspect he never will.
Team Jackson has no one willing or interested in getting in the muck with the types who sling this stuff and live in the muck, which inherently means that those who do will double and triple down on getting their narratives pushed by the scoop jockeys. NFL teams are loaded with them – nepo babies and climbers and wounded execs looking for sympathetic figures in the media who will launder their reputations and push them for jobs and help them create narratives that are incredibly important to their careers and job security.
I lived in that world for 15 years; I know exactly how the sausage is made and who plays the game at the dirtiest and shadiest levels. The stories are uniquely driven by the “sources” of such veiled speculation (then packaged as “reporting”), which is serving the self-interest of those pushing it to whomever will print it first or Tweet it first, with no pushback.
The fact that Jackson has amassed NBA levels of power and control and leverage over the 2027 Baltimore Ravens offseason and roster decisions and, in many respects, their very direction is truly unique ( Domonique Foxworth explained Jackson’s unicorn status ), And it bedevils execs and agents and media-types around the league who cannot control this situation nearly in the way they do most others.
So here is all you need to know about what’s next for Jackson: He will be back when he feels like himself and able to do everything he needs to do to protect himself, especially behind one of the worst offensive lines in the NFL. Only if it also truly makes sense in the standings and, I suspect, only if this looks like a football team that could muster anything in the postseason.
It won’t matter what Minter says in the interim or what the talking heads say between now and then. But rest assured that Minter, who would not even comment last week on if surgery has taken place, will continue to call it a decision where the player and doctors and team all agree it’s right for him to play.
“I think it's just a decision for his best interest,” Minter said often in October during the ankle injury. “That's really what every decision is always going to be about."
Jackson…

title: Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are in the midst of an historically horrific four-game losing streak in which their offense has averaged just under 11 points per game and the defense is allowing nearly 30 points per game.
While it doesn't feel like there's much to be hopeful about as it pertains to the Charm City franchise, the face of it isn't ready to throw in the towel just yet. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , star quarterback Lamar Jackson told his teammates that he plans to return this season, with the hope of leading them on a late-season push for the postseason.
In his first game back after missing three games with a high ankle sprain, the two-time league MVP suffered an injury to his right thumb on the first play from scrimmage in a Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Per Rapoport's source, the three-time First Team All Pro selection underwent surgery to repair a fracture and dislocation in his injured throwing hand.
The Ravens placed Jackson on injured reserve, along with primary backup Tyler Huntley, who suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the same game and half against the Bills. Thankfully, the typical recovery for Jackson's injury is at least six weeks, although it could take up to nine weeks.
Jackson's message to the team that was paraphrased to Rapoport was, "Just stay alive."
After starting the season winning four of their first five games, the Ravens now sit at 4-5 and currently sit outside of the current playoff picture at the bottom of the AFC North division standings. With eight games and a bye week remaining on their schedule, in order to return to the postseason after just falling short last year, they'll need to start stacking some wins.
The earliest Jackson is eligible to return is Week 14, when the Ravens host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, following the team's Week 13 bye. That will be five weeks post-op and at the earliest possible end of the spectrum for his potential return.
Fortunately for the Ravens, unlike their last four opponents, who all possess winning records, their next four all have records under .500. It's a far less arduous stretch, and they brought in much-needed reinforcements at quarterback by trading for veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett to steady the ship on offense and take some pressure off their struggling defense.
If the Ravens can rattle off four straight wins or at least go 2-2 over that span, they'll be in a great position to make Jackson's push to return worthwhile. It'd be just in time for their final four games, all of which are against AFC North rivals, including a pair of bouts with the current division-leading Pittsburgh Steelers.
The first team standing Baltimore's way is the winless Los Angeles Chargers, who just dropped their eighth straight to start the season in a 44-22 blowout loss to the Houston Texans in Week 9, which might have them consider giving their face of the franchise a much-needed mental reset.
In his second game back from a bye, the Chargers' two-time Pro Bowl QB, Justin Herbert, continued to look like a shell of himself as he was sacked a career-high eight times, added to his league-leading interception total and might've suffered a fractured finger on his left non-throwing hand.
This matchup between  two ailing and surprisingly underperforming teams will take place under national spotlight on Monday Night Football. It has all the makings of the ultimate GBOT (get back on track) for the Ravens on both sides of the ball.
On offense, Brissett helped lead the Arizona Cardinals to an impressive upset win over the Chargers in Week 1 and is poised to beat them again after they just allowed C.J. Stroud to carve them up through the air for almost 400 passing yards and five touchdowns. Defensively, this is the perfect oppertunity for the pass rush to get going, for the secondary to make plays on the ball and front seven to dominate the line of scrimmage.
If the Ravens want keep any glimmer of hope of still being alive and in contention for the postseason by the time Jackson is able to return to action, they can't afford to lose to the only winless team in the league. It might end up being a battle of backup quarterbacks if the Chargers decide to sit Herbert so he doesn't embarass himself or get further banged up in primetime.

title: The Ravens Shunned Experienced Coaches After Firing John Harbaugh. So Far, That Looks Regrettable
full_text:
The Ravens ran a funky head coaching search.
They gave a nominal look at former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski, a two-time coach of the year, but people close to that coach all along felt like Baltimore wasn’t really interested and he quickly ended up in Atlanta. After general manager Eric DeCosta won the power struggle with potential Hall of Fame head coach John Harbaugh following a terrible 2025 season, the NFL believed Baltimore wanted a young guy.
Owner Steve Bisciotti defended DeCosta’s personnel record to a ridiculous level (“he’s batting .800”) and made a point of letting his fans know DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown had wide swath over the coaching search. The Lombardi Trophy expectations were still the same (“pursuing championships,” Brown said) but they seemed to wanted a guy with roots in their building all along. Even when Buffalo surprisingly fired Sean McDermott – who had won at least one playoff game five straight years – Baltimore made no effort whatsoever to even reach out.
“Not a phone call – nothing,” said one league source with direct knowledge of the situation.
It was going to be Minter and it was Minter – seen as a product of their front office and “winning culture” from his days as a young assistant in Baltimore. The question always lingered around the NFL – was that the right dynamic? Should they really have one of only two staffs in the entire league without a former NFL head coach on it ? And with Harbaugh clearly making a push for NFL Coach of the Year with the Giants (5-2-1 in first place)– a team short on proven starpower and one of the youngest teams in the NFL – execs around the NFL are talking about Baltimore’s lack of direction.
If the team had the alleged roster DeCosta thought it did – with two-time MVP Lamar Jackson having total leverage over the team in 2027 ) would a bunch of novice head coaches be able to get them to click immediately, and take them beyond where Harbaugh could? Shouldn’t experience have been more the rule, if not for the head coach than for the bulk of his staff? Did Brown and DeCosta prize consolidation of power and lack of pushback from first-time coaches over truly trying to seek the best and brightest available to get the team over the top?
With the Ravens likely already having played their last truly meaningful game of the season already and a season spiraling wildly out of control , doing things on offense and defense that are unprecedented in franchise history (in the worst way possible), it’s a disaster. There is a cogent case to be made that DeCosta should have been fired after offensive-line debacle he authored in Buffalo in Week 7.
It would be a surprise if the Ravens (4-5) did the right thing and sold at the trade deadline and it would be even more surprising (with two AFC wins against teams that have three total wins between them) if they salvaged this season. And there is a growing sense that the profile of this staff does not mesh with what was an overwhelmingly veteran roster (in fact, too old and too overpaid at too many key starting spots).
One NFL GM told me over the summer: “Older team, heavy expectations, really young staff. That’s a weird mix.”
I’ve heard variations of this from several people around the NFL I’ve probed about the Ravens in recent weeks. And it makes total sense, and, frankly, made total sense all along.
“Look, that’s an older team, a team that can’t get over the hump, a lot of guys who are in their last year there,” said one longtime NFL personnel executive who has watched the Giants and Ravens closely, among others. “They are used to being coached by experienced coaches, and doing things a certain way.
“You bring in a bunch of young guys, a lot of them have never done it before, you set yourself up for problems. You bring in a bunch of college coaches – that’s not the same thing. Those guys are recruiting, there is so much they do … it’s just not the same thing as what goes on in the NFL. The players see everything. They are going to get away with as much as they can, and that’s what you’re seeing out there …
“You’re seeing it, really, on defense more than anywhere else, and trust me, that’s a big problem in that building right now. They all see the same thing we do. That’s Jesse Minter’s side of the ball. And then look at New York. Total opposite.
“They have a young team, bunch of college kids, don’t know how to win yet. They got a guy who is super experienced and knows how to win. They know the kind of staff he’s going to bring, and the young players see that. That defense is overachieving. It’s the opposite of Baltimore. They’ve got big problems. The film is bad.”
Another NFL GM told me: “A lot of us were saying it when they set up the interviews. Minter was their guy. DeCosta wanted young guys he could control. Now they have to try to fix it.”
Minter is going to have to learn to juggle running a defense and coaching the entire football team at the same time. Declan Doyle still doesn’t even know here he should be calling plays from ( try it from the sidelines, rook). The choking that began under Harbaugh immediately met new lows under this staff.
We’ll never know what might have been with a staff led be proven winners. That’s never where this was going. But there is no denying the impact Harbaugh immediately made with the Giants , and no denying just how massive Minter’s learning curve has proven to be.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills' Week 10 Injury Outlook for Dalton Kincaid, Spencer Brown, Christian Benford
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills took care of business on Monday Night Football in Week 9, and they appear to have avoided any new serious injuries in the process.
In all, four Bills' players visibly received medical attention at some point during the November 9 victory over the Minnesota Vikings . All four eventually returned to action, but they'll warrant monitoring in Week 10 as Buffalo prepares to visit the New York Jets.
The Bills, who placed wide receiver Josh Palmer on Injured Reserve prior to the primetime kickoff, were without the starting left side of their offensive line in the 23-6 primetime road win.
With left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson scratched due to injuries that emerged in Week 8 against the Baltimore Ravens, and seemingly week to week, starting right tackle Spencer Brown was dinged up again on Monday night.
Additionally, tight end Dalton Kincaid apparently rolled his ankle early during the fourth quarter. He was slow to get up, but missed minimal time.
Both Brown and Kincaid were already on the injury report due to other issues.
In the defensive backfield, lead cornerback Christian Benford and safety Damar Hamlin both needed trips to the locker room late in the first half.
Here's what we know about each player with a November 15 divisional road game looming.
After recovering from a back flare-up that kept him out against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, Brown picked up a lower body injury against the Vikings.
Brown, who was visibly experiencing discomfort at different points on the field, reportedly rolled his ankle during the first half, and proceeded to grind through the rest of the way. He played every snap until the final three kneel downs.
"I'm just playing football right now. It's a tough sport. That's why I play it. That's why I love to play it. I look forward to next week and getting back out there again," said Brown after the win .
It's important to see how the ankle reacts when the Bills begin prep for the New York Jets on Wednesday in Orchard Park.
Kincaid's ankle was twisted up as he went to the ground blocking for wide receiver DJ Moore along the sideline on a 2nd-and-8 play with 14:12 remaining in the fourth quarter.
Briefly leaving to have his ankle examined and subsequently taped, Kincaid quickly returned later during the same possession. With 8:12 left, the tight end made a nice snag for a five-yard gain to convert a 3rd-and-3.
Kincaid had been on the Bills' official injury report due to a ribs/chest issue that dates back to October 18 against the Las Vegas Raiders. He was upgraded to a full participant in practice leading up to Monday Night Football.
Benford's injury seemingly warrants the most cause for concern out of the four players. He apparently jammed his wrist while taking Vikings' wide receiver Justin Jefferson to the ground following a catch with less than 1:00 remaining in the first half.
The Bills' cornerback got a head start to the locker room while being ruled questionable to return. After apparently checking out satisfactorily , Benford was back on the field for the first snap of the third quarter.
Buffalo pulled Benford for the remainder of the night later in the quarter, but he remained on the sideline in full uniform. Officially logging 28 of a possible 48 defensive reps, he reportedly told Buffalo News' writer Jay Skurski that X-rays on his hand/wrist were negative.
Back in a starting role since Chauncey Gardner-Johnson's dismissal, Hamlin reportedly cramped up right around halftime . As a result, Geno Stone started the third quarter in his place.
Reportedly receiving IV in the locker room, Hamlin was unavailable for the first defensive possession after halftime. Missing only four total snaps, he returned to action with 5:59 left in the third quarter.

title: Analyzing New Safety Amani Hooker's 2026 Season & How He Can Vastly Improve Bills Defense
full_text:
We went into deadline day on Tuesday hoping the Buffalo Bills would make a trade for a safety because of their obvious need there.
Well, Bills general manager Brandon Beane has answered the bell and made the kind of trade fans were hoping for after he acquired safety Amani Hooker in a trade with the Tennessee Titans.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Hooker is coming to Buffalo in exchange for a second-round pick, but the Bills are receiving a fifth-rounder back, also.
That's an overpay for Hooker, who is a very good but not elite safety, but that doesn't really matter. Beane needed to do something big to help his struggling defense, and he finally did it.
Now, let's dive into the details and see what Hooker brings to defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit.
The first thing that jumps off the page at us is Hooker's five interceptions this year, which are tied for the most in the NFL.
New Bills safety Amani Hooker ranks 1st in interceptions (5) among safeties this year The Bills entire safety room has 1 interception so far this season
Now, three of those came in Week 8 against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals, but Hooker has always had a nose for the football, as evidenced by his four or more picks in two other campaigns.
Hooker is showing he can do a little bit of everything this season. According to Pro Football Focus , Hooker is sporting grades of 75.2 in coverage and 83.9 in run defense.
Those marks from PFF are good enough to rank 10th and 13th, respectively, at the safety position, which makes Hooker one of the more well-rounded safeties in the NFL.
We already talked about Hooker's nose for the football with his five picks and 17 career interceptions over seven-plus seasons. His five picks are four more than Bills safeties have combined.
Hooker is a versatile player with his experience playing as a box and free safety, and he even has snaps in the slot. However, he thrives most at the latter safety position, where he can roam downfield and makes plays on the football in coverage.
According to Pro Football Focus ' John Kosko, Hooker is one of the elite safeties in deep zone coverage in the NFL, something the PFF writer proclaimed in 2025 — and that hasn't changed since.
"Hooker isn’t a household name, but he’s been a solid safety for several years," Kosko wrote. "In 2024, he notched career highs in interceptions and pass breakups, preventing separation and reading routes and the eyes of the quarterback at a high level."
Amani Hooker showing off some insane body control and focus for the interception pic.twitter.com/9DCMYkarkd
That makes Hooker a great fit, as the Bills need someone down the field who can help limit explosive plays. Buffalo has given up 28 completions of 20-plus yards this season.
With his five picks and six passes defensed through seven games, Hooker is well on his way to surpassing his career-highs in both those categories in 2026.
When you add it all up, it's shocking that Hooker has never been voted to a Pro Bowl or received an All-Pro nod, but he has also flown under the radar with a Titans team that doesn't get any semblance of consistent attention from the NFL world.
It's a safe bet that now that he's in Buffalo, Hooker is not going to be flying under the radar any longer.

title: Buffalo Bills Acquiring Amani Hooker in Trade With Tennessee Titans
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have reportedly agreed to a trade with the Tennessee Titans for safety Amani Hooker.
The Ringer's Tom Pelissero was the first to report the news.
"Trade! The Titans are sending standout safety Amani Hooker to the Bills," Pelissero reported.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Bills are sending the Titans a second-round pick and will be getting a fifth-rounder back from Tennessee.
"The Titans are trading S Amani Hooker to the Bills, with a 2nd round pick going and a 5th rounder coming back, sources say," Rapoport reported.
General manager Brandon Beane has officially answered the prayers of Bills fans who were hoping the team would pull off a significant trade for a safety.
The Bills had a clear need at the safety position, and that was true before the team released C.J. Gardner-Johnson recently .
With Gardner-Johnson gone, the Bills were looking at a starting duo of Cole Bishop and Damar Hamlin, which wasn't ideal. Backing them up were guys like Geno Stone, Sam Franklin and rookie Jalon Kilgore, who was left inactive in Week 9.
Now, with Hooker in the mix, the Bills have shored up their safety spot in a big way.
A former fourth-round pick of the Titans in 2019, Hooker isn't an elite safety, but he is definitely in that next tier at the position.
Hooker offers versatility with his ability to play back deep and in the box. His best attribute might be his ability to turn the ball over, with the veteran safety notching five picks this season, and he has posted four or more interceptions three times during his career, giving him 17 in total over seven-plus seasons in the league.
In 2026, Hooker is having a phenomenal year, both in coverage and in run defense. According to Pro Football Focus , the Iowa product has posted grades of 75.2 in coverage and 83.9 in run defense, ranking 10th and 13th at the position.
With the addition of Hooker, the Bills will now sport a one-two punch of Hooker and Cole Bishop, and that will push Damar Hamlin back to the backup role he's better suited for.
Giving up a second-round pick for a player who is a very good but not elite safety qualifies as an overpay, but getting the fifth-round selection back softens the blow a bit, as does the fact that Hooker has two more years left on his deal after this one.
But I don't think Bills fans are going to care all that much about what Beane gave up because they have been wanting him to make a big move and show he's all-in. This amounts to the biggest addition Beane has ever made near the trade deadline.
Hooker isn't the top of the heap when it comes to all-in moves, but giving up a second-rounder for him is as close as Buffalo is going to get. Most importantly, the Bills' defense is now better with Hooker in the fold.

title: Budda Baker Trade Rumors Give Bills Mixed Signals For Potential Deadline Deal with Cardinals
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills need a safety and Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker seems like a logical trade candidate for the Bills to pursue.
After all, the Cardinals are going nowhere this season and it makes sense to trade a soon-to-be 31-year-old safety who is likely to be on the decline before the Cardinals are competitive again.
The logical approach for the Cardinals would be to trade Baker and get some draft capital to help the rebuild.
However, the Cardinals still don't appear willing to trade Baker, even though the veteran safety is rumored to be interested in joining a contender, per Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer .
"The Cardinals have gotten calls on star safety Budda Baker, who I’ve heard wouldn’t mind being dealt to a contender. Thus far, (the Cardinals) haven’t been as receptive to moving him," Breer wrote.
This is the second report in recent days that has stated Baker wouldn't mind a change of scenery .
"My sense is Budda Baker would welcome chance to play for contender if (Arizona) entertains talks (big if)," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported.
Talk about mixed signals. The player wouldn't mind getting traded but the team doesn't want to trade him.
The good news for the Bills, who are reportedly in the market for a safety, is that Baker's desire to join a contender might push the Cardinals to trade him.
It's just hard to fathom that the Cardinals wouldn't oblige his desire after all Baker has meant to the franchise. We'll know soon enough if that's the case.
When trying to figure out what Baker could cost, there are a few factors, like how much of his contract the Cardinals will be willing to pick up. That's something the Bills will likely need them to do with Buffalo's miniscule amount of cap space ($3.9 million).
We would hold up the Jacksonville Jaguars' trade with the Atlanta Falcons for Jessie Bates as an example of what Baker may cost.
Jacksonville gave up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for Bates, and the Falcons picked up some of Bates' base salary as part of the deal.
With Baker and Bates on an even playing field in terms of their stature as two of the better safeties in the NFL, the Bills could be looking at giving up as much as a second-round pick and then another selection, assuming Arizona picks up some money.
If the Bills take on all of Baker's contract, then it could cost a third-round pick and a Day 3 selection.
Now, both of those deals are expensive for a safety, but the Bills should have no issue paying up. After all, they have a big need at safety and should be all in during another season in which they are a legit Super Bowl contender.
Josh Allen isn't getting any younger and now is as good a time as ever to strike on a big trade, whether that's at safety or another position of need.
Whether or not general manager Brandon Beane actually gets it done remains to be seen, but history suggests he won't.

title: NFL Trade Deadline: Three Reasons Bills Should Pass on Cornerback
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills need help on defense, and multiple reports have confirmed that Brandon Beane's focus at the deadline has been trying to help Jim Leonhard's struggling unit.
A tweet on Saturday from NFL reporter Albert Breer specified which positions Beane is looking at, which mentioned corner and safety as deadline targets for Buffalo.
I recently examined four salary-cap-friendly safety targets for the Bills because I believe it is their strongest position of need. I don't feel the same about the state of Buffalo's cornerbacks, so here's three reasons why Beane should not give up draft picks and salary cap allocation to the CB position at the deadline.
IGB has been a surprise contributor for Leonhard's defense, after Maxwell Hairston struggled to start the season.
The rookie has recorded eight pass break ups already this season, surrendering a 51.5% completion percentage when targeted. There's no reason to give up the premium assets necessary to acquire a CB that would start over him.
The former Buckeye needs to clean up the penalties - already with six in seven games - but sometimes that is a consequence you can live with given the physical edge he brings to each and every down.
If the Bills are truly interested in a CB, but someone that would fill in as depth behind Benford and Igbinosun, that would make more sense. However, they just acquired their CB3 a few weeks ago.
Tre'Davious White had a strong campaign in 2025 considering it was his age-30 season. Starting 16 games, he recorded 10 passes defended and an INT, along with 40 tackles and six TFLs. In coverage, opposing QBs had a 71.1 passer rating when targeting the veteran, completing just 51.1% of their passes.
White isn't the All-Pro he once was - multiple season-ending injuries will do that to a player - but he's still a roster-caliber player who hasn't shown signs of a steep decline just yet. The Bills should take advantage of the experience and leadership they currently possess on the practice squad, and have White serve as the team's third boundary corner come the postseason.
After surprisingly drafting IGB in the second round of the draft, Beane emphasized the importance of having depth at the CB position. I'm not here to debate that. However, the Bills have more depth than usual between White, Hairston, and technically Dee Alford.
Alford has been the team's primary slot corner this season, where he's had his ups and downs, but the former Falcon also has experience playing on the outside. In 2025, he recorded 143 snaps on the boundary, showcasing his ability to play wherever Atlanta needed him.
I'm not advocating for Buffalo to officially move him to the perimeter, but in a pinch, the emergence of a former practice squad player might make that decision easier.
Te'Cory Couch enjoyed a stellar game last week against the Ravens. Yes, Joe Fagnano was in at QB, but that didn't change the fact that he was matched up against the talented Zay Flowers and capable Rashod Bateman. Couch's understanding of coverage assignments, sticky man coverage, and communication skills were on full display, and should give Buffalo confidence to deploy him when necessary moving forward.

title: James Cook Praise, Joe Brady Criticism Among Four Main Takeaways from Bills' Road Win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills appeared to do it the hard way at times, but the end result was just what the doctor ordered .
Going up against the Minnesota Vikings and their vaunted defense on the road, the Bills posted a 23-6 victory on Monday Night Football in the final Week 9 game.
Buffalo's 23 points were the most allowed by Minnesota in eight games this season. Meanwhile, the Bills' defense held their opponent under 200 yards of total offense for the second week in a row albeit against inept quarterbacking.
The Bills (7-1) are far from perfect, but they have yet to lose a road game under first-year head coach Joe Brady and would be the AFC's No. 1 seed if the playoffs began today.
"We haven't done a damn thing yet. We haven't earned anything in this league yet," said Brady following the November 9 win .
While Buffalo still has plenty to prove, they showed a lot on Monday. Here are four main takeaways from the gritty road win.
Cook wasn't gaining much traction early on, but the Bills' bellcow running back kept pounding. Primarily known for his explosion and acceleration, the reigning NFL rushing champion dug deep against a stingy Vikings' defense.
Carrying the ball 31 times, Cook exceeded the 100-yard mark for the fourth time in eight games. He rushed for 107 hard-earned yards and one touchdown.
Cook eventually wore down Minnesota's defensive front, gaining 47 yards on an important fourth-quarter touchdown drive.
“I mean, that's James Cook," said quarterback Josh Allen , a five-time NFL MVP finalist. "It was awesome to sit back and kind of watch him run, especially late in that drive, and making guys miss and finding his way into the end zone. Again, the more times we can get James Cook the ball, the better we're going to be as an offense."
Yes, the opposing quarterback play has been inept to say the least. Still, there's no denying that the communication is crisper and the performance is improved.
Over the past two weeks, the Bills limited the Baltimore Ravens and Minnesota Vikings under 200 yards of total offense. Furthermore, they forced three turnovers in each win.
Buffalo has allowed only one touchdown and 16 combined points over the two-game clip coming out of the bye week, which allowed defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard a reset of sorts.
With Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone picking up the reps, the safety play appears improved following CJ Gardner-Johnson's release. Meanwhile, inside linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams seem more comfortable.
Also, it's worth noting that Leonhard has called the game from the coaches' box the past two weeks, breaking with his pre-bye week approach.
Bass scored 11 points for the Bills, nailing all three field goal attempts to go along with two PATs. He has yet to fail on a field goal try this season.
After missing the entire 2025 campaign due to injury, Bass has returned better than ever. His 19 consecutive successful field goals to start the season stand as a Bills' franchise record.
“This is the only Tyler Bass that I was expecting to get," said Brady. "Like I said, I don't even look at the field goals because I have the confidence in him."
Bass actually made a fourth field goal, splitting the uprights from 54 yards with about 1:00 remaining in the third quarter, but Lloyd Cushenberry was whistled for a false start, so the play never happened.
"T-Bass is doing a really good job. He's playing confidently. And I wish I didn't have to take a field goal off the board for him," said Brady.
Cushenberry's self-inflicted error is only one on a list of Bills' miscues that could prove costly when the stakes are high. Right tackle Spencer Brown accounted for two pre-snap penalties, moving early on two different second-down plays.
In all, Buffalo committed eight accepted penalties to Minnesota's four. The unforced errors, however, are no less worrisome than Joe Brady's second straight poor first-half performance as Bills' offensive play caller.
The Bills' first three possessions began in Minnesota territory, but yielded only three total points. Brady appeared slow to adjust to the Vikings' heavy pressure and heavy boxes.
In addition to a stubbornness that led to seven run plays over the game's first nine first downs, Brady has occasionally chosen low-percentage calls in short yardage situations.
With the Bills facing a 3rd-and-2 late in first quarter, Brady call a toss left running laterally instead of straight upfield. That strategy failed when Allen tried it on 3rd-and-goal from the 1 against the Ravens, so why not double down? Making his decision more puzzling, this time, he called the play in the direction of two backup lineman with second-string tackle Tylan Grable flagged for holding.
The Bills must exercise greater discipline , and Brady needs to stop over coaching.

title: Josh Allen, James Cook Combine to Make NFL Rushing History in Bills' Week 9 Win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills defeated the Minnesota Vikings 23-6 on Monday Night Football, scoring the most points allowed by the Vikings defense this season.
This was in large part due to the success of Josh Allen and James Cook, with the former throwing for 234 yards and a touchdown, and the latter rushing for 107 yards and a touchdown.
On the way to victory in Minnesota, Buffalo's QB1 and RB1 made history, adding to their all-time resumes. They are making the case to be known as the most-effective QB-RB rushing tandem in NFL history.
With his 15 rushing yards on Monday night, Allen became the fifth QB in NFL history to eclipse 5,000 career rushing yards, joining Lamar Jackson, Michael Vick, Cam Newton and Russell Wilson.
Currently sitting at 5,006 in his career, he trails Wilson by 562 yards to move into fourth all-time.
Setting Allen apart from the other four, he became the first QB in NFL history to record 32,000 passing yards and 5,000 rushing yards with one franchise.
In the passing game, Allen's touchdown to Keleki Latu tied him with Peyton Manning for the most passing TDs all-time by a player in their first 10 seasons. Allen is midway through his ninth season.
On the same drive that Allen reached 5k career rushing yards, Cook accomplished the same feat. According to Maddy Glab , they are "the first QB-RB duo in NFL history to reach 5K as teammates in the same season." He is now up to 5,073 yards in his career.
Cook trails Fred Jackson by 573 yards to move into third in franchise history in rushing yards, where he'd be trailing only OJ Simpson and Thurman Thomas.
Additionally, Cook recorded a rushing TD and at least 75 rushing yards in the seventh consecutive game, the longest streak in team history. This also marks the longest streak by any player since LaDanian Tomlinson's eight games in 2006.
Cook was tabbed one of five "winners" from the Bills' gritty road victory that kept the team atop the AFC standings. He has four 100-yard rushing performances through the season's first eight games.
