title: Bills Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor, Reported Move for Buffalo
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have one more day to make an addition to their roster via trade, as the NFL trade deadline will fall on Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET.
Sitting at 7-1 after a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night, the Bills once again have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations in 2026, and that means general manager Brandon Beane should be aggressive in order to improve his roster. Unfortunately, there isn't any guarantee he'll actually be aggressive.
The focus is clear for Beane. The Bills desperately need to improve their defense that has been terrible this season. Buffalo has given up 29 points or more in five games, and the three games the Bills' defense did play well, they came against the lowly Los Angeles Chargers and two teams that were starting backups, the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens.
As Beane and the Bills navigate deadline day, you can follow our tracker below for the latest rumors and reported moves Buffalo makes (note: most recent updates are at the top).
TRADE: Bills acquiring Amani Hooker
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Bills are sending the Titans a second-round pick in exchange for Hooker and a fifth-rounder.
Well, the Bills have finally landed the safety they needed, albeit it at an overpay. Hooker isn't elite, but he's in the second tier of players at his position and will provide a boost to Buffalo's defense, so the price was worth it.
You can read more about the Bills' trade for Hooker right here .
Bills have checked in on Budda Baker
According to PHNX Cardinals' Johnny Venerable , the Bills have called the Cardinals about Budda Baker, but it remains unclear whether or not Arizona wants to trade him.
"Can confirm the Buffalo Bills have "checked in" on Budda Baker, per multiple sources. No word on if the Cardinals will move off their Pro Bowl safety. Would likely take ownership approval to sign off on a trading a franchise icon," Venerable reported.
Baker open to trade, but Cards won't move him?
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer is yet another insider reporting that Baker wouldn't mind a trade but the Cardinals don't appear willing to make a move.
"The Cardinals have gotten calls on star safety Budda Baker, who I’ve heard wouldn’t mind being dealt to a contender. Thus far, they haven’t been as receptive to moving him," Breer said.
Free Budda! And, taking it a step further, free him to Buffalo.
In all seriousness, it's hard to believe that the Cardinals won't give Baker what he wants. That would be a major slap in the face to a player who has meant so much to the franchise.
Budda Baker might want a trade, Amani Hooker staying put
Two players linked to the Bills often have been Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker.
Jeremy Fowler reports that Baker might be open to a trade , but it remains to be seen if the Cardinals want to trade him. Meanwhile, the Titans are keen on keeping Hooker.
"My sense is Budda Baker would welcome chance to play for contender if AZ entertains talks (big if). Tennessee has calls on Amani Hooker but wants to keep him," Fowler reported.
Bills looking for safety, cornerback help
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler is reporting that the Bills "have scanned the safety pool of late."
Both Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer and The Athletic's Jonathan Jones have previously reported the same , although both added cornerback as another position the Bills are looking around for.
"The Bills have made calls on safeties and cornerbacks," Jones wrote
"I had it in my last trade column, and will add it here — The Bills are still looking in to adding a piece on the defensive side of the ball. And specifically at corner and safety," Breer said.
TRADE: Bills acquiring Amani Hooker, fifth-round pick from Titans for second-round pick ( read more here ).
History of Bills' in-season trades under Brandon Beane
Over his tenure as general manager, Beane has made eight trades during a season. Here's a look at what he has done in the past:
2017: DT Marcel Dareus to Jaguars 2017: WR Kelvin Benjamin from Panthers 2018: OL Marshall Newhouse to Panthers 2019: WR Zay Jones to Raiders 2022: S Dean Marlowe from Falcons 2023: RB Nyheim Hines from Colts for RB Zack Moss, R6 pick 2023: CB Rasul Douglas from Packers 2024: WR Amari Cooper from Browns
Safety: The Bills need a starter here after cutting C.J. Gardner-Johnson . Damar Hamlin is having a nice season, but he's better suited as a backup.
Cornerback: With uncertainty surrounding Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston, the Bills could use help on the boundary across from Christian Benford. Slot cornerback is another spot where Buffalo could add with Dee Alford's struggles.
Linebacker: An addition at this position makes sense for the Bills because they could use an upgrade over Dorian Williams and it doesn't look like Kaleb Elarms-Orr is ready to be that guy.

title: Why Brandon Beane, Bills Should Not Trade for Defensive Help at NFL Deadline
full_text:
The final hours until the 2026 NFL trade deadline await the Buffalo Bills , and in the midst of their Week 9 battle against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night, it's decision time for general manager Brandon Beane on whether he wants to improve an ailing defense .
The Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears are two teams that have swung trades to acquire defenders, whether they're big names or depth pieces, and Beane has been pressured to kingdom come to be as aggressive as James Gladstone, Ryan Poles and other GMs.
However, there are reasons for Bills fans to feel optimistic about their defense, which ranks 23rd in the NFL in EPA per play and 28th in EPA per dropback as of Monday, if Buffalo does not acquire anyone of note before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline.
Heck of a read by Geno Stone on IGB's interception! I expect the Bills to utilize these Dime groupings with 3 Safeties on the field a lot the rest of the season. pic.twitter.com/4mxHwkZMa6
C.J. Gardner-Johnson's release following his one-game suspension for spitting on Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers came with another reason: Geno Stone, who signed a one-year deal in March . After failing to make the 53-man roster, he joined the Bills' practice squad and made his debut on November 1 against the Baltimore Ravens.
Stone tied for the team lead with six tackles while adding a tackle for loss and a pass defended. He was also partially responsible for Davison Igbinosun's first career interception, tipping a Joe Fagnano pass into the air for the rookie corner to snatch.
Stone was called up from the practice squad again on Monday just before the Bills' game against the Vikings, and if he plays well against Carson Wentz and Justin Jefferson, that may deter Beane from going after someone like Budda Baker .
Davison Igbinosun has quietly been one of the STICKIEST CB’s in the NFL this season. Through six games, Igbinosun LEADS the Bills’ defense with 7 PD’s (T-6th in NFL). The Bills rookie CB might find himself as the team’s CB1 sooner rather than later 😳🔒 pic.twitter.com/Zcr4q4AWqR
Speaking of Jefferson, the Bills' second-round rookie cornerback out of Ohio State , Igbinosun, may have to face him a few times. If he does, it'll be a great chance to present himself to a national audience as someone on the rise.
Igbinosun took the starting cornerback spot opposite Christian Benford from former first-round pick Maxwell Hairston against the Ravens. After three passes defended against the Raiders in Week 6, he tallied another to go with his first career pick in Week 8.
The Bills' defense as a whole rebounded nicely against the Ravens, even if they went up against a third-string quarterback for the majority of the game, and Igbinosun was a main reason for that.
Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard, the Bills' two main linebackers, have struggled in spots this season , and if they play poorly on Monday night, things may need to change. Buffalo may not have to look outside their organization for help, however.
The answer may come in the form of giving fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr more snaps or elevating Shaq Thompson , who made six starts for the Bills in 2025, from the practice squad.
If Thompson were to be elevated, his experience would mesh nicely with a Buffalo defense that does not have a player whose first season in the league was earlier than 2018.
Regardless, Monday night's game will be very telling as to whether Beane will or will not feel the urgency to make a trade acquisition to aid the defense.

title: Five Winners, One Loser from Bills' Gutsy Road Victory over Vikings on Monday Night
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills dominated on defense, and its offense wore the Minnesota Vikings down over the course of a 23-6 road win on Monday Night Football.
The Bills possessed the ball for an astounding 42:32, holding their second straight opponent under 200 yards of total offense. Buffalo's defense did not permit a third-down conversion on eight attempts.
Meanwhile, going against the Vikings' vaunted defense , the Bills did enough when they had to.
As for the individual actors who led the Bills (7-1) past the Vikings (6-2), here five WINNERS and one LOSER.
It was tough sledding for most of the night, but Cook kept at it. The reigning NFL rushing champion didn't stop grinding, accounting for 107 yards and one touchdown on a season-high 31 carries.
Cook rushed for 47 yards on a fourth-quarter possession punctuated by the running back's five-yard touchdown burst. He has four 100-yard rushing performance through the first eight games.
Latu's first career touchdown reception came with the Bills struggling to gain traction during the first half. Buffalo's fourth tight end hauled in a 25-yard scoring strike on a broken play.
With Allen escaping the pocket, the defense seemingly forgot about Latu, who was waiting alone in the end zone. Rolling right toward the sideline, Allen stopped and fired a beauty for the game's first touchdown.
Much like the first half against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, the Bills' offense looked out of sync through the opening 30 minutes on Monday Night Football. Brady called rushes on seven of the first nine first-down snaps despite repeatedly running into a wall.
After Josh Allen failed on trying to go wide at the goal line against the Ravens, Buffalo foolishly called an outside run on a key 3rd-and-2 inside Vikings' territory rather than opt for a higher percentage play. Running behind backups at left tackle and left guard, Cook was dropped for a two-yard loss while Tylan Grable was called for holding.
Rousseau single-handedly derailed a Vikings' second-quarter possession in Bills' territory. He sacked Carson Wentz on first down followed by a pressure and pass deflection on 2nd-and-21.
After one sack, three quarterback hits and two pass deflections against the Ravens, Rousseau kept the heat on against the Vikings. He also recovered a fumble when a lateral pass to Justin Jefferson went awry.
Bernard has been criticized for appearing slow and out of position in the Bills' new defense , but the co-captain looked like his old self on Monday.
In addition to making a couple nice hits that held the opponent short of the sticks, Bernard made a nice interception and subsequently dropped a second pick. Leading the team with six tackles, Bernard held it down in the middle of the defense.
Playing alongside Bernard, Williams made three tackles in the victory. Furthermore, the inside linebacker was effective in pass coverage, which hasn't necessarily been his strength as a pro.
After Bernard was flagged for a 19-yard penalty that gave the Vikings a 1st-and-10 from the Bills' 37, Williams delivered a true momentum shifter. On 3rd-and-5, Williams intercepted an underthrown ball by Wentz while covering Vikings' tight end TJ Hockenson one-on-one down the seam.

title: Despite Doing Nothing, Panthers’ NFC South Title Chances Grew at Deadline
full_text:
There is one division in the National Football League where all four teams are each at least three games over .500. That would be the formidable NFC North, led by the 7–2 Chicago Bears, a pair of 6-2 teams in the Detroit Lions and the Minnesota Vikings and the 6-3 Green Bay Packers.
Then there’s the other side of the coin. There’s a division in which all four clubs are at least two games under 500. Both the Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints, who face each other this week in the Superdome, own 3-5 win-loss records. Just behind them are the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Atlanta Falcons, each with a 3-6 résumé.
It’s certainly anyone’s guess who is going to emerge as the winner of this mess, and with what record? Keep in mind that twice in the previous four seasons, the 2022 Buccaneers and the 2025 Panthers were crowned champions with 8-9 marks.
On Tuesday afternoon at 4:00 pm ET, the window closed when it came to trading players. Both the Saints and Falcons were involved in deals earlier this week. On Monday, New Orleans sent defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a conditional 2028 sixth-round selection.
Meanwhile, Atlanta traded former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates, tied for the team lead with 60 tackles, to Jacksonville for a second-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round choice in 2028. The Falcons were also involved in a deal on Tuesday in which they acquired guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick for center Ryan Neuzil from the Baltimore Ravens.
On the other hand, the Panthers, who suffered their third straight loss on Sunday, sat on their paws and made no deals to fortify their injury-riddled roster. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain on injured reserve, as does right tackle Taylor Moton. Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips has missed the last three games. This is a banged-up football team.
Nonetheless, general manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales appear to be content with the hand they have been dealt to date. Perhaps an even bigger point is the fact that both the Saints and especially the Falcons were willing to part ways with performers that could certainly help a side of the ball that seems to be each club’s weak spot.
Entering Week 10, the Saints are 29th in the league in total defense, are allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per game and giving up the fifth-most passing yards per contest. The Falcons are 23rr in total defense and have already surrendered 24 offensive touchdowns in nine games.
This Sunday at the Superdome, Bryce Young and company look to get back in the win column and raise their record within the division to 2-1 with a victory over Kellen Moore’s team, who swept Carolina in 2025. Apparently, the shorthanded but still-talented Panthers are content to play with the hand they’ve been dealt— and it may indeed prove to be the right strategy.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Panthers Made a Huge Mistake at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone , and the Carolina Panthers roster looks the exact same. No moves were made by a Carolina team that's on a three-game skid , sitting at 3-5 this season, and somehow still at the top of the NFC South.
No matter where a team sits in its division, 3-5 isn't good enough, especially for a Carolina team that made the playoffs in 2025. The roster is riddled with injuries, something no one wants to see.
However, Carolina could have addressed those holes in the roster with plug-in players who wouldn't cost absurd draft compensation.
Now, with the roster intact, Carolina has to roll with what they got, and in some areas, there's very little depth because the depth chart is so thin at positions like the secondary.
Another puzzling piece of this is that Carolina has its draft capital. The Panthers were never going to make some big swing at a Jonathan Taylor or someone else who warrants a first-round pick, but could've added some solid depth at areas that need it.
Carolina has four cornerbacks injured right now; three of them are on IR, including starters Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn. The secondary proved to be a massive problem against the Denver Broncos.
On obvious passing downs, such as third-and-long situations, the Broncos targeted Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton. Even when they didn't complete a pass, the Broncos drew penalties against defensive backs who don't get in-game reps against high-level opponents.
Adding a corner like Riq Woolen, a proven starter who was part of a Super Bowl defense in 2025, made perfect sense for Carolina. Other corners like Alonte Taylor or Keisean Nixon would've made sense.
Another helpful move would've been to address the pass rush, since Carolina only has only 12 sacks this season. The Panthers could've done so by targeting Will McDonald IV of the New York Jets. Khalil Mack from the Chargers would've been nice too, but it became clear leading up to the deadline that the Chargers weren't going to be sellers.
Speaking with the media on Monday, the Panthers' head coach said that he's opening the 21-day practice window for WR Xavier Legette. Furthermore, Canales added that both Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn "are close," which is fantastic news.
However, Carolina needs to find wins now, and adding another corner while Jackson and Horn ramp back up would've been ideal. Over the next month, Carolina faces elite receivers like Chris Olave, Zay Flowers, and Justin Jefferson. Carolina will need its starting secondary sooner rather than later.
The Panthers head to New Orleans for a crucial division matchup with the Saints on Sunday.

title: The Panthers Trade Deadline Showed Us Exactly Who They Are
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers, for the second straight year, stood pat at the deadline. Despite having rampant needs on a first-place (shockingly) team and expendable players they could've used to bring in draft capital, they did nothing.
The division is so open that either path would've been smart. The Panthers could afford to offload a few players to get picks for the future without mortgaging their chance to defend the NFC South crown. But they're also in first place with a host of injury-related needs, so adding players to bolster the first-place roster would've been good, too.
Instead, the Panthers sat on their hands. They were aggressive over the offseason, signaling that they felt the division was theirs to take. Now, when they had another chance to be aggressive and take hold of the South, they balked.
It is so clear that this team is a playoff contender when semi-healthy. They have the offense to score with anyone so long as Bryce Young gets a modicum of time in the pocket. They have the pieces on defense to get stops when needed as long as they have functioning cornerbacks.
This is a team that beat the Detroit Lions with no cornerbacks . It's a team that nearly beat the Green Bay Packers despite a roughly 50% pressure rate surrendered by the offensive line. They are a couple of plays away from having a really good record.
Now, if they were 3-5 in the NFC North, you could dismiss the argument that they're close to being a good team because that division is so good. But in the NFC South, that argument should be everything. It should be evidence that a couple of additions would be game-changing.
It's not like the Panthers need to add Jonathan Taylor or Maxx Crosby. They're not looking for a quarterback like the Minnesota Vikings are. And they don't need superstar, long-term additions.
They need a cornerback who can play at the NFL level for a few weeks and some people who can block. Offensive line depth is low around the NFL, but we're not asking for Quenton Nelson here.
There's obviously a lot more to it than just seeing a need and addressing it, but the Panthers didn't seem to try. They were content taking advantage of being in a bad division and remaining a bad team.
But at the same time, not trading away Ja'Tavion Sanders or AJ Dillon makes little sense, either. They want to have their cake and eat it, too.
In other words, they showed everyone exactly who they are and who they want to be.

title: Panthers' Week 9 Loss to Broncos Sends Clear Message Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Panthers had a chance to send a message to the rest of the league on Sunday as they took on the Denver Broncos. However, the Panthers were defeated by the Broncos 26-21, dropping to 3-5 on the year after losing three consecutive games.
The Panthers proved that they can compete with a good team in the AFC but also showed that there is still a lot of work to be done with this team. Bryce Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns, but costly mistakes kept Carolina from coming away with the win.
The Carolina Panthers have until Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET to make a trade . Carolina's general manager, Dan Morgan, must decide whether to add a player to help the team make a push for the playoffs or be patient and continue building through the draft.
That decision was made a little easier on Sunday with the Panthers' loss to the Broncos.
This is still a work-in-progress team that is showing signs of growth in some areas but is still a far cry from being a complete football team. There have been times when the offense has looked very good, but even when Carolina moves the football, mistakes and missed opportunities have made it difficult to finish games.
The defense has given up too many big plays in several games, and there are still questions about whether the team has enough talent to get consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks.
These are issues that will not be resolved by the addition of one player via trade before Tuesday afternoon.
The Panthers have tried to build a team for more than one season over the last few years. Giving up draft picks for a player who may help the Panthers for a few months but then leave in free agency is not in the best interest of a team currently sitting below .500.
While there is some value in exploring possible trades, Morgan should be cautious about overpaying for a player just to win a few more games this season. Carolina's injuries at cornerback have already raised questions about how much the team should be willing to give up for help .
There is a huge difference between making a trade that helps build the Panthers' roster for the future and making a trade to try to win more games this year.
While the Panthers lost on Sunday, they also showed that they are not as far away from competing with the upper echelon of the NFL as their record would indicate. Carolina moved the football well against Denver and had a chance to win the game late.
That gives the coaching staff something to work with for the remainder of the season. But it does not mean that the front office should start dealing future assets to try to make the playoffs this season.
Morgan needs to continue focusing on building a more talented defense for the Panthers and building around Bryce Young rather than trying to find quick solutions.
By the end of the season, the Panthers should have a better understanding of which players on the current roster need a bigger role on the team and which positions need to be addressed in the offseason.
While there is nothing wrong with trying to make the team better before the deadline, it would be wise for the Panthers to avoid overpaying for a player who does not fit into the organization's long-term plans.
The Panthers have enough talent to take another step forward this season. However, they are not ready to mortgage the future of the organization to make the playoffs this year.
Sunday's loss to Denver was another reminder of that.
General manager Dan Morgan should be willing to listen to offers and make a move if the right opportunity presents itself. But if nothing happens by Tuesday's deadline, that wouldn't be a bad thing either.
Sometimes the best move a general manager can make is knowing when not to make one.

title: Panthers' Cornerback Injuries Expose a Problem Dan Morgan Can't Ignore
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have had many cornerbacks go down with injuries this season, and Panthers general manager Dan Morgan is currently searching for some healthy bodies to put out on the field. The Panthers also had a lack of depth at the position even before all of these injuries occurred.
Now, with Tuesday afternoon's NFL trade deadline approaching, Morgan is going to have to make a decision as to whether or not to trade for a cornerback or wait until the offseason.

To make matters worse, Akayleb Evans was placed on IR on October 29. Additionally, rookie Will Lee III suffered a hamstring injury against the Packers. The Panthers were down to their last healthy cornerbacks on the roster for the Broncos game.
Chau Smith-Wade is listed as a starting cornerback for the Panthers, with Malcolm DeWalt IV listed as a backup on the depth chart.
Of course, the coaching staff is trying to get the best out of what's left of the roster, but there's only so much they can do with so many players injured.
The number of injuries the Panthers have experienced at cornerback this season was unforeseen by many. However, the injuries have exposed the need for the Panthers to have a better plan behind their starters at cornerback.
Carolina does not have to make a trade before today's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. Morgan could look to add a veteran cornerback to help the team out for the rest of the year. He could also look to use an early pick in the draft on another cornerback or make it a priority in free agency.
Horn and Jackson will return at some point, but that doesn't mean the Panthers will be in good shape at the position if either player goes down again for an extended period of time.
Morgan can't just go out and find another cornerback to put on the field. He has to find a player who can do what the coaching staff wants him to do without forcing the rest of the defense to make so many adjustments when a starter is out of action.
The Panthers have tried to put together a roster to contend in the NFC South over the last few years, but cornerback is still a position of concern.
Morgan doesn't have to make a desperate move before the deadline, but he does need to make sure the Panthers have better options behind their starters moving forward.

title: 2 Trades the Panthers Have to Make After 3rd Straight Loss
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline is here, and there's potential for an active day filled with surprising moves and big names dealt to new franchises. The Carolina Panthers are in a precarious spot entering Tuesday's deadline.
Coming off a third straight loss , this time at home to the Denver Broncos. The Panthers have taken a nosedive from their 3-2 start. However, they still remain alive for the division title because the NFC South is so bad this season.
The NFC South went 1-3 in Week 9, with the New Orleans Saints as the lone winner. Due to tiebreakers, the Panthers are still sitting atop the division despite a 3-5 record. With the division title still being a real possibility and a pivotal Week 10 matchup against the Saints ahead, Carolina needs to make moves.
Here are two trades that make perfect sense for the Panthers.
Part of the loss to the Broncos that was so frustrating for the Panthers was the issues in the secondary. It was clear that Denver head coach Sean Payton wanted to test the back end of Carolina's defense, and it worked.
Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton received seven penalty flags. Wilson was especially undisciplined, drawing multiple flags for pass interference and even for a taunting call.
If there weren't penalties, then it was either missing assignments or just losing one-on-one matchups against Denver's receivers.
There's still time before Jaycee Horn or Mike Jackson returns to the field, so Carolina needs to trade for a bridge starting corner, enter Riq Woolen.
Woolen is coming off a Super Bowl season with the Seahawks, being a contributor to that elite defense. Now he's with the Philadelphia Eagles, who could be in fire-sale mode based on their recent deal involving DT Jordan Davis.
Carolina wouldn't have to give up more than a fourth-round pick for Woolen. The Panthers own two fourth-round picks this year, including their own and the Vikings'.
Carolina's pass rush was supposed to be the team's most improved unit on this team. However, injuries have plagued it thus far. Carolina began the season without budding star Nic Scourton, who tore his ACL, and has been without Jaelan Phillips for weeks due to a hamstring injury.
If there's one way to help the secondary without directly addressing it, it's adding to the pass rush. Will McDonald IV is a key name to watch at the deadline. McDonald requested a trade from the New York Jets because he hasn't seen much usage.
There's clearly talent there, as McDonald has had a double-digit sack season before, with 10.5 in 2024. This could be a situation where a change of scenery unlocks his potential once again.
Carolina would have to give up a valuable asset, likely a second-round pick or a package of a third and a sixth. That said, one of those picks could very well be worth it for a 27-year-old pass rusher who's in the prime of his career.

title: Panthers Stock Up, Stock Down: Two Bright Spots Can't Hide Bigger Problems
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers lost their third consecutive game on Sunday to the Denver Broncos by a score of 26-21. The Panthers are still trying to put together four quarters of quality football this year.
Several Panthers played well in the game, but there are still some major issues that the Panthers have yet to fix this season. Here's a look at whose stock rose and whose stock fell in the game against the Broncos.
Darren Walle r had a phenomenal game for the Panthers, recording eight receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos. This was easily Waller's best game of the season, as he recorded his highest number of receptions and receiving yards in a game this year.
His eight receptions on Sunday were also the most by a Panthers tight end in a single game since Greg Olsen had eight receptions in 2019. The Panthers have been searching for a reliable target in the middle of the field all season, and Waller showed on Sunday that he can be that guy.
Young connected with Waller for a 15-yard touchdown in the third quarter to give the Panthers their first lead of the game. He now has four touchdowns on the year.
The Panthers need to find more ways to get Waller the ball. Young has found another target to trust, especially when the receivers aren't getting open.
Corey Thornton had to step up in a big way against the Broncos. With numerous injuries at cornerback, the Panthers were forced to put Thornton into the starting lineup. Thornton had three tackles, three passes defended and an interception in his first career start.
There were some rough spots for Thornton, including two pass interference penalties, but overall, Thornton showed that he belongs on the field. His interception was one of the better defensive plays of the day for the Panthers.
The Panthers will need even more from Thornton in the coming weeks if the injuries at cornerback continue to mount. While he will make mistakes, Thornton's first career interception and three passes defended in his first career start are something that the coaching staff can build upon.
Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns in the game, some of his better numbers of the season. However, the Panthers' offensive line could not keep the pressure off Young when the Panthers needed another drive to win the game.
With 1:24 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Panthers trailing by five, Broncos linebacker Nik Bonitto stripped the ball from Young and recovered the fumble, ending the Panthers' hopes of scoring late to win the game.
Young was sacked three times against the Broncos after being sacked six times against the Packers the previous week. That is nine sacks in the last two games for Young.
The Panthers' offense had some great moments in the game, but when they needed to score late to win, the protection broke down, and the Panthers never got another opportunity.
There are some good players on the Panthers' roster, but there are some holes as well. The depth at cornerback is definitely one of them. The Panthers have suffered numerous injuries at cornerback, but that does not mean they should be relying on practice-squad players against some of the best teams in the NFL.
The Broncos attacked the Panthers' cornerbacks early in the game. Corey Thornton and Marco Wilson were called for four enforced defensive pass interference penalties, and the P anthers finished with 13 penalties for 119 yards.
The Panthers were already short-handed at cornerback before the game, and Denver took advantage of that weakness.
There are many good things that Morgan has done as general manager of the Panthers, but cornerback depth is still a problem that needs to be addressed. It is hard to expect the defense to play well when players who were not expected to start are suddenly expected to play at a high level.
There is still time before Tuesday's trade deadline for Morgan to make a move to acquire more depth at cornerback. He does not have to give up valuable draft picks to get help, but whether he makes a move now or in the offseason, the Panthers need more dependable players to back up their starting cornerbacks.
The Panthers can hang with the best teams in the NFL, but they need to find a way to finish those games. Until the Panthers solve some of their roster problems, great individual performances like those of Waller and Thornton will not always be enough to win games.

title: Slumping Panthers Still Atop an NFC South in Total Disarray
full_text:
A season ago, the NFC South was won by a team that lost more games than it won. That would be the Carolina Panthers, who captured its first division title since 2015 with an 8-9 win-loss record. Of course, that was also the case back in 2022, when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finished 2022 also managed an 8-9 mark and walked away with the top spot in the division.
Speaking of the Panthers, they are currently tied for the best record in the NFC South with the 3-5 New Orleans Saints. Dave Canales's team currently has the tie-breaking edge due to the fact that they have split a pair of divisional games. On the other hand, Kellen Moore’s club was blasted at home by the Atlanta Falcons, 45-24, on a Monday night in Week 4 in the club’s lone clash with an NFC South rival this season.
That changes this week when the Saints host the Panthers on Sunday afternoon for the first of their two meetings. A year ago, Moore’s team finished 6-11 and in the division basement (the 3 other clubs all posted 8-9 records), but they managed to sweep Carolina. And given the way things have gone for each of the four clubs at home this season, it’s anyone’s guess what will happen at the Superdome.
Not only is every team in this division at least two games under .500, the four clubs all own sub-.500 marks at home. Now keep in mind that the Saints and Falcons have “home” losses to the Steelers and Bengals in Paris and Madrid, respectively. Take those setbacks out and Carolina (1-3), New Orleans (1-3), Tampa Bay (1-4), and Atlanta (1-3) are a combined 4-13 in their own buildings this season.
As for Canales’s club, it is currently in the midst of a three-game skid, the latest loss a 26-21 home setback to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. The slide began back in Week 7 at Bank of America Stadium, when the Bucs opened up a 33-6 halftime advantage on the way to a 43-13 victory. That was followed by a Thursday night loss at Lambeau Field and yesterday’s loss to Sean Payton’s surging club.
The Panthers OL finally gave Bryce Young time to breathe and he rewarded them with a strong performance against the Broncos defense pic.twitter.com/GCGbIlw1cw
Ultimately, it may be the Saints who decide who wins this division due to the fact that they will face NFC South rivals in four of their final five games.
Here are the latest NFL Power Rankings via Vinny Iyer of The Sporting News , and it certainly speaks volumes when it comes to this quartet. He has the Buccaneers as the division’s top team, but at No. 21. They are followed by the Falcons at No. 22, the Saints at No. 23 and the slumping Panthers at No. 25.
Is it a foregone conclusion that the NFC South will have a champion with a losing record for the third time in five years? And is it possible we could see this division by a team with 10 losses?
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Three Greatest Challenges Facing the Bears in Season's Second Half
full_text:
Any disappointment Bears fans might feel from the lack of a trade at the deadline only shows how little they know about the NFL.
Multiiple in-season trades by teams are uncommon occurrences even at the deadline, and the Bears already made their massive one by bringing aboard Jeffery Simmons .
Instead, the roster Ryan Poles and Ben Johnson built will need to try to improve from within, or they could add an unsigned player. Few of those can be very impactful at this time of the year — they'd be on a roster already if they possessed the kind of talent to let them turn a team's fortunes.
Improvement needs to come, though, as the Vikings have just elevated their offense by signing 38-year-old Kirk Cousins. The Packers have apparently improved and also are bringing back Micah Parsons at whatever level of play he can contribute following his knee surgery. And Detroit added a safety, although it still has defensive issues.
NFL FILMS WITH A CINEMATIC MASTERCLASS: An incredible look at the #Bears epic Sunday Night Football victory over the #Bucs at Soldier Field. Ben Johnson has completely transformed Chicago’s culture alongside Caleb Williams. Building something special 🫡 pic.twitter.com/ljEiOQJ9vJ
The Bears face three overriding problems when they begin they play New Orleans in Week 11 after the league goes through the first week of the schedule's second half this weekend.
None of these should seem shocking and the order can be debated. Here's how it looks.
It's an issue they've begun to clean up by adding Simmons, although they did allow one deep ball for 58 yards on Sunday. QBs shouldn't have the time to attack them deep as often. They had a disastrous game at Green Bay that skewed their statistics somewhat, gave up a long one to Seattle, as well. But the number of deep passes has slowed.
Luke Goedeke and the Buccaneers complained that Jeffery Simmons was too physical in the trenches in the Bears' win Sunday. Neville Gallimore shared his perspective, calling it "a part of the game" and saying the Buccaneers were just frustrated that Simmons had such an impact. pic.twitter.com/wN85gRZc8m
It needs to continue. After a first half of the season when they r anked near the bottom of the league in preventing yards per pass attempt and were actually last for a while, they've come up to 26th and are 22nd over the last three games despite facing two Super Bowl teams.
Whether it means Tyrique Stevenson being benched for big plays allowed, or possibly a rotation of corners with Malik Muhammad returning from a toe injury and sharing time with Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson, the Bears might want to look at more change.
The safety position should be fine with improving rookie Dillon Thieneman and veteran Cam Lewis now getting more adjusted to the Dennis Allen scheme. It could really get effective if Coby Bryant returns at safety from his knee injury.
The Bears' defense is currently (with schedule adjustments): - 32nd in early-down EPA per play - 1st in late down success rate A Very Normal Team.
The stats say they're sixth against the run but as former defensive coordinator Greg Blache said, numbers lie. They 23rd in yards allowed per attempt and their overall rushing yardage is low because teams gave up on the run when they were being outscored by Caleb Williams and the Bears offense. They were also hard-pressed for time with the Bears piling up possession time and couldn't run.
The No. 1 third-down defense in the league is no fluke. They are getting opponents into passing situations and have been top three much of the month in forcing three-and-outs. That's because they're getting better at stopping runs on first or second down. Simmons' arrival should help them as much here as with his pass rush. They almost gave up a 100-yard game to Bucky Irving Sunday but there are plenty of defenses doing that. It's a matter of using Simmons well and the rest of their run stuffers continuing to work together better.
They're 20th in limiting rushing yards per attempt in the last three games, so there is a small amount of improvement. Their run defense is already on pace (46) for their most tackles for loss since 2018. It's more a matter of limiting the longer runs than stuffing more runs behind the line.
Jeffery Simmons hustle reel from Week 9. He has the 5th highest single play top speed (over 17 MPH!) among defensive tackles this season, per @SumerSports pic.twitter.com/YbzrnSxVJf
This is where Ben Johnson's offense is built. They started the year cruising a No. 1 and then came Kyle Monangai's injury, the knee injury to left tackle Braxton Jones and more recently a shoulder injury to Jones' replacement, Theo Benedet. All the while they're hoping to get left tackle Ozzy Trapilo back at full strength but he didn't play a down in the last two games.
The Bears still rank third in yardage and more importantly are No. 1 in attempts. Because they're now at nine games, this will drop after other teams catch up to there game total following the bye week. What they are not doing well is averaging solid yardage. They're at 13th in yards per carry at 4.2 and over the past five have failed to average 100 yards rushing per game (98.6).
The trend is definitely downward and it all began right after Monangai's injury in Week 4, when he was coming off his 146-yard rushing day against the New York Jets. Certainly facing three straight difficult run defenses hurt, but having him back in two weeks could make a huge difference.
Another Jeffery Simmons note from @NextGenStats , he was off the field last week for 8 snaps; the Bears allowed 106 yards and a TD on those 8 plays (13.3 yards per play) compared to 146 yards and just one score on 48 plays with Simmons on the field (3.0 yards per play).
Johnson speculates that it might just be the lack of explosive runs. "Being able to have nine games of sample size at this point is going to be really good for us to look into," he said.
The other difference would be a healthier Benedet as he played through a shoulder injury on Sunday. He still had the second-highest Pro Football Focus blocking grade and second-highest pass-blocking grade on the team.
They are still missing an important part of their run game Kyle Monangai. The teams running game  hasn't been the same without him. pic.twitter.com/qQ0DdcwvtL
"He’s tough as nails," guard Jonah Jackson said. "Guys all over the board are dealing with stuff, some things you guys just might not know about. Credit to him doing his job and doing it at a high level." It's a trait often mentioned as necessary by coaches. "We talk about how there are going to be games over the course of the season where you're not 100%, and yet we need you going out there and giving every little ounce you got in your 90% or you're 85%," Johnson said. "I think that was a case of him last night pushing through and being out there for his buddies." Not needing to overcome health issues would be a way to help kick-start the running game, whether it's at guard or at running back.
The Chicago Bears just got their own episode with Caleb Williams, Ben Johnson and Jeffery Simmons in the latest #GridironHeights 😂 🎥: @BleacherReport pic.twitter.com/ccDgkbCZ5c

title: Bears' Cam Lewis Quickly Becoming One of Ryan Poles' Best Offseason Additions
full_text:
Bears defensive back Cam Lewis was initially expected to provide quality depth at both nickelback and safety when he signed a two-year, $6 million deal this offseason.
However, an injury to Coby Bryant at the start of training camp opened the door for him to run with the starting job there. They initially weren't thrilled with that development, bringing in veteran Xavier Woods to compete with Lewis on the back end a week later.
However, Coby Bryant's injury at the start of training camp opened the door for him to grab a starting safety job. They initially weren't thrilled with that development, bringing in veteran Xavier Woods to compete with Lewis on the back end a week later.
Woods got badly exposed in their 31-7 loss against Green Bay, though. That marked the end of his uneventful tenure in the Windy City. Conversely, Lewis' role grew from that point, and he's made the most of the added opportunities .
Lewis has missed only one defensive snap over the past three weeks and has seemingly gotten more comfortable with his role in the scheme. He has an interception and two pass deflections over their past two contests, and has looked confident coming down and making plays in run support.
He's also displayed some physicality in coverage. Lewis is 5'9", and 183 lb, but you wouldn't know it by watching him play.
He set the tone on the first third-down against Seattle, laying a huge hit on Seahawks receiver Tory Horton over the middle.
Cam Lewis with a nasty hit and PBU pic.twitter.com/5k6aRBcjn3
Still, his most impressive play in coverage came on Sunday night against Tampa Bay. He read Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's eyes and jumped in front of a pass when they were driving ahead of halftime.
What an INT by Cam Lewis 🔥 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UiIkSO4Vjo
Lewis has become a jack of all trades for the Bears. In many ways, he has perfectly replaced the impact that C.J. Gardner-Johnson provided last season. He might not be as effective as a blitzer ( we actually called out that area of his game in Week 7 ), but he's more versatile and well-rounded.
Unlike Lewis, CGJG had no interest in playing safety . Lewis, on the other hand, has embraced the position switch after spending much of his time in the slot for Buffalo over the past few seasons. Much like they did last year when Kyler Gordon returned to the lineup in late November, they'll have another interesting spot when Bryant makes his debut next month.
Chicago's big-ticket free agent signing will obviously play a key role when he's ready, but Lewis' presence could allow them to ease him into the lineup. When he is ready to play a full complement of snaps, Lewis can also seamlessly transition to the slot (as we saw when Gordon briefly left the game on Sunday night) and play a key role in dime packages.
The Bears have made a few quality free agent additions since Ryan Poles became the team's general manager in 2022. Andrew Billings made a big impact on their run defense for a bargain-bin price, while T.J. Edwards and Kevin Byard III developed into key starters and filled leadership voids.
It's still too early to group Lewis with those players (although he's already squarely in Billings' tier), but he's well on his way to entering those conversations. He's been one of the Poles' best free agent bargains since taking over the job.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Face a New Division Threat After Vikings Reunite With Kirk Cousins at the Deadline
full_text:
The Chicago Bears let the NFL trade deadline come and go having made one major trade and letting the rest of the NFC shuffle the deck around them. After the Jeffery Simmons trade with the Tennessee Titans a few weeks ago, Ryan Poles and Co. were silent on November 10 .
The Minnesota Vikings certainly weren't within the division, reuniting with Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders to give the Vikings a reliable option under center. Neither were the Detroit Lions, who acquired safety Andre Cisco from the New York Jets on trade deadline eve.
How do these NFC North deals, and others from around the conference, change the game for the Bears in their quest for a first Super Bowl appearance in two decades?
Cousins was playing well in Las Vegas before being dealt back to the Twin Cities, owning a 6.7% negative play rate and owning a low 9.8% sack rate on drop-backs. Behind a suspect Raiders offensive line that has drastically overperformed, that is extremely promising.
Being back with Kevin O'Connell should only bolster Cousins' game over the next few months in a familiar professional place. Cousins' best statistical season was in 2022, O'Connell's first year as the Vikings' head coach.
He's a major upgrade over Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, who, despite leading Minnesota to a 6-2 record, gave the Vikings a lower ceiling.
Cousins was the most significant trade at the deadline and the only blockbuster involving a quarterback on deadline day. Jacoby Brissett was moved out of the NFC when the Baltimore Ravens landed him from the Arizona Cardinals.
Chicago is a trade deadline winner simply by virtue of the rest of the conference (besides Minnesota) largely sitting on their hands.
Detroit needed more help than Cisco but chose to run it back for the most part. The Green Bay Packers are clearly hoping injury returns, mainly Micah Parsons', is enough of an answer not to have further emptied the war chest.
Outside of the NFC North, there weren't many major moves in the conference. The AFC, however, stole the show.
The Jacksonville Jaguars were the biggest buyers, giving up five draft picks in deals for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
Elsewhere, the Indianapolis Colts continued their sell-offs, and the Titans and Eagles practically completed theirs.
This was a day and trade season where talent flocked to the AFC while largely leaving the NFC. Because of that, the Bears are arguably the biggest winners for their most significant league-shifting Simmons trade.

Andrew graduated from Brooklyn College with a degree in journalism in 2017 and has been a sports fan since 1993.

title: Ranking Bears' Most Important Games Left in Second Half of Season
full_text:
It's been an emotional few weeks for the Chicago Bears. After two straight victories on primetime over last year's Super Bowl teams, the Bears' undeserved Week 9 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers served as a heat check. This team is still capable of winning it all, but Caleb Williams needs to play much smarter than the way he did on Sunday, and there's no reason to believe that he won't.
Nevertheless, ugly wins count the same as pretty wins, and the Bears will enter their badly needed Week 10 bye with an impressive 7-2 record and sole control of first place in a loaded NFC North division. Everything is still on the table, from winning the division for a second straight year to earning the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoffs.
But if the Bears are going to get to that No. 1 seed, they'll have to get through another gauntlet. They have eight games remaining on their schedule, almost all of which are against playoff contenders. But which of these games are most important for the Bears? Let's take a look.
When I picked the Bears' most important games on the 2026 schedule this offseason, I said that their Week 16 matchup against the Packers could very well decide the division champion, and that appears to be holding true. The Bears may have suffered a disastrous Week 5 loss to the Packers, but this upcoming game will be a completely different matchup.
For one thing, Caleb Williams missed that game as he continued to rehab his hamstring injury. And for another, the Bears had not yet pulled off their blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons . This will be a motivated, dominant team the Packers have to face at Soldier Field, and the division crown will very likely be on the line.
The Bills look like the best team in football right now, especially after their thrilling Week 9 win over the Vikings , and Josh Allen may be headed for his second MVP award. While they are an AFC opponent, this is still a critical game for the Bears to win because there's a good chance they lose a divisional matchup that they shouldn't. If they can steal a road win against Buffalo, a game in which they will almost certainly be underdogs, it will give them a bit of a cushion in the NFC North race.
After dropping their Week 2 meeting with the Vikings, this Week 18 contest is one that the Bears have to have. The Vikings are a hot mess, and even though analysts are picking them to swing big on a quarterback trade before today's deadline, that's not likely to save their season. By this time, they could be out of the playoff picture entirely.
That should give the Bears an opportunity to claim the No. 1 seed in the season finale against a vulnerable opponent, as long as they handle their business in their remaining games.
Why is a Week 14 game against a team competing for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft so important? As aforementioned, there's a chance that the Bears drop a winnable game in their last eight weeks, which is what makes stealing a win against a team like the Bills so important. But that's far easier said than done.
Instead, the Bears should simply win the games they're supposed to win, and that includes this matchup with the Dolphins. They can recover from a loss to the Bills, the Jaguars, even a division rival. What the Bears will find difficult to recover from is a loss to one of the worst teams in the league.

title: Where Ben Johnson Sees Bears Evolving Leaves One Step After Bye
full_text:
Heading into their bye, the Bears view what happened Sunday night as reaching a new level of play following the 27-24 win over Tampa Bay .
This isn't to mock them, which would be easy after a victory so tainted. Rather, coach Ben Johnson sees what happened as a type of natural progression. The bye week now lets them reset to tweak issues from the second half of the win, or simply to get players back healthy and they feel they have been through about everything as a team.
"I think that's the next evolution of this team, not just that we win but the manner in which we play," Johnson said. "So, we've got to continue that."
The Bears dominated early, controlled play but then squandered everything they'd built through a series of turnovers before finding a way to win in the end. It was a different scenario than anything they had previously done this year or last year.
The other NFC North teams should collude and have each the Lions, Packers and Bears trade for a potential Vikings QB trade target as a luxury backup option, you can't allow that defense to get a competent QB.
The final turnover allowing for the tie wasn't really a mistake as much as a mishap. Luther Burden III didn't lose the ball as much as he lost consciousness from a hit and released the ball. After the defense had fought to keep the lead for that long, giving it away at their own 17 was one final flaw they couldn't cover. The entire process only showed the team that they can't let teams back in games when they have chances to put it away.
It was a win teaching a lesson without the cost of a damaging loss in the NFC North standings. It left room to improve with a free lesson learned.
NFC North: Which team is the best of this bunch right now? pic.twitter.com/1ww6UGe0Xt
“One hundred percent, 100%, because a lot of guys know it's a lot of meat on the bone," safety Cam Lewis said.
Ultimately, they did show they still know how to turn on the last-drive magic Caleb Williams displayed last year.
"I think it's unique because we haven't been in that situation a lot this year," Johnson said, thinking back to seven game-winning drives last season. "And I hate to keep drawing back to last year, but maybe it's that confidence from a lot of those familiar faces still being a part of this team that we're going to be at our best when the pressure is the highest. And it just felt like we were back on the bike, and we were riding that bike again."
NFC North gonna cannibalize itself unfortunately. One of those good teams not gonna make it to the postseason and that’s unfair for how hard those men worked this season to not get rewarded
The next step by Johnson's way of thinking, and the players, is to play consistently like they did against Seattle and New England.
"We've got some time now," Johnson added. "I think there's a great opportunity at hand just to look at these first nine games and come away with what we're doing well and what we can lean on going into the last stretch of the season and certainly some areas of improvement that we need to get better at moving forward.
"This will be a fun dive over the next few days as a (coaching) staff just to make sure that we're aligned properly to get better here.”
The evolution of the Bears doesn't call for revisiting what they went through Sunday or even worse,  with something similar ending in a defeat.
The real next step for the Bears after hitting a mile marker by surviving a scare is winning over divisional teams, because the NFC North teams have been their remaining problem. They don't get to take that step up until Thanksgiving in Detroit.
By then, the entire NFC North picture could look much different than it does now, with the Bears in first place and other teams scrambling to solve problems through trades.

title: Bears NFL Power Rankings For Week 10: Chicago Remains on Doorstep of No. 1 Despite Ugly Win
full_text:
It wasn't pretty, but the Chicago Bears managed to escape with a win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 to move to 7-2.
With that victory, and with a loss by the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night, the Bears now sit in first place in the NFC North entering their bye week.
The NFL trade deadline came and went on Tuesday and the Bears didn't make another move after the blockbuster Jeffery Simmons deal late last month.
Now, a look at where the Bears sit in the NFL power rankings of experts as we enter Week 10.
Orr is reveling at how much of a difference-maker Simmons is, as are we all, and he thinks Chicago has the look of a Super Bowl contender.
"More Jeffery Simmons mythmaking in Chicago, Volume II: Daring an offensive lineman to block him without a chipper and then throwing said person into another universe," Orr said.
"The Bears most certainly fit my requirements for a team making every effort to go to the Super Bowl," he added.
Simmons had another strong game with four tackles, including one for loss, one sack and one pass defensed. He also had a Buccaneers offensive lineman in his feelings after the game .
Davis marvels at the fact that the Bears were able to win despite Caleb Williams throwing four picks. He also rightly points out that Chicago's offense stands to get even better when Kyle Monangai returns, which is looking like it could happen after the bye .
"If they're going to win games on nights when QB Caleb Williams throws four picks, whether or not they're his fault?" Davis asked. "Look out for these guys, especially with RB Kyle Monangai likely back on the other side of the bye week."
The Bears' defense has been excellent this season and that unit is going to allow Chicago to win ugly offensive games like the one we saw on Sunday night.
The most exciting part is that the defense isn't even 100% healthy right now.
ESPN's Courtney Cronin had to name the Bears' most important game of the second half of the season and she picked the one against the Green Bay Packers.
"The Bears need to gain ground in their division after early losses to the Vikings and Packers. Chicago's home rematch with Green Bay on Christmas Day carries significant tiebreaker implications and is the first of three straight NFC North games to end the regular season," Cronin said. "The Bears will be in good position to defend their division title if they can pick up two NFC North wins over their next six games, beginning with the Lions on Thanksgiving before the Dec. 25 matchup with the Packers.
We would also throw the Vikings into the mix here because the Bears lost to them back in Week 2 and need to erase the head-to-head tie-breaker advantage Minnesota has like the Packers do.
But we would put the game against the Packers ahead of the one versus the Vikings like Cronin does here because Green Bay looks like a bigger threat to Chicago's division crown thanks to having a better all-around team than the Vikings and Detroit Lions.
Prisco was rightly surprised to see Williams have the game he did on Sunday night.
"Who was that playing quarterback for them Sunday night against the Bucs? Caleb Williams threw four picks and looked lost for much of the game, which was weird," Prisco wrote.
It was odd to see Williams go from playing great football to downright terrible ball after the first quarter.
It was very clear Williams didn't handle the Bucs' blitzes all that well, so that's something he's going to have to clean up because the memo is out around the NFL and teams are going to be challenging him on a weekly basis.

title: Why Bears Didn't Make a Trade on Deadline Day and What NFC North Rivals Did
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has now passed and the Chicago Bears did not end up making a move on Tuesday.
There were no shortage of rumblings that the Bears were at least scoping out available cornerbacks , but an addition never came there or at any position on Tuesday and instead the Bears are staying pat.
But, unlike in years past, Bears fans are hardly going to be upset about this. After all, general manager Ryan Poles can do no wrong at this point after he pulled off the blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons, who has already made a massive impact.
Now, let's dive into the details and see what could be behind the Bears not making a trade on deadline day and we'll also take a gander at what the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions did.
What we can say with a fair amount of certainty is the Bears' lack of a move wasn't because they didn't try.
Even after the trade for Jeffery Simmons, reports said the Bears were making calls about a cornerback , a position they needed more depth at because of the uncertainty surrounding Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, both of whom have struggled.
And we would venture to guess they were looking at edge rushers, too, after reportedly putting in a call to the Los Angeles Chargers to inquire about Khalil Mack a few weeks ago.
The most likely explanation for the Bears' lack of a move is they just couldn't get the player they wanted at the right price.
What might have made a potential deal even tougher is Chicago's likely hesitance to overpay for any player after they shelled out a historic package for Simmons that cost two first-round picks and amounted to the first defensive tackle trade that involved multiple first-rounders in the common draft era.
We would have loved to see the Bears make another deal, no doubt, but we aren't mad about the lack of action on Tuesday, either.
The Simmons trade was more than we could have ever hoped for and anything else would have been a bonus.
The Minnesota Vikings made the biggest splash on deadline day with their acquisition of quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick.
Minnesota had a major question mark at quarterback thanks to the struggles of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, which is why they made the play for Cousins, who should amount to an upgrade.
As for the Lions, they made a minor acquisition with the trade for safety Andre Cisco on Monday, but they didn't do anything on Tuesday. That trade does nothing to move the needle for Detroit, as the Lions needed a major trade to improve their defense that has been one of the worst in the NFL.
As for the Green Bay Packers, it was total crickets. Green Bay did not make a move on deadline day, or even before it.

title: Chargers Trade Rumor Gives Bears Shred of Hope for Khalil Mack Deal
full_text:
It seemed all hope was lost for the Chicago Bears when it came to a possible Khalil Mack trade, but the latest Los Angeles Chargers trade rumor has cracked the door open slightly.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Chargers have now changed their tune on trading players in contract years and are possibly willing to deal.
Schultz adds that Mack, who is in a contract year, is still a long shot to be traded, but that presents more of a chance than the Bears had going into today.
"Sources: The Chargers have been more receptive to trading players over the last 24 hours," Schultz wrote. "Khalil Mack is still considered a long shot, but other expiring contract players are available if the offer makes sense."
A few weeks ago, it was reported that the Bears had called Los Angeles about Mack , which was the first sign they had interest in him.
However, reports have suggested for weeks now that the Chargers weren't interested in selling, even amid a horrific campaign that now has Los Angeles sitting at 0-8.
Los Angeles had also stated publicly that they didn't want to trade Mack, and the future Hall of Famer also noted that he wanted to remain with the Chargers .
"Yeah, they know how I feel, man," Mack said when asked if he told the Chargers he wants to stay. "It's just tough with all the outside noise. And so, ultimately I want to be here and I want to help them win. Even though it's tough right now, you always see the light at the end of the tunnel."
“I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team," head coach Jim Harbaugh said .
But clearly something has changed, at least when it comes to the Chargers' willingness to make a trade, and perhaps Mack will be changing his stance in the waning hours, also.
It isn't clear if the Bears ever had a legit offer on the table for Mack, but if they did, perhaps sweetening it a bit will be enough to entice the Chargers to let him go, assuming Mack is down to be traded.
That said, if Mack doesn't want to be moved, the Chargers are almost certainly going to oblige because of the immense amount of respect they have for him.
The Bears are reportedly in the market for a cornerback and the Chargers have a veteran cornerback who is on an expiring deal.
That is Donte Jackson, who is set to be a free agent in 2027.
Jackson isn't having a good season by any stretch, but he could offer some depth for Chicago during a season in which Jaylon Johnson has seen massive struggles .
For the cheap price it would cost to acquire Jackson (probably a late Day 3 pick), it might be worth it to take a swing on him for insurance behind Johnson.

title: Ben Johnson Shares Thoughts on Chicago Bears NFL Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
To trade or not to trade? That is the question the Chicago Bears and their fans are asking on Tuesday.
As of 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10, trades will no longer be possible, so the clock is ticking on the Bears' ability to make another move.
The Bears have already made their all-in addition with the trade for Jeffery Simmons, but reports suggest they are still in the market for a cornerback .
Edge rusher has been another position Chicago has been linked to possibly adding at .
When asked about what the team could do on Tuesday, head coach Ben Johnson wasn't ruling out another deal or two happening.
However, he also noted that he believes the team has enough as is to be just fine the rest of the season.
"I think Ryan (Poles) is doing a phenomenal job every day. He’s going through and seeing how we can improve this roster, what we need the most of," Johnson said, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin .
"The coordinators are certainly talking every day right now, just with where their concerns lie within the roster. So we’ll see. We’ll see if there is another move or two to be made or if we stand put. I feel really confident about the guys we have in this locker room right now. And I think we’ve proven at this point that we can find a way to win each and every week with this group," he added.
While a lot of times you can't take what a coach says at face value when it comes to how he views his roster, we can do so here with Johnson.
That's because the Bears already looked like a true contender before the Simmons trade, and they are in even better shape following that blockbuster deal.
That said, general manager Ryan Poles' actions show us that this team is no doubt all-in, so it certainly wouldn't be at all surprising for the Bears to make another deal or even two before 4 p.m.
We already mentioned cornerback and edge rusher.
The Bears could use more depth at both spots, and especially at cornerback, where the team needs an insurance policy for the struggling Jaylon Johnson .
Chicago is in pretty good shape along the edge as long as Dayo Odeyingbo can get back from injured reserve in due time.
Another position to keep an eye on is tight end after Chicago lost its No. 2 tight end, Cole Kmet, to a season-ending knee injury.
The Bears deploy multiple tight ends sets more than the vast majority of teams in the NFL, so having a deep room is key.
Right now, it's hard to say the Bears have that behind Colston Loveland, as rookie Sam Roush has had issues and Stephen Carlson doesn't offer much outside of blocking.
After all of the rumors and speculation, we'll finally have answers by 4 p.m. ET today.

title: Trades Chicago Bears Might Make Today and Chances the Deals Will Happen
full_text:
The Bears were linked to interest in Mack by FOX Sports' Jay Glazer a few weeks back, which makes sense because Chicago could use more depth at edge rusher.
Unfortunately for the Bears and their fans, it doesn't look like a reunion is likely.
The Chargers have said publicly they don't want to trade Mack, and Mack has said he doesn't want to be traded. Adding to that, reports suggest the Chargers and Mack aren't lying .
"Despite their 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers continue to tell teams that they have no interest in trading away Khalil Mack, and the veteran pass rusher will not be going anywhere before Tuesday's deadline, according to sources," ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported.
There's a few reasons why we're holding out hope. One of them has to do with the fact that this could simply be posturing on the Chargers' part in order to try and get more for Mack.
It also makes no sense for both sides to stay together. Mack may very well be in the final year of his career after mulling retirement in the past and it's hard to fathom him staying with an 0-8 team going nowhere. The Chargers would be better served moving on and picking up a draft pick.
The Bears could use another starting-caliber player at cornerback given the struggles of Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson this season. At the very least, more depth is needed.
Woolen is a great fit because he thrives in man coverage, which the Bears play at the second-highest rate in the NFL this season, and Woolen has plenty of starting and even playoff experience, and has been better than Johnson in 2026.
The Philadelphia Eagles showed they are ready to sell after trading Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, and it makes sense to deal Woolen, also, as he'll be a free agent in 2027.
Cost will be important here, but with Woolen's price likely being a fourth-round pick, at most, we could see the Bears making this trade.
Wright left for the New York Jets in free agency and that proved to be a colossal mistake for the veteran cornerback.
Wright has not played a single snap on defense this season and has routinely been a healthy scratch. Safe to say, Wright likely wouldn't mind getting out of there and Gang Green probably wouldn't be opposed to trading him, either.
Wright started in 16 games for the Bears last season and was pretty solid. He also proved to be a turnover matchine after notching five picks.
There wouldn't be much of an acclimation period, either, thanks to Wright's experience in Dennis Allen's defense. He will also be dirt cheap, which only adds to the likelihood the Bears will at least have interest in him.
After losing Cole Kmet to a season-ending injury , the Bears, who use a lot of 12 and 13 personnel, are relying heavily on rookie Sam Roush, who has struggled this season, and uninspiring veteran Stephen Carlson behind Colston Loveland.
The Bears could use a well-rounded tight end like Goedert, who has proven to be a solid blocker and very good pass-catcher during his career.
The rules for why the Eagles would trade Woolen apply for Goedert, although the latter obviously has a deeper connection with the Eagles because he has spent his entire career there.
At a reasonable price of a fourth- or fifth-round pick, it wouldn't shock us to see the Bears trade for Goedert, although we don't believe it's likely, either, since the Bears have bigger fish to fry.
Here's a more realistic option for the Bears at tight end.
Alie-Cox doesn't offer as much in the pass-catching department as Goedert, but he's serviceable in that area and is as good, if not better, as a blocker. Alie-Cox will come cheaper than Goedert, also, with it likely costing a sixth-round pick, at most.
The Indianapolis Colts are in the midst of a fire sale after trading off Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, so everyone is on the table right now, and especially when it comes to players who are slated to be free agents like Alie-Cox is.
If the Bears do come away with a tight end on Tuesday, look for it to be Alie-Cox, or someone like him.

title: Reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford Makes Big Statement About Joe Burrow
full_text:
Joe Burrow's MVP campaign has support from the quarterback who won the award last season.
Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford believes the Cincinnati Bengals' star should be leading the race at the halfway point. Speaking with Jim Gray on this week's episode of SiriusXM's "Let's Go" podcast , the Rams QB picked Burrow when asked who he considers the current MVP leader.
Burrow has helped Cincinnati win four straight games, reaching 6-2, with the Bengals scoring at least 31 points in each victory.
"There are a lot of quarterbacks and a lot of people playing at a high level," Stafford said. "I think Joe Burrow, what he's done the last three, four, five weeks, whatever it is, I mean, he's been on fire.
“That offense has been clicking, throwing a bunch of touchdowns, keeping his team alive, playing well. Defense is playing good too, but I would say Joe Burrow, for what he's done this season, they've stayed healthy and he's rocking and rolling at a really good clip.
Burrow's latest performance in Madrid strengthened that case. He completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns, with no interceptions, in Cincinnati's 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Burrow also scored a touchdown on the ground in the second quarter.
Over the four-game winning streak, Burrow has thrown for 1,215 yards and 16 touchdowns, with just three interceptions. All three interceptions came against Tennessee, a game in which he threw five touchdown passes and ran for the winning score in overtime.
“So I'd give it to him halfway through, as we know [there’s] a lot of football to be played, but he's been special the first half," Stafford said.
Last month, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor called Burrow the most accurate passer in the world, but made it clear he has no idea how the star signal-caller is so accurate.
"I don't know," Taylor jokingly answered when asked about Burrow's accuracy. "Watching how he works in practice between reps. Watching how he works in pre-practice, watching how he throws in pregame, watching his body movements... It's really impressive."
As for the Bengals, Cincinnati is tied with Pittsburgh atop the AFC North at 6-2. They host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, with a chance to take control of the division lead.
