title: 2 Winners & 2 Losers From Bengals 2026 Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline has passed, and Cincinnati sat it out .
Director of Player Personnel Duke Tobin and the rest of the front office did not add any talent to bolster Joe Burrow's hot run.
Eagles defensive end Arnold Ebiketie looked like he was headed to Cincinnati in a deal this morning, but it got scrapped once Over The Cap's Nick Korte pointed out  Cincinnati would lose its 2027 third-round compensatory pick if they finalized things.
Then the rest of the AFC contenders (outside of Pittsburgh) added at least one new talent via trade. Jacksonville's flurry in recent days got matched by Kansas City (wide receiver Josh Downs), Buffalo (safety Amani Hooker), and Denver (linebacker Daiyan Henley).
Let's dive into Cincinnati's Winners & Losers from the deadline:
Cincinnati had a chance to make their first deadline addition in two years at clear positions of need like starting linebacker, safety depth, and tight end depth, but did nothing.
No one was asking them to go through with the rough cost for Ebiketie earlier in the day, but adding somewhere would've been huge for the team's depth on paper.
The cap appeared to be a sixth-round value or worse for what they were willing to dive into with this market. Maybe Burrow's good enough to carry this roster as is to the ultimate prize, but everyone they're directly battling against in this conference (outside of Pittsburgh) added to their talent pool, and Cincinnati bowed out.
Not knowing the rules around how adding players affects your draft-pick pool isn't an ideal look either.
Adding a running back like Jonathan Taylor had been the marquee talking point around the deadline in recent weeks, and now it's definitely Chase Brown's backfield for the rest of the season.
He and Samaje Perine ran well in Madrid on Sunday, and Brown has been steady overall all season (32nd in yards after contact per rushing attempt, 27th in PFF grade, sixth in pass-blocking grade). It never made sense to trade the curious haul the Colts wanted for a position that Brown and Perine have covered.
Now, he gets to play for some type of new deal in the offseason from Cincinnati or another team.
Burrow is playing better than any quarterback on earth right now and leading an offense miles better than any other in the NFL over the past month.
Since Week 5, Burrow's offense is notching 0.25 EPA/play (no other team higher than 0.16), and he is atop Ben Baldwin's EPA/PFF grade blend leaderboard this season.
He's going to win MVP if this heater keeps up against one of the three easiest schedules left in the NFL, yet Cincinnati did nothing. The fact his MVP competitors added around him while Burrow has to trudge on with this roster could help him a bit in that pursuit.
He wants a different trophy much more, and Cincinnati didn't do anything on paper to boost the chances they carry the Lombardi Trophy in February. We may look back on this February like we did with some roster choices on the last Super Bowl roster.
The front office has stamped their approval of this roster; now go show you can do it.
Linebacker's been a hammered talking point for over two years now for good reason. Barrett Carter is improving at a palatable rate this season, but Demetrius Knight's posting another sub-50 PFF grade like he did as a rookie. The missed tackles improved a bit from 14% to 12% this season, but he has to step up for Cincinnati's defense to really maximize.
The whole locker room reportedly bonded heavily across their trip to Spain, and the ultimate team sport can come down to those tight-knit bonds in the big moments. Cincinnati seems to have that and didn't throw any starter into an uncomfortable spot with a splash move.
They get the ultimate chance to reward the front-office faith facing the Steelers on Sunday.

title: Bengals Fail at Trade Deadline as AFC Contenders Make Moves
full_text:
The trade deadline came and went and the Bengals stayed pat.
It's the two words that head coach Zac Taylor used on Tuesday.
Their actions said otherwise. The Bengals agreed to a deal that would've brought Arnold Ebikete to Cincinnati. Instead, that deal fell through in embarassing fashion. Our own Russ Heltman has the details here.
That failed deal will get the attention it deserves, but it didn't have to be the story of the deadline for the Bengals. They still had hours to add to their roster.
The same roster that has Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level. The same roster that has Dexter Lawrence in position to make a real run at Defensive Player of the Year. Tee Higgins is playing the best ball of his career. Ja'Marr Chase is the best receiver on the planet.
The Bengals have a ton of talent and can make a real run at a Super Bowl. So why add?
That's what contenders do.
The Buffalo Bills are considered the top team in the AFC. They didn't sit on their hands at the deadline. They went out and got the guy that intercepted three of Burrow's passes in Week 8. Amani Hooker is a heck of a football player and gives the Bills a real playmaker at safety.
Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes has a new weapon to throw to. Josh Downs is headed to Kansas City. The slot receiver has a chance to make a major impact for the remainder of the season. The Bengals face the Chiefs in December.
The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, including a deal for Jessie Bates that would've been a costly, but worth it type of deal for the Bengals. Bates was a great player for the Bengals. He got even better in Atlanta and would've been a plug-and-play piece in the back-end of Cincinnati's defense.
Even the Broncos got in on the fun. No, they didn't add another weapon for Bo Nix. Instead, they addressed arguably the Bengals' biggest weakness: linebacker. They made an in-division trade with the Chargers for linebacker Daiyan Henley.
All four of these AFC contenders addressed needs with big moves. All four of these teams are much better today than they were on Sunday. Meanwhile, the Bengals didn't get the deal done for Ebiketie after botching the compensatory pick implications and didn't follow it up with another move to bolster their roster.
Never count out Joe Burrow or Ja'Marr Chase, but the Bengals didn't get better on Tuesday. Their biggest competition did.

title: Bengals NOT Striking Trade Deal For Eagles Pass Rusher Arnold Ebiketie Due To Key Reason
full_text:
After NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the Bengals are trading a 2027 sixth-round pick for Arnold Ebiketie, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported roughly an hour later that the deal was not happening.
Cincinnati got cold feet after it surfaced that they would lose their 2027 third-round compensatory pick if they struck the deal.
"Plot twist! The Bengals and Eagles deal for DE Arnold Ebiketie has fallen through and will not happen, per sources. The trade falling through is not physical or performance-related, per sources," Schultz posted on X .
Rapoport confirmed they are exiting the deal to retain the third-round compensatory pick.
"The Bengals have now called off this trade intending to keep a future comp pick they would've lost with this deal. Agreement was reached, but not official," Rapoport posted .
Back to the trade drawing board for Cincinnati, which clearly is putting a heavy premium on that top-100 pick they are slated to get back after Trey Hendrickson signed a new deal in Baltimore and triggered the pick for his old team.
The NFL rules state below how the Bengals would've lost the pick. Ebiketie was a CFA signing by the Eagles this past offseason.
"If a Club qualifies for more than four Compensatory Draft Selections, only the four highest selections will be awarded to the Club. If a Club trades for a player who was a CFA during that League Year, whether the player was another Club's CFA or the acquiring Club's own CFA, the player will be considered a CFA gained by the acquiring Club and will be included in the Compensatory netting process described above," the rules state.
A rough fake-out for Bengals fans, who thought they were about to get their defense beefed up, and a rough look for the team's front office.
They appear to not have known this compensatory pick language existed until Over The Cap's Nick Korte tweeted about it right after the announced deal.
"Arnold Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles. The Bengals lost 3 CFAs and signed 2 (Cordell Volson not qualifying); thus, while they gain a 2027 sixth-round comp pick, they lose a 2027 third-round comp pick that was via Trey Hendrickson going to Baltimore," Korte posted on X before expanding further. "Obvious correction here: the Bengals gave up a regular sixth-round pick, they did not gain one. The main point is of course about the third round compensatory pick that this trade would cancel out."
Cincinnati has less than four hours to add talent ahead of the deadline at 4 p.m. ET.

title: Report: Bengals Trading For Defensive End Help Ahead of 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals have made a trade to boost their defense ahead of the deadline at 4 p.m. ET. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday that the team is adding Eagles defensive end Arnold Ebikite for a sixth-round pick in 2027.
It helps boost the team's defensive end depth after having to put Cashius Howell on injured reserve last week.
"Sources: The Eagles aren't done, trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 6th-round pick," Rapoport noted .
This is the team's first Deadline Day acquisition since 2024, when they traded for Bears running back Khalil Herbert in the final hours.
Cincinnati needed help along its defensive front and got it in the veteran, who has 16.5 total sacks in his career. He has 25 tackles with the Eagles this season but has been very consistent since entering the league in 2022.
Ebikitie has never posted a season-long Pro Football Focus grade below his current 60.5 mark in 2026 and has played over 2,128 snaps. He posted a 74.9 PFF grade last season and has yet to post a sack in 2026 but had six across the past two seasons (played 48% of the snaps for the Eagles this year, 25 tackles, two QB hits, 0 sacks in nine games).
He posted a 7% pressure rate this season, but had a monstrous 16.4% rate last season and could tap into that as a Bengal. According to ESPN's Ben Baby, the team is taking on the rest of his expiring deal this season worth $650,000, with another $3 million in incentives possible.
Cincinnati should be able to get him on the field and up to speed for Sunday night's massive battle against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Whoever wins that game will be in first at the top of the AFC North. ESPN's FPI currently gives the Bengals a 79.5% chance to win the division once January rolls around.
"I think all the divisional games going forward are going to be big games for us," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said in Spain. "That's nothing new. I'm not going to talk the game down. It's going to be nice having our fans at home. I think they'll be fired up for this one, so we should have a great atmosphere. Now, again, it's just on us to handle the week the right way."
The 27-year-old newest Bengal will be rowing forward with his new team soon.

title: Bengals Can Solidify Key Positional Depth With Bargain Trade Ahead of 2026 Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals have a clear depth need at tight end right now, and a forgotten name on the Panthers roster could be a great option to round out that room.
ESPN's Bill Barnwell broke down which contenders should be aggressively trading for talent last week, and Cincinnati slotted into his "Should Be Selectively Adding" group of teams. Panthers tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders was an underrated bargain target Cincinnati could go after.
Eagles LB Zach Baun was his main pick for the Bengals to pursue, but there is zero indication the Eagles are listening to realistic deals for Baun. Alas, he's only due to hold a $5.48 million cap hit in 2027, a palatable number for a Bengals team that's going to be very expensive next year with Amarius Mims, DJ Turner, and more due to anticipated new deals.
Sanders would cost close to the minimum in salary and has flashed in the league before.
"Panthers tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders got off to a promising start as a rookie, but he managed just 190 receiving yards over 13 games in 2025 and has been a healthy scratch for the entirety of the 2026 season so far. He needs a change of scenery, and while the Panthers have clearly soured on him, Sanders' athleticism and ability after the catch played up in 2024. He would be an interesting receiving tight end option for the Bengals as a replacement for Tanner Hudson," Barnwell noted .
The third-year talent might be had for seventh or sixth-round pick max after warming the bench in the first half of the season. The Texas product played 924 offensive snaps for Carolina in 2024 and 2025.
Mike Gesicki is technically a tight end, but he operates much more like Cincinnati's third wide receiver than a typical tight end.
One more injury to that group after today and Cincinnati won't have a chance to add any tight ends via trade. They have three healthy names besides Gesicki right now: Drew Sample, Jack Endries and Cam Grandy.
Sanders isn't going to come in and start lighting up defenses as a blocker and pass catcher, but he could solidify Cincinnati's depth at an important offensive spot.

title: Bengals Could Land Perfect Trade Deadline Addition for Affordable Price
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals can't afford to stand pat at the NFL trade deadline if they want to separate themselves as contenders at the top of the AFC. They need to add to a few spots on defense, and it wouldn't hurt to add some supporting players on the offensive side of the ball.
The Athletic and its writers, including Daniel Popper, recently put together a mock NFL trade deadline scenario in which the Bengals showcased interest in trading for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker, but couldn't pull it off. Still, in reality, trading for Hooker would make a lot of sense. And it could be affordable.
"The Bengals offered a 2027 fifth-round pick for Hooker," Popper wrote. "The Bills came in with an aggressive initial offer. Safety is a huge need for Buffalo, which has an elite offense and a struggling defense. The Bills wanted to solidify this position ahead of a potential Super Bowl run. Hooker, a versatile safety, leads the NFL in interceptions. The offer: a 2027 third-round pick in exchange for Hooker and a 2027 seventh-round pick."
Hooker is the perfect trade target for the Bengals.
They have had some issues in the secondary this season, and Hooker would be the perfect plug-and-play option for them to add. He's off to an incredible start in Tennessee, as he already has five interceptions this season. The Bengals know Hooker very well, as he intercepted Joe Burrow three different times earlier this season. He's also been good in coverage overall and recorded six passes defensed.
The asking price for Hooker might not be out of Cincinnati's price range either. He could realistically be had for a third-round pick and a pick swap, which seems like a steep price to pay, but for a big-play defensive back, it would be a huge add for Cincinnati.
Hooker's dominance against Cincinnati was enough to prove that he belongs on a playoff-caliber defense. The Bengals could look to make a big trade in the near future that would beef up their defense in a big way. Hooker could be their missing piece, especially considering his splash play ability.

title: Zac Taylor Shoots Down Idea That Bengals Will Make Trade Before Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is quickly approaching, and rumors and deals are gaining momentum.
Many experts believe the Bengals have a strong roster but need to make a move or two to improve their chances of winning. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor thinks differently.
"No, I feel good about where we're at," Taylor said when asked whether any specific areas of the team need improvement from the outside.
The Bengals have been mentioned in rumors as being interested in Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, as well as actively looking for "middle-tier options across the board," according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
When pressed again about what the next 24 hours would look like for Taylor with the trade deadline looming, he again said, "That's just that's a bunch for everybody to talk about, but we're good."
"We're just focused on Pittsburgh right now. It's our biggest focus," Taylor continued.
Taylor keeps dismissing trade talk, emphasizing that roster building depends on execution and internal development, not midseason trades. Taylor believes the Bengals' success starts in their own locker room. They need to tune out the outside noise and focus on what they can control. Taylor highlights how guys on the practice squad and backup unit step in seamlessly when injuries hit, specifically on the offense.
"Smart players get an opportunity to play here...We hold them to the same standard as Ja'Marr and Tee... The next-man-up mentality has been really good for us, and those guys have embraced it and stepped up."
Taylor clearly believes in the current roster and sees no need to bring in outside help.
The Bengals are betting on themselves. Of course, Taylor's comments don't mean the Bengals won't add at the deadline. They've made in season trades in each of the past two seasons. They also swung a blockbuster deal with the Giants for Dexter Lawrence in April.
Taylor can't come out and say they're hoping to add to the team. That's out of his control. His job as head coach is to focus on the players in the building.
The Bengals have won four-straight games. They host the Steelers on Sunday with first place in the AFC North on the line.
"We're not running from divisional games. A team that's gotten us once," Taylor said. "I think we've done a good job of just focusing on the opponent in front of us and making that game the biggest game of the year, and that will be no different this week when Pittsburgh comes down."

title: Report: Bengals 'Explored' Trade Options Ahead of NFL's 2026 Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals have reportedly "explored the middle tier" of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline market, but nothing has come to fruition.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that nugget on Monday afternoon as we sit a little more than 24 hours from the deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
Cincinnati has a big hole at starting linebacker and depth tight end, but no move has happened yet.
"After speaking to league sources over the weekend and really last week, let's dive into it," Schultz said. "Let's start with the Kansas City Chiefs looking for a wide receiver. Also, the 49ers are looking for a wide receiver and a pass rusher. The Bills would love to improve their defense. I could see them targeting a safety. The Broncos are looking for a running back or tight end.
"The Jags defensive tackle. They already made the big move for Jesse Bates. Pittsburgh wants a receiver and a corner. The Bengals explored the middle tier across the board. Chicago would love to add to their secondary with a corner."
Cincinnati is back in town as a team following the trip to Spain, and Zac Taylor didn't sound like the front office is going to make a definitive move before the deadline.
"Nothing, that's a bunch for everybody to talk about, but we're good," the Bengals' head coach said about trades to the media on Monday.
The Bengals shouldn't be overpaying for anyone that's reportedly on the market right now. They have clear needs at linebacker, but other than that, there aren't a ton of glaring holes that one move could fix right now.
Still, a fellow AFC contender in Jacksonville traded away multiple picks today, including a second-round selection, to go after new blood at safety and defensive tackle for a Super Bowl push this season.
Cincinnati needs to make sure they don't let a good deal pass them by with the lightning bottled right now. They sport the league's third-most efficient offense on the season by EPA/play and most efficient in the past month, the second easiest remaining schedule on ESPN's FPI, and the MVP frontrunner in Joe Burrow.
Team scenarios like that don't roll around every year, and Cincinnati has to do everything it can (rationally) to maximize this season. Many thought they'd be in the Super Bowl multiple times back in Feb. 2022, and they are yet to go back.

title: One Game’s Enough To Remind Browns What They Gave Up by Trading Myles Garrett
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are currently a Top-10 team in the NFL when it comes to sacks (26) and pressure rate (32.7 percent) against opposing offenses.
Sounds pretty good, right? Not when you expected to be so much better.
If the Browns keep up their current pace, they would end the regular season with 49 sacks, four less than last year’s total. And their pressure rate is around 2.4 percent worse than last year’s.
The big difference, of course, is that Myles Garrett no longer plays for Cleveland. Garrett, who set the single season sack record last year with 23, was traded to the Los Angeles Rams during the offseason for a 2027 first-round, 2028 second round and 2029 third round pick, along with edge defender Jared Verse.
And this is the real concerning part: the Browns have been able to generate decent 2026 pass rushing numbers without Garrett on the roster, and without Verse making a noticeable contribution.
Thread on Browns DE Jared Verse's production this season: In addition to not registering a sack yet, Verse has been credited with six initial pressures. His pressure rate (3.3%) ranks 185th out of 198 qualifying players. His EDGE pass-rush win rate (10.8%) ranks 57th out of 58…
After nine games with the Browns, Verse has been credited with 15 pressures by Pro Football Focus, while ESPN analytics had him ranked 185th out of 198 qualifying players with a pressure rate of 3.3% before this weekend’s Saints game. During this matchup, Verse also saw his snap count percentage dip below 60.0 on defense (57.3) for just the second time this year.
Meanwhile, Garrett has appeared in just two contests so far in the season--the Week 1 game in Melbourne where he came away with zero sacks and tackles, and last Sunday’s monster performance against Washington, where he literally took over.
In 309 fewer defensive snaps, Garrett has already produced three sacks and one forced fumble more than Verse, as well as one tackle for a loss and three quarterback hits less than his counterpart. Just to be clear: yes, those numbers for Garrett have come in seven full games less than Verse.
. @RamsNFL @Flash_Garrett Superman was back in uniform and played like he was trying to make up for lost time in rehab... #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/1fms3ZUbTk
Since Day 1, Cleveland has made a point of talking up how much of a positive impact Verse has had since arriving on the Berea campus, especially in the locker room.
Everybody pointed to how Verse stayed after practice to help rookie Spencer Fano during summer workouts, or how his in-practice fight with Fano a few days later helped the team gain full confidence in the first-rounder and his readiness for the starting job.
He’s also been a very vocal leader, even prompting Browns’ captain and arguably the team’s best defensive player, Denzel Ward, to say this about the two defensive ends back in early October:
"Definitely brought a lot of juice and just mentality, as well," said Ward regarding what Verse brings to the table , according to Rams Wire. "Myles is a heck of a player, great player, but I think Jared, he's more vocal, more of a vocal player, vocal leader out there for us. Since the first day he stepped in the building, just yelling, screaming and making his mark out there in meetings and on the practice field, kind of rallying guys. So definitely respect who he is as a player and the way he approaches the game and how he brings guys along."
All that sounds great. But you know what else would be great? It would be great if Verse’s notable leadership skill came accompanied by the kind of on-the-field production that led to him being appointed Defensive Rookie of the Year and an essential condition in order for the Browns to go along with the Myles Garrett trade.
Of course, Cleveland has yet to execute three high draft picks, and depending on who they select over the course of the next few years, they could come out clearly on top of this deal. But as things stand right now, the Browns might even feel forced to invest one of those picks at the defensive end position, either on a trade or through the draft .
There’s no way of knowing how good the Browns’ defense could be this year if Garrett were still on the team, playing alongside pleasantly surprising contributors such as Michael Hall or Sam Williams . His injury this year creates an enormous "what if?" scenario. But we will know, in time, what Verse’s eventual output for the club will be.
And we also know beyond a shadow of a doubt, that what he’s done for the team after the first nine games in a Cleveland uniform is quite simply not enough.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: What Jerry Jeudy Keeps Doing for the Browns Explains Why He Wasn't Traded
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline has come and gone.
And after weeks of speculation about what the Cleveland Browns would do, the answer was ultimately nothing.
The front office decided to keep all four quarterbacks, controversial wide receiver Jerry Jeudy and their 2027 draft picks. Rumored to be in the market for a backup edge rusher and a blocking tight end, the Browns are keeping the core group that has led them to a 5- 4 record and trust the guys in-house.
Of everything that was possible at the deadline, the Browns sticking with Jeudy stands out the most.
Currently projected to have career-lows in nearly every statistic, all while being practically a non-factor on game day up until the fourth quarter, it seemed that the two sides' best fit was going in different directions.
But instead, the Browns stuck by the 27-year-old.
There is a reason the Browns have kept Jeudy around, even if he has just 18 catches for 208 yards and zero scores this season.
While his numbers don't jump off the sheet , not by any means, he has continued to show up when Cleveland needs him the most.
This past weekend, in a one-point loss to the New Orleans Saints, Jeudy was one of Shedeur Sanders' go-to targets down the stretch. He had zero catches going into the team's final drive, but hauled in a 30-yard pass to help set the Browns up for a game-tying field goal a few plays later.
His ability to make plays down the stretch, especially in close-knit contests, has become an underrated part of what he brings to the Browns' offense this year.
Whether it is his ability to find space, make a difficult catch with a defender right on top of him or just simply situational understanding, his experience has become invaluable, especially with so many youngsters playing alongside him.
The Browns had many obvious reasons to move on from him, most notably the emergence of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, all while second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr. continues to dominate, but it is the overlooked parts of his game that make it worthwhile to keep him into the back half of the season.
And after all, Jeudy being your third option in the wide receiver room and fourth target in the passing game isn't a bad thing at all. The more depth, sometimes, the better.
While Jeudy and the Browns could reassess the current situation in the offseason, the conversation should revolve around his long-term plans in the league.
If Jeudy believes he is still a No. 1 option, then a trade should be made to give him the opportunity to go and do just that . The last thing Cleveland needs is a guy frustrated with his role, especially if his targets remain on the decline as Boston and Concepcion continue to grow.
However, if Jeudy is understanding of where he is at in his career and what the plans for the Browns are moving forward, the two sides should discuss a potential contract restructuring.
It isn't that the Browns want to take away his money, but rather to find a way to spread his cap hit out across a few years, giving the team less financial strain on a third or fourth option offensively. He is under contract through the 2027 season, where he will have a cap hit of roughly $13 million.
It seems unlikely that the two sides will ever part ways, especially considering the Browns stood by Jeudy at this year's trade deadline.
However, if the 2027 NFL Draft rolls around the bend and it makes sense to flip Jeudy for a late-round draft pick, he could end up in a new uniform by the time next season begins.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: What the Browns Standing Pat at the Trade Deadline Means for the Bigger Picture
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and a handful of teams upgraded their roster. The deadline provides an opportunity for teams to upgrade their rosters and fill positions of need to help them improve their playoff and Super Bowl chances.
But the Cleveland Browns, whom many expected to be somewhat active, decided to stay quiet and stick with the guys they already have on the roster.
However, others made their phone calls and strengthened their sides before the back half of the season gets underway.
The Minnesota Vikings sent a third-round pick to reunite with quarterback Kirk Cousins, and multiple first-round picks were used by teams looking to upgrade their defense. Other teams sought veterans to fill injury-plagued position groups.
The Browns, who have multiple areas that they could have addressed for a playoff push, chose to stay with their current roster and future picks.
#Browns made no trades by Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline despite working the phones.
Andrew Berry may have made the correct call by not giving up any assets prior to the deadline, though.
The team got off to a hot 5-2 start, and the playoff conversation was very real, but they have dropped two straight games, and the outlook of the season may be shifting.
They showed that they want to take a real look at Shedeur Sanders at some point this season. Deshaun Watson was cleared from a concussion protocol prior to Sunday’s game, but they still chose to start Sanders.
The bye week is coming up, and a shift to permanently start Sanders could end up being sooner rather than later.
The Browns do not have a projected starting quarterback for next season, and Sanders is the closest person that it could be. They have two first-round picks next season, and there are multiple quarterbacks expected to go in the first round.
The Browns more than likely have played themselves out of a top pick, meaning a quarterback is off the table, and they will need as many assets as possible going into the draft to build around who they already have.
The defensive line could use help to stop the run, but the two linemen who were traded at the deadline went for first-round picks. That price is too steep for a team with no real Super Bowl aspirations this season.
A player like Los Angeles edge rusher Khalil Mack, who is older and on an expiring deal, could have been landed for a low-round pick, but the Chargers seemed to be asking a lot for him.
Currently, Browns edge rushers Isaiah McGuire and Jared Verse are having a quiet season and would be better off getting all the reps for the remainder of the season, then bringing in a fresh face who would be looking to learn a new scheme as well.
The offense could have used a run-blocking tight end to allow Harold Fannin Jr. to do what he does best by catching the ball.
Although a tight end would be cheap on the trade market, the Browns have three fourth-round picks and two fifth-round picks next year. A good blocking tight end can be had in the middle of the draft and would be under team control for four years under a rookie contract. That could be Cleveland's mindset.
The Browns could have also used a running back to help spark their offense. Tony Pollard would have been a good option for this season, but he is older and on an expiring contract. Other running backs would cost a high draft pick, like Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor, which the Browns would probably rather use to get a running back on a rookie contract.
Standing pat at the deadline was Berry’s best decision.
He has had two fantastic drafts in a row and has kept all of his ammunition to try and run things back a third time.

title: 'They’re Drowning Right Now': Former WR Jarvis Landry Rips Browns' Recent Loss
full_text:
Down 23-22 in overtime against the New Orleans Saints, Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken was faced with a decision: kick the extra point for the tie, or go for two for the win.
After Shedeur Sanders failed to connect with Denzel Boston in the end zone, the two-point try cost Cleveland the game .
On Monday, former Browns wide receiver Jarvis Landry didn’t hold back when sharing his thoughts on the head coach’s play call.
“I’m gonna say this. A tie is better than a loss,” he said on the 4th and South podcast. “You can’t go into these games, into these situations… I listened to the Todd Monken press conference after the game, he said it was either a tie or lose, or tie or win, or some s— he said. I don’t know what he said, it’s just that confusing, as confusing as the decision he made to go for two.”
“A tie is better than a loss… I think it was a horrible call.” 😤 Jarvis Landry says Todd Monken’s two-point gamble against the New Orleans Saints cost the Cleveland Browns 🏈❌ #Browns #DawgPound #Saints #NFL pic.twitter.com/BfymFeVvfC
The Saints had possession to start overtime, putting together an 11-play, 5:43 drive that ended in a touchdown.
Sanders then took the Browns down the field and capped off Cleveland's drive with a 39-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. to bring the score within one point with a minute on the clock.
“You’re on the road, you have your backup quarterback who is doing the best he can to stay on his feet to throw the ball down the field, and you're gonna go for two?” Landry said. “I think it was a horrible call… Calls like that is what defines a season. That tie could be something that could help them get into the playoffs. They’re drowning right now.”
Despite the failed attempt, Monken defended his decision after the game.
“You make the decision as the clock winds down a little bit, because you’re at that point to where they still have their two timeouts. So if you kick the extra point, the way the overtime rules are with 10 minutes is that they’re going to be in two-minute with two timeouts and need a field goal to win it. So, you’re not going to get the ball back, probably. So you’re really saying, tie or lose.”
Monken also gave credit to Sanders, who, despite completing just five passes for 38 yards in the first half, put together a performance that kept Cleveland in the game. He finished with 297 yards after completing 19 of 31 passes for two touchdowns .
“He gave us a chance at the end, he really did. Made some plays, made some plays with his legs to extend plays and get us first downs,” Monken said. “I’m really proud of him.”
Sunday’s loss gives the Browns a 5-4 record and the No. 3 spot in a tight AFC North race.
They’ll look to avoid a three-game losing streak on Sunday, Nov. 15, as they host the 3-5 Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field.

title: 2 Late Moves the Cleveland Browns Could Make at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are headed into the back half of the 2026 campaign with a 5-4 overall record.
Fortunately, even though things have been bumpy over the last couple of weeks, the top spot in the AFC North is still well within reach.
In order to round out the roster nicely, all while addressing a few areas of the team that need a bit of a boost, the front office should at least make a couple of moves at the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline , which hits at 4:00 p.m. EST on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
Here are two late moves the Browns could make:
Ebiketie was initially signed by the Philadelphia Eagles this past offseason, joining them from the Atlanta Falcons.
The 27-year-old is a former second-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, having already posted 16.5 sacks across the last five seasons. He has also totaled 154 tackles, 43 quarterback hits, 17 tackles for a loss and six pass deflections, giving his team a good balance of help in both the passing and rushing attacks.
This season, he has played in all nine games, but failed to record a sack, all while posting just two quarterback hits and zero tackles for a loss. He has also not deflected a pass.
Looking for a change of scenario, the Eagles sent him to the Cincinnati Bengals for a sixth-round pick. However, the deal would end up failing to go through after the Bengals realized they would lose a pick.
Sources: The #Eagles aren't done, trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the #Bengals in exchange for 2027 6th round pick. pic.twitter.com/8EYzDf6px6
Now, though, the Browns can swoop in and make a move for Ebiketie.
In need of better depth at the edge rusher position, the Browns sending a fifth- or sixth-rounder to the Eagles seems like a no-brainer, especially now that the value for him is public knowledge.
If the front office is serious about competing, Ebiketie should be on the list of targets at the deadline.
While Ebiketie has already been dealt and then brought back to the team, Kahlil Mack hasn't been that deep in trade talks just yet. Well, at least to the public's knowledge.
Mack ending up in a trade is reportedly being explored by the Chargers, even if the price remains relatively high.
After all, the nine-time Pro Bowler and three-time First-Team All-Pro is one of the game's best edge rushers, even at age 35.
From the age of 30 on , he has maintained consistency on the gridiron, posting a total of 76 starts in 77 games, 236 combined tackles, 73 quarterback hits, 56 tackles for a loss, 45.5 sacks and 21 total pass deflections. He has also forced four fumbles and recovered 13.
Cleveland already has a really young defensive line, including anchors Mason Graham and Jared Verse, so adding a veteran presence like Mack would be huge.
Not only would he help the team with his productivity on the field, but also help bring the locker room around in different learning ways.
If the Browns were really interested in making the playoffs this season and getting to the top of the division standings, they should be on the phone with Los Angeles, at least to hear what his value is at the moment.

title: Cleveland Browns NFL Trade Deadline Live Tracker: Trades, Rumors and More
full_text:
This article will be live-updated as rumors swirl and moves are made by the Cleveland Browns as the trade deadline nears.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is set for Tuesday, November 10th at 4:00 p.m. EST.
Follow along as the Browns' trade rumors continue to swirl through headlines and deals are made ahead of the deadline.
After all the rumors and clear gaps in the roster, the Browns decided to stay quiet during this year's trade deadline.
Now, they will look to make a playoff push with the guys in-house.
With roughly 15 minutes left in the trade deadline, the Miami Dolphins put quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve.
Browns quarterbacks Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders are still options Miami could make a move for in the final minutes.
The Indianapolis Colts have traded wideout Josh Downs and a seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for fourth- and fifth-round picks.
This leaves Browns wideout Jerry Jeudy as one of the final top receiver options for the final few minutes of the trade deadline. Looking at some of the trades made today, his value sits at around a mid-round draft pick
The Minnesota Vikings have sent a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for quarterback Kirk Cousins.
Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, who could have been options for Minnesota, remain with Cleveland for the time being. It will be interesting to see if either receive interest from other teams now that the Vikings are off the table.
The Indianapolis Colts are sending veteran wideout Keenan Allen to the 49ers for a 2027 6th-round pick.
The Browns now gain a better understanding of the value for Jerry Jeudy, who they could deal before the deadline ends.
The Cincinnati Bengals, one of the Browns' biggest in-division rivals, and the Philadelphia Eagles have called off a trade involving DE Arnold Ebiketie. The 27-year-old is definitely someone to watch if the Browns want to make a move.
Ebiketie would help bolster the defensive line, one of the biggest areas needing improvements here at the deadline.
As it stands, Cleveland's main interests at the trade deadline are tight end and edge rusher.
While the Browns' offensive line has been pretty bad, it seems as if Andrew Berry and Todd Monken want to finish the year with the offensive line they freshly constructed over the summer.
As for names, guys like Jadeveon Clowney, Khalil Mack, and Will McDonald IV have been tossed around as potential edge rushers
For the tight end, the biggest and most frequent name has been Dallas Goedert from Philadelphia.
Developing: The Vikings have begun making calls around the league about trading for a quarterback ahead of today’s 4 pm ET deadline, per @rapsheet and me. pic.twitter.com/nzZkSKweUp
As of 11:00 a.m. Tuesday morning, reports from Adam Schefter said the Minnesota Vikings are shopping around for a quarterback while they deal with an injury to Kyler Murray.
While some may say the Vikings could go all in on a guy like Justin Herbert or Dak Prescott, that would completely dismiss their effort to go out and get Kyler Murray this offseason.
Especially after trading away JJ McCarthy, the Vikings may actually be looking for a young quarterback with a lot of upside and little proven success.
That criteria fits Shedeur Sanders more than anyone else in the entire NFL.
Coming off an impressive performance against New Orleans, it would not be a shock if the Vikings made a move for the 2025 fifth-round pick.
As of Monday night and Tuesday morning, the Philadelphia Eagles are on a fire sale. Clearly, if they are willing to trade away a guy like Jordan Davis, they will be willing to let Goedert go.
The good news for the Browns here is that it may not take an arm and a leg to get the 31-year-old tight end on their team.
If it can be done, this trade would give Harold Fannin Jr. the opportunity to explode in this Browns offense, and Todd Monken the ability to run sets with two dynamic tight ends.
As for an edge rusher, this is where the Browns may be more inclined to spend some bigger assets.
So far this season, we all know the deal with Jared Verse. Andrew Berry and Todd Monken may want to go out and get a guy who will not only be great for the defense but also unlock the 2024 defensive rookie of the year in Verse.
Going forward this season, winning games, making the playoffs , and even competing for their first-ever AFC North division title is still very possible for Cleveland.
The division is most definitely still up for grabs, but the Browns must make some moves to try to improve their roster.
After the past few games, it is very clear that there are some major gaps in this team, but also some very bright spots.

title: What the Browns Need to Do in the Second Half of the 2026 Season to Make the Playoffs
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are officially over halfway through their season with a 5-4 record. Their two-game losing streak has dropped them out of first place in their division and to the eighth seed in the conference.
Only eight teams are above .500 in the AFC, and the Browns are behind only the New England Patriots due to a tiebreaker.
The Patriots have won more AFC games, which propelled them past the Browns in the standings. The second half of the season presents opportunities for them to overtake the last spot in the wild card. The opportunity is in front of them, but several things will need to fall into place to make that happen.
"We're 3-0 at home. Guess what? We have the next four at home and a bye week. It's all right there in front of us. It really it is." pic.twitter.com/So0o9PyURj
The Browns have only played three games at home in the first half of the season. They are 3-0 in Cleveland and are coming off a three-game road trip. They have five games in Cleveland to finish out the season, including a four-game homestand starting on Sunday.
They only play one team over .500 at home the rest of the way, against the Cincinnati Bengals. If they can win the other four of their home games, then it will guarantee a winning season and set up a meaningful road showdown against the quarterback-needy Baltimore Ravens towards the end of the season. The Patriots have five more games against teams over .500.
#Browns Todd Monken said he's not ready to name his starting quarterback for Sunday's game vs. the #Texans .
Deshaun Watson started the first eight games of the season before giving way to Shedeur Sanders last week. Watson was cleared from the concussion protocol before the deadline, but Todd Monken chose to switch to Sanders.
The offense looked the same as it did under Watson, with the first three quarters being a snooze fest, and then flipping a switch in the fourth quarter. Monken has been uncertain about which quarterback to play on Sunday.
The bye week is coming up, and the Browns should have a clear plan in place for their starting quarterback for the rest of the season. The competition should not be a week-to-week decision , as the young roster needs consistent reps. Monken should open up the offensive play-calling early in the games to avoid their season-long drought in the first three quarters.
Week after week is the same story with their inability to run the ball. They struggled last week against the New Orleans Saints, and stopping the run was their Achilles' heel. They will play in cold weather in every game for the remainder of the season. The running game has to find a way to get production for them to win second-half games.
Quinshon Judkins has struggled all season, but Dylan Sampson has shown that his speed can be a factor in the backfield. Jaleel McLaughlin has had minimal carries this season, but when he has gotten opportunities, he has run hard and shown some elusiveness. The running back room needs a shakeup to get any amount of production.
Mason Graham began the season as a force to be reckoned with, but then he got hurt and has not looked the same since. The bye week could give him some time to recover and return to form. The defensive line has been ultra-aggressive against the run, which has resulted in over-pursuits and big holes for the offense.
This has put a lot of pressure on Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams. Both linebackers have had a good season so far, but they are banged up. An extra week of rest before the home stretch may be just what they need.
Jared Verse has not provided any production, and if he can step up his game to an average level, then the defense should be better at stopping the run.
To even speculate on the Browns making the playoffs is a big surprise given where the team was in training camp. Their destiny is in front of them, and they just need to improve in a couple of areas to knock on the playoff door.

title: Rams Exploring Wide Receiver Options at Trade Deadline, Could Browns Have a Fit?
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is approaching quickly.
And after the first nine weeks of the regular season, the Cleveland Browns are 5-4. Somehow, someway, the Browns are playing competitive football with a roster that was counted out by many before the year began.
But while success is being found by a number of different players, many being on the offensive end, one player has fallen into the shadows of the franchise: wide receiver Jerry Jeudy.
On Monday, Nov. 9, news broke that the Los Angeles Rams were "exploring all avenues", according to Rams head coach Sean McVay, at the wide receiver position due to injuries to both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. If that is the case, the Rams should consider giving the Browns a call for Jeudy.
“I think you’ve got to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up," McVay said when asked about LA's activeness at the deadline.
McVay: Rams will "explore all avenues" at WR.
Jeudy wouldn't be a bad addition to the Rams' squad, even if Nacua gets healthy and Adams returns to the gridiron towards the back half of the season. He would fit seamlessly into their pass-heavy offense led by quarterback Matthew Stafford.
The 38-year-old leads the league in passing attempts with 346, completing a league-high 230 as well.
Jeudy hasn't gotten the looks many thought he would in Cleveland this season, mainly due to the breakout of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. In order to continue developing them both, Jeudy will continue to slip down the total targets list.
And after all, at just 27 years old, he seems to still have a lot in the tank.
While the Rams may not be the most competitive team in the league, owning a 5-4 record and a second-place spot in the NFC West Division , adding a bit of talent back to the offensive side of the ball could be in the picture at the deadline. It could end up being the difference between them making the playoffs or wasting one of Stafford's final seasons of his career.
Jeudy's situation in Cleveland has changed considerably since he was traded to there back in 2024.
Earning a Pro Bowl selection that campaign, he would haul in 90 passes for 1,229 yards and four touchdowns. But from then on, his production dipped heavily ; in 2025, he made 50 catches for 602 yards and two scores. This season, he has just 18 catches for 208 yards.
The emergence of both Concepcion and Boston has given the Browns more reasons than ever to evaluate their long-term plans at the position, too. Not to mention, tight end Harold Fannin Jr. remains as dominant as ever, taking even more targets away.
With the Browns potentially having their next generation of receiving talent already in place, moving Jeudy now for additional draft capital could be worth considering.
The Browns aren't going to be able to land a first- or second-round pick for Jeudy, but if the Rams are desperate, a third- or fourth-rounder could be tossed across the table. From recent speculation, the latter is what the Browns are hoping to receive if he ever did get moved.
The deadline will be on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4:00 p.m. EST.
And it will be interesting to see whether the Rams or Browns make any trades.

title: Browns Have 4 Difficult Roster Decisions to Make Before the Next NFL Season
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns look to recover from a second straight loss in order to get ready for a home game against the Texans before the bye week arrives, the team still has its sights set on postseason play despite falling to a 5-4 record.
However, things aren’t looking quite as peachy as they were just a couple of weeks ago, and it’s never too early for the team to start thinking about upgrades for the upcoming offseason.
Here are four difficult roster decisions the Browns will have to face before next season comes around, despite the fact that Cleveland still has eight more games to play this year:
Based on what we’ve seen through the first half of the season, it’s starting to look like the front office whiffed on the Tytus Howard trade .
Listen, a full offensive line swap was never an easy proposition. Rookies Fano and Austin Barber have struggled at times, but both have been good additions overall. Zion Johnson is steadily improving, and Elgton Jenkins is the team’s best pass-blocker.
Howard, on the other hand, has been a liability because of penalties and play. He’s signed through 2028, with cap hits of $10 million for next year and almost $17 million for the year after that. Cutting him loose during the next offseason won’t be cheap because there are also four void years attached to the end of his deal.
Howard would carry a dead cap hit of around $28.5 million for next year, while the team would lose an additional $18.4 million in cap space if he gets cut after this season. Designating him as a post-June 1st cut would translate into a $17.2 million dead cap hit and an additional $7.2 million in cap space lost for 2027, plus an $11.2 million dead cap charge for 2028.
The Browns could choose to experiment with a tackle swap to the left side, with Fano going right, or kick him inside to right guard, with Barber taking the right tackle spot. They could also give Dawand Jones a shot at right tackle, and leave Howard as the --pretty expensive-- swing tackle option. Or they could stick it out with Howard and wait for some improvement.
In any case, Howard hasn’t lived up to the expectations so far.
Jeudy went from being WR1 to WR3 on the Browns’ roster in a hurry. Buried on the depth chart behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, he’s currently on pace for 34 catches and less than 400 receiving yards. He’s also yet to find the end zone. The Browns really don’t need to pay that much for this kind of production.
Should the Browns decide not to trade Jeudy before this year’s deadline , then cutting him after the season would certainly seem the way to go.
Because cutting him outright would trigger a $25.4 million dead cap charge and an additional loss of around $12 million in cap space, designating him as a post-June cut makes sense, as the team would then take on an $8.8 million cap hit in 2027 along with cap savings of $4.6 million, along with a 2028 cap hit of $16.6 million.
The team likes a lot of things about its No. 1 running back. But after a season and a half averaging just 3.5 yards a pop, the Browns need to be honest in asking themselves if he truly is a franchise back .
The rest of the season should serve as an audition to see whether Dylan Sampson and/or Jaleel McLaughlin can handle a bigger share of the workload--Sampson has already started to eat away at Judkins' snaps.
If the answer is no, and Judkins doesn’t show a sizeable improvement either, then the team will most likely have to go hunting for a running back in the draft, where, luckily for the Browns, it doesn’t always cost a fortune in resources to find a stud.
As things stand, Cleveland will want to split Deshaun Watson’s accelerated void year cap charge of $86 million in two, with $34.7 million affecting the 2027 cap and $51.5 million on standby for the 2028 cap. They will need to process him as a post-June cut for this to work.
After that, the team will have to make a call on Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, and see if any one of those passers could drum up a little interest in the trade market .
Then, of course, the Browns will be faced --once again-- with one colossal decision: Who will be the team’s next quarterback?
Could Cleveland sniff around other teams for a potential trade? Will free agency be an option? Or will the franchise wait and see what comes out of a once-promising draft class at the quarterback position?
All this, provided that the Browns don’t actually extend Watson beyond this season in the NFL’s worst example of the sunk cost fallacy ever.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Todd Monken Pushes Back on Report About Browns' Starting QB
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns face a quarterback controversy yet again.
Shedeur Sanders, the Browns' second-year quarterback, made his first start of the season against the Saints on Sunday after the starter, Deshaun Watson, missed most of the week's practices due to a concussion.
#Browns QB Deshaun Watson (concussion protocol) returned to practice today. pic.twitter.com/LHaXZFaXl3
Watson cleared concussion protocol Saturday, a day after head coach Todd Monken named Sanders the starter because Watson had missed team reps. That’s where things took an unusual turn.
Sanders’ first start of the season began quietly, as he threw for just 38 yards before halftime with the score tied 3-3. In the second half and overtime, however, Sanders came alive, finishing with 297 yards and two passing touchdowns.
Sanders also put the Browns in position to win, leading a drive that set up Andre Szmyt’s game-tying field goal late in the fourth quarter. Then, Sanders threw a touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. in overtime, setting up a potential game-winning two-point conversion. Unfortunately, the Browns did not convert.
Sanders’ start left the fan base divided on what the Browns should do next. Some saw the same pattern that has defined Watson’s season: a slow start followed by clutch plays late . To them, that was reason enough to start the younger quarterback . Others, including ESPN Cleveland’s Tony Rizzo, point to Watson’s 5-3 record as a reason to retain him.
On Monday morning, a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler made it seem as if a decision had already been made:
The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs the Texans, per source. Shedeur Sanders filled in Sunday in New Orleans, but returning to Watson was the expected move once he cleared concussion protocol.
Fowler reported that Watson was expected to resume his starting role against Houston. With Monken scheduled to speak hours later, attention turned to whether the coach would confirm that plan.
Asked Monday who would start against Houston, Monken declined to commit. “I really haven’t thought through it other than getting through this morning’s tape,” he said.
Following @JFowlerESPN report, Todd Monken is not prepared to name #Browns starting QB for #Texans this week https://t.co/Sz6demBKD7 pic.twitter.com/EUneEV57SC
Now, Browns fans are yet again left to debate who should be the starter for their team. Monken has not announced a timetable as his staff reviews Sunday’s performance, but one thing is for sure: the Browns still have an opportunity to compete.
At 5-4 with one game remaining before their bye week, the Browns are still in a solid position to contend for a playoff spot and potentially an AFC North title. A distraction such as a quarterback controversy only hinders that.
Monken attributed Watson’s inactive status on Sunday to his lack of team reps during the week, despite examples of quick returns from concussion, like Brock Purdy in 2023 . His refusal to name a starter after Sunday’s game and again on Monday, even after reports pointed to Watson, keeps the debate alive. Is a trade coming? Is there pushback from ownership? Only time will tell.
Regardless of what is happening behind the scenes, Cleveland must focus on its home matchup against Houston. A win would put the Browns back on track heading into their bye week.

title: Dallas Cowboys Signing Former Saints Running Back After Tyler Goodson Injury
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys lost running back Tyler Goodson to an injury after the Week 9 game against the Indianapolis Colts, but they have now added a replacement.
With Goodson on the shelf for now, the Cowboys only had one healthy running back on their active roster, which is of course Javonte Williams, and two on their practice squad in Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin, so they needed more help.
Well, the Cowboys have now added someone.
According to Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News , the Cowboys are signing former New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller to the practice squad.
"The Cowboys will do something today, a person with knowledge of the situation said the team will sign RB Kendre Miller to practice squad," Watkins reported.
Miller was a 2023 third-round pick of the Saints out of TCU.
He has spent all four years of his career with the Saints, compiling 184 carries for 656 yards and five touchdowns to go along with 29 receptions for 217 receiving yards in 27 games.
Miller's most productive season was actually his rookie year in 2023, when he posted 156 rushing yards and career-highs in receiving yards (117) and scrimmage yards (273).
The former Saints draft pick is a decent runner and pass-catcher, but he doesn't do anything special in either area. He also struggles in pass protection, so he won't be an ideal option to play on obvious passing downs.
Miller does have good size at 6-foot and 220 pounds, but that size has not helped him avoid injuries. Over his three-plus seasons in the NFL, Miller has missed a total of 29 games, including 10 last season due to a torn ACL.
Thankfully, Goodson, who suffered a knee injury in Week 9, did not come down with a major injury, but he is expected to miss multiple weeks. It isn't yet clear if he'll need an injured reserve stint.
According to his dad, Maurice, it's "just a sprain" for Goodson, and ESPN's Todd Archer reports it's a sprain of his MCL and ACL .
It's a shame for Goodson, who was starting to emerge with Dallas after a strong showing against his former team, the Colts, that saw him tally 77 yards on 12 carries.
Goodson was claimed off waivers by the Cowboys back in September and has appeared in seven games since then.
In those seven contests, he's tallied 163 rushing yards and over four yards per carry, and he has also added 23 receiving yards.
Prior to his stint with the Cowboys, Goodson had spent the last three seasons with the Colts.

title: Why Dallas Cowboys Didn't Make a Trade on Deadline Day and What NFC East Rivals Did
full_text:
After a lot of talk from owner Jerry Jones about his willingness to make a trade, even after the deal for Joey Porter Jr., the Cowboys remained quiet on deadline day.
The 4 p.m. ET deadline came and went and the Cowboys did not make a deal on Tuesday. To be quite honest, that really wasn't a surprise, as Jones had said on a few occasions that he didn't expect anything to happen.
Jones was still open to a deal when he spoke to 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday, but he also stated he didn't expect anything significant for the Cowboys on deadline day.
“You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling. It’s really not ringing," he said. "But don’t count it out," Jones said. "A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”
Now, let's dive into what might have led to the Cowboys standing pat, and we'll look at what the rest of the NFC East did.
There could be a whole host of reasons why the Cowboys didn't make a deal.
For starters, the Cowboys needed a major move, especially for an edge rusher, but those guys are rarely available. And, if they are, the price is astronomical.
Even if there was a trade available for an elite edge rusher, Dallas would have had a tough time making it work given their lack of draft capital as a result of trades in recent years.
There were probably smaller trades to be had, but, again, Dallas was likely in the market for something big because of how poorly the defense has played this season. A lesser move would not have been worth giving up the draft capital for.
There is also the possibility that Jerry realizes there was probably no trade that can help this team and he might have sworn off a deal entirely in order to salvage the draft picks he has left.
Like the Cowboys, the Giants and Commanders did not make a move on deadline day. The Giants in particular were involved in plenty of rumors, but in the end they didn't do anything.
As for the Eagles, they almost made a trade on deadline day by sending Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals, but hilariously, the Bengals pulled out of the deal after realizing it would cost them a third-round compensatory pick they are due to get after the departure of Trey Hendrickson in free agency.
The Eagles did, however, pull off a blockbuster trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars on Monday that sent Jordan Davis to Duval. That's good news for the Cowboys because now they won't have to deal with the mammoth interior defensive lineman twice a year anymore. Philly did, however, get a nice haul of a first- and second-round pick.

title: Dallas Cowboys Showing Interest in Signing Former Saints RB Before Week 10
full_text:
It feels unlikely that the Dallas Cowboys will be making any trades ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday at 3 p.m. CT.
But that hardly means Dallas will stay quiet when it comes adding some new faces to the roster through free agency.
The Cowboys will be without backup running back Tyler Goodson for multiple weeks after he suffered a knee injury in the win over the Indianapolis Colts. As a result, Dallas faces some legitmate depth concerns behind running back Javonte Williams. The Cowboys recently signed former training camp running back Jashaun Corbin to the practice squad but Dallas needs a more immediate solution.
Now, ahead of Week 10's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, the Cowboys could be on the brink of getting exactly what they need at the backup running back spot.
The Cowboys are hosting former New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller for a visit on Tuesday, per reports from ESPN's Todd Archer.
This comes after Jerry Jones said that the Cowboys would be adding a new running back through free agency, a move that became obvious once Goodson went down.
Miller, 24, has been with New Orleans since 2023, playing primarily as a backup. Despite running back injuries of their own, the Saints waived him on Saturday.
In 27 career games and three starts with the Saints, Miller posted 184 carries for 656 yards and five touchdowns along with 29 catches for 217 yards.
A native of tiny Mount Enterprise High School in East Texas, Miller was a little-known recruit before bursing onto the scene with the TCU Horned Frogs.
After 10 total touchdowns combined across his first two seasons, Miller helped lead TCU to the College Football Playoff National Championship game in 2022, finishing that season with 224 carries for 1,399 yards and 17 touchdowns. This production motivated the Saints to take him in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft.
Cowboys fans that double as TCU fans in the Fort Worth area are all too familiar with Miller and have likely kept watch of his journey through the NFL since leaving college.
After the Cowboys-Saints preseason game in August, Miller gathered with three former TCU teammates on the Cowboys -- linebacker Dee Winters, wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end DJ Rogers -- for a postgame picture.
Fast forward a few months later, and it's possible he could be joining Dallas, though time will tell. Don't expect Miller to be the only free agent running back the Cowboys show interest in.

title: Trades Dallas Cowboys Could Make Today & Chances Deals Happen
full_text:
NFL trade deadline day is here and this will be the last chance the Dallas Cowboys have to make a deal to improve their roster for the second half of the season.
Jerry Jones has maintained over and over again that he is open to making another trade, even after the Joey Porter Jr. deal, but in recent days he has expressed pessimism about getting something done.
"If it's substantive for sure... you don't have any idea until you have the meeting of the minds and it's done. At this point I don't see it," Jones told 105.3 The Fan .
Edge rusher remains the Cowboys' biggest need ahead of the trade deadline. With that in mind, here's a look at some possible targets for the Cowboys and the chances Dallas will acquire them.
Crosby recently reiterated that he wants to stay with the Raiders and reports suggest Las Vegas won't deal him .
However, we've already seen the Raiders trade him once for a big package, so we wouldn't rule it out from happening again if the Raiders get an offer they can't refuse.
The Cowboys will have to throw at least two first-round picks at the Raiders, which they have, and we could see Jerry doing it because adding an elite edge rusher is the only kind of move Dallas can make to even have a chance to save its defense.
That said, we find it hard to believe Crosby is going anywhere.
Sweat is a more realistic option than Crosby given the state of things over there in Arizona, as the Cardinals are having a bad season and are in the midst of a rebuild. Sweat will also be far cheaper than Crosby, so that's another reason.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz recently reported that the belief is Sweat is open to a trade, but it remains to be seen if Arizona actually wants to move him, Schultz added.
It sure would make sense for Arizona to move him because the team needs more draft capital for its rebuild and Sweat could decline before the Cardinals are good again.
The problem is the Cowboys might have to overpay in order to get him and we're not sure they're willing to do that given the team's dwindling stable of picks.
McDonald has reportedly requested a trade , but rumors suggest the New York Jets aren't interested in trading him and head coach Aaron Glenn has also said that publicly.
If the Jets are willing to move McDonald, he's probably the most realistic option on this list because of cost. Because he's less proven than Sweat, McDonald should come cheaper, and potentially for a fourth-round pick.
We could see Jones having the stomach for this kind of trade more than overpaying for Sweat.
Speculation has run rampant about a Pickens trade in recent weeks as the Cowboys have struggled mightily.
However, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports the Cowboys have no interest in trading Pickens.
"The fifth-year pass-catcher and second-year Cowboy is playing this season on the franchise tag after the team elected not to discuss a long-term contract with him in the offseason. Despite trade rhetoric around the time of that decision being announced, the Cowboys never engaged in trying to send him away. Seven months later, that strategy remains the same ahead of the deadline, according to multiple sources," Harris said.
That said, as we saw with the Chicago Bears' trade for Jeffery Simmons, just about anyone can be had if the offer is big enough. Knowing that, we wouldn't rule out a team throwing an offer at the Cowboys that they can't refuse.
The Cowboys may look to add at cornerback, safety or linebacker, but needs at those spots aren't dire as long as Dallas' injured players can get back.
At cornerback, the Cowboys aren't benching DaRon Bland even though he's terrible, and they obviously have Joey Porter Jr. and Cobie Durant, so there's enough there, assuming Porter can get past his ankle injury .
When it comes to safety, the Cowboys just lost P.J. Locke to yet another concussion, so that's a concern, and Jalen Thompson remains on injured reserve and we don't know when he'll be back, although he is now eligible to return off IR.
At linebacker, DeMarvion Overshown is hurt again and clearly the Cowboys can't depend on him. Dallas has also apparently lost faith in Jaishawn Barham after he played just three snaps in Week 9.
All that said, we continue to believe if the Cowboys pull the trigger on any trade, it's going to be at edge rusher, although we wouldn't totally rule out an addition at these three spots.
Trade chances for Linebacker: 30% Trade chances for safety: 30% Trade chances for cornerback: 10%

title: Jerry Jones Teases Dallas Cowboys Trade At NFL Deadline Without Going All-In
full_text:
There has been rampant speculation about whether the Dallas Cowboys will make a splash at the NFL trade deadline , with the team needing massive improvements on the defensive side of the ball.
Last season, the Cowboys added All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to the roster, while trading for cornerback Joey Porter Jr . earlier in the season. While those were improvements for the team, there is still a lack of overall talent on the roster.
With the deadline coming up in a matter of hours, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones stopped by 105.3 The Fan to share his thoughts on what could be coming for the team.
Once again, Jones teased a potential move for the Cowboys , but indicated it would not be anything groundbreaking or a headline-making move.
According to Jon Machota of The Athletic, Jones said “don’t count out” the Cowboys potentially making a move at the deadline, but it came with an unfortunate disclaimer.
“You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling. It’s really not ringing … but don’t count it out," Jones said. "A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”
If the Cowboys were in the process of making a splash, Jones would likely be more excited and teasing the move in order to make headlines. We've seen that is the way that Jones likes to operate. But, for now, the Cowboys appear poised to stand firm with their current roster for the rest of the season, though they could add a few rotational pieces.
We will find out how everything plays out over the next few hours, with the NFL trade deadline coming at 4:00 p.m. ET. If there is a move, let's hope it is to improve the team on defense, because the current NFL rankings are less than inspiring.
Total Defense : The Cowboys currently rank No. 30 overall in total defense, giving up 372.7 points per game. The team has allowed 27 touchdowns.
Passing Defense : Dallas has seen an improvement in recent weeks, moving to No. 18 overall in the league. The Cowboys have allowed 16 passing touchdowns, while giving up 225.2 passing yards per game.
Rushing Defense : The Cowboys have been brutal against the run, ranking No. 31 overall above only the Las Vegas Raiders. Dallas has allowed 147.4 rushing yards per game and 11 rushing touchdowns.

title: Will George Pickens Return in Week 10? Latest Injury Update on Dallas Cowboys WR
full_text:
For the first time since he was acquired in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last year, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens missed a game due to injury.
Pickens had been battling multiple injuries in recent weeks, but he was able to suit up through them to play before he missed Sunday's contest against the Indianapolis Colts.
Pickens was able to shed his shoulder injury in Week 9, but he was still battling a hamstring injury that left him limited at practice all week before he drew the questionable tag and was inactive.
As we turn the page to Week 10, here's what we know about his chances of suiting up.
Pickens' status is still very much up in the air for this week.
On Monday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer made no promises about Pickens for Sunday, with Schotty saying Dallas would "try to get" him on the practice field to see where he's at.
When co-owner Stephen Jones was asked about Pickens and Joey Porter Jr., his answer was very much of the wait-and-see variety.
"I think we just have to get them out there, get them going again, and see how they're coming along," Jones said . "We're certainly going to have to really see what our injury situation is this week. We're going to have some challenges."
On the bright side, the fact that Pickens was able to log limited practices last week suggests he isn't far off from playing, so we would say he's got a better chance to suit up than not.
We'll have a better idea of where Pickens stands when the Cowboys release their first injury report on Wednesday.
With Pickens sidelined, Ryan Flournoy played on a season-high 97.5% of snaps and recorded two catches for 53 yards. His previous snap-share high in 2026 was 87.2% of snaps.
Jonathan Mingo and rookie Camden Brown also benefitted from Pickens' absence, with Mingo appearing for a season-high 39.2% of snaps and Brown seeing a career-high 36.7%.
However, Mingo caught just one ball for 23 yards and Brown wasn't targeted and instead contributed on returns with three kickoff returns for 78 yards.
While there has been a lot of speculation about Dallas possibly trading Pickens amid a poor season, there has been nothing to suggest the team is interested in doing so, according to Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram .
"The fifth-year pass-catcher and second-year Cowboy is playing this season on the franchise tag after the team elected not to discuss a long-term contract with him in the offseason. Despite trade rhetoric around the time of that decision being announced, the Cowboys never engaged in trying to send him away. Seven months later, that strategy remains the same ahead of the deadline, according to multiple sources," Harris wrote.
Never say never in the NFL, but as of right now it looks highly unlikely, at best, Pickens gets moved.

title: DeMarvion Overshown Criticized by Cowboys' Stephen Jones For Dumb Penalty
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys escaped Lucas Oil Stadium with a 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, and the game certainly wasn't without its fair share of wackiness.
Dallas nearly blew another double-digit lead thanks to a wild catch-and-run fumble from CeeDee Lamb in the fourth quarter that appeared to give the Colts a massive boost of momentum.
Fortunately, the Cowboys responded by forcing a fumble of their own in the red zone, as Quinnen Williams punched the ball out of Jonathan Taylor's grasp. The takeaway helped stall a Indianapolis drive that was aided by 55 yards worth of penalties from the Dallas defense.
But as the Cowboys gathered to celebrate the turnover, another flag was thrown , this time on linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. Inactive with hamstring and back injuries, Overshown looked just fine as he illegally ran on the field in street clothes, drawing an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty against Dallas.
During an appearance Monday on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys vice president Stephen Jones didn't hold back his honest thoughts on Overshown's penalty.
“It is (unacceptable). … It’s not a good look. It’s not a disciplined look," Jones said. "We certainly didn’t play a disciplined game yesterday with (14) penalties. We have to be better than that.”
Fortunately for Dallas, Overshown's mistake, as dumb as it was, didn't hurt the team's chances of winning the game. The Cowboys certainly had a slew of other penalties that were much more impactful, including DaRon Bland's 40-yard pass interference that came only a few plays before Overshown ran onto the field.
Overshown took to social media to acknowledge his mistake.
"Was just tryna celebrate with the guys... my bad G," Overshown wrote on Instagram.
Cowboys already have mixed feelings about Overshown, who has dealt with a ton of injury issues and has only played in 22 of a possible 60 games in his career with the team. Sunday's penalty doesn't exactly improve this outlook, especially since he ran on his injured hamstring.
Overshown had been playing well in the two contests prior to Week 9, as he had an interception and forced fumble following a five-game absence. Hopefully he returns to action in Week 10's home game against the San Francisco 49ers.
