title: Ex-NFL GM Isn't Buying Cowboys' Rumored Stance on Trading George Pickens
full_text:
While there has been increasing speculation about the Dallas Cowboys possibly trading wide receiver George Pickens, the rumors suggest the Cowboys aren't interested in doing that.
Most recently, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Nick Harris put out a report stating the Cowboys have no plans to trade Pickens , and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport has said nothing is going on there.
However, former Tennessee Titans general manager Ran Carthon isn't buying that and he believes the Cowboys are "definitely exploring" trading their No. 2 receiver before the deadline.
"I think (the Cowboys) are definitely exploring it," Carthon said on CBS Sports. "Because, again, I think the writing is on the wall that they're not going to bring him back in terms of signing him to a long-term deal."
"So, if you're the Dallas Cowboys, why not explore being able to move on from (Pickens)," Carthon added. "Ryan Flournoy gives you that option now. He's a guy that's looking reliable, he's a guy that's going to show up, do his work, and he is one of the few guys on that offense as a whole who plays hard every single down."
The writing is on the wall that Pickens is not going to be back in 2027.
Co-owner Stephen Jones has already said in the past that it's tough to keep two high-paid wide receivers on the roster, which Dallas would be doing if it extends or even tags Pickens in 2027.
"The situation we have with George Pickens going alongside CeeDee.. I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said. "So, yeah. That's going to be a real difficult situation as we move forward. We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year."
It's clear the Cowboys might need an overhaul on defense again next offseason, or at the very least some improvements, and they will have to extend Joey Porter Jr. Having all of that money tied up in two receivers will leave the Cowboys with less wiggle room to accomplish everything they need to.
Furthermore, if the Cowboys do tag Pickens, we don't envision the veteran wideout simply accepting that again and entering another year without future certainty, so a hold out is more likely this time.
The tag-and-trade scenario is an option, but the Cowboys will have to keep that money on the books until he's moved and if they can't get a trade done quickly, that will hinder them in free agency.
So, when it comes down to it, the best courses of action are to either trade Pickens now or let him walk in free agency next offseason to get a compensatory pick, and only the former avenue guarantees what the Cowboys will get.
Some might view trading Pickens as waving the white flag on the season, but what exactly have the Cowboys accomplished with their star-studded duo at wide receiver? Nothing.
Unless Pickens can play cornerback or rush the passer, keeping him isn't going to make a dent in Dallas' playoff hopes in 2026.

title: Dallas Cowboys Breakout Star Expected To Miss Time After Career Game
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' running game saw a resurgence during Sunday's crucial Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium, but it may have come at a cost.
While starting running back Javonte Williams rushed for 101 yards and a touchdown, backup running back Tyler Goodson also came through with the best game of his career. Goodson rushed for a career-high 77 yards on 12 carries, but suffered a knee injury that is expected to sideline him for a few weeks.
During his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys COO Stephen Jones provided an update on Goodson, who was briefly sidelined on Sunday afternoon.
Jones revealed the team has its "fingers crossed" on the Goodson injury front. He added, "He’s got a real injury that unfortunately he’s probably gonna miss some time with .” To add to the Cowboys' injury concerns, star wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. are also battling lingering issues that the team will be forced to monitor throughout the week.
With the Goodson, Pickens, and Porter injuries, among others, the Cowboys could once again be short-handed when they take the field against the San Francisco 49ers next week. That comes at an unfortunate time with the team looking to build momentum entering a key stretch of the season.
Unlike the Indianapolis Colts, who appear to be preparing for a firesale ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the 49ers are a loaded team that will test the Cowboys on both sides of the ball.
Goodson's injury especially stings, because he provided some explosiveness to the running game as the offense was attempting to get back on track. Dallas has become more reliant on the run, but will now need to look elsewhere for additional depth until Goodson is healthy enough to return to the field.
Through the first nine weeks of the season, the Cowboys rank No. 21 overall in rushing, with 103.6 yards per game and 11 touchdowns. We'll have to see who the team calls on to contribute behind Williams for the foreseeable future as the week rolls on.

title: Grading Broncos' Daiyan Henley Trade: What Denver Really Got
full_text:
For the first time in several years, the Denver Broncos actually made a trade ahead of the NFL deadline.
On Tuesday, the Broncos sent a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers in exchange for veteran linebacker Daiyan Henley . It's not often that division rivals will trade with each other, especially during the season, but the winless Chargers are in a unique position and the Broncos were smart enough to capitalize.
Henley is a fourth-year linebacker whom the Chargers drafted out of Washington State in the third round (No. 85 overall) back in 2023. He also played some college ball at Nevada.
The Broncos didn't make a trade for a running back, tight end, or offensive lineman, as many fans hoped. Sean Payton said, " I like this team a lot ," after beating the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday, and the lack of a trade to help the offense not only reinforces that, but also shows much confidence in the Broncos' skill positions.
The Broncos expect to get RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie back from injured reserve soon, and beyond them, the team is apparently content with rookie starter Jonah Coleman and veteran complement J.K. Dobbins, even if fans wanted the team to add one more running back while it still could.
The trade deadline has passed, with the Broncos making one trade. What grade should Denver get for the Henley trade? Let's break down how he fits before grading this trade.
At 6-foot-0 and 225 pounds, Henley is not a big linebacker, but that doesn't mean he's afraid to mix it up. He's very physical and offers sideline-to-sideline ability as a three-down linebacker.
Henley is a two-time team Chargers team captain and he led them in tackles thrice — if you count this season (51 tackles). He's only 26, and although he's in a contract year, the Broncos have the flexibility to see how he fits with half the season to go, plus the playoffs, before deciding on whether to re-sign him.
With a 2026 salary of $3.674 million, the Chargers have already paid half of that, leaving the Broncos with only a minor salary-cap liability with Henley. The Broncos had to be smart financially ahead of the deadline, with just $4.6 million in cap space. Henley will fit with plenty of room to spare.
Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad are the Broncos' starting linebackers, so Henley will begin his tenure as a depth player, depsite his experience as a 41-game starter. Much like last season when Dre Greenlaw was healthy and available, the Broncos will employ a three-man rotation at linebacker, based on down and distance.
In a perfect world, I'd like to see Henley on the field more than Singleton in obvious passing situations, but as the defender with the green dot on his helmet, it's hard to see the Broncos taking their team captain off the field much. But Singleton has already played an insane number of snaps, including the most coverage snaps among all NFL linebackers this season, so for more reasons than one, it would behoove the team to carve out some of his snaps for Henley.
That being said, Singleton plays 100% of the Broncos' defensive snaps for a reason. I doubt they'll move away from that, so as Henley gets worked into the rotation, it's likely to be at Strnad's expense . I'm okay with that, too.
Henley has proven to be a difference-maker in coverage and a reliable tackler against the run, when he's able to get off blocks cleanly. His nose for the ball is a nice bonus. He has four career interceptions, plus two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery.
Singleton has three career interceptions, three forced fumbles, and five fumble recoveries since entering the league in 2019. Strnad has exactly one career interception and one fumble recovery. Henley is more of a ballhawk with great instincts.
The Broncos have some decisions to make at linebacker after this season, with Singleton about to turn 33 and Strnad already over 30. Both were re-signed this past spring, with Singleton being under contract through 2027 and Strnad through 2028.
Singleton is the one to watch in the offseason, though. He's played quite well this season, earning Defensive Player of the Month honors for October, but he punctuated his 2026 campaign with a stinker to start the year and another in Carolina last week.
Singleton is on pace for a 200-tackle season, but Father Time is undefeated. The Broncos began planning for the future by selecting linebacker Red Murdock with the last pick in the 2026 draft, but he has spent his rookie year competing on the practice squad.
Hopefully, Murdock is developing, too. If things work out with Henley and the Broncos opt to re-sign him, it would give them two under-30 investments to potentially build around for the future, independent of what happens with Singleton after the 2026 season.
Karene Reid and Jordan Turner will be 27 and 25, respectively, when next season starts, so the Broncos have some youth on their side at linebacker, even if their current depth beyond Henley is inexperienced.
The Broncos needed a coverage linebacker. The best illustration is the nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns they've allowed to tight ends over the past three games alone.
Henley may not be a cure-all, but he upgrades the Broncos' defense and gives Vance Joseph a viable weapon to deploy against opponents with athletic, pass-catching tight ends. It just so happens that Henley is also very good against the run, so adding a three-down linebacker at the trade deadline should be celebrated, especially given the cost.
What an INT by Daiyan Henley! LACvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/qyp5jYJbVF
Things didn't pan out last year with Greenlaw, but Henley could be a totally different story. There's less baggage and no injury jacket, and Henley arguably brings a more reliable resume to Denver than Greenlaw did.
The Broncos are expected to land a fourth-round compensatory draft pick in 2027 for the free-agent departure of defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, which offsets the higher draft pick given up to the Chargers for Henley.
In other words, when it all comes out in the wash, the Broncos just added a three-down linebacker with coverage chops for the price of a fifth-round pick two years from now. How could anyone pan this pick?
Factoring in Henley's age, health, fit, and cap impact, this was a home run of a trade. He fills a big, lingering need, and the Broncos have the flexibility to decide on his post-2026 future after the season ends.
I may be slightly mystified that Denver spurned the opportunity to also upgrade the backfield behind Bo Nix, but that's not what I'm grading here. This is purely a grade of the Henley trade, and the Broncos pass with flying colors.
Let's see how a few of our staff writers graded the Henley trade.
I love this move for the Broncos. Henley was struggling on an 0-8 Chargers team, but his upside as a coverage linebacker cannot be overstated.
The Broncos have needed help in that area for years, and they didn't give up much to get him. The fourth-rounder is probably recouped as a compensatory pick for losing Franklin-Myers in the offseason, so sending a 2028 fifth-round pick for a starting-quality player who could be extended after this season is great work by GM George Paton.
A trade for an inside linebacker is not something I imagine most Broncos fans thought would happen, especially with a division rival. But Henley will help take some of the load off Singleton and Strnad.
And given what the Broncos gave up for Henley, it wouldn't surprise if they extended him at some point. This is a good move by the Broncos.
The Broncos get linebacker depth for basically a fifth-rounder, due to JFM netting them a fourth-round comp pick. Henley is likely a future replacement for Singleton.

title: How Broncos Made Roster Room for Newly-Acquired LB Daiyan Henley
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' acquisition of inside linebacker Daiyan Henley meant the team would need to make a corresponding move on their 53-man roster — someone had to go with Henley arriving.
That someone, the team announced , is defensive back Sean Fresch Jr., who was waived from the active roster, with designs of re-signing to the practice squad. That could happen as early as Wednesday, assuming Fresch clears waivers.
In preparation for such a maneuver, Denver also released DB Ugo Amadi from the practice squad. Amadi was on his second stint with the organization, and it's possible he resurfaces again this season.
Undrafted out of Rice in 2025, Fresch joined the Broncos in June following a successful tenure in the United Football League. Initially on the practice squad, he was promoted to the active roster and made his NFL debut in Week 5. Fresch, too, appeared in last week's victory over the Panthers, returning two kickoffs for 62 yards — including a 41-yard runback on the game's opening play.
"[He's] really smart at the nickel, he’s a returner, got quick change of direction," head coach Sean Payton said of Fresch in June.
In addition to his special teams duties, Fresch was also on the 53 to serve as insurance at the cornerback position, which has been beat up by the injury bug this year. Although the Broncos lost Riley Moss to a concussion against Carolina, Moss is likely to return when the club emerges from its Week 10 bye — rendering Fresch expendable.
Assuming Moss is back against the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 22, the Broncos' primary cornerback room will be at full strength with Patrick Surtain II also recovered from a previous ankle injury. The team also hopes to return CB Kris Abrams-Draine from his own ankle issue.
Henley, meanwhile, is reportedly anticipated to open his Broncos career as the third ILB behind incumbent starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, pushing Karene Reid and Jordan Turner further down the depth chart — one of them, potentially off the roster.
Henley is regarded as a fierce tackler with solid pass-coverage and blitzing chops who wore the green dot during his time with the Chargers. He'll immediately see snaps as a rotational 'backer for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, but it wouldn't at all be a surprise if he's starting over Singleton or Strnad sooner rather than later.

title: Broncos' Daiyan Henley Trade Creates Big Winners & Losers
full_text:
Instead of a running back or tight end, the Denver Broncos traded for a linebacker ahead of Tuesday's NFL deadline.
Denver gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers for fourth-year linebacker Daiyan Henley . A two-time team captain who led the Chargers thrice (counting this season) in tackles, Henley is a physical presence at the second level of the defense who also brings — finally — some coverage upside to the table.
As with any trade, signing, or draft pick, a roster addition creates some ripple effects. Let's break down the Broncos' biggest winners and losers of the Henley trade.
Joseph has sorely lacked a true coverage linebacker since returning to Denver as defensive coordinator in 2023. The Broncos have tried to mask their tight-end coverage woes with one of the NFL's best secondaries, but the cornerbacks and safeties often have their hands full.
Over the past three weeks alone, the Broncos have allowed nearly 300 receiving yards and three touchdowns to tight ends. That had to be one of the motivating factors behind the Henley trade.
Once Henley gets up to speed on the playbook, Joseph will have a new weapon to deploy in coverage. I don't want to make Henley out to be some miracle salve that will heal all of Denver's coverage wounds, but he's going to be a big, big help.
In terms of coverage, Strnad is the Broncos' best linebacker, but it's relative. He just signed a two-year extension in the spring and has been the team's undisputed starter next to Alex Singleton this season.
Singleton never leaves the field , while Strnad will at times. I'm open to the possibility of Joseph taking Singleton off the field in obvious passing situations, but in all likelihood, the reigning Defensive Player of the Month will continue to play 100% of the snaps.
The Broncos love Singleton, and they rely on him as the defensive signal-caller. I don't expect his role to change, but it should , at least on third down. I'm not talking about benching Singleton, but the Broncos should start giving some of his snaps to Henley.
Henley is going to see the field, but it will likely be at Strnad's expense. If the Broncos were smart, though, they'd start giving the soon-to-be 33-year-old Singleton a few breathers in-game and utilize Henley as their coverage linebacker.
Henley might not have the green dot on his helmet, but the Broncos could work around that, no problem. Singleton never leaves the field, and that's often a good thing.
However, unless he's blitzing, Singleton is a liability in obvious passing situations. Henley, at least, gives Joseph the option of trying other personnel combinations at linebacker in those situations. At the end of the day, when it comes to Singleton's role changing because of this trade, I'll believe it when I see it.
Henley's arrival means fewer snaps for Strnad, but it might not happen overnight. The Broncos have both Strnad and Singleton under contract beyond 2026, while Henley is in a contract year, so the team has to quickly figure out what it has in the ex-Charger team captain.
The Broncos rotated three linebackers down the stretch last season when Dre Greenlaw was still in Denver and healthy. Expect that to be the plan again coming out of the team's Week 10 bye.
One of these linebackers could be waived to make room for Henley on the 53-man roster. My guess is that it'll be Turner, but it's a coin flip between him and Reid.
Reid offers a bit more upside on special teams and defense. Turner contributes on special teams, too, but as a linebacker, he's a one-trick pony. Turner is a true stack linebacker, but the Broncos don't use him on defense.
Reid is more athletic and versatile, but the Broncos could base this decision on which linebacker they view least likely to get claimed on waivers. That's why it's a coin-flip decison.
Then again, the Broncos could opt to keep five inside linebackers on the 53-man roster for now and waive defensive back Sean Fresch Jr., wide receiver Lil'Jordan Humphrey, or rookie tight end Dallen Bentley, the last of whom is yet to dress this season. As a 2026 seventh-round pick, I doubt Bentley would be claimed on waivers, since he was the second-to-last pick in the draft and didn't do much to distinguish himself on tape in the preseason.
Whether the Broncos waive one of their linebackers or keep them all on the roster, though, the Henley trade is still a setback for Turner and Reid, simply because it puts one more obstacle between them and any playing time on defense.

title: Broncos Raid AFC West Rival in Trade for LB Daiyan Henley
full_text:
You don't often see intra-divisional trades, but one just went down in the AFC West.
The Denver Broncos have acquired Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley via trade for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, per ESPN 's Adam Schefter . The Chargers remain winless, so in this unprecedented situation they find themselves in, the Broncos get to benefit.
Schefter forecasted a Broncos move on Monday , and he was right.
Henley, 26, is in his fourth NFL season and the final year of his rookie contract. In 2023, the Chargers drafted him in the third round out of Washington State, and he has 41 career starts under his belt.
In Year 2, Henley became a starter, totaling 147 tackles (84 solo), seven tackles for a loss, a sack, and an interception. He followed that up in Year 3 with 103 tackles (54 solo), five for a loss, 3.5 sacks, and two interceptions.
With eight games under his belt this season, Henley has already totaled 51 tackles, a half-sack, a forced fumble, two fumble recoveries, and an interception. He's a difference-making linebacker, with a nose for the ball and the ability to cover.
Henley led the Chargers in tackles in each of the past two seasons, and exits L.A. as the club's leader in that department this season, too. He's a two-time team captain (including this season), so from a make-up perspective, he checks the boxes Denver covets as well.
That coverage ability is what the Broncos surely coveted, given that they've allowed nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns to tight ends over the last three games. Alex Singleton may be the reigning AFC Defensive Player of the Month , but he's a liability in coverage.
Justin Strnad is better than Singleton in coverage, but not by a long stretch. The Broncos re-signed both Singleton and Strnad this past offseason to serve as their starting linebacker duo, and the results thus far have been a mixed bag.
Henley can step in for Singleton in obvious passing situations and make a huge difference to Denver's passing defense. Singleton plays 100% of the Broncos' defensive snaps, as a team captain and the man with the green dot on his helmet, but the team might finally be considering alternatives.
Singleton is a great run-defending linebacker and a bona fide tackling machine, but his coverage is lacking. Strnad is a solid all-around linebacker, but the Broncos need a true answer in neutralizing opposing tight ends, and Henley gives it to them.
With the Broncos on bye this week, Henley will get plenty of time to assimilate the system. The NFL trade deadline came at the most opportune time for the Broncos, especially with them actually making a trade.
After the bye, the Broncos will host the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11, who just traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. That means Denver will face Fernando Mendoza — the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft — for the first time.
I'd expect to see plenty of Henley in that game. Now, what this means for backup linebackers Jordan Turner and Karene Reid remains to be seen, but both are key special teams contributors, so it wouldn't be a shock if the Broncos try to find a way to keep them on the 53-man roster.
But if they have to waive one of them, it'll likely be Turner. And odds are, he'd pass through waivers unclaimed to be re-signed to the practice squad, where he could be elevated on game day.
Broncos fans may have been hoping for a running back or a tight end , but Henley absolutely checks a box and gives the team something it was missing. The Broncos are better with Henley on the roster, and he'll get half the season to prove whether he deserves an extension in the spring.

title: Broncos' Evan Engram Emerges in 11th-Hour Trade Buzz
full_text:
To buy or to sell, that is the question.
The Denver Broncos have been perceived as buyers at the NFL trade deadline, given their 7-2 record. But we've heard veteran running back J.K. Dobbins's name floated in trade discussions , and as of Tuesday, tight end Evan Engram.
Per ESPN 's Jeremy Fowler, the 32-year-old Engram is "on the radar" around the NFL, as teams make final arrangements ahead of today's 2 p.m. MDT deadline.
"Another TE on the radar is Broncos' Evan Engram, who has garnered interest. But he's considered unlikely to be moved in part because Denver doesn't have a replacement (though the Broncos have called around just in case)," Fowler reported on X .
The Broncos have been checking the tight end trade market, looking for upgrades. Alas, Denver's wishlist target — Trey McBride — plays for a team that has zero interest in trading him.
Sam LaPorta is another intriguing option, though the Detroit Lions have been telling teams that he's not available. All it takes is the right offer, though, to blast open the door of possibilities, especially given that LaPorta is in a contract year and has publicly voiced his disappointment in not having an extension yet.
Engram is in his second year with the Broncos, and suffice it to say, his production hasn't been comensurate with his two-year, $23 million contract. He finished third on the team in 2025, with 50 receptions for 461 yards and one touchdown.
This year, though, Engram has been a bit of an afterthought, though Bo Nix's early-season slump didn't help matters. Engram is coming off one of his most productive games of the season, catching four passes on five targets for 33 yards in the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers.
The Broncos don't have an obvious replacement on the roster, were they to trade Engram, but they do have seventh-round rookie Dallen Bentley, who's been a healthy scratch all season. Beyond the rookie, the Broncos have Adam Trautman and Nate Adkins, both of whom are blocking tight ends who play in-line.
Engram has played in-line far more this season, but he's an 'F' tight end the Broncos try to use as a mismatch weapon. Alas, they haven't been able to exploit many matchups with Engram, whether that's due to Father Time slowing him down, Nix's middle-of-the-field avoidance, or the scheme/play-calling is anyone's guess.
We've heard that Denver is more interested in tight end and safety than running back ahead of the trade deadline. If true, Jonah Coleman's emergence has much to do with why, but it's hard to see a tight end coming in and elevating this offense in the same way that an experienced running back could.

title: Adam Schefter Forecasts Broncos' Last-Minute Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
All eyes are on Denver Broncos HQ to see whether GM George Paton will make a deal ahead of the NFL's 2 p.m. MDT trade deadline.
The Broncos have been linked to a handful of players over the past few weeks, including Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride , but it's been a long time since Paton made an in-season trade to acquire players.
And yet, the NFL's most famous insider — ESPN 's Adam Schefter — doesn't expect the Broncos to sit on their hands ahead of the deadline. In fact, Schefter told Altitude Sports Radio 92.5 FM hosts Vic Lombardi and Brett Kane on Monday that he expects Denver to "make a deal," so long as it "makes sense."
"I think they're going to work the phones. I think they're going to look to make a move. When you win a game before the bye week, and you're sitting there at 7-2, I think that you want to look at every opportunity you can to just shore up any spot you can," Schefter told Altitude Sports Radio . "Expect them to be active, to make a deal. But unless there's something that makes sense, they're not going to make a deal just to make a deal."
If the Broncos make a move, will it be for a running back? From what we're hearing, the Broncos may have cooled on targeting a running back because of Jonah Coleman's emergence and the stiff asking price teams are sticking to around the league, and are instead looking at tight end and safety.
Tight end is understandable, given the lackluster blocking of Adam Trautman and Evan Engram and their relative lack of impact in the passing game, but even if the Broncos managed to orchestrate a blockbuster trade for a McBride or a Sam LaPorta, you have to wonder whether the capital relinquished would be worth the production on the field.
Bo Nix has always avoided the middle of the field, though he's been a bit more aggressive in this regard of late. Keeping it in context, though, Engram just had one of his bigger receiving games of the season, and we're talking only four catches for 33 yards.
Tight ends get short shrift in the Broncos' passing game. That's just the brutal truth.
Now, would having a top-tier tight end change that somehow? Maybe, but it would be in relative terms, which again calls into question whether the juice would be worth the trade squeeze, so to speak. Nix has a strong preference for targeting receivers outside the numbers.
If the Broncos really are intent on trading for a safety, it makes me a bit more concerned about the health and post-bye well-being of Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones — the team's starting duo. Both missed Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers , which was Hufanga's fourth straight absence (the Broncos didn't put him on injured reserve, though).
Jones suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8's win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but the Broncos did not place him on IR, suggesting they expect him back within the next two games. If that's true, I'm not sure I see the need for a trade, as the Broncos currently have five safeties on the active roster, plus Taylor Rapp on the practice squad, the latter of whom has seen action in each of the past three games.
Granted, the Broncos' safety play has suffered with both Hufanga and Jones sidelined, but that's a temporary challenge. JL Skinner was not great in his start against the Panthers, but Devon Key was solid and made a game-changing interception in the second half on a play that was equal parts acrobatic and heads-up.
I guess I don't see the need for a safety. Perhaps what I'm hearing is a smokescreen — it's hard to say this close to the deadline.
The clearest indications of any trade interest the Broncos have shown have been at running back and tight end, so if they make a move, I'd be a little surprised if it's any other position. Then again, the Jacksonville Jaguars just set a new precedent by trading for two defensive linemen and a safety at the trade deadline, so perhaps all bets should be off.
There's no rule that says the Broncos have to pick one position. They could make multiple trades, like the Jaguars. But we've heard Sean Payton say "we like the guys we have" enough that it feels like the truth, especially given the Broncos' relative inactivity in free agency this past offseason.
If anyone has a bead on the Broncos' mindset ahead of Tuesday's deadline, though, it's Schefter. That doesn't mean the Broncos make a deal, but at the very least, it sounds like Paton will be working the phones to find the right combination of value, need, and fit before the opportunity to make a trade evaporates until the offseason.
The Broncos did end up making a trade, acquiring linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Schefter's hunch was right.

title: What Jonah Coleman's Increased Playing Time Reveals About Broncos' Plans
full_text:
It was a little dicey there for a moment, but the Denver Broncos prevailed over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, 26-21.
It was the Broncos' 16th straight victory in a one-score game, which set a new NFL record. The 2008-09 Indianapolis Colts — led by Peyton Manning — previously held the record with 15 straight one-score wins.
At 7-2, the Broncos now get to enjoy their bye week, but there are some potential matters of business to address first, with the NFL trade deadline coming on Tuesday, November 10, at 2 p.m. MDT. Some have wondered whether the Panthers game was a referendum of sorts that would tip the scales on Denver potentially making a trade, but time will tell.
As always, the Broncos' snap counts from Week 9 reflect the ever-changing flux in role for players on both sides of the ball. Bo Nix and the Broncos' starting offensive line played 100% of the snaps, with 66, with depth lineman Alex Palczewski again getting five snaps.
With that said, let's dive into this week's snap counts to see how each player's role is evolving as the season marches on.
Since returning from injured reserve, Coleman has outearned Dobbins in snaps and touches. Three straight games have hammered home the reality that Coleman is Denver's new RB1. Coleman also started this game.
Against the Panthers, the rookie had a season-high 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown, with four catches on four targets for an additional 33 yards. Dobbins had four carries for 18 yards and one catch for four yards.
Schrader was elevated from the practice squad, but unlike last week, he didn't get even one snap, let alone a touch. Meanwhile, Prentice, the fullback, had four more snaps than the $8 million Dobbins.
This is not a case of the Broncos protecting Dobbins for usage down the stretch. He's not getting the job done, while Coleman has provided a clear boost to the offense.
Can Coleman carry the RB1 load coming out of the bye? The Broncos don't have to force the issue; a running back trade could help take some of the pressure off of the rookie, and help keep him healthy for the stretch run and playoffs.
No Lil'Jordan Humphrey in this game. As has been the trend since Sean Payton took back the play-calling, Sutton led in snap share, and that translated to a team-high five receptions (on nine targets) for 45 yards and a touchdown.
Waddle was poised to have a big game before going down with a concussion. He caught his only target for 22 yards.
Franklin had one of his most productive games of the season, catching three passes on four targets for 31 yards, while Bryant starred in his first game back from injured reserve. "Patty Ice" caught four of his five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown.
Alas, Mims was the forgotten man, but it's his own fault. Until he improves his effort and gives 100% on every snap, he'll continue to post stat lines like he did in Carolina: one catch on two targets for zero yards, along with one rush for five yards.
Trautman and Engram were close in snap share, but the former had the edge by three. Still, Engram turned in one of his better statistical performances of the season, catching four of his five targets for 33 yards.
Adkins brought up the rear in snap share, but if the Broncos were smart, they'd start eating into Trautman's blocking snaps. Adkins is so much more effective, but the Broncos spent the money on Trautman this offseason, and they're intent on getting a return.
Beware the sunk-cost fallacy , Broncos. No team wins championships by stepping over a dollar to pick up a dime.
Allen was a beast in this game, though it wasn't fully reflected in the box score. He led in snap share and totaled the most pressures on Bryce Young, too (four). The Panthers went out of their way to run the ball away from Allen, but he still impacted the game.
Roach had another strong day, totaling two pressures and a half-sack. D.J. Jones held it down at nose tackle, while Sai'vion Jones was the fourth lineman to take the field, with Eyioma Uwazurike on IR, even though Jackson has more experience.
For the first time this season, the Broncos dressed Onyedim — their highest draft pick — and he didn't disappoint. The rookie not only forced a fumble but also finished as the Broncos' highest-graded run defender, per Pro Football Focus .
Given Denver's struggles against the run this season, if that's not a sign that Onyedim needs to play more, I don't know what is.
For the first time this season, we have a perfectly symetrical snap share between the starters and depth rushers. Bonitto and Cooper led with 40 snaps each, with Robinson and Tillman getting 26 snaps each.
Bonitto played well against the run and sealed the game late in the fourth quarter with a strip-sack on Young, recovering the fumble. Cooper notched his first sack action of the season, splitting one with the aforementioned Roach.
Robinson continues as force to be reckoned with, totaling three pressures. Tillman was better against the run, but it's a great four-man rotation, with Jonah Elliss still on IR.
Singleton played 100% of snaps, but he turned in one of his worst games of the season, despite being named the AFC Defensive Player of the Month on Thursday. He missed a couple of tackles, and his decision-making on his run fits was hit-and-miss.
I wish I could say that Strnad had a better game overall, finishing with five tackles (one fewer than Singleton), but I can't. He was targeted six times in coverage, allowing five completions for 43 yards.
Singleton allowed all three of his targets to be completed for 23 yards. Let's hope the bye does both linebackers some good.
Surtain played 100% of snaps in his second game back from injury. Alas, it was a far cry from the great game he had against Kansas City, giving up three completions on five coverage targets.
It only led to 16 yards, but one of those completions was a four-yard touchdown catch by Tetairoa McMillan. It looked as if PS2 may have been expecting help inside, as he played outside leverage, and gave McMillan a free release inside. Oops.
Bryce to T-Mac and it's not over yet in Charlotte DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AsmEct0FD7
Moss suffered a concussion early on, which is always a bummer, but it was especially disheartening, given how well he was playing to start the game. With Kris Abrams-Draine ruled out of this game, Barron was the only depth corner the Broncos felt comfortable playing (Sean Fresch Jr. is on the active roster now), and he had a terrible game.
Young went after Barron, targeting him a whopping 10 times and completing seven of them for 70 yards and a touchdown. Barron also had a pass-interference penalty in the end zone, which set up an ensuing touchdown.
It was definitely a setback for Barron, but his season overall has been encouraging. It's way too early to give up on the former first-round pick.
Sadly, McMillian's day at the office wasn't much better. He allowed completions on all five of his targets for 49 yards and was bullied in the run game.
McMillian did notch a sack, though, so it wasn't all bad for the Broncos' nickel corner.
With Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones ruled out , the Broncos did something a bit different this week. Instead of Rapp or Key getting the start, it was Skinner — a reward for his impactful play last week against Kansas City.
Alas, Skinner proved to be unequal to his opportunity. He allowed allowed both of his coverage targets to be completed for 36 yards and a touchdown, and he struggled in his run fits, though he finished third on the team with five tackles.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos won't be relying on Skinner to play starter snaps again, unless the injury bug again forces their hand. Rapp had a so-so day, with one completion for 20 yards allowed on his only coverage target, and four tackles.
Key made one of the plays of the day, though, picking off Young in the end zone to prevent the Panthers from going up by eight points late in the game. Payton had to challenge…

title: Jonathan Taylor's Price Tag Just Changed Again—And That's Big for Broncos
full_text:
Late last week, the Denver Broncos reportedly cooled on the prospect of trading for running back Jonathan Taylor .
When the Indianapolis Colts decided to ask for first-round value in exchange for Taylor, the Broncos backed away. At the start of last week, the Broncos were the odds-on favorites to land Taylor before the November 10 trade deadline, but they're no longer the frontrunners.
The New York Giants have leapfrogged the Broncos as the favorites, per Hard Rock Bet , and as of Monday afternoon, even the New England Patriots are rising as a top trade suitor. The odds rank the Giants, the Colts, the Broncos, and then the Minnesota Vikings as the teams Taylor is most likely to be on by Tuesday night.
That being said, the Colts may be shifting their asking price for Taylor in the face of the hard reality that giving up first-round value for a soon-to-be 28-year-old running back so close to the dreaded 2,000-carry milestone may be a bridge too far for interested teams. It is now believed that Indianapolis will accept the best available offer for Taylor.
That may re-pique the Broncos' interest. The best possible offer will, of course, be dictated by the demand for his services. The more teams that throw in an offer, the more likely the price is to rise.
Teams will likely stop short of a first-round pick, though, so it may come down to a second-rounder, plus some additional mid-to-late-round compensation. The San Francisco 49ers gave up a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers for running back Christian McCaffrey four years ago, but he was younger than Taylor is now and much farther away from the 2,000-carry milestone.
Still, a second-rounder plus a fourth- and, say, a fifth-round pick? I could see the Broncos being willing to part with such draft capital to acquire a difference-making running back of Taylor's caliber.
Again, though, it all depends on the market. The laws of supply and demand will factor in. With there being only one Jonathan Taylor, the supply is extremely limited, though a team like the Broncos could look at other potential backs around the league, like Tennessee's Tony Pollard or Baltimore's Derrick Henry.
I just don't expect any team to be willing to part with a first-round pick for Taylor. Never say never, though, as desperation can make teams do strange things, and that's especially true when backed up against a deadline.
Jonah Coleman has become the Broncos' bona fide RB1 . But to get the Broncos' run game out of the doldrums, the team can't expect the rookie to do it alone.
Coleman had 17 carries against the Panthers on Sunday, while  J.K. Dobbins got only four. The Broncos will continue to lean on Coleman, but he needs help .
Whether that comes in the form of the Broncos figuring out what's wrong with their blocking schemes over the bye week or whether it's a trade ahead of Tuesday's deadline remains to be seen. But last year serves as a cautionary tale for the Broncos when it comes to relying so heavily on a rookie running back down the stretch.
Coleman is far more suited to the RB1 responsibilities than RJ Harvey was last year, but the takeaway remains the same. And given that Coleman has already missed four weeks on injured reserve with an ankle injury, how much are the Broncos willing to tempt fate?
Because, after Tuesday at 2 p.m. MDT, the Broncos' options will be limited to guys who are available on the street. The trade window will have closed until the 2027 offseason.

title: Broncos Player Grades vs. Panthers: Bo Nix Is Starting to Turn a Corner
full_text:
The Denver Broncos pulled off another record-setting one-score victory by beating the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday.
It wasn’t a great performance, and the injuries the Broncos have suffered on defense definitely hurt . Thankfully, the Broncos are hitting their bye and will benefit from a two-week break.
Overall, the Broncos' offense did well against Carolina, despite some third-quarter struggles, but the defense acquitted itself well with timely takeaways and some big-time plays in crucial moments.
On defense, the grades reflect the high variance of individual play. The defensive grades also show how badly injuries hurt the Broncos in Carolina, with three of their four worst-graded players being backups.
Offensively, things were much better, and the Broncos got another good game overall from their offensive line and most of their skill players, with two of their three lowest-grade players barely below average (average being the 50-point starting spot).
With that said, let’s get to Week 9's player grades.
Adkins played only 18 snaps, but 13 of them were as a run blocker, where he excelled, just as he has for most of the season. It would be great to see Denver use and trust him more as a blocker at the position, and even tap into his underrated ability as a receiver, instead of consistently rolling out a tight end they overpaid.
The Broncos continue to fall prey to the sunk-cost fallacy over in Adam Trautman when starting Adkins, and playing more, would provide much better returns in the run game.
Now, Bonitto didn’t lead the team in pressures, but his impact was immense because of the attention the Panthers were forced to give him. He consistently pulled help to his side and still created pressure, muddying up the pocket.
While Bonitto typically has issues in the run game, he wasn’t one of the main culprits behind the Broncos' run-defense issues this week, and his strip-sack at the end of the fourth quarter sealed the victory.
It was great to see Nix come out and attack deep on the first two plays of the game. He dropped back 38 times, took one sack, and went 25-of-37 with an average depth of target of 8.1 yards.
Even after Nix threw an interception, which was a terrible decision against cover-2, he didn’t shrink back into his shell for the rest of the game. He licked his wounds, played it safe for a while, then came out swinging, leading back-to-back touchdown drives to retake the lead, and never relinquished it.
I wrote in last week's grades that Nix's confidence was clearly coming back; after this game, is there any further debate on the subject?
Allen had a monster game, and the Broncos' run-game issues were hardly on him. He wreaked havoc against the Panthers' offensive line and led the team with three pressures.
Allen's run defense was strong and mostly consistent, with the Panthers actively trying to work away from where he was lined up.
Strnad is the coverage backer for this defense, and he did quite well. He got away with being a little early on contact that could’ve drawn defensive pass interference (the no-call is the right call, but by the letter of the rule it could have been thrown), and that play led to a game-changing Devon Key interception. Strnad also did well against the run, though his lack of size at the second level was an issue.
Bolles actually led the Broncos in pressures allowed with three of them, but he made up for it in the running game, where he was the best run blocker on the offensive line, and it wasn’t even close. While it wasn’t perfect, Bolles's run-blocking play was darn near textbook.
Powers is getting a lot of heat for bad plays that weren’t even his fault. He allowed a single pressure in the passing game, and while he isn’t much of a mover in the run game, he is a technician and allowed a few good-sized runs because of his ability to seal his blocks.
It wasn’t perfect by any means, with a couple of plays he'd like to have back, but the Broncos' left guard turned in a good overall game.
It's a shame Moss suffered a concussion after 17 snaps, because he was playing well. He picked up a big stop and allowed only one of two targets to be caught for 11 yards, and he nearly made a great interception on his other target.
With Bryant back from injured reserve, Nix gets one of his safety blankets back. When things get muddy in the pocket, or Nix needs a reliable catch to move the ball, he has increasingly turned to Bryant, which helped him lead the Broncos in receiving yards against the Panthers.
When Moss exited the game, Bryce Young painted a target on Barron, and he hit the bullseye multiple times. Barron was targeted 11 times, allowing seven catches for 69 yards and a touchdown.
The touchdown Barron allowed could raise a lot of questions about his football IQ, as it seemed like he thought he was playing a high safety zone instead of a corner.
McMillian had a full box-score game with a sack, three stops, and his coverage numbers, but it was a mess. He allowed all six targets to be caught for 58 yards, and his tackling was an issue, with two missed tackles. His lack of size in the slot was something the Panthers intentionally attacked in both the pass and run game.
After a goal-line stop against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Broncos gave him more playing time, but this game showed why he is a depth piece. His downhill run fills were consistently off, and his coverage left him out of position far too often. He allowed both targets to be caught, and they went for 36 yards and a touchdown.
Engram had a few big receptions, including a 19-yard catch-and-run on a delayed tight end screen, but he finished with 33 yards. He isn’t dynamic with the ball in his hands, and his athleticism has dropped off, which hurts his ability to be a consistent mismatch weapon. Maybe that's why the Broncos called the Arizona Cardinals about Trey McBride .
If Mims can deliver consistent effort, he could be a good wide receiver and not just a gadget-type player. Alas, his effort remains a problem. When he's on the field and the ball isn’t going his way, it's obvious off the snap. There were a few times the Panthers' defense took advantage of Mims’s effort tells.
This wasn’t a terrible game for McGlinchey, as he allowed only one pressure in the passing game, but his run-blocking inconsistencies continue to be a problem. He struggled to contain defenders and generate push, and it's tough to watch because he's always been a better run blocker than a pass protector.

title: Sean Payton's Latest Comments Fuel Broncos Trade Deadline Intrigue
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 7-2 with some big decisions to make — and fast — before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
The Broncos have been linked to several players in the trade rumor mill over the past few weeks, including Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. However, the Cardinals shut down Denver's "ambitious" and "outrageous" McBride inquiry, per Adam Schefter .
But one thing the Colts and Cardinals have in common is a woeful sub-.500 record. The Cardinals began a rebuild earlier this year by letting quarterback Kyler Murray walk and hiring head coach Mike LaFleur, while the Colts are facing one as a new reality after firing GM Chris Ballard.
Both will need the draft assets to effectuate a rebuild, so never say never. What the Cardinals need is a true franchise quarterback, and trading McBride at the peak of his market value could provide them with the draft capital to land such a signal-caller.
With rumors flying left and right, Broncos head coach Sean Payton was asked about his plans after his team defeated the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday . Payton was asked point-blank whether the Broncos would be "active" ahead of the trade deadline.
"I mean, that's impossible to predict. We'll discuss what's out there, and I think we'll see what happens, but I like this team," Payton said.
"There's room for us to get better, but I like this team a lot. We just got to take advantage of the position we're sitting in right now."
It's no coincidence that Payton ended his post-game presser immediately after fielding that trade-deadline question. He's trying to avoid being put on the spot, perhaps because there's a lick or two of flame at the base of all this recent trade smoke.
However, Payton did acknowledge publicly that he and GM George Paton will "discuss what's out there." But they already know what's out there, for the most part. Sunday's slate of games may have changed the outlook somewhat for a few teams, but the far-below-.500 teams are still what they are, including the Colts and Cardinals.
If the Broncos are going to be anything this year, they'll be buyers, though it's worth mentioning that running back J.K. Dobbins's name has reportedly been "discussed" in trade talks over the last week. It's unclear whether that's due to the Broncos actively checking his trade market or teams calling to check on him.
I can't imagine it's the latter possibility, given how bad Dobbins has looked this season. He's a far cry from the back who boosted the Broncos' offense for 10 weeks last year before a Lisfranc injury ended his campaign.
Meanwhile, rookie running back Jonah Coleman has emerged as a bona fide difference-maker since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. As great as Coleman has been, the Broncos can't expect the rookie to carry the offense's entire rushing load coming out of the bye. He needs help.
Now, the Broncos expect to get RJ Harvey back after Week 12, but that's still a ways off, and he's more of a receiving weapon out of the backfield than a true runner who could help shoulder the between-the-tackles load. That being said, Payton is getting fed up with all the questions about running back roles and playing time.
"Yeah, Jonah did good. Those runners are going to be important," Payton said on Sunday. "I'm not going to answer running-back depth questions, and certainly our running backs are not going to sit in front of a 15-minute interview about their playing time."
If the Broncos viewed Week 9's game against the Panthers as a referendum on their run game or a deciding factor on whether to make a trade, it may have pushed Payton and company closer to pulling the trigger , because he wasn't happy with his team's ground attack in Carolina, finishing with just 82 yards and averaging 3.0 yards per attempt.
"J.K. played, Jonah played, RJ will be back here shortly, and I'm glad we got both of them," Payton said. "I didn't feel like we ran it particularly well with either of them, and it wasn't back-driven. It was ‘Oh, that was a Buffalo front.’ Like, it took us a minute. And now, we threw it better for chunk plays than we ran it, but we got the runs when we needed it later."
Yes, the Broncos got the runs they needed in the fourth quarter — from Coleman. The rookie had 17 carries against the Panthers to Dobbins's four. The writing is on the wall in the Broncos' running back room: Coleman is RB1.
And that's great. The best guy should be the top guy, and that's clearly been Coleman.
But as a rookie who has already been injured badly enough this season to spend four weeks on IR, how much do the Broncos really want to push their luck with Coleman's workload, especially after being forced to rely on Harvey in that way last year to frustratingly inconsistent results?
My education guess is that Payton and Paton will spend much of their time over the next 36 hours focused on and discussing trade targets. Paton will work the phones, but whether the Broncos are willing to pay Indy's asking price of a first-round value for Taylor remains to be seen.
Remember: the Broncos have made a first-round pick in just two of the past five drafts. That can catch up to a team in the long run, especially a rapidly aging squad like the Broncos.
I'd put the chances of the Broncos acquring a running back via trade before the deadline slightly above 50/50. Say 60/40.
As for trading for a tight end? 10/90. And if the Broncos do make a move, it should be for a tight end with a reliable run-blocking skill set.

title: Grading Lions NFL Trade Deadline: Did Brad Holmes Ruin 2026 Team?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions made one move before the NFL trade deadline.
On Monday, the Lions swung a deal to acquire defensive back Andre Cisco from the New York Jets. While the move is intriguing, many believed that an additional move could be coming to help fortify their defense in particular.
Ultimately, the Lions elected to stand pat aside from the Cisco trade and elected to not make another move before the 4 p.m. deadline on Tuesday. This came as something of a surprise given how active other teams in the mix were.
As the Lions look to make a push for a third NFC North title in four years and a return to the postseason, their relative inactivity at the deadline appears to be a vote of confidence in their roster along with the addition of Cisco.
Around them, the San Francisco 49ers, Minnesota Vikings, Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks were all active in making moves prior to the deadline. The 49ers added a defensive end in De'Forest Buckner, the Vikings added a quarterback in Kirk Cousins, the Bears brought in defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons and the Seahawks bolstered their offensive line with Quinten Nelson.
Now, the Lions will be tasked with running the divisional gauntlet with Cisco providing defensive depth. It will be interesting to see where Cisco fits within their secondary, as Brian Branch is back in the fold and Kerby Joseph is working toward a return.
Cisco has experience playing both as a box safety and a free safety, so he will provide valuable depth even if Joseph is able to return and play at a high level. Joseph won't play against New England in Week 10, meaning the Lions will have to activate him before their Week 11 game or elect to keep him on the Physically Unable to Perform list for the remainder of the season.
Detroit could also elect to activate Joseph and keep him as an inactive if they don't feel that he's able to play right away. Still, Cisco will give them some options even with Branch and veteran Chuck Clark both playing well.
The Lions didn't make the flashiest move at the deadline amongst their NFC counterparts, and these big trade deadline moves have mixed results over the past several seasons.
Additionally, the Lions have a need at the linebacker position after Jack Campbell suffered a significant injury. He leaves a big hole in terms of production as an All-Pro a season ago, and many believed the Lions could be looking to add a linebacker moving forward.
However, they elected not to and thus provided a vote of confidence in the likes of Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske.
Because of how valuable Campbell was to Detroit's defense, the Lions may wind up regretting not adding an option to the linebacker room.
It's hard to call the Lions' decisions at the deadline an abject failure. Their biggest need was the cornerback position, and there wasn't a single cornerback dealt at the deadline. Joey Porter Jr. was the only cornerback traded in season, while the others who were believed to be on the market ultimately remain with their current teams.
Because there wasn't a market for players at Detroit's biggest position of need, it appears as though the Lions made the right move holding on to their valuable draft capital. They were able to make an addition that will help them moving forward, but didn't make the level of splash that a team like the Bears did.
Ultimately, the roster as constructed has been good enough to win two divisional games amidst a 6-2 start. Their cards are now on the table, and it's up to Dan Campbell's team to prove their leadership right.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Detroit Lions Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions wore down and defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9. The Lions kept Malik Willis and the young Dolphins in check, advancing to a 6-2 record on the season.
At points, it was not the prettiest game, but the Lions were able to find a way to keep scoring points and keeping Miami out of scoring range.
Here is the good, bad, and ugly from the contest.
The Lions needed every one of their four field goals on Sunday, and Jake Bates was perfect on his attempts. It was a game where both defenses were delivering standout performances, and points were at a premium.
Fittingly, Bates, long snapper Hogan Hatten, and the unit were at max efficiency every time they were called upon.
The punting unit was not needed much, as they were not called upon in the second half. However, in two times they were called upon, they delivered. The first punt of the game for Jack Fox was a 54-yarder, and then he used his arm on the next time in punt formation, passing to Tay Martin for a first down on a fake punt.
Kelvin Sheppard and the Defense
Facing a Miami Dolphins offense with Malik Willis limited by a groin injury, the Lions were expected to win. However, Kelvin Sheppard’s defense delivered much more than expected, especially with two starting linebackers and both DJ Reed and DJ Wonnum out.
Sheppard’s unit only allowed nine points, all via a field goal. The longest Miami play from scrimmage came on a fake punt. Alim McNeill tallied a sack while rookie Derrick Moore added the first two of his young career. Aidan Hutchinson and Skyler Gill-Howard each forced holding penalties on plays. Undrafted rookie Anthony Lucas added a quarterback hit.
Chuck Clark tallied an interception. The corners held Willis to 125 yards passing on 25 attempts. It was a strong effort all around, with the entire unit playing for Jack Campbell. It is safe to say that the effort by Motown likely made Campbell smile.
In yet another week, the Lions passing offense fell flat . Jared Goff got sacked early along with throwing an interception. Considering Miami statistically has one of the worst teams in passing yards per play, it was a disappointing effort.
Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa combined for two catches for 40 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs was held without a catch for the first time since week four in 2024 and only the fourth time in his career. Sam LaPorta tallied four catches for 32 yards.
The only player producing at their expected level was Amon-Ra St. Brown, with the All-Pro having eight catches for 86 yards.
While the Lions did not need an All-Pro or MVP-level day from Jared Goff, it was not up to the early season standard that Goff has set.
The red zone offense was not ideal. In fact, the saving grace for this is that Jake Bates was perfect on his field goals. The Lions came away with one touchdown on four red zone attempts. If it was not for Sheppard’s defense playing the game of the season thus far, it could have been a much more embarrassing result for Motown.
The shorter fields enabled Miami to be more aggressive, and Drew Petzing had not answers. Even on their lone touchdown drive, the Lions were held to a fourth down, where a well-called fake dive and pitch to Jahmyr Gibbs got a touchdown.
It was not a day to remember in the Miami sun for the offensive line. They gave up three sacks in the first 17 minutes of game action, alongside seeing Miles Frazier whistled for a hold and a false start. First round pick Blake Miller was also whistled for a false start of his own.
Frazier was given a start after Christian Mahogany had violated team rules , and the Dolphins attacked the LSU product. Frazier gave up multiple run stuffs on a two-penalty day.
While the line regained momentum late, pushing for first downs to drain the clock, multiple red zone failures fall on the line not having solid days. In the end, the defense saved the offense and the Lions organization from an embarrassing loss to the one-win Dolphins.

title: Detroit Lions Stand Pat on 2026 Trade Deadline Day
full_text:
The Detroit Lions elected not to make another move on trade deadline day after making one the day prior.
As a result, the Lions will enter the stretch run of their season with one trade made, that being to acquire New York Jets safety Andre Cisco on Monday . To land Cisco, the Lions parted ways with a 2028 sixth-round pick.
However, with Tuesday being the final day for teams to make trades, the Lions did not add another option to the roster. Though there were intriguing options thought to be available, the Lions ultimately did not make any more moves beyond adding Cisco.
The Lions were viewed as a team that may need defensive reinforcements based on the fact that they were without several starters in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum all did not play, and while Campbell is the only one of the three on injured reserve, the depth they have defensively would've benefitted from a re-stock. However, it was not to be as the Lions stood pat.
Detroit has a tough stretch upcoming, starting with a trip to Munich to take on the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots. After that, they will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before playing the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving as part of a stretch that includes three games in 11 days.
Currently, the Lions sit in second-place in the NFC North behind the Bears. All four of the NFC North teams currently are in the playoff picture, as all four have winning records and are at least three games above the .500 mark.
The Bears and Vikings both made moves at the deadline. Chicago made a splash by trading multiple picks to the Tennessee Titans for defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons, while the Vikings made a move to reunite with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins.
Detroit's season will be defined by their performance in their four-game stretch to end the year. They will play at Minnesota in Week 15, then finish the year with road games at Chicago and Green Bay after hosting the New York Giants in Week 16.

title: Lions 2026 Midseason Rookie Report Sees DL Ascend Up Depth Chart Quickly
full_text:
With the NFL calendar turning to Week 10, we are beyond the midpoint of the 2026 season.
The Detroit Lions have now had eight games to evaluate their rookie class, with several of their players playing prominent roles in that timeframe. While they still have nine games remaining, meaning their season isn’t quite at its midpoint due to their Week 6 bye, with the NFL season reaching its halfway point it’s time to take a look at the group’s performance.
Here’s an updated look at how Detroit’s rookie class has fared throughout the first eight games of the 2026 NFL season.
Miller has started in all seven of the games he’s appeared in, as he missed the Lions’ Week 2 game against Buffalo with an ankle injury. Thus far, he’s been better in pass protection than as a run blocker. He ranks 23rd among all tackles in Pro Football Focus’ pass-blocking grade, while he’s 73rd in run-blocking.
Relative to his fellow rookies, he ranks first among first-year tackles who have played at least 93 snaps this year in pass-blocking grade but seventh in run-blocking.
It has been somewhat up-and-down at times, most recently with the Lions’ Week 9 win over Miami. He struggled against Chop Robinson, and was called for holding for the first time in his young career in that game.
Overall, Miller has outperformed his rookie counterparts as a pass-blocker opposite one of the game’s best in Penei Sewell, and continues to show growth in the run game.
Moore may have had his breakthrough on Sunday. After a slow start to the season where he played a marginal role at best, an injury to DJ Wonnum opened up a legitimate opportunity for him and he made the most of it.
The Michigan product racked up two sacks against Miami on Sunday, the first two of his career. While Wonnum has also played very well and is expected to return to his starting role upon being healthy, Moore proved himself worthy of another opportunity.
He’s been utilized mostly as a rush end throughout the start of the season, providing pop on passing downs. In his extended role Sunday, he showed that he can set an edge against the run as well. It was a promising showing after a very quiet start to the season.
Injuries have been unfortunately a theme for Rolder in his rookie season. He missed most of training camp with a hamstring injury, and his absence bled over to the start of the season as he was inactive for the first two games.
He debuted in Week 3, and had played a small role on defense in Week 4. Then, he got chances after the team’s bye week to help out in a rotational capacity. He logged his first career sack as well as two tackles for loss in the win over Minnesota by the time the fourth quarter rolled around.
Unfortunately for Rolder, he suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in that fourth quarter that may require surgery. It was an abrupt end to a solid stretch of football for him since the bye week.
The Lions have utilized Abney in multiple ways already this year. For much of training camp and into the start of the regular season, he was a backup cornerback with the ability to contribute as the nickel.
After Avonte Maddox suffered a season-ending injury, things changed for Abney. He began to take on more work at the safety position, eventually earning his first start there in Week 5. In that game, a win over the Cardinals, he recorded his first career interception.
Time will tell what Abney’s role is moving forward, as Brian Branch has returned and Kerby Joseph is on his way to coming back as well. Add in the fact that Chuck Clark has played well, and it could be challenging for Abney to get snaps at safety.
At the worst, though, Abney will serve as a super sub with the ability to play boundary corner, nickel and safety moving forward.
Law is out for the season with a torn ACL suffered in offseason workouts. Based on the timing of the injury and recovery, he should be able to participate in training camp next season.
Gill-Howard has been one of the biggest surprises up to this point in the season. He has taken to the role assigned to him very well, as he has been one of the most productive rookie pass-rushers through the midway point of the season.
The Texas Tech product has earned a significant amount of snaps due to his athleticism and ability to win off the line of scrimmage. He and Tyleik Williams, Detroit’s run-stuffing first-round pick in 2025, compliment each other nicely.
Gill-Howard ranks first amongst all rookie interior defensive linemen in pressures, and sixth amongst all rookies in general. His pass-rush win rate is tied-for-fifth at 6.7 percent. He’ll continue to be a big part of Detroit’s defense moving forward.
We've even see Gill-Howard play some on offense, as the Lions have utilized him as a fullback or extra tight end throughout multiple games this year.
O’Neill has remained on Detroit’s roster as an undrafted free agent out of Rutgers, and has carved out a nice role. He is among the leaders in special teams snaps played, and has also mixed in some work on defense.
He has earned a 58.3 PFF defensive grade on his 16 defensive snaps played, 11 of which have been pass-rush snaps. O’Neill has been very solid on special teams, as he’s made seven solo tackles in that phase of the game.
Lucas made his NFL debut Sunday as a practice squad elevation with Wonnum sidelined. He wound up playing 12 snaps, with nine coming as a pass-rusher, and recorded one pressure.
Detroit’s willingness to utilize him as an elevation over Ahmed Hassanein shows that he has impressed the coaching staff. He seems to be an option Detroit is confident in should there be an injury moving forward.

title: Detroit Lions Playoff Standings Improve With Vikings Loss
full_text:
The Detroit Lions remain in the mix for the NFC North division title.
After a win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, the team is now 6-2 and winners of four straight games. This stretch of winning has included two wins over divisonal opponents, those being the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings in Weeks 7 and 8.
The North remains the only team in the league where all teams have a winning record. Up to this point, the AFC North had also been in the running with all four teams being at least .500, but the Baltimore Ravens lost this week to fall to 4-5 on the year.
The Lions are the only team in the NFC North that is unbeaten in the division. They've won both their divisional games, while Minnesota has wins over Chicago and Green Bay but a loss to Detroit.
Green Bay beat Chicago but has lost to Minnesota and Detroit, while Chicago is winless in the division with a Thanksgiving game against Detroit looming.
It has been a historic start to the season for the division, as all four teams have at least six wins through the first nine weeks of the season.
Despite all the success within the division, the leader of the pack is still not the top team in the NFC. With the Vikings' loss to Buffalo, the San Francisco 49ers are the top seed in the NFC with a 7-1 record.
Elsewhere, the NFC East and South divisions are led by the New York Giants (5-2-1) and Carolina Panthers (3-5). The Wild Card race figures to be a battle between five teams, the three that don't win the NFC North, and a pair of 5-4 NFC West teams in the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks.
As almost the antithesis of the NFC North , the NFC South has four teams that all have three wins. The Carolina Panthers currently lead the pack thanks to their head-to-head win over New Orleans with both teams being 3-5. Meanwhile, the Buccaneers and Falcons both haven't had their bye weeks and as a result are 3-6.
Aside from those five, there is just one other NFC team with at least four wins, that being the Dallas Cowboys. With the team in the 7th and final playoff spot currently at 6-3, it will be an uphill climb for any team with three or fewer wins to get back into the mix.

title: Some In Detroit Lions Building Said Jack Campbell Could Return in 2026
full_text:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has captivated the hearts and minds of supporters, his teammates and the coaching staff.
Since Campbell suffered a serious injury at Ford Field against the Minnesota Vikings, many have wondered about his playing future. The team made decision this week to place him on the injured reserve list, meaning he must miss the next four games.
During a recent appearance on The Jim Rome Show, NFL reporter Mike Silver dropped an interesting bit of information regarding the playing future of the former first-round draft pick.
"Well Jim, it is more positive than I would have expected, based on the lack of information we were getting after the initial injury, which is not a good sign," said Silver. "Jack Campbell issued that statement last week saying he had full movement in his lower extremities, and was regaining movement in his upper extremities, or it was improving. There are people in that building who are even saying he could come back this year.
"I have no idea if that is just emotion talking. Obviously, the doctors and Jack and his family are going to be very, very careful about what goes down. But in the meantime, wow, they are feeling him ..."
Quarterback Jared Goff was asked following Detroit's 19-9 victory against the Vikings about the emotion of the game and how the team handled it throughout the week of preparation.
“Yeah, I think all week, certainly early in the week, it was really hard to kind of get your mind back into what we have to do, and certainly for those guys on defense , he's their nucleus," said Goff. "To be able to come back to work and work the way they did and then play the way they did and us as a team kind of rallying around each other and leaning on each other a little bit and yeah, it was hard. It was hard, but I think as the week went on, you start to think about what would he want, how would he want us to play?
"He wouldn't even want us talking about him right now. He wouldn't want us doing all this stuff about how we're going to play for him. He wouldn't want any of that, but he's a special guy to us and it means a lot.”

title: Grading Detroit Lions Trade: How Quickly Can Andre Cisco Help Defense?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have acquired help for their secondary.
On Monday, the team traded a 2028 sixth-round pick to the New York Jets in exchange for safety Andre Cisco. The veteran, formerly a 2021 third-round pick of the Jacksonville Jaguars, is on an expiring contract.
At first glance, this trade is one of value for Detroit . They surrender a pick in a future draft as opposed to the upcoming one to acquire a veteran with legitimate productive experience. Cisco has been a role player for New York this year, with four starts in nine games, but has 59 career starts under his belt.
This year, Cisco has been behind Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick for most of the season, and could be in a better opportunity in Detroit at least for the short-term. Last year, he started all eight of his games played but suffered a torn pec that ended his season.
The Lions saw Cisco in Week 3, when they defeated the Jets 31-24. In that game, Cisco recorded a sack amidst six total tackles in 65 snaps played. Since that game, his role has diminished as he has played a total of 22 defensive snaps in the last six games.
Cisco also has some familiarity with a member of the Lions' coaching staff. Current cornerbacks coach Deshea Townsend was on the Jaguars' coaching staff as a cornerbacks coach and passing game coordinator from 2022-23, when Cisco was a starting safety on the team.
He will also come to Detroit with an inherent understanding of the scheme, as the Lions' philosophy under defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is heavily influenced by former coordinator and current Jets head coach Aaron Glenn.
This trade is intriguing for Detroit, as their biggest need ahead of the deadline was thought to be the cornerback position. While the secondary as a whole has struggled at points this year, the issues appeared to lie predominantly with the cornerbacks on roster.
The Lions were depleted at the safety position earlier in the year, but appear to be getting healthier. Avonte Maddox is out for the year, but Brian Branch has played in three games since returning from the Physically Unable to Perform list, while Kerby Joseph is in his second full week of practices and could be activated at some point over the next two weeks.
Even Thomas Harper, who has been out since suffering an injury leading up to Week 3, could be on track to return in short order. Because of this, plus the performances of Chuck Clark and rookie Keith Abney II, adding another safety seems somewhat puzzling on the surface.
This move could be an indicator that the Lions plan to ease Joseph into his return and play him rotationally.
Detroit could also see Cisco as a potential option for the nickel cornerback spot, where he has had limited experience throughout his career. He has played just six snaps in that role this year, according to Pro Football Focus.
One other option the Lions could consider is utilizing Cisco as a sub linebacker in certain defensive packages. Because he has experience as a box safety, he could pair nicely with the tandem of Branch and Clark, or Joseph when he returns.
Cisco can also cover well and has range, so he provides Kelvin Sheppard with some flexibility within the scheme.
As far as timeline is concerned, the Lions could get him involved in practice starting Wednesday with the plan to get him ready for this week's game. However, the Jets don't have their bye until Week 13, so if he were to play every game with Detroit he would log 18 games this season.
Detroit also has a trip to Germany to play the New England Patriots this week, and as a result he may not suit up for them until next week when they play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers if Dan Campbell doesn't want to rush him into action.
While Cisco isn't a flashy name, he fits the mold of players the Lions have targeted through trades in the past. However, his presence creates a sort of log-jam at the safety position when everyone is healthy.
The Lions still have a need for a cornerback, or perhaps a linebacker with Jack Campbell being out. It's a decent, low-risk move to acquire help for the secondary, but it isn't the complete answer to Detroit's defensive struggles.
