title: Keenan Allen Trade Opens Door for More Colts Moves Before Deadline
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have made their third midseason move ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline , sending wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick.
The #49ers are adding a WR, completing a trade for #Colts WR Keenan Allen, per me and @AdamSchefter . Another pass-catcher for Brock Purdy. pic.twitter.com/TyOvlKVAaV
Allen's departure marks another development in what has become a significant roster reset for Indianapolis, which has already parted ways with All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
With the Colts continuing to prioritize future assets over immediate production, Tuesday's trade could open the door for additional moves before the 4 p.m. ET deadline.
When Indianapolis signed Allen to a one-year contract in August, the veteran was expected to be an important addition to an already promising offense. Following Alec Pierce's offseason ankle injury, the Colts needed another established receiving option to supplement the depth chart
Allen got off to a relatively slow start in Indianapolis, but he eventually established a strong connection with Jones. His 40 receptions led the team and his 351 receiving yards is just three behind Josh Downs for the team lead.
Allen also continued climbing the NFL's all-time receiving leaderboards, finishing his Colts tenure with 1,095 career receptions, good enough for eighth all-time.
However, with Indianapolis shifting its attention toward the future, moving a 34-year-old receiver on an expiring contract makes sense. The sixth-round pick gives the Colts something in return for a player who otherwise could have departed in free agency this offseason.
For San Francisco, the move addresses an immediate need. The 49ers have dealt with significant injuries throughout their receiving corps and are making another push toward a Super Bowl. Allen's experience, route-running ability and reliability should give Brock Purdy another dependable option as the team enters the second half of the season.
The six-time Pro Bowler also gets an opportunity to return to the West Coast and join a legitimate contender.
With Allen now out of the picture, several other Colts players could attract interest before the deadline.
Josh Downs remains one of the most realistic candidates after requesting a trade. However, with Allen gone, the Colts' already thin receiving corps could make them more reluctant to move Downs without an appealing return.
Grover Stewart is another name to monitor. The 33-year-old is playing on an expiring contract and has reportedly generated interest from contending teams looking to bolster their defensive line depth. Indianapolis has maintained a relatively high asking price, though, which could slow negotiations.
Daniel Jones' situation is worth revisiting after Indianapolis initially informed him he would not be traded. The Minnesota Vikings are searching for quarterback help, which could potentially put Jones back on its radar. Financially though, the Colts would benefit from keeping Jones through the season and pursuing an offseason release, which could generate substantially more cap savings than moving him immediately.
The belief around the NFL is the #Vikings will attempt to trade for a QB today as another option to have for this season before the 4 pm ET deadline. “They won’t sit still,” a source said. “They can’t.” https://t.co/SAPIWX9RRi pic.twitter.com/7FBUZWoZx9
Then there's Jonathan Taylor. The biggest potential blockbuster remains the least likely of the four. Indianapolis has fielded considerable interest in its star running back but has maintained a significant asking price, reportedly not accepting an offer from the New York Giants which included a second and fifth-round pick. The Colts reportedly view Taylor as part of their future, even though he's the most valuable trade asset they have left.
The #Giants offered the #Colts a 2nd- and 5th-round pick for RB Jonathan Taylor, but that offer has since been pulled, per @JayGlazer . pic.twitter.com/oim2SyLcuR
Allen's departure doesn't guarantee another trade, but it does kick the tires on a revived fire sale in Indianapolis. With the deadline rapidly approaching, the Colts likely aren't done dealing just yet.

title: Jonathan Taylor Sweepstakes Tracker: Colts Analysis, Trade Rumors, and More
full_text:
Unfortunately for Indianapolis Colts fans, Jonathan Taylor and trade request are two terms that have been used together in a sentence before.
Back in 2023, the Colts' prolific running back requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts amid ongoing contract disputes. Taylor infamously showed up to practice in a black hoodie during his subsequent hold-in, signifying the trying times of a franchise that was entering its first season with then-rookie Anthony Richardson at quarterback.
Following the reporting of Taylor's trade request, former longtime Owner Jim Irsay made sure the league knew he was going to do whatever it takes to keep the star rusher around for the then-rebuild, which was really more of a slight re-tooling, a more conventional dart throw, but I digress.
“We’re not trading Jonathan [Taylor]... end of discussion,” Irsay said in a text to Sports Illustrated ’s Albert Breer . “Not now and not in October!”
And as fate would have it, the Colts would up re-signing Jonathan Taylor in October to a three-year $42 million contract extension, which included $26.5 million in guaranteed payments.
But just three years later, the star running back is back at the center of trade talks.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline at 4 PM EST on November 10th is quickly approaching, and it's become increasingly likely that Jonathan Taylor has played his last snap as a member of the Indianapolis Colts.
We're breaking down everything we know about the state of the sweepstakes in question, and will update this article as new information presents itself.
Without further ado, let's dive into how we got here, which teams are reportedly interested in Jonathan Taylor's services and what they're offering.
Despite loud rumors and an ongoing fire sale suggesting otherwise, Taylor has not requested a trade.
In all honesty, it feels and looks like Taylor is one of the few remaining longtime veterans on the Colts roster who genuinely still wants to be in Indianapolis.
Earlier in the offseason, Taylor signed a two-year extension to stay in Indianapolis through the 2028 season. Taylor said he wanted to remain a Colt for life before the extension, hinting toward the goal of a long-term deal, but he and the Colts found a solution that satisfied both parties.
Chris Ballard was already on the hottest seat in general manager history as he entered the final year of his deal, and the Colts didn't want to fully commit to another era under his rule.
And it was smart to think that way, considering we are wrapping up Week 8 and Ballard has been out of the building for two weeks now. Along with him went longtime franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and all eyes have been on Jonathan Taylor ever since.
Mere months after committing to stay in Indianapolis for the next three seasons, Taylor appears to be on his way out.
In his first game without Quenton Nelson leading the way, Taylor rushed for just 23 yards on eight carries. The Colts failed to establish any sort of rushing attack against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and Taylor saw just five carries come his way in the first half.
After the game, Taylor appeared to be rather emotional and was giving multiple teammates and coaches hugs. Sure, it could've just been a lot to take in, or perhaps I am looking too far into it, but it truly felt like this was the last we've seen of Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis.
Couple this with the fact that ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween, the day prior, that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Taylor and have been active in talks, and it seems like he's as good as gone.
Schefter also reported that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick, along with additional compensation, for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package, or at least the one Indianapolis is seeking, is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Taylor doesn't quite warrant the first-round consideration as a pure rusher who is a subpar back in the passing game, though he does have an argument.
Regardless of his flaws as a third-down back, Taylor's ability as a true rusher is nearly unmatched. He remains at the top of his game at 27 years old, is durable, and carries a favorable contract for the next two seasons.
The Colts already paid Taylor his $15 million signing bonus before the season, so a potential suitor would only be on the hook for $15 milllion in 2027 and $9.46 million in 2028.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help the next regime's outlook tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league.
According to Schefter, the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
Per Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, the New York Giants appear to be all-in on Taylor, but it must be at the right price.
"The Giants are one of those teams, and they are very interested. They view Jonathan Taylor as being on par with Derrick Henry in that second tier, just below the best running backs in the NFL. The general concern at this point, though, is that the Colts want too much," Florio said following Week 8's Sunday slate .
“One source with one of the teams currently in the mix with Taylor puts it at 50-50 as to whether it gets done before the trade deadline."
Furthermore, Denver Broncos beat reporter, The DNVR's Zac Stevens, said that he feels the Broncos are truly all-in on Taylor.
"I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor...." Stevens said in a postgame reaction piece on the DNVR Broncos Podcast. "The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now."
That wraps up just about everything we're aware of as of Monday, November 2nd. Be sure to check back in for any updates regarding the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
Here’s everything I know about the #Colts ’ trade talks involving RB Jonathan Taylor, WR Josh Downs, DT Grover Stewart and other players, including which teams are interested and why Indianapolis is trading players away. Discussed with @Realrclark25 on #ThePivot : https://t.co/ZANCGWaIE2 pic.twitter.com/h2YyOt9mb3
"My understanding is that 5-6 teams have been aggressively pursuing him: Giants, Packers, Broncos, Seahawks, Bengals, Vikings," Schultz said on The Pivot .
"I think it'll take at least a second-round plus additional compensation to get it done, and I actually do expect that to happen."
The aforementioned Christian McCaffrey blockbuster haul remains the ideal return for the Indianapolis Colts.
ESPN NFL Insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano reiterated this morning that the Indianapolis Colts are still open to trading…

title: Colts Position Grades: Young Defense Shows Life in Week 9 Loss
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have now lost five straight games, falling 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys in another disappointing showing at Lucas Oil Stadium.
In a surprising twist, the defense actually looked serviceable on Sunday. The offense? Not so much.
What's frustrating is watching these young defenders finally step up while the franchise is being torn apart, largely because of how poorly this defense has performed.
But once again, Indianapolis walks away with another loss, falling to 2-7.
Here are my position grades from Week 9.
Daniel Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, one touchdown, and an interception. But his 15.4 QBR tells the real story.
Jones earned a team-low 36.7 offensive grade, per Pro Football Focus. Interestingly, he graded significantly better against the blitz (69.6) than without it (30.4).
I'm going to defend Jones here. He's never been a quarterback who can consistently elevate a struggling supporting cast, but give him weapons, a rushing attack, and decent defense, and he can win games.
Unfortunately, Indianapolis just traded away one of the best offensive linemen this franchise has ever drafted.
This is the season from hell, and Jones isn't the biggest problem. But he certainly didn't play well Sunday.
Something looks off with Jonathan Taylor.
JT managed just 46 yards on 13 carries and lost a costly fumble. Meanwhile, rookie Seth McGowan continues to impress, rushing for 45 yards and a touchdown on six attempts.
Both were effective in pass protection, but Taylor needs a resurgence. Maybe Tuesday's trade deadline will finally quiet the noise surrounding him.
Where is the separation? This unit combined for 121 total receiving yards.
Ashton Dulin provided the lone explosive play, turning a screen into a 55-yard touchdown. Otherwise, this receiving corps was painfully average.
With Alec Pierce eventually returning, this group still has potential. But right now, nobody is consistently stepping up.
Tyler Warren continues working his way back from injury, hauling in four passes for 44 yards.
The entire group contributed in pass protection, and while the others weren't involved much offensively, tight end was far from the problem.
Surprisingly, this unit wasn't terrible.
Indianapolis allowed two sacks and roughly 10 pressures, with respectable performances in both pass protection and run blocking.
Not dominant, but certainly not the reason Indianapolis lost.
The Colts generated three sacks and consistent pressure on Dak Prescott, but the run defense remains a problem.
Javonte Williams rushed for 101 yards, while Dallas totaled approximately 179 on the ground.
The pressure was encouraging. The inability to stop the run wasn't.
Bryce Boettcher and C.J. Allen are finally finding their footing.
The young duo combined for 22 tackles, providing some much-needed consistency in the middle of this defense.
Neither was spectacular, but both continue showing why they deserve opportunities moving forward.
Dallas threw for 335 yards, and CeeDee Lamb absolutely torched this secondary.
Sauce Gardner held up relatively well early before surrendering a critical 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy.
This was a bend-don't-break performance, but allowing that much production through the air isn't acceptable.
Cam Bynum delivered one of his better performances, earning the team's second-highest coverage grade.
Meanwhile, Hunter Wohler led Indianapolis with an incredible 16 tackles.
The young safety is making the most of his opportunity, and this group was one of Sunday's brighter spots.
Spencer Shrader is officially back.
The Colts kicker drilled all three field goals, including bombs from 59 and 50 yards.
Rigoberto Sanchez was reliable, kickoff coverage improved, and Anthony Gould and Seth McGowan provided encouraging returns.
The most frustrating part of Sunday's loss wasn't even the final score. It was watching a defense that has been historically bad at times finally show signs of life, only for the offense to completely disappear.
Indianapolis has now lost five straight, and with Tuesday's trade deadline approaching, this roster could look even worse by next Sunday.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Week 9 Stock Report: Rookies Shine Despite Fifth Straight Loss to Cowboys
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts suffered their fifth consecutive loss on Sunday, falling 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys to drop to 2-7 on the season. Despite another disappointing result, several young players continued to show encouraging signs, while others had performances they'd like to put behind them.
Here's a look at whose stock is trending up and whose is heading in the opposite direction following Week 9.
Caden Curry continues to make the most of the extra opportunities he's earned in the last two weeks.
Curry recorded his first pro sack and recovered a fumble against Dallas, becoming the first Colts rookie to record a sack and fumble recovery in the same game since Josh Mallard in 2002. His ability to consistently make plays around the football has been an encouraging development for a defense searching for reliable contributors.
Curry has proven to be an excellent find in the seventh round of last year's draft as he's beginning to establish himself as a player worth giving more runway too the rest of the season.
Fellow rookie defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau also turned in an impressive performance against Dallas.
Tuimoloau also recorded his first career sack and generated four pressures, continuing what has been an encouraging stretch for the second-year pass rusher. Tuimoloau has steadily worked his way into the defensive line rotation and is beginning to show why Indianapolis invested a second-round pick in him, even if results weren't immediate.
With the Colts potentially giving more opportunities to their younger players down the stretch, Tuimoloau has an opportunity to build on his recent progress.
Seth McGowan rushed for 45 yards on just six attempts, averaging 7.5 yards per carry while scoring his first career NFL touchdown, building on what is turning into an impressive rookie campaign.
His 36-yard run was the longest rushing play of the afternoon for Indianapolis and demonstrated the explosiveness he can bring to the backfield. With Jonathan Taylor's future in Indianapolis increasingly uncertain with the trade deadline on the horizon, McGowan could have an opportunity to step into a much larger role. His performance was an encouraging development for the Colts' future at running back, regardless of if Taylor is a part of that future.
CJ Allen is making a strong impression after stepping into a larger role in the Colts' linebacker corps. The rookie followed up his first NFL start with a second straight game with double-digit tackle numbers.
Allen has demonstrated an encouraging level of confidence and awareness despite being thrown into a difficult situation. Even in a defense which has struggled throughout this season, Allen's presence is clearly felt when he's on the field. His ability to contribute immediately is particularly important for a defense that has dealt with injuries and significant personnel changes. Indianapolis could have an important building block in its young linebacker.
Jonathan Taylor endured a difficult afternoon. The veteran running back finished with 46 rushing yards on 13 attempts, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, while also losing a key fumble late in the game.
Although Indianapolis' offensive line deserves some responsibility for the team's recent rushing struggles, Taylor hasn't been able to consistently generate the production expected of him. His future is also becoming an increasingly prominent storyline with Tuesday's trade deadline approaching. If Sunday's performance was his final appearance in Indianapolis, it wasn't the finish anyone envisioned.
Bernhard Raimann had an unusually difficult afternoon against Dallas. Indy's $100-million left tackle committed three penalties that contributed to several frustrating offensive sequences. One illegal formation penalty erased an eight-yard completion to Deion Burks on third down, while a fourth-quarter holding penalty turned a manageable third-and-six into a much more difficult third-and-16.
Raimann has established himself as an important piece of the offensive line, but Sunday's performance was a step in the wrong direction for the veteran tackle.
Josh Downs had a particularly disappointing afternoon against Dallas, finishing with three receptions for 24 yards on six targets. More concerning were his two drops, including a critical third-down opportunity late in the fourth quarter that forced Indianapolis to settle for a field goal.
The Colts needed their receivers to make plays in a close game, and Downs failed to deliver when his team needed him most.
Downs' ongoing trade situation has also added another layer of uncertainty to his future in Indianapolis. With the deadline approaching, his stock has taken a hit at an unfortunate time .

title: Colts Trade Candidates Did Themselves No Favors Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts entered Sunday's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys with two of the NFL's most notable trade candidates still on their roster.
With the Nov. 10 deadline approaching, the organization had one final opportunity to evaluate its options and potentially strengthen its negotiating position before the 4 p.m. EST cutoff.
However, Sunday's performances for some notable trade targets did little to help their respective trade cases. Both players entered the week amid considerable speculation about their futures in Indianapolis, but neither gave interested teams much reason to increase their offers.
Josh Downs had an opportunity to make a positive impression on potential suitors Sunday, but his performance against the Cowboys did little to accomplish that.
Downs finished with just three receptions for 24 yards on six targets, while dropping two passes on third down that could have helped extend drives.
The struggles are becoming increasingly difficult to overlook, particularly given the circumstances surrounding his future in Indianapolis. Since his trade request became public, Downs has appeared to be mentally elsewhere, and his recent performances have done little to suggest he's fully focused on helping the Colts turn their season around.
The two games since his trade request became public have produced just seven catches for 47 yards and one touchdown. While Downs has continued to receive opportunities in the offense, he hasn't done much with them. His inability to consistently create production has become an increasingly difficult problem for a player attempting to demonstrate his value to potential new teams.
To his credit, Downs didn't shy away from his mistakes after Sunday's loss.
"I stunk today," Downs admitted. He also pushed back on the suggestion that the trade situation had distracted him, insisting he had practiced well throughout the week and was focused on his responsibilities.
#Colts WR Josh Downs, asked if his trade request weighed on his performance: “I don’t really have an answer for that. …” Asked if he expects to be in Indy after the trade deadline: “I’m not worried about that right now. I got some things I gotta fix …” @TheAthleticNFL pic.twitter.com/jR4AdF4dfz
Still, the optics aren't good. Downs has appeared increasingly disconnected from the team's situation since his trade request became public, and his latest performance only adds to the perception that a change of scenery might be best for both sides.
That doesn't necessarily mean his trade value has disappeared. Downs is still a young receiver with established NFL experience and a skill set that could appeal to teams looking for help in the slot. However, Indianapolis reportedly initially sought a third-round selection before informing interested teams that it had received an offer in the fourth-round range.
For a receiver hoping to attract a stronger return, Sunday's performance was hardly encouraging. Between his declining production, the two costly drops and the uncertainty surrounding his future, Downs hasn't done himself many favors heading into Tuesday.
Taylor has arguably been the biggest name on the NFL's trade market over the past several weeks, with multiple contenders reportedly exploring the possibility of acquiring the Colts' superstar. Following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard and the subsequent trades of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Taylor emerged as one of the most attractive potential additions available ahead of the trade deadline due to how valuable he could be to a team looking to contend for a Super Bowl.
The Colts reportedly sought a first-round selection or a package comparable to what the Carolina Panthers received for Christian McCaffrey in 2022. The New York Giants were among the teams showing significant interest, reportedly offering a 2027 second- and fifth-round pick before ultimately pulling that offer off the table. With Indianapolis unwilling to settle for less than its desired return, Taylor's future has remained one of the biggest unanswered questions heading into the deadline.
Unfortunately, his performance against Dallas didn't exactly strengthen the Colts' negotiating position. Taylor finished with just 13 carries for 46 yards, averaging 3.5 yards per attempt, while adding five receptions for 18 yards. His most costly mistake came early in the fourth quarter when he fumbled near the Cowboys' 20-yard line, eliminating a prime opportunity for Indianapolis to take the lead.
The disappointing outing continued a recent decline in production for Taylor. He's rushed for just 258 yards over his last four appearances, averaging 4.3 yards per carry without recording a 100-yard performance. He's also now gone 16 consecutive games without reaching the century mark on the ground, an unusually lengthy drought for a player who has established himself among the league's premier backs.
Taylor has maintained that the trade speculation hasn't affected his preparation, emphasizing throughout the week that his focus remained on helping Indianapolis win. However, following Sunday's loss, he acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding his future when asked whether he had played his final game with the Colts.
"I'm not sure. I know as much as you," Taylor said. "If it is (my last game with the Colts), I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."
Taylor also accepted responsibility for his costly fumble, explaining that he needed to do a better job securing the football regardless of the circumstances.
"No matter what happens, I gotta make sure if it touches my body, if it touches my hands, I gotta try to clamp down on it immediately," Taylor said.
There's little question that Taylor remains an attractive option for teams looking to strengthen their backfields for a postseason run. He's still just 27 years old, has eight rushing touchdowns this season and is under contract through 2028 after signing a two-year, $44 million extension in August.
However, his recent production and ball-security issues haven't necessarily given interested teams additional incentive to meet Indianapolis' asking price.
For a player who has been the face of the trade deadline this season, Sunday's performance was an unfortunate opportunity missed. Taylor hasn't erased the value he's established throughout his career, but he didn't do much to justify an already ambitious asking price.
The Colts have less than 48 hours to determine how they want to proceed with the remainder of their roster. Indianapolis has already informed interested teams that Daniel Jones will not be traded, but the futures of Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs remain uncertain as negotiations appear to have stalled .
Despite the amount of speculation surrounding potential deadline activity, ESPN's Stephen Holder reported Sunday that the next few days could be relatively uneventful for the organization.
According to Holder, a source believes the deadline is "pretty likely to be anticlimactic," when it comes to the Colts.
League source on trade speculation surrounding the Colts: "This [trade deadline] is pretty likely to be anticlimactic." Obviously, situations are fluid and deadlines spur action, so time will tell. But I am personally adjusting expectations.
Additionally, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, Indianapolis has already informed quarterback Daniel Jones, another player recently rumored to be the subject of trade talks, will not be traded before the deadline.
The Colts informed QB Daniel Jones on Saturday they’re not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Teams called and the Colts listened. But they never had any intention of moving him. Despite speculation, Jones is staying in Indy. pic.twitter.com/Ew0cVkmEuW
That doesn't mean Taylor or Downs are guaranteed to remain in Indianapolis. However, the Colts must determine whether the offers currently available provide enough value to justify moving on from either player or whether keeping them…

title: Jaguars Winners and Losers After the Trade Deadline: Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates Alter Big Plans
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Well, it has been quite the week, hasn't it?
The Jacksonville Jaguars were the story of this year's trade deadline , making three trades on Monday and making the biggest trade of the entire deadline by trading a first- and future second-round pick for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis.
The Jaguars, as they have often been under James Gladstone, Liam Coen, and Tony Boselli, were bold, aggressive, and willing to fight against conventional wisdom as they made moves that could cement their case as the AFC's best team in 2026 and beyond.
“Yeah, I think the idea that this is an all-in move isn't necessarily how I characterize it. I characterize it as getting better as a football team and prioritizing getting better as a football team," Gladstone said Tuesday. "I look forward to seeing it all come to life and being a part of bringing it to life here this week and beyond. But really that’s the intent behind any decision that we make is what's in the best interest of this team in particular and the organization as a whole moving forward.”
So, who benefited the most from the Jaguars' flurry of trade deadline moves? And who had their futures, or presents, impacted in the other direction? We break it all down below.
There can not be a happier man in Duval than Anthony Campanile, especially considering the next two months could solidify his case as one of the NFL's top head coach candidates moving into the 2026 hiring process. After Campanile lost two key veterans in one game 10 days ago, the Jaguars have now upgraded nose tackle and safety with legit blue-chip talents who fit the scheme like a glove. He has to be over the moon.
Bates is a perfect fit for what Campanile likes to do, and his ball skills and range should give the Jaguars the ability to continue to be versatile on the back end. Add in his elite tackling ability, and he could be the defense's best player soon. Davis, meanwhile, is one of the few players in the NFL who could do for the Jaguars what Hamilton has done for the last two seasons. Campanile already had a good defense. Now, he should be well on his way to leading a great unit. The Davis and Bates additions are genuine game-changers, and Campanile could very well be leading the AFC's best defense as a result.
In a league where more and more general managers are risk averse because they want to hold onto job security, it is refreshing to see a general manager who is willing to push in his chips. But what I liked the most about what James Gladstone did on Monday was the flexibility he gave the Jaguars beyond just 2026. Many moves made at the trade deadline are short-sighted, but Gladstone's are clearly about the future.
The Jaguars were able to add big pieces like Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis despite having limited cap space because that is how Gladstone made the deals. He paid a big price for Bates, but the Falcons ate most of his 2026 money, and the Jaguars can still easily re-sign him. They basically bought the rights to negotiate with him early for two picks. As for Davis, his cap hits over the next few years are insignificant, and the Eagles are still paying him a pretty penny. Gladstone again bought cap flexibility and talent by leveraging draft picks, which is smarter than just dealing picks for the sake of adding talent.
The Jaguars did not add to their edge group at all during the trade deadline, which bodes well for situational pass-rusher Dennis Gardeck and the rest of the Jaguars' pass-rush depth. Gardeck often serves as the team's No. 3 edge rusher behind Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen, but there was a real chance he would lose snaps if the Jaguars added anyone at the defensive end spot. Ultimately, that didn't happen.
This is not to say the Jaguars didn't try. According to SI's Albert Breer, the Jaguars had an offer on the tape for pass-rusher Will McDonald. But no deal was made, and the Jaguars are set to continue to use Gardeck as a key piece of their pass-rush plan across from Hines-Allen and Walker as the season goes on.
The Jaguars have had a need for an interior pass-rusher for some time, and the Jaguars added Ruke Orhorhoro in a trade this offseason with hopes of him helping there. He has been solid, posting multiple pressures more often than not, and he has the second-highest pressure rate among all Jaguars defensive linemen. But had the Jaguars added a player like Christian Barmore or Moro Ojomo, it would have been hard to see a scenario where Orhorhoro would have seen the field very often.
While the Jaguars added two defensive tackles, both players are nose tackles. Neither is an athletic three technique like Orhorhoro and Arik Armstead are, and it is clear the Jaguars will still need that duo to provide some pass-rush from the interior spots. Davis and Godchaux are massive additions, but neither should take many pass-rush reps away from Orhorhoro.
If there are two players whose long-term futures were changed during the trade deadline, it was Eric Murray and Davon Hamilton. Each player already had some questions about their roster spot when it came to 2027, and the Jaguars now have blue-chip players at the safety and nose tackle spots who are ready to take over in 2026 and beyond. There was no gurantee Murray or Hamilton would return as starters, or even return to the roster, before these moves. Now, it is harder to see a scenario where each replicates their roles in 2027.
Hamilton, who is in a contract year, could still sign a deal with the Jaguars before he hits free agency. But the chances of him earning big money to be the Jaguars' nose tackle of the future have likely hit near-zero considering Davis is younger and already under contract for years to come. As for Murray, the Jaguars could easily slot Bates into his spot with a new deal. For that to happen, though, Murray would likely have to be one of several players who gets released for cap space purposes.
The two players who lost the most playing time, or lost a path to future playing time, after Monday's moves were both rookies. Third-round picks Jalen Huskey and Albert Regis have not seen a ton of playing time on defense this year, though Huskey has gotten some snaps in the last two blowouts and Regis cracked the nose tackle rotation in Week 9 after Davon Hamilton's injury. That likely all changes now, though, starting with Week 10.
Huskey was a healthy scratch for the Jaguars at the start of the year when they had a healthy safety room, and he was clearly behind Rayuan Lane and Kaevon Merriweather in the pecking order as the season has gone on. Expect for him to be a healthy scratch once again with Bates added to the starting lineup and Lane and Merriweather pushed down a spot. Same goes for Regis, especially after the Jaguars added not one, but two defensive tackles. The Jaguars could use both players a year from now, but they will likely sit and watch the rest of the season.
The trade deadline came and went and, for the second year in a row, there was no Brian Thomas Jr. trade. This is not to say Thomas' long-term future with the team isn't still murky in terms of 2027 and beyond, but for the rest of this season and the subsequent playoff run, the Jaguars are keeping Thomas on their roster. This was the expected outcome considering where the Jaguars are as a team and where they want to go, even with Thomas' role decreasing over the course of the season.
“We have a ton of value when it comes to BTJ. His role and what I imagine his contribution will be down the stretch here is going to be notable," Gladstone said Tuesday. "He's such a good person to work with, such a good teammate, and so I expect a lot of good that comes in what lies in front, knowing that at this point in time, our wide receiver room in particular has got such a range of skill sets at its disposal and those that complement each other really well.
The fact we saw the San Francisco 49ers give up picks for 2026 Keenan Allen says it all about this…

title: The Jaguars' Move For Jessie Bates Looks Even Better After the Bills' Amani Hooker Response
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars made a big move to add star safety Jessie Bates to their defense on Monday.
Adding Bates was already a massive haul for the Jaguars, even considering the price they paid with a second- and fifth-round selection for the former Pro Bowler and All-Pro. A productive veteran who fits seamlessly with the defense and the culture, making it a move that would be hard to top.
A day later, the move looks even better after a similar price was paid by the Buffalo Bills for their new safety Amani Hooker.
The Bills sent a second-round pick to the Tennessee Titans for Hooker and a fifth-round pick. The late-second round pick is basically a trade down to the early fifth-round, the difference of about 80 picks. In 2026 NFL Draft terms, it is the difference between taking Anthony Hill Jr. in the second and taking Fernando
 Carmona in the fifth. It is a good bit of ground to give up for a safety while also not getting any of the money relief the Jaguars got in the Bates deal.
Titans are not eating any money on Amani Hooker’s deal in trade to Bills, per source. Buffalo will take on the rest of Hooker’s roughly $4.4 million salary this season. NFL INT leader is under contract for 2 more seasons. 2027 - 10.2 million 2028 - 13.5 million pic.twitter.com/shO8WjIE6P
There are other differences, of course. Hooker will get the "younger" tag, which is technically true by a year. Let's not act like that year exactly serves as a fountain of youth-sized difference, especially considering Bates is still playing at a high level. If we are just comparing their talents today, then Bates has a significantly lower missed tackle rate than Hooker, has more defensive stops, and has similar ball production outside of Hooker having the edge with five interceptions to one.
What is more likely, though: that Hooker has become the NFL's best ballhawk overnight, or that he is having a good year when it comes to the NFL's most volatile defensive stat? Hooker has been a solid player throughout his career, but he has played just one fewer year than Bates and has 11 fewer interceptions and about 47 fewer pass breakups. Bates also has 14 forced fumbles to Hooker's five.
Hooker is having a career year, but he has never been as good as Bates. The only thing he has done better is nab interceptions this season, but last year he had zero. It can be a flukey stat, and should not exactly be the one anyone uses as an argument to compare their talents.
Bates is seen as a top-tier safety for a reason. Hooker is a nice player, too, but he isn't within Bates' tier. Bates is a difference-maker worth paying the high price for, while Hooker seems like the knock-off version who the Bills had to settle for. The Bills needed to add a safety, and they probably should have just done the Bates deal if they were willing to pay this much for Hooker.
The Bills do have Hooker under contract for a few more seasons, while Bates is set to be a free agent at the end of the year. But the Jaguars have already proven they can make these types of trades and keep the player under contract for years to come, and they have given no indications that this isn't the plan with Bates. With how much cap space they should be expected to clear next offseason, keeping Bates should be a non-issue.
The question here is simple. Would the Titans have ever gotten a second-round pick for Hooker without the Bates deal going down? The answer is almost positively no.
As a result, the Jaguars changed the market, and their already-strong deal now looks even better after just a day and some change.

title: Grading Jaguars' NFL Trade Deadline: Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates Moves Are About More Than Super Bowl LXI
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Just like that, the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline has come and gone.
The deadline ended with the Jaguars making three moves, with each trade coming on Monday. All in all, here is what the Jaguars did:
In short, the Jaguars added Bates, Godchaux, and Davis for a 2027 first-rounder, 2027 second-rounder, 2028 fifth-rounder, 2028 sixth-rounder, and a 2029 second-rounder.
So, how do we think the Jaguars and general manager James Gladstone made out as they look to stake their claim as the AFC's best team? We break it down below.
The Jaguars' path forward is simple: they think they are a Super Bowl team. They should, too, since they are perhaps the only team in the NFL that can boast that they have both a top-5 offense and defense. The Jaguars' offense is in a good place with Trevor Lawrence playing MVP-level football, and the Jaguars have now answered questions at two key positions of need after season-ending injuries to Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray at nose tackle and safety.
By adding Bates, the Jaguars are now putting a former Pro Bowler and All-Pro in a spot that otherwise would have been held by second-year safety Rayuan Lane. Lane has played well in spots this year, but Bates is a massive upgrade. Bates would have even been an upgrade over a healthy Murray, and the price the Jaguars paid is reflected in that. This deal will look different after the season as wekk once we know whether Bates will be re-signed or not.
If the Jaguars traded a second- and fifth-round pick for half a season of Bates, that would clearly be far from ideal. But the Jaguars can easily open up cap space with a few expected releases, and they have shown before that they can add a rental and keep him as a long-term piece. They did it with Jakobi Meyers last year, trading two Day 3 picks for him when he was entering the final two months of his deal. A month later, he signed a three-year extension.
"From everything that we've heard, the guy, the competitor, obviously, but also the person in the community, in the locker room, felt like this was similar to [WR] Jakobi Meyers type of dude, type of competitor, football and personal character. That's why I think it'll only help that room and help that group in the back end continue to provide confidence and communication," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday, already starting the Bates/Meyers comparisons.
If the Jaguars were to not re-sign Bates, they could be eligible for a compensatory pick based on how next March's free agency plays out. It feels unlikely the Jaguars would look to be big players in free agnecy, but it also feels unlikely Bates would sign a deal worthy of landing a third-round pick four years after he did so the first time. Perhaps they could get a fourth, but that would be in 2028 regardless.
This is a better move for the Jaguars if they re-sign him. My complete expectation is that they will, but a lot of this deal hinges on that factor.
As for Godchaux, there is not a ton to say. Flipping a sixth, likely in 2027 due to the compensatory picks the Jaguars are set to get, for a rotational run-stuffer makes sense. He hasn't had a great year in New Orleans, but he has ties to Anthony Campanile and is a better fit as a pure nose tackle for the Jaguars' scheme than both Matt Dickerson and Albert Regis.
This feels like a neutral move that the Jaguars will likely feel like winners after as long as he contributes to their run defense, but they paid the same cost for him that they did for Daniel Faalele Quinn Ewers. Godchaux can help the Jaguars a lot more this year than a sixth-round rookie could next season or in 2028.
Then there is the big move. The Jaguars sent two premium picks to the Eagles for Jordan Davis, though one of those picks is not set to be due until 2029. The Jaguars, simply, will never, ever been seen as the winners of this deal on paper, in the football community, among insiders and analysts, and whomever else. Accept that now.
The reason why is simple. Trading such a large package of picks for a two-down player would, in most cases, look disastrous. But consider a few factors from the Jaguars' point of view. For one, not all nose tackles are the same, and not all teams value nose tackles like the Jaguars do. Teams with attacking, gap-shooting defenses who are all about creating negative plays on third-down would likely have a much-different valuation on Davis than the Jaguars.
The Jaguars, though, do not live on every down and distance looking for a chance at the quarterback. The Jaguars' entire scheme is based around stopping the run on early downs and forcing 2nd- and 3rd-and-longs for the offense. When that happens, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile turns up the heat with pressure looks and disguised coverages, the biggest reason the Jaguars have created so many turnovers the past two years.
But to get to third down and force quarterbacks into mistakes, the Jaguars have to win on first and second down. That is why Davon Hamilton was the most important piece of their defense, and that is why his loss to a season-ending injury was such a crushing blow. The Jaguars are the rare team where the nose tackle and run defense set the done for the pass-rushers and defensive backs, and Davis should fit in like a glove.
There is also the fact that the Jaguars have several defensive tackles on expiring deals after 2027. Hamilton's deal is up, and as is Arik Armstead's. So is Godchaux's for that matter. Had the Jaguars not traded the first-round pick for Davis, there is a good chance they would have had to use that pick on a defensive tackle. And that right there might be why they wanted to trade for Quinnen Williams a year ago and for Jeffery Simmons a few weeks ago.
What would the Jaguars prefer? A 26-year-old defensive tackle who should start to now hit his peak, which the Jaguars have said they believe is around that age at the position ... or a rookie who would have to be an impact player right off the bat, despite late-first round defensive tackles ever amounting to that type of player.
By trading for Davis, the Jaguars filled their defensive tackle hole for 2027 and likely beyond. The same can be said about Bates and the safety spot when he gets re-signed. That means these moves not only increase the Jaguars' Super Bowl odds in 2026, but they should increase them entering Week 1 of 2027 as well as long as Bates is retained.
The Jaguars paid a big, big price. James Gladstone will now go through his first three drafts using just one first-round pick. That is a lot of risk. But the reward could be about much more than just this year's Super Bowl. It could be the shot in the arm the Jaguars need to go from good to elite.

title: 4 Jaguars Who Had Their Futures Dramatically Changed After James Gladstone's Flurry of Trades
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars' defense got quite the facelift on Monday.
The Jaguars already had one of the NFL's best defenses entering the final 48 hours of the trade deadline, but general manager James Gladstone gave the unit a significant injection of talent with trades for Jessie Bates III, Jordan Davis, and Davon Godchaux.
While there are still a few hours to go in the trade deadline as of this writing, the Jaguars could be done making moves after their trio of trades to kick off the week. Ifd that is indeed the case, then it is not hard to see how the Jaguars' future plans have changed for a number of vetertans.
So, which Jaguars' future roles look different now that Jacksonville is entering the playoff push with three new faces on defense? We break it down below.
This is the most obvious one. The Jaguars signed Eric Murray to a three-year, $19.5 million deal last March that was always expected to be a short-term floor-raising move as the Jaguars started to put the pieces together. Even before Murray sustained a season-ending elbow injury in Week 8, it felt like from the start of the year that the long-time NFL veteran would be entering what would likely be his final year with the Jaguars. Now that Jacksonville has Bates in the mix , this case should be even more evident.
Yes, Bates is on an expiring deal, but so was Jakobi Meyers when the Jaguars traded for him. It would be surprising to see the Jaguars hand over a second-round pick without already having intentions of re-signing Bates, who will be 30 next season. The Jaguars signed Murray to a three-year deal and made him a starter when he was 31, so why would they hesitate with an All-Pro player who they just gave up picks for?
Re-signing Bates will take cap space , though, and releasing Murray is one thing the Jaguars can do to free some up. Bates is simply on another level as a play-maker than Murray, so the decision should already be made. Murray has been a good soldier for the Jaguars' defense since signing, but releasing him with a post-June 1st designation next year would free up $6.5 million for the Jaguars, while giving them a dead cap hit of over $2.5 million, according to OverTheCap.
This is one that would hurt, but it must be talked about. Davon Hamilton was arguably the MVP of the entire Jaguars defense until he got injured, playing at a Pro Bowl level and putting out the most dominant tape of his career. It seemed like he was hitting his speak as a nose tackle, and it was also happening during a contract year, making it perfect timing for Hamilton. That timing got disrupted in a big way last week when his season ended, though.
The Jaguars did not trade such a big package for Davis with hopes of him being just another cog in their defensive front. He is the new present and future of their nose tackle position, and he is set to be under contract and in Duval for the next several seasons. That spot likely would have continued to belong to Hamilton had he ended the season healthy, and he would have earned it after such a stellar season.
That is not to say there is no chance Hamilton returns now. He is beloved inside the building, and could you imagine a Jaguars depth chart that has Davis and Hamilton as its top two run-stuffers? But it would likely have to be a shorter and less significant deal, and it is at least a question now. Two weeks ago, Hamilton looked like the must-keep of the Jaguars' impending free agents. That has changed a bit now.
With the Jaguars adding Bates and Davis in one day , those are blue-chip players who will have big dollar signs attached to their deals while they are in Jacksonville. Davis is under contract for the next few years while the Jaguars will likely attempt to sign Bates to a deal in the range of three seasons before the regular-season ends. Add in the expiring deal of Parker Washington and a few other key Jaguars, and cap space will be needed.
Two ways the Jaguars can create that cap space? By shedding some contracts of older veterans such as Jourdan Lewis and Patrick Mekari. The Jaguars didn't find replacements for them like they found replacements for Murray and Hamilton, but Lewis and Mekari still offer two clear ways to save money without hurting the on-field product all that much. Lewis has made some big plays for the Jaguars this season but could be slowing down ahead of the final year of his deal, while Mekari has not seen the field this year due to injuries.
According to OverTheCap, the Jaguars would save $8 million in cap if they release Lewis with a post-June 1st designation. Add in another $13 million if they release Mekari, and the Jaguars could create $21 million by moving on from two older players who were likely always going to be short-term stop-gaps to begin with. Add in the Murray move, and that is almost $30 million in cap space freed up.

title: Jaguars NFL Trade Deadline Rumors Tracker: Latest Updates After Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates Moves
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The NFL Trade deadline is just seven days away, and it sure feels like the Jacksonville Jaguars are a team to watch.
The Jaguars have been one of the more active teams in terms of trades since hiring general manager James Gladstone, including one trade deadline move last year to land wide receiver Jakobi Meyers. The last few weeks have been about identifying which targets might be next for the Jaguars to take a look at.
With recent injuries to Eric Murray and Davon Hamilton, the Jaguars did not sit and wait when it come to the trade deadline. Jacksonville made blockbuster moves for Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates and also added New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
The Jaguars look different now than they did the last time they were on the field as a result of the moves, with Jaguars head coach Liam Coen speaking Monday following the Bates trade that sent a second- round and a fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons.

He was obviously on that list," Coen said. "So, when you're going through the processes of it, you guys asked me last week, right, what’s the balance of bringing guys in versus not, reach and grabs, and this was a guy that we had enough familiarity with in terms of the competitor and just happened to make so much sense.”
A lot has changed for the Jaguars after their big moves, but that does not mean the trade deadline is over. There are still a few rumors out there worth tracking, which you can do so here.
Do not forget to keep checking back here as each situation develops ahead of today's deadline, either.

The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN

title: The Jaguars' Case for the No. 1 Seed After Major Trades: Getting Past Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have a chance to do something they have not done in over 25 years: win the AFC's top seed.
There is still an entire half of the season left to play after Week 9, but the 6-2 Jaguars have been as good, if not better, as any of the top teams in the AFC. The Jaguars haven't walked into the playoffs as the No. 1 seed since 1999, but there feels like a very real chance that could change this year if the Jaguars continue down their current path.
This is even more true after the wild Monday the Jaguars had. Jacksonville already looked like one of the best teams, if not the best overall, in football before they added Jessie Bates III, Jordan Davis, and Davon Godchaux in some critical blockbuster moves ahead of the trade deadline.
So, what case do the Jaguars have moving forward when it comes to the race for the No. 1 seed? We break it down below, starting with their biggest competition.
The Jaguars' biggest rival for the No. 1 seed looks like the Buffalo Bills, who beat the Jaguars in a heartbreaker in the Wild Card round last year. The Bills were likely the only thing standing between the Jaguars and the Super Bowl a year ago, and there is a good chance they are once again going to be their primary hurdle. That is why getting a piece like Bates before the Bills could jump was so critical,
The Bills do still get to play both the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins twice, but they also have the Broncos, Chicago Bears, and Green Bay Packers on the schedule. The Jaguars only have to play one of those teams over the second-half of the season, and the Bills have already proven that they are indeed human after several close wins against teams with worse records. They could drop at least two of those games, which could be all the Jaguars need.
The Broncos are sitting at 7-2 and already beat the Jaguars earlier this season at Mile High, giving them an edge over Jacksonville if their records end up the same. That gives the Broncos their most notable advantage over the Jaguars when it comes to the pursuit of a No. 1 seed, and the Broncos also do not have many tough games left. They still get to play bad teams like the Raiders twice, the olphins, the Jets, and the Chargers. They have games that could be close against the Bills and Steelers, but it is an easy slate.
With that said, the Broncos do not always making things look easy. They had close calls with both the Carolina Panthers and Los Angeles Chargers, and their offense looks average at best with the way Bo Nix is playing. The Broncos rank No. 16 on offensive EPA/Play, and it simply doesn't look like they have the firepower to be able to sail through their second-half schedule with no concerns.
After a 5-0 start to the season, the Kansas City Chiefs have come back to earth. They beat the New York Jets on Sunday, but this was only after back-to-back losses to playoff teams like the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, and right now the Chiefs' only win against a team with a winning record came in Week 1 against the Broncos. The Chiefs other wins came against teams witha combined record of 9-34. The Chiefs have not been as impressive as their record might suggest, in short.
Kansas City still has some tough games moving forward against the Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati Bengals, San Francisco 49ers, and the New England Patriots if they ever decide to get serious this season. That is a much tougher schedule than the Jaguars have moving forward, and the Chiefs are from looking like a team that is capable of going on some kind of juggernaut run through their second-half schedule.
The AFC North is a weird place, man. The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals are at the top of the division at 6-2 and look like the most likely teams to represent the division in the playoffs. The Cleveland Browns are still alive at 5-4 but they are not as good as even their near-.500 record indicates, while the 4-5 Ravens have floundered without Lamar Jackson under center as they deal with injuries.
The Jaguars have already defeated the Bengals in Cincinnati, a game that was close in score but not nearly as close on the field. The Jaguars had two touchdowns and an interception into Bengals' territory called back that game, and it is clear the Jaguars' defensive boosts could go a long way against Joe Burrow, especially the addition of Bates . The Bengals, like the Jaguars, have an easy schedule the rest of the way, but their high-volume passing game could have them lose a game they shouldn't like they almost did against the Tennessee Titans.
As for the Steelers, the Jaguars will see them at home on Monday Night Football on Dec. 14. The Steelers passing game is brutal, though they do rank No. 1 in rushing EPA/Play and No. 7 in rushing success rate. Adding Davis to the mix after losing Davon Hamilton should go a long way in that matchup, but it doesn't appear the Steelers have the horses in the passing game to earn the top seed anyways.

title: 3 Moves the Jaguars Could Still Make Before the Trade Deadline Ends
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars had a busy Monday. Maybe the busiest the franchise has ever had.
Jaguars general manager James Gladstone and the franchise made three trades Monday, landing All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis in two different blockbusters. They also added rotational defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the mix.
Most teams would, well, be done after three moves. But what if the Jaguars have any more tricks up their sleeve to boost their defense? With that in mind, here are three moves Gladstone and the Jaguars could still make before 4 p.m.
The Jaguars certainly boosted their already-elite run defense on Monday by adding two space-eaters in Davis and Godchaux. They also improved their secondary with the addition of Bates after a season-ending injury to Eric Murray a few weeks ago. The only spots of their defense that they have yet to touch, though, are at the linebacker spots and on the edge of their defensive line. They don't need any more linebackers, but adding some juice to the edge would make sense.
Former first-round pick Will McDonald certainly has that. He has been productive as a speed rusher throughout his career, though he has reportedly requested a trade from the Jets due to a diminishing role in the defense. But McDonald still has three sacks, 20 pressures, and a 14.9% pressure rate that would rank No. 1 on the Jaguars' defensive line by quite a bit. The Jaguars have already sent their first and second-round picks. What about a third to add McDonald and give them a top-level third-down package with him, Travon Walker, Josh Hines-Allen, and Arik Armstead?
We have been banging the drum for the Jaguars to trade for Josh Uche for probably four or five years in a row now, and we aren't stopping. The one thing the Jaguars have missed in their defensive end room for years now is a speedy pass-rusher who can threaten the edge with an explosive first step. They have plenty of power guys, but adding a designated pass-rushing threat like Uche would give the Jaguars something they just not have.
The Jaguars likely hope that B.J. Green or Bryan Thomas Jr. can turn into that type of pass-rusher, but there is no hoping when it comes to Uche. The mercenary pass-rusher has already proven he can get the job done as a change-of-pace pass-rusher. He has three sacks and 14 pressures this year and would fit in with what the Jaguars like to do scheme-wise considering he plays in a similar scheme in Miami, and he would likely cost not much more than Godchaux did.
Dorance Armstrong would likely be a pure rental for the Jaguars since he is in the last year of his deal, and the Commanders would likely also need to eat a bit of his money. But considering the flashes he has shown as a pass-rusher in the past, he could be the perfect type of option to add to the Jaguars' pass-rush rotation alongside Hines-Allen and Walker, especially if he can get back to his 2025 form.
Armstrong has not had a very good 2026, but last year he had a pressure rate of nearly 20% and he has proven he can get after the quarterback. The Commanders are in a lost season, and they would be better off dealing anyone they can to prepare to build back toward 2027, because the 2026 Commanders are not going anywhere significant. Sending a Day 3 pick to add Armstrong to the rotation would be a legit boost.

title: Predicting Jaguars Starting Defense After Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates Trades
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars defense looks a lot different than it did a few days ago.
On Thursday night, the Jaguars' defense left the field after dominating the Baltimore Ravens as one of the top units in the NFL. After three trades for safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux, the defense looks even better today.
So, what do we think the Jaguars' starting defensive lineup looks like now that they have made a trio of trades to boost the unit ? We break it down below.
Defensive End: Josh Hines-Allen; Travon Walker
3-Technique: Arik Armstead
Simply put, the Jaguars not make this kind of deal without slotting Davis right into the middle of their defense. The Jaguars paid a big price to land Davis' talent and contract for the next few seasons, and there is no other logical direction they can move in but one that puts him front and center for their new-look defensive line. The Jaguars had a big need for a nose tackle after the loss of Davon Hamilton, and Davis fills it.
Matt Dickerson started Thursday's game against the Baltimore Ravens and played fine, but he is far from being at the level of Davis and Hamilton. He would have slotted in as the team's second nose tackle, but I do think that spot now goes to Davon Godchaux. The Jaguars have the same exact edge depth they had entering the season, while Arik Armstead and Ruke Orhorhoro will handle the pass-rushing reps on the inside.
This was a big move for Jacksonville, and they will need Davis to make an impact right away. The Jaguars want to get to third-down to let their blitzes and coverages force quarterbacks into mistakes. To do that, they need to win on first- and second-down. When Davis is at his very best, that is exactly what he doesn.
Middle Linebacker: Foye Oluokun
Weakside Linebacker: Ventrell Miller
The only level of the defense that didn't get touched on Monday was the linebacker spot, which tracks considering how well both Foye Oluokun and Ventrell Miller have played. Oluokun has had one of the best years of his career and is riding a bit of a hot streak out of the Jaguars' bye week, while Miller has been one of the most reliable and consistent linebackers week-to-week in the entire NFL this season.
With the way the Jaguars have invested in the linebacker position since James Gladstone took over as general manager, I would be very surprised to see linebacker ever be a part of the Jaguars' trade deadline plans. The Jaguars value the position and its value and impact in Anthony Campanile's scheme, but they are not going to put a lot of picks into the spot either; not high-profile picks at the very least. This is a good duo for the Jaguars.
Cornerback: Travis Hunter; Montaric Brown
Slot Cornerback: Jourdan Lewis
Free Safety: Jessie Bates III
Strong Safety: Antonio Johnson
The Jaguars badly needed an experienced and productive veteran to step into the starting spot across from Antonio Johnson, and that is exactly what they are getting from Bates. The 29-year-old safety is still playing at a high level after 7.5 seasons in the NFL, and the expectation should be for him to be an every-down player for their defense once he is caught up to speed along the way, whether that is this week against the Tennessee Titans or next week against the New York Giants.
"The playmaker that he is, competed against him twice a year obviously in Atlanta there in Tampa. So much impact on a game. I mean, he punched out balls against us, critical interceptions, had 14 tackles yesterday. Then the human being and the competitor that we look at, think that it'll be a really good fit in the locker room, culturally," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday.
"The amount of text messages I've received from people that have been around him, coached him, been in the building with him, all I've heard is he makes people around him better, will be an immediate high football character type guy. So, that's kind of what made it very appealing.”
Johnson is one of the defense's best players, but the Jaguars badly needed help across from him. Now, Rayuan Lane can be the No. 3 safety instead of taking on the starting safety role like he has over the last two weeks, giving him a more logical fit in the Jaguars' defense.

title: 3 Instant Observations on Jaguars' Massive Trade for Jordan Davis: James Gladstone Goes All-In
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- A big day just got a lot bigger.
The Jaguars weren't done after one trade on Monday. They weren't done after two, either. Instead, the Jaguars waited until Monday night to make their biggest move yet: trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis.
Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT
So, what do we make of the latest James Gladstone blockbuster ahead of the trade deadline? We break it down below.
There was never any real doubt the Jaguars would go all-in on a wide-open window in the AFC, right? Because that is exactly what the Jaguars have done, trading away a first-round pick, two second-round picks, and a fifth-round pick on the same day to land Davis and new star safety Jessie Bates. There has never been a more aggressive trade deadline in franchise history, and the Jaguars are clearly operating like a team that knows its window is now.
Do the additions of Bates and Davis change the math for the Jaguars when it comes to those aspirations? That remains to be seen, but one could see where the logic is. Bates fills the need of a reliable, rangy safety who can add experience to the room, while Davis is one of the few nose tackles in football who can actually fill the role of Davon Hamilton after his injury.
I thought the Jessie Bates trade meant the Jaguars were done taking a big swing. I thought this was even more clear when they added a rotational run-stuffer in Davon Godchaux during the afternoon. The Jaguars, of course, had other ideas, and the only reason why this is the case is because they are looking for their first Super Bowl.
This has also been said about the Travis Hunter trade, and that is true. But trading into the top-two of the draft to take a blue-chip player is different than dealing a first- and second-round pick at the deadline for an in-season trade, especially when it comes to a player who has already been paid and one who has not exactly been dominant in 2026. Gladstone has made it clear a few times now that he is cut from the same exact cloth as Les Snead and has takenan "Eff them picks" mindset, and that mindset will largely be graded on a scale that corresponds directly with this trade.
Mind you, there will be virtually nobody but the Jaguars who will believe they won this trade. Like the Hunter trade, there will be countless thinkpieces, counterarguments, and even snickers when it comes to the deal that James Gladstone pulled off. But, like the Hunter trade, literally none of that will matter if it works out. The Hunter trade has worked out thus far for the Jaguars, thus the noise has amounted to, well, nothing.
Will the same be said for the Davis deal? That depends entirely on how big of a role he plays in the Jaguars winning games moving forward. If he doesn't pan out, this will be a trade people look back to and point out as a reason to never push your chips all the way in.
I thought the Jessie Bates trade was a 10/10 move with no real notes or issues. The Davis trade I do think you have to be more open-minded to the fact that is a massive risk, especially considering the fact that Davis isn't having one of the stronger seasons of his career. The upside with this move is clearly that it would help the Jaguars seamlessly replace Hamilton, who was the most important player on the defense as it relates to running Anthony Campanile's scheme. When Davis is at the top of his game, he is an elite run-stuffer who can allow the Jaguars to continue to play their brand of football. He also offers more in terms of pass-rush juice than most noses, despite the low sack totals.
The cons are clear. While Davis is far from a non-factor as a pass-rusher, he is not the archetype of defensive tackle you normally see get moved for these kinds of packages. Jalen Carter, Jeffery Simmons, Quinnen Williams, these are the types of pass-rushing skill-sets that would normally land this kind of trade package. Davis hasn't been that player in his career, and the Jaguars are giving up a big price for a player the Eagles may not have as many issues replacing as one may think.
In terms of pure value, the Jaguars will of course be on the losing end of this deal. They will need Davis to transform more than just their run defense to change that, and I am not sure that it his game. We will find out soon.

title: 3 Instant Observations on Jaguars Trading for Davon Godchaux: How Rest of Deadline is Impacted
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars aren’t done.
A few hours after the Jaguars made their trade deadline blockbuster for star Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars have reportedly made another move.
According to Netflix’s Tom Pelissero, the Jaguars will be sending a 2028 sixth-rounder to the New Orleans Saints for veteran defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, a pick that can reportedly become a 2027 sixth if certain conditions are met.
So, what do we make of the Jaguars making the move to land the big man in the middle of the defense? We break it down below.
Before we get into where Godchaux can help the Jaguars, we should first discuss what this move really says. It became clear after the big trade for Bates earlier in the day that the Jaguars were not going to pull off some master blockbuster move for a defensive tackle like so many had been hoping, and perhaps even expecting. The Jaguars had been linked to defensive tackles for weeks, but dealing such a big package for Bates suggested that the Jaguars took their swing on defensive linemen, but it didn’t take and they instead pivoted to their safety need. The fact that they made a cheap move to land a rotational run-stuffer just a few hours later suggests this is the case.
Godchaux is about as ho-hum as you can get in terms of adding a veteran defensive lineman. It is not the type of move that really moves any needle, even if it does help the team’s depth situation at defensive tackle. The Jaguars were likely always going to have to go this route at defensive tackle after the Bates move, so it isn’t surprising to see the Jaguars make this kind of addition. A dream scenario would’ve been Bates and a blue-chip defensive tackle, surely. But it just wasn’t going to be overly realistic, and a Bates + Godchaux haul does make the Jaguars a better team today than they were when they left the field in Baltimore a few days ago.
It is clear what the Jaguars like about Godchaux and where they think the 10th-year veteran can help them. It was always going to be easier to find a rotational nose tackle to help ease the loss of Davon Hamilton than it was going to be to find an impact pass-rusher at the defensive tackle spot, and that is exactly what the Jaguars have done with this move. Jacksonville got solid play from the backup nose tackle spots with Matt Dickerson and Albert Regis against the Baltimore Ravens, but neither is an exact replacement for Hamilton as a two-gapping run-stuffer. Now, Godchaux is far from being Hamilton, but he is at least a similar style of defensive tackle.
Godchaux should be able to give the Jaguars some solid reps in a rotation against the run, though it is important to keep expectations realistic. He will not take games over like Hamilton, and he also will not give the Jaguars the same pass-rush value from nose tackle that Hamilton was giving them this season. But he should at least improve their nose tackle depth for the next two months, which was their ultimate goal with the move.
The Jaguars have now added to both the safety and defensive tackle rooms, giving away second-, fifth-, and sixth-round picks in the process to land the two defenders. It feels like we can expect the Jaguars to be mostly done at the deadline now as a result and, hey, Brian Thomas Jr. is still on the squad. Since the Jaguars have been able to fill their two biggest needs on defense without giving away Thomas in order to help get picks to offset the packages given away, there doesn’t seem like there is much reason left to trade Thomas this season. Had the Jaguars needed compensation from a Thomas deal to land Bates or a defensive tackle, perhaps it would be a different story, but they didn’t need to do that.
If the Jaguars get offered a second-round pick for Thomas, that would feel hard to pass up, but this was always the case. Anything less, and it feels like the Jaguars would be making their roster and depth chart worse without the reward that would make it worth it. Since the Jaguars don’t need to make such a move to land defensive reinforcements, the Jaguars should hold onto Thomas for the rest of the season and then reevaluate his trade market once next offseason begins. If he has value now, he should have value then.
