title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: What's the Deal With Cyrus Allen?
full_text:
With the dust officially having settled on Week 9 and the NFL trade deadline , the Kansas City Chiefs are one step closer to figuring out who they are ahead of the most important stretch of the season.
Sunday's victory over the New York Jets featured a return to dominance for most of the game, although it was likely just an example of a good team taking care of business against a bad one. With that said, it served as a prime opportunity for some of the club's young players to continue developing.
Following Week 9, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each qualifying 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, whose practice window was opened a while back, isn't included while he's still on the physically unable to perform list .
Left tackle Josh Simmons remains off the list after going to injured reserve . The same exemption applies to running back Brashard Smith .
Nohl Williams just keeps on proving why he's one of the best cornerback building blocks on a rookie deal. His breakout year rolled on in Week 9, as he dominated in coverage against the Jets' banged-up receiver room and did exactly what he should've on the afternoon. If he's rejoined by Mansoor Delane this weekend versus the Atlanta Falcons, which is expected , it could be tough sledding for the home offense.
The further that second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte gets from his plantar fascia injury , the more he looks like a somewhat reliable starter opposite George Karlaftis. At the very least, he's a nice one-two punch with rookie R Mason Thomas, although the former received 44 snaps in Week 9 to the latter's 28. According to Pro Football Focus , Gilotte finished with a pair of pressures and a stop on Sunday to Thomas' respective marks of one and zero.
A week after going 5-for-5 on targets and receptions for 128 yards and the first touchdown of his NFL career, rookie running back Emmett Johnson rushed for a career-high 34 yards and his first-ever score on the ground. Being in a blowout game allowed the Nebraska product to get some more work in the run game, and he certainly delivered.
It's impossible to move rookie tackle Kahlil Benson down a tier, so he's stuck in this one until he improves his play. Considering the back half of Kansas City's schedule, that doesn't seem probable . The former CFP National Championship winner from Indiana gave up more pressures (five) than any Chiefs lineman over the weekend, which doesn't bode well for his long-term prospects.
The wide receiver room is suddenly in an interesting position. Jalen Royals made the most of both of his targets on late downs on Sunday, although there may not be a ton more to his role at this juncture and he's now battling an ankle issue.
Fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen fumbled on special teams and didn't see an expanded workload on offense, which may be something to monitor given that Josh Downs was acquired at the deadline. The next few weeks could be a make-or-break stretch for Allen's debut year in the Chiefs' wideout ranks.
Defensive tackle Peter Woods is far from an empty snaps player, but he hasn't made too many high-impact plays as of late and also didn't play in Week 9 because of a neck injury. The Chiefs anticipate him back in Week 10. Bryson Eason, who played 20 snaps in Week 8 when Woods first got hurt, saw his total drop all the way down to five.
Fourth-round cornerback Jadon Canady has experienced a tale of two games in Weeks 8 and 9, going from flashing his playmaking upside to being a special teams liability. The good news for this category is that tight end Jake Briningstool receives a promotion after logging season-high thresholds for offensive snaps (15) and targets (two).
Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa still isn't going to crack the rotation on defense, but he made his second big-time special teams play of the year when he recovered Allen's fumble on the Chiefs' opening kickoff return. At the safety spot, Xavier Nwankpa went over the 20-snap mark for Dave Toub's unit for the second consecutive game.
Not a ton to see here. With backup quarterback Justin Fields not being moved at the deadline, rookie Garrett Nussmeier will remain the emergency third signal-caller on game days for the remainder of the year. In fairness, there was never any smoke surrounding a Fields trade.
Offensive tackle Diego Pounds and defensive end Jack Pyburn are safe on the 53-man roster for the time being.

title: How the NFL Trade Deadline Changed the Chiefs' Wide Receiver Depth Chart
full_text:
Perhaps the worst-kept secret rolling into the 2026 NFL trade deadline was that the Kansas City Chiefs needed a wide receiver.
Given the combination of questionable talent and injuries the club faced after nine weeks of play, it seemed like only a matter of time until general manager Brett Veach added talent to the room. Despite making folks wait for a big chunk of the day on Tuesday, Kansas City's front office did just that and landed its man.
Longtime Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs is the newest Chief, bringing some quality route-running chops along with him. The hope, for Kansas City's sake, is he can solidify the floor of the receiver collective now while also helping contribute to a potential ceiling come playoff time.
With the addition of Downs, where does he stand compared to his new Chiefs teammates? Let's dive into an updated projection of the Kansas City wideout depth chart in a tier system.
There's a defined hierarchy beyond the top three, although sorting out that first group of Chiefs receivers might prove tricky for head coach Andy Reid and company in the coming days.
Even at the beginning of the season, KC was trying to force Worthy as the featured piece on offense. In Weeks 1-3, he received 165 snaps to Rice's 160, also logging a combined 13 targets in the first two games of the year. It's been tough sledding for the former first-round pick, however, and he also sustained a hamstring injury in Week 9's win over the New York Jets.
Simplifying Worthy's role whenever he's healthy seems to make plenty of sense, especially given the overlap between him, Rice and Downs if that doesn't happen. Aside from a deep-ball connection from quarterback Patrick Mahomes years ago, Rice has shown next to nothing as a vertical threat.
Downs, for as productive as he can be in the short and occasionally intermediate areas of the field, is more of the same kind of player. There's also the matter of alignment, as Downs spends more time in the slot than on the boundary but Rice is a heavy participant there, too, and Worthy is far from a full-time 'Z' receiver.
It'll be interesting to see how the workload is distributed. Maybe Week 1 is a nice example, as Rice actually led the way by playing 83% of available snaps and was followed by Worthy (77%) and the now-injured Tyquan Thornton (68%).
Even more intriguing is the long-term possibility for the 2026-27 campaign should Thornton make it back for the end of the regular season or the start of the postseason.
Last year's fourth-round pick, Royals, suffered an ankle injury on Sunday. It isn't expected to hold him out for an extended period of time, though, and he's coming off a game in which he hauled in both of his targets for 18 yards. Both receptions came on third down, with the real kicker being that he (21) was right alongside Armstrong (22) and rookie Allen (19) in snaps.
Armstrong is the player who stands out most in terms of build, although he's more of a blocking mercenary than anything else. There's a nonzero chance he winds up back on the waiver wire and, eventually, the practice squad at some point.
The real draw is Allen, a 2026 fifth-rounder who made numerous plays during the summer but took a long time to find a role on offense. That process is still happening; it doesn't help that he struggled on special teams over the weekend.
Kansas City is in a strange position where Downs can be right now what many wanted Allen to turn into over the course of the year. Keep an eye on how the division of labor unfolds in the next month or so.
Remigio is almost exclusively a special teams player at this point. In a world where Downs might not be ready to play by Sunday and Worthy is out a week, maybe he gets on the field for several snaps, but that just doesn't seem likely.
It's worth mentioning veteran Justin Watson's name here, even with him being on the practice squad. He has one elevation left for the rest of the regular season and possesses plenty of experience in the Chiefs' offense and on Dave Toub's special teams unit.

title: Chiefs Acquire WR Josh Downs From Colts: What It Means for Kansas City’s Offense
full_text:
After waiting for what felt like an eternity , the Kansas City Chiefs have finally made an addition to bolster their roster.
According to multiple sources, the Chiefs have acquired former Colts wide receiver Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-rounder before Tuesday's trade deadline passed. In return, Indianapolis will receive a fourth and fifth-round pick in the upcoming NFL Draft.
BREAKING: The #Chiefs are trading with the Indianapolis Colts for WR Josh Downs, per @TomPelissero pic.twitter.com/e4KXeEzqBI
A fifth-year wideout out of North Carolina, Downs was one of the most sought-after receivers on the market this year. There were reports linking Downs and Kansas City for weeks, and the move finally became official today. While KC had to add slightly more draft compensation than most fans thought they'd have to give up, general manager Brett Veach was still able to hold on to his top three selections in the next draft while adding an elite separator. Although Downs' numbers on the year (33 receptions, 354 yards) are modest, he was in an unfavorable situation with Daniel Jones and the 2-7 Colts. He'll get a much-needed fresh start in his new home and hopes to revert to his 2024 form when he hauled in 72 catches for over 800 yards.
Despite his short stature at 5-foot-9, 171 pounds, Downs is now undoubtedly the best route-running receiver the Chiefs have. He primarily operates out of the slot and beats man coverage as well as anyone at his position in the entire NFL.
Downs ranks fifth among 104 qualified receivers in separation score this season. For reference, Kansas City's top two receivers before the trade — Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy — rank No. 103 and 76, respectively. That is a testament to how well Downs beats defenders and the ease with which he can get open on quick-developing concepts.
The Chiefs' wide receiving corps was already in a precarious spot before the season began , but it has been stretched thin ever since losing Tyquan Thornton to a gruesome ankle dislocation. Worthy went down this past Sunday with a hamstring ailment himself, which could knock him out for some time and leave the receiver room even more depleted.
Downs' arrival gives quarterback Patrick Mahomes a reliable option on third down and someone he can look to when nobody else is open. What he lacks in size and blocking ability, he makes up for with his shiftiness and precise route-running skills.
Earlier this year, Downs essentially auditioned for his spot on the Chiefs when they took on the Colts on Sunday Night Football . In that contest, Downs secured seven of his nine targets for 72 yards, absolutely carving up Kansas City's defensive backfield all night long. It could take some time for Downs to be fully incorporated into the offense, given that he'll have to learn a new playbook right away. At the same time, the Chiefs aren't in a comfortable enough position where they can confidently trot out backups like Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen every snap if Worthy is sidelined.
With the trade deadline having come to a close, it's likely that the Chiefs have made their first and final move, barring an unexpected buzzer beater from the franchise. Regardless, this is an acquisition that could prove to be a game-changer for Kansas City and one fans should be tremendously excited about.

title: Chiefs Stock Watch: Multiple Defensive Linemen on the Rise After Week 9
full_text:
You can only play who's in front of you on the schedule, which is precisely the conundrum the Kansas City Chiefs found themselves experiencing in Week 9. Although a blowout win over the lowly New York Jets doesn't mean anything is fixed, it was still a heck of a way to respond to consecutive losses.
Within that 35-12 outcome, several players made statements with their play. The defensive side of the ball, for instance, started a bit slow but surged over the course of the afternoon. Elsewhere, even in a comfortable victory, there were some reasons for concern if improvement doesn't occur.
Let's dive into the good and bad from the Chiefs' Week 9 win against New York and single out three players whose stock is trending up, as well as three who could use a better showing in Week 10 and down the stretch of the year.
These players stood out for positive reasons on Sunday, potentially changing the trajectory of their seasons in the process.
Prior to Week 9, there was plenty of chatter about the floor and ceiling of the Chiefs' pass rush if defensive tackle Chris Jones wasn't himself. There was no reason to believe that wasn't the case, either, as the seven-time Pro Bowler had just half a sack through seven games and wasn't winning as quickly — or as often — as he had in the past.
Jones extinguished every ounce of those doubts, at least for one weekend.
The CEO of 'Sack Nation' terrorized the New York offensive line, recording his first two full sacks of the year. Both of them were on third down, serving as a glimpse of the Jones of old. It was a historic outing for one of the club's best players, and one that saw him look and grade out like someone who was fresh and firing on all cylinders.
There's a serious case to be made that along the Chiefs' defensive front, edge rusher George Karlaftis has been their best player in 2026. That was likely true before the Jets game, and even Jones' strong performance may not have been enough to change it considering Karlaftis matched him with a tremendous showing of his own.
The first sack for "Furious George" came on a second-and-5 play on the opening drive of the second half. His last was on a fourth-and-3 in the final frame to force a turnover on downs with the game out of reach. The sack department wasn't the only place he stood out, however, as he had a nice run stop on New York's third drive and also a batted pass on a free rush in the second quarter.
Karlaftis is enjoying a career season in Kansas City. Now he has some more sacks to further justify that.
In any scenario where you get benched twice in a four-game span , you simply have to be a "stock down" player in general. Whenever you respond by getting back in the starting lineup and you come up with a nice performance in response, there's no way you can't be a "stock up" Chief!
Left guard Kingsley Suamataia tied for a team-high in snaps on Sunday, making the most of it with Pro Football Focus grades of 82.7 for run blocking and 80.9 for overall offense. The former second-round pick looked comfortable, but at the same time, he played with a mean streak and intensity that made it glaringly obvious he wanted to send a message.
Sent and received, even with head coach Andy Reid still not explaining why he benched the BYU product in the first place.
Take a look at #76 here on this Kenneth Walker TD. That's #Chiefs G Kingsley Suamataia. That will be on film in every building this week. 💪💪 pic.twitter.com/tDHq5Z0s81
These three players didn't meet the bar in Week 9 and desperately need to recover moving forward.
It's been a whirlwind of a year for Jaylon Moore. Entering the offseason, he seemed to be the unquestioned starter at the right tackle spot. Throughout the summer and into training camp and the preseason, though, undrafted rookie free agent Kahlil Benson was given competitive reps . Benson then wound up being the starting left tackle due to Josh Simmons not being available , leaving Moore to assume his normal post and conduct business as usual.
With that said, the standard norm hasn't been good enough for Kansas City.
Moore's surrendered 16 pressures on the year in 231 opportunities, with Week 9 being one of his worst games to date. The former San Francisco 49ers standout ceded four pressures on Sunday, marking the third time he's done so this campaign. He also appeared to sustain some sort of lower-body injury, which doesn't bode well considering he already was in the NFL's concussion protocol earlier this season.
With L'Jarius Sneed going on the injured reserve list , that left the door open for fourth-round rookie Jadon Canady to earn some snaps in the slot and find a role in Steve Spagnuolo's defense. He took the opportunity and ran with it in Week 8's loss to the Denver Broncos, playing seven snaps but maximizing them by way of impact. That trend didn't hold this time around, primarily due to shortcomings in the other phase of the game.
In an expanded workload, the Oregon product was a non-factor in coverage and also flopped twice on special teams. The first mishap came on a punt return by Jets wide receiver Isaiah Williams, as Canady missed a tackle and effectively got his ankles broken on an 18-yard bring-back. Later on, he committed a holding infraction on a 69-yard return from Chiefs receiver Nikko Remigio that wiped out the play entirely.
Oftentimes, the way to more playing time on offense or defense in Kansas City is special teams. Canady will have to keep that in mind and shape up his play if he wants to earn continued reps.
This inclusion is twofold. Fifth-round rookie receiver Cyrus Allen has long been praised by those in Chiefs circles as a potential answer at the wide receiver spot, and he started to generate some momentum in his last three pre-Week 9 games when he combined for five receptions and 65 yards. Unfortunately, both his snap count and level of output decreased on Sunday against the Jets.
A week removed from logging a career-high 31 snaps, Allen's total fell to just 19, and that's even with Xavier Worthy going down with a hamstring ailment . The Cincinnati man was targeted only once in the passing game and committed a special teams error when he coughed up the first kickoff to Kansas City. The team is still confident in his ability to affect the game in multiple aspects, although he took a step back here.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Could KC Free Up Space by Cutting Harrison Butker?
full_text:
We've been tracking all of the Chiefs' trade deadline reports and rumors here on Chiefs On SI , but in this edition of the Chiefs On SI mailbag , we're focusing on some familiar names to see where the Chiefs stand at the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season.
Every week, we take your questions on Twitter/X and BlueSky to see what queries bubble up from around Chiefs Kingdom. Even at 6-2, there are plenty of areas for improvement for this Kansas City squad.
What would it cost KC to release Butker? - @mrscecilwade.bsky.social
This is part of the issue with Harrison Butker's recent struggles; cutting him wouldn't help the cap situation at all for the 2026 season.
Butker's entire 2026 salary is fully guaranteed , meaning that there's nothing to be financially gained by releasing him. If the Chiefs do cut Butker this season, it would be solely for the sake of opening a 53-man roster spot; his $7.3 million cap hit isn't decreasing. If they part ways with Butker any time before next season, he would have a $2.8 million dead cap hit in 2027, accounting for the remainder of his prorated signing bonus.
Who are the real Chiefs? The first-half Chiefs or the second-half? - @ReidsNuggies
That's the beautiful thing about this sport: they're both the real Chiefs!
The version of the Kansas City defense that allowed the New York Jets to march down the field before holding New York to a series of field goals? We've seen that kind of bend-but-don't-break defense from Steve Spagnoulo's unit many times this year and in the recent past. The pass rush that recorded five sacks against a quarterback who holds the ball too long? We've seen that before, too!
Are Creed Humphrey's snaps a recurring problem? Yep. The undeniable issues at offensive tackle that almost got Patrick Mahomes injured? Seen it. The dominant rushing effort on the ground with that same O-line and Kenneth Walker? That's familiar. Being (overly) reliant on age-37 Travis Kelce, but still scoring 35 points with him as your leading receiver? That's the Chiefs, too.
We'll take a closer look at the pass rush with the next question, but as is usually the case, teams are a collection of all the moments—good and bad—that make up their season. The Chiefs are flawed in some key areas, and they're also 6-2 and quarterbacked by Mahomes.
Can the D-line keep up what we saw, or was that a matchup thing? - @chefnewgaard.bsky.social
Hopefully, a little bit of both! We knew that Geno Smith entered that game tied as the second-most-sacked quarterback in the league this year, but we had also seen the Chiefs' pass rush underperform against often-hit quarterbacks at other times this season, so I don't think Sunday's five-sack effort needs to be downplayed. That's still a huge positive step forward , even if it was "supposed" to happen that way. Still, there's more work to be done; the KC pass rush will need to put up similar efforts against Atlanta and Arizona before they're tested by Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving.
Is a Kareem Hunt signing a possibility to fix the short yardage issues? - @KCARROWHEAD29
It seems like the time for a Kareem Hunt reunion has probably passed, but I've had this same thought many times this season. Heck, even after signing Kenneth Walker and drafting Emmett Johnson, I wondered if Hunt would at least get a chance to spend training camp with the Chiefs before taking a practice squad spot, similarly to how Clyde Edwards-Helaire hung around on the practice squad in 2025.
With Brashard Smith on injured reserve and undrafted rookie Jaydn Ott on the active roster, I'm still at least slightly curious about a Hunt reunion, even though it feels more unlikely with every passing week. Hunt obviously doesn't have much tread left on the proverbial tires, but he seemed to have a uniquely excellent ability to find first downs in short-yardage situations, and the Chiefs would be 7-1 if they could have executed a short-yardage score against Denver. I'd also assume that Hunt would still be a viable pass protector on third downs, which was the other reason I half-expected to see him with the team in St. Joseph this summer.
For all of the Chiefs' frequent reunions with former players who are a few years past their prime, this was one that I would've understood, though I doubt we see it at this stage unless there's another injury in the running back room.

title: Chiefs Trade Deadline Tracker: Latest Moves, Rumors, Reports for Kansas City
full_text:
The sands are rapidly passing through to the bottom of the hourglass as time continues to tick for the Kansas City Chiefs to send away or add players at the 2026 NFL trade deadline .
By 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, general manager Brett Veach must notify the league office of any pending moves or otherwise not be able to make swaps until the offseason. After a bit of a down period, Monday saw plenty of trade activity throughout the sport, and Tuesday figures to bring more of the same.
With multiple holes on the roster and plenty of 2027 NFL Draft capital at its disposal, will Kansas City strike while the iron's hot and find a way to improve a 6-2 team? In a wide-open AFC race, it may be wise to do so.
Follow along with our Chiefs trade deadline tracker for the latest rumors, news and reports prior to this afternoon's cutoff. You'll also find a history of how KC's approached the deadline, as well as which positions need to be addressed the most.
Just over 20 minutes before the deadline, the Chiefs landed their man. Per Jordan Schultz , Kansas City is adding Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs and a seventh-round pick in exchange for a fourth-round pick and fifth-round pick.
Downs, who is on an expiring rookie contract, is primarily a slot option who has 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown this season. His best year came in 2024, when he hauled in 72 passes for 803 yards and five scores.
Read more about the Downs addition here.
Sources: It’s a 4th and 5 for Josh Downs to the #Colts , and a 7 back to the #Chiefs . https://t.co/LdmrHAkNPX
Be sure to check our Chiefs trade deadline tracker throughout the day for continued updates to find out whether Veach strikes gold.
It wouldn't be a trade deadline without the pot being stirred on the local and national scenes. Here's the latest buzz on who the Chiefs could be targeting, what it may cost and how likely a deal is to be made. The most recent discourse is up top.
In a series of tweets on Tuesday afternoon less than two hours before the deadline, Arrowhead Corner summarized part of a radio segment from Nate Taylor of ESPN on local radio station 96.5 The Fan in Kansas City.
Per one post , Taylor said Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs "wants to play" for the Chiefs. In another, it's revealed that it's "Downs or bust" for KC.
. @ByNateTaylor says it’s Josh Downs or bust now for the #Chiefs at the NFL trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/Xg3naNCMpn
On a Monday episode of "The Aftermath" on NFL Network , insider Ian Rapoport revealed that Kansas City has been eyeing Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. for a while now.
"For the Kansas City Chiefs, they have been interested in Brian Thomas Jr. for some time, even going back to last year," Rapoport said. "It feels like a matter of when, not if. We just don't know if that's something that's going to happen this season or maybe in the offseason.
"As we've discussed, one of the issues for the Jaguars is how much do they want to help a team that could potentially be someone they would see down the road? He does seem to be — Brian Thomas Jr. seems to be — the player that is garnering the most interest on the receiver market."
From The Aftermath on @nflnetwork : How willing are the #Colts to make trades? pic.twitter.com/kBErOWP7NX
During Sunday's Week 9 triumph over the New York Jets , CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson relayed some of her conversation with Veach. While Kansas City didn't necessarily get the news it wanted regarding a big-name wide receiver trade, the front office planned to keep pushing forward into Tuesday.
"Guys, we've been talking about the lack of deep threats for the Chiefs," Wolfson began. "I spoke with GM Brett Veach before the game. He told me that as the trade deadline approaches, the focus continues to be at that wide receiver position.
"There has been increased dialogue this week, and he found that some of the major franchise players they looked at are off the market. But they will continue to have conversations over the next 24 hours to see if they can get something done by the trade deadline."
With the trade deadline approaching, Chiefs GM Brett Veach told @tracywolfson the team will continue to have conversations with the focus being on a move for a wide receiver. pic.twitter.com/xNs8WaQzcZ
In a November 7 story for The Athletic , Jonathan Jones dove into his latest intel from around the league. Regarding moves he felt were "more likely than not to happen," he issued a prediction that the Chiefs "will have a new wide receiver" by the time the deadline passes.
Jones added that multiple sources told him the Chiefs sought after a "big-name receiver," although a rival executive told him the club is "checking on everyone." Downs continues to be the flavor of the week here .
Earlier in his Chiefs tenure, Veach constructed a reputation for overcorrecting during the offseason and handing out early-round picks to opposing front offices like candy in exchange for their established talents. He's since shifted to a different extreme approach, making gutsy calls to swap out some stars for more NFL Draft capital and, thus, more bites out of the apple.
Examples of the former are trades for defensive end Frank Clark (2019) and left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. (2021). On the latter side, think of Kansas City moving wide receiver Tyreek Hill to the Miami Dolphins (2022) and cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Los Angeles Rams (2026).
Those were all offseason moves, though. Here's a breakdown of every in-season trade Veach has made dating back to the beginning of his time with the organization as general manager.
Here are the most pressing areas of need for Veach and company to consider at the deadline, ranked in order of how much an addition would help.
Wide receiver: The wideout spot is far and away the biggest position to go after if you're the Chiefs. Given the extended absence of Tyquan Thornton and the recent injury to Xavier Worthy , it only makes more sense. There are numerous names available , although not all of them are true needle-movers.
Offensive tackle: Kansas City is backed into a tough spot here. The club has already moved for Joshua Ezeudu via trade earlier this year and added Diego Pounds in the same fashion, so investing more seems silly. There's also the question of whether left tackle Josh Simmons will eventually return from injury . Still, an improvement over one of Kahlil Benson or Jaylon Moore would be a big-time boost.
Defensive end: In Week 9's win over the Jets, the Chiefs enjoyed a five-sack performance that flashed the ceiling of their pass rush. With that said, it was against an offensive line and quarterback who are notorious for finding themselves in that position. Another nice piece at the defensive end spot is a nice idea, although the easiest solution could simply be giving rookie R Mason Thomas more reps.
Tight end: Travis Kelce isn't getting any younger and might be entering the home stretch of his final NFL season. Behind him, Noah Gray is a well below-average blocker. Jake Briningstool has all of three catches on five targets this year.
Linebacker: With NFL teams seeming to live in their subpackages, the Chiefs don't have a true need for a third linebacker. That said, it's never a bad idea to invest in some depth, especially with Drue Tranquill in the final year of his contract.

title: Chiefs Receive Promising Injury News About Patrick Mahomes With Andy Reid’s Latest Update
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs were able to get back into the win column yesterday against the Jets, several key players went down with injuries. The most concerning was undoubtedly the one suffered by Patrick Mahomes .
On a dropback in the second quarter, Mahomes got tangled up awkwardly with Jets rookie David Bailey , resulting in a strip sack that NY recovered. After the play, the Chiefs' superstar signal-caller was in considerable pain, limping off the field as he favored his right arm.
Although Mahomes returned to the game without missing a single offensive snap, he spent much of the afternoon in game-manager mode with Kansas City winning comfortably. There were still questions about whether he'd miss any time once the adrenaline wore off. Head coach Andy Reid referred to the injury as one in the "elbow region" following the victory, though he was unable to provide a definitive diagnosis. Today, Chiefs fans received much more clarity regarding the situation during Reid's press conference.
"Patrick, he's really day-to-day right now. It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick," Reid told the media on Monday . "It looks like it's just a matter of some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We'll just see where it goes from there, but he's in good spirits today. I have seen him today, so he's in good spirits."
Patrick Mahomes comes off the field in pain with an apparent injury to his throwing arm following a turnover pic.twitter.com/5fsqKGPaFz
Mahomes underwent a subsequent MRI scan yesterday, which thankfully revealed no structural ligament damage. That aligns with Reid calling him "day-to-day" for the time being.
Even if the three-time Super Bowl champion feels lingering effects from the elbow ailment, it sounds like he plans to suit up next Sunday versus the Falcons regardless. He echoed that sentiment when he spoke to reporters after the victory. "If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes confirmed. "That's part of the game, that's part of playing. It scares you in moments where you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn't feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and then was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."
The Chiefs are obviously going to remain cautious with Mahomes considering he's less than a year removed from a major knee injury , but it appears they avoided the worst-case scenario with yesterday's brief scare. "We'll see where he's at [Wednesday]," Reid later added. "He feels pretty good today. He's sore, but I'm glad we're not practicing today."

title: Is the Chiefs' Pass Rush Fixed After Five-Sack Performance vs. Jets?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' pass rush has been a significant topic throughout the 2026 season, often due to disappointing zero-sack games littered throughout the first half of the year. On Sunday against the New York Jets , the defensive line came alive, sacking Geno Smith five times in a blowout victory. So, is the Chiefs' pass rush fully fixed? It's not quite that simple.
First and foremost, it was a great day at the office for Kansas City's pass rushers , particularly Chris Jones and George Karlaftis, who each recorded two sacks. That doubled Karlaftis' season total after entering the game with two sacks on the year, and Jones recorded his first full sacks of the season, bringing him to 2.5 in 2026. Add in one sack from Ashton Gillotte, and you've got the Chiefs' most productive day of quarterback-wrangling in quite some time.
The pressure also wasn't fluky or due to particularly horrendous quarterback play. According to TruMedia , Jones and Karlaftis each had six pressures, while Gillotte had five . Jones was the highest-graded Chief on either side of the ball by Pro Football Focus , and rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas got 28 snaps (44%), a small uptick from his lower-usage dips in Seattle and Denver (29% and 27%, respectively).
It's also worth noting that the Chiefs were without both of their first-round rookies, defensive tackle Peter Woods and cornerback Mansoor Delane . Woods could have helped add more pressure on Smith, while Delane's performance in the secondary theoretically would've bought the D-line even more time to get after the quarterback. I'm not going to adjust for hypothetical sacks, but it's nice to see that performance come at less than full-strength.
That's a lot of positive takeaways. Great day of work for the KC D-line. No notes on this performance. All good things. ...So, are we ready for the other side of the coin?
#Chiefs sacks by week this season 📊 Week 1 — 4 Week 2 — 0 Week 3 — 0 Week 4 — 0 Week 5 — BYE Week 6 — 4 Week 7 — 0 Week 8 — 1 Week 9 — 5 pic.twitter.com/cyYKuTpWYQ
The Chiefs now have 14 sacks in 2026, still the fourth-fewest in the league . Incredibly, 13 of those sacks have come in three games: Week 1 against the Denver Broncos (four), Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers (four), and Sunday against the Jets (five).
In the season-opener, Bo Nix was flummoxed. Against LA, Justin Herbert was playing behind a battered O-line and in an impossibly toothless offense. Against New York, Smith entered the game tied for the second-most sacks taken by any quarterback this season. I wrote about this exact possibility on Saturday.
"It would be a good sign to see them bring Smith down early and often on Sunday, but that's a matchup where the Chiefs should be able to pad their stats," I wrote. "Even if they do find their footing against Smith, they'll have to do it again against better offenses down the stretch."
As impressive as Sunday's performance was, I can't strike any of those comments from the record. That's all still true. Another zero-sack performance would have been disastrous. A mere one-or-two-sack day would have been uninspiring. Five is a stupendous effort, but it's also the second five-sack game the Jets have surrendered this year .
Where does that leave the Chiefs' pass rush? In a much better place than it was before this game, but not all the way to a place of non-concern. I'm hugely encouraged by Jones' performance, seemingly proving that there's still a game-wrecking version of Jones to be found in his age-32 season, and I'm continually impressed by Karalftis' growth as a well-rounded defensive end who is under contract with the Chiefs with a series of reasonable cap hits through the 2030 season .
Led by the stars of the defensive line, the Chiefs did everything you could want from a pressure perspective on Sunday against the Jets. Now, they just have to continue to find multi-sack performances against better lines, better quarterbacks, and better teams.

title: Where the Chiefs Stand Before the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs find themselves in a complex space with the 2026 NFL trade deadline on the horizon. While the club is 6-2 and looks like a team with a Super Bowl ceiling, the roster's talent and health at certain positions raise questions about that upside.
Add in a pair of recent losses to perceived contenders, and it becomes a tricky exercise when attempting to nail down what this year's Kansas City squad truly is. One way to help gain clarity, however, could be making a trade before it's too late.
Ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, let's dive into everything you need to know from a Chiefs perspective, ranging from available capital to ideal fits and much more.
The 2026 NFL trade deadline, in the blink of an eye, is almost here. Each trade-related transaction must be filed with the league office by 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. Make that 3 p.m. CT for those working from the offices up at Arrowhead Stadium.
Some moves may trickle in and be reported after the deadline has passed, which is commonplace in several other sports as well. Expect some potential chaos and perhaps a buzzer-beater or two, in addition to news of trades thats were close but never quite manifested.
One important note is that after the trade deadline and for the remainder of the season, all players become subject to the waiver claim system if released. That includes vested veterans, those with at least four accrued seasons, who would've otherwise gone straight into the free agent pool before the Tuesday cutoff.
Let's break this down into two buckets. One of them is a lot more positive than the other.
Getting the bad part out of the way, the Chiefs simply don't have the funds to make a splash for the type of player many are seeking right now. Estimates for their available salary cap space vary. The NFLPA's public salary cap report , for example, puts Veach at having $1.36M to work with. Spotrac is a bit kinder at rounding up to $1.4M, whereas Over the Cap swings the pendulum in the opposite direction ($1.08M).
There are certain in-season levers that can be pulled to create space, but wiggle room is tough to come by this time of year.
Picks are a totally different story. While it's hard to see Veach parting ways with a first- or second-rounder at this juncture, he's currently projected to possess two picks each in the third and fourth rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft. He also has some picks to swap late on Day 3 of the draft.
Add in a decent complement of 2028 NFL Draft selections, and being hung up on not having that kind of capital shouldn't be the case.
It's safe to say Kansas City has a pretty clear hierarchy of needs with the deadline closing in. Using a combination of current depth chart status, health, recent performances and more, here are the top three positions that make at least some sense to add a body for the final stretch of the campaign.
This is easily the most pressing need the Chiefs have with Tuesday's deadline approaching. The wide receiver room was already on thin ice in September, and that was before Rashee Rice failed to recapture his peak form, Tyquan Thornton sustained a significant ankle injury and Xavier Worthy also went down with a hamstring ailment .
With the free agent market not looking good whatsoever, improvement almost has to come by way of a trade unless a reunion with Tyreek Hill is in the cards. We've outlined some of the more realistic options for Veach and Co., although none of them is going to single-handedly save the season.
It may still be worth it to try, though. Many Chiefs fans want a star now, but that's more of an offseason route. The middle ground for 2026-27's purposes has always seemed to be Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts .
The Chiefs' offensive tackle situation is a tough one.
On one hand, undrafted rookie free agent Kahlil Benson started off the season faring better than just about anyone expected, and veteran Jaylon Moore has enjoyed spurts of productive play in the past. On the other hand, Benson seems to be getting exposed more over time. His peer on the right side of the line also isn't holding up and seems to be hobbled.
Jaylon Moore hobbled off the field & threw his helmet in frustration. He appears to have a lower body injury. Joshua Ezeudu is in at right tackle.
Joshua Ezeudu's usage is interesting at best. He was primarily a piece on the left side of the New York Giants' offensive line before coming over via trade , yet he's been filling in for Moore as needed at right tackle. Pickup Diego Pounds isn't seeing the field barring a serious injury to Benson.
All of this said, it's difficult to envision the Chiefs sinking another real asset into the tackle spot prior to free agency or the 2027 NFL Draft. Of course, the simplest way to potentially see some improvement would be former 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons returning from the injured reserve list and finally making his season debut.
This is more of a luxury possibility. If there's a bad team out there that wants to deal a quality role player at the edge rusher spot or an unexpected high-level contributor comes available for an affordable price, the Chiefs would be wise to pick up the phone. The problem is the odds of either path presenting itself seem remarkably low.
The Kansas City pass rush showed a pulse against the New York Jets, getting to quarterback Geno Smith five times and making an impact on late downs. Star defensive tackle Chris Jones led the way with a pair of sacks , and players like George Karlaftis and Ashton Gillotte also held up their respective ends of the bargain.
It's clear that the latter two are useful players for the defensive end role. There's also the versatility that Jones provides along the defensive front, on top of the same possibilities with former first-rounder Felix Anudike-Uzomah. Should 2025 second-round tackle Omarr Norman-Lott come off the physically unable to perform list , coordinator Steve Spagnuolo would have even more avenues to go down.
That's without mentioning rookie R Mason Thomas , who's as twitched-up and intriguing as any player up front for the Chiefs. It isn't like the team doesn't have a need for more production in the sack department, but the cupboard also isn't bare.
An honorable mention goes to the prospect of landing a nice backup tight end who's a capable blocker. Noah Gray has flashed his pass-catching chops on occasion, but there isn't much depth at the position right now and KC isn't using fullback Ben VanSumeren like many had hoped.
If we're cheating and extending this list to five spots, I'd add linebacker.
According to head coach Andy Reid last week, he and Veach began the discussion process for potential trades "about a month ago." Although these aren't the days of Reid being the executive vice president of football operations like he experienced with the Philadelphia Eagles, he still gets considerable pull when it comes to transactions.
Reid trusts Veach to get the job done if there's a trade to be made.
"Brett does all of that," Reid said. "If he gets to a point where something is up and he feels comfortable about it, then he hits me up on it. He takes care of all of that. Those guys — you know how Brett is wired. He’s endlessly looking for people and trying to bring people on to make us better. That’s how he goes about it.”
Following Sunday's win over the Jets , quarterback Patrick Mahomes echoed a similar sentiment. He has faith in the decision-makers to do the right thing, but he's also confident in the club's internal options if no swaps occur by the deadline.
"I leave that all up to Veach and coach Reid," Mahomes said. "Whoever's in that building, I go out there and try to make the most of it and win football games. I think we've done a great job of that with a lot of different guys. I see the work these guys put in every single day, and they're ready. They're ready to go out there and make plays when their number is called. I leave that up to those guys."

title: The Winners and Losers of Week 9’s Chiefs win over the Jets
full_text:
It may have taken two quarters to put away the now 2-7 New York Jets, but once again, you never apologize for a win in the NFL. The Chiefs dominated the second half after taking a 14-12 lead into the break.
They led 28-12 by the end of the third after the defense allowed minus nine yards and the offense exploded even after a short-lived Mahomes health scare. A late fourth-quarter Emmett Johnson touchdown run sealed the 35-12 win. That score, especially, is one you don’t apologize for, no matter the opponent.
The game was a mixed bag of some hopeful signs of things to come and some frustrations boiling over from recent weeks. Let’s dive into the winners and losers of Week 9.
Defensive tackle Chris Jones 2026 season has officially begun. Week 9 came a little later than expected, but after coming into the game with .5 sacks through seven games, he took down quarterback Geno Smith twice in this game alone. And en route to it, he became the Chiefs' second all-time sack leader with 90 sacks, surpassing Tamba Hali
The first came late in the second quarter. On a third-and-six, Jones dominated a one-on-one situation, pushing the Jets back to a long 53-yard field goal. Jets kicker Jason Sanders was 4-for-4 up to that point, but this one was just far enough to force his first miss. With a make, New York would have gone into halftime up 15-14.
The second one also came on a third down, forcing a punt late in the fourth quarter, a stop that preceded Johnson putting the game away with his touchdown run. Two sacks on third downs are something the Kansas City could have used in their loss to Denver last week. For the Chiefs, hopefully it is a sign of things to come as the second half of the season arrives.
There was a real, heavy moment in this game when some inside Chiefs Kingdom felt the season was sabotaged. The Chiefs led 14-12 against a team they were heavy favorites to beat, and then the biggest scare of the afternoon happened.
Right tackle Jaylon Moore was beaten badly by 2026’s second-overall pick, defensive end David Bailey, and as Mahomes was letting it rip, Bailey violently strip-sacked his fellow Texas Tech alumnus. The mid-throw hit on his elbow put him in obvious pain as he walked off the field with his right arm limp after the Jets recovered the fumble.
As bad as it looked, he didn't miss a single offensive play, even completing a 12-yard pass to tight end Travis Kelce moments later. After the game, additional testing revealed no significant damage, and he was described as having an elbow strain/sprain.
Based on the three touchdown drives he led after the injury, he appears to be in good shape moving forward. Mahomes ended the day going 23-for-31, 242 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Chiefs Kingdom can take a sigh of relief.
After two subpar performances against the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos, star running back Kenneth Walker looked as he did in the first five games of the season. He took 18 carries for 102 yards and scored on a short-yardage touchdown run.
There was one distinct difference, however. This was not one of those games where Walker was a complete magician, forcing double-digit missed tackles. The offensive line was powerful and cohesive, creating massive holes for Walker to run through.
They struggled mightily in pass protection at times, especially the offensive tackles , though guards Trey Smith and Kingsley Suamataia made way with terrific blocks downfield on a 25-yard screen pass that Walker caught for a touchdown. Both Walker and Emmett Johnson averaged 5.7 yards per carry, and they forced only three missed tackles combined, which is a hopeful sign for the big boys up front.
Following Sunday’s game, kicker Harrison Butker is now 12-for-19 in field goal attempts for the season. So far, he's been perfect in only 2 of 8 games, and even then, he went 1-for-1 in both instances.
You have to go back to Week 4 to find a game where Butker didn't miss a kick. With Week 10 on the horizon, Butker’s display this week against New York may have been the most illustrative of how bad things have gotten.
With seconds left in the first half, Butker attempted a 56-yarder that clanked off the upright, but the Jets jumped offsides, giving him a shot from 51 yards. That attempt went completely wide right. He made all five of his extra points, but with how little confidence anyone has in Butker to make a kick, you have to wonder if they will activate Justin Tucker next week in Atlanta.
The Chiefs put 35 points on the board while missing a field goal and turning it over twice, which is fairly impressive. Kansas City came into the game top-five in the NFL in giving the ball away, but they struggled in that area in this Sunday noon game, putting the ball on the ground five times.
The first two fumbles came on the game’s opening drive. In the first return opportunity of his career, rookie receiver Cyrus Allen fumbled the Chiefs' opening kickoff, luckily with linebacker Jeffrey Bassa there to recover. The other was on the ensuing third-and-one when head coach Andy Reid called for a quarterback sneak featuring Justin Fields, and the snap never fully made it into his hands. This time, Kansas City was not so lucky, as linebacker Demario Davis recovered, giving the Jets a 6-0 lead moments later.
Speaking of poor center-to-quarterback exchanges, Creed Humphrey again put the ball out of shotgun for his seventh fumble this season. It was ultimately a drive-killer, leading to one of the Chiefs' three punts on the afternoon. Mahomes fumbled twice on the same drive, and Bailey forced it both times. Moore recovered the first one after giving up the sack. These are unlikely to become trends, but they do help explain the Chiefs' slow start to the ballgame.
The Chiefs faced plenty of questions last week when they marched down the field with less than two minutes to go, clear to the Denver Broncos' 4-yard line with a chance to win the game. The heat came when the Chiefs ran three plays from the 1-yard line.
On third-and-fourth-and-one, quarterback sneaks convert well over 80 percent of the time in the NFL, a much higher success rate than traditional runs or passes. On the two particular plays Kansas City had a shot at last week, it appeared that Mahomes could merely waltz into the end zone in between Humphrey and Smith. Instead, the Chiefs threw an incompletion and had Walker get stuffed, leaving room for criticism.
The Chiefs have not run a sneak with Mahomes taking the snap since 2019, when he injured his knee on the play. He didn't run it today either, but Reid called for it with Fields under center on the very first drive of the game, and to say it went poorly would be an understatement. Fields fumbled before he could even try to get a push. With it being such an easy button around the league, hopefully Reid and company will examine the play for next time, rather than abandon it altogether.

title: Chargers Winners and Losers After the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has finally passed, with all 32 NFL teams now unable to make trades with one another to help improve their current or future rosters. The deadline is often an exciting time, considering that change and, by virtue of it, hope can occur.
This hope was desperately needed from the Bolts, with the team being 0-8 and coming off an absolutely horrid blowout loss to the now 3-5 Houston Texans.
General manager Joe Hortiz opted to make one move at the deadline, trading away Daiyan Henley to divisional rival Denver Broncos in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Henley has been a vocal leader for the Bolts since his breakout season in 2024 but has unfortunately regressed on the field since then. This gave the Chargers the opportunity to trade him away and opt to play other individuals...some of whom will be on this list as a winner.
Marlowe Wax is the first name that should come to mind as a winner for the Chargers post-NFL trade deadline. Before Henley was traded away, Wax was already climbing up the depth chart, playing more and more in the LB rotation.
Now that Henley is gone, Wax should be expected to start and/or see a major increase in playing time, even with Denzel Perryman being expected to return from injured reserve.  So far this season, in his limited snaps (48 total), Wax has recorded 15 tackles and a pass deflection, which resulted in an interception...coincidentally for Henley.
Omarion Hampton is considered a "loser" in this scenario as both Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal both remained on the roster after the trade deadline. Both RBs are young with production, giving reason for them to be traded to a team that could use a rushing threat.
Instead, they remain on the roster, which I believe to be the right move. However, this still means that Hampton will be splitting carries with Mitchell and Vidal, making his sophomore-slump likely to continue for the rest of the NFL season.
RJ Mickens should be considered a winner after the deadline, as he should be expected to see a small uptick in snaps. With Henley being traded away, this will likely prompt the Bolts to play more dime packages or packages that see fellow safety Tony Jefferson playing closer to the line of scrimmage in an LB-esque role, giving Mickens more opportunities on defense.
Akheem Mesidor has been quite solid in his rookie year, showing flashes as the team's third EDGE rusher. Unfortunately, the team is 0-8 and no one is talking about how well he is playing. With more playing time, that could have changed, but for Mesidor, it seems his role will stay the same post-NFL trade deadline due to the Bolts' best and most talked-about trade asset, Khalil Mack, not being traded to a contending team.

title: Chargers’ Daiyan Henley Trade Deadline Deal is a Weird Gamble
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers didn’t put up a white flag and admit a tank job by trading away Daiyan Henley at Tuesday's deadline.
The Chargers didn't just trade away Henley: They gave away one of the core locker room leaders…to an AFC West rival. And the move would seem to imply that the front office has tried, or didn’t think it would be able to work out a contract extension with him.
It’s a pretty shocking thing for the Chargers to do on a day most seemed to feel that a Donte Jackson-type player might be dealt. That, or an offer they just couldn't refuse for Khalil Mack.
Henley, though, is a pretty telling gamble on multiple levels.
The Chargers wanted to “send the right message” at the NFL trade deadline.
Keeping Mack but trading Henley makes for an odd message.
No doubt Chargers coaches and brass will window-dress up the move. They like the guys they have on the depth chart like Del-Shawn Phillips and Marlowe Wax. And those guys getting some run down the stretch could be good for their development, sure.
But the Chargers aren’t exactly ever hurting for cap space. Paying up on a Henley extension to keep a core leader around for a rebuild wouldn't have been that big of a deal.
Don’t ask current Chargers players:
https://t.co/z0UhPatIth pic.twitter.com/F7paSo0OQR
There are levels to this. Non-elite linebackers in the NFL are pretty replaceable. Henley has been erratic over the years. But good luck rationalizing that to a winless locker room and a fanbase wanting the Chargers to either go all-in on the sell or just stand still, not this weird middle-road thing.
The Chargers had zero leverage in any trade talks, so it’s probably a miracle they got what they got for Henley. Khalil Mack was the other likely trade piece, but it sure feels like he wants to stick no matter what.
Still, it would be hard to blame someone for accusing the Chargers of making a move just to make a move. Losing a key younger leader with the green dot and doing nothing else is just an odd thing all around, especially to a rival.

title: Chargers Agree to Trade Daiyan Henley to Broncos at NFL Deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers aren't sitting still at the NFL trade deadline after all.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chargers have agreed to send linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick.
The winless Chargers had been adamant for the better part of a monthy that they would not be sellers at the NFL trade deadline. It speaks to how much that has changed that they are willing to trade a leader on defense to an AFC West rival.
Henley, 26, was a third-round pick on the last year of his deal. The Chargers have pleny of future cap space to play with, so this might be a sign that they are open to a big blow up over the offseason.
Across 56 games with the Chargers, Henley totaled 317 tackles, five sacks, one forced fumble and four interceptions. His depature will mean half-season auditions in the base defense for names like Del'Shawn Phillips, Marlowe Wax and others.

title: Chargers’ Trade Deadline Stance Suddenly Changes: Separating Fact From Fiction
full_text:
A Los Angeles Chargers NFL trade deadline tracker feels like a desert void of any life-sustaining water at this point, based on how head coach Jim Harbaugh and anyone else has talked about the idea of making deals before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline.
Harbaugh himself, though, just changed the conversation with one quick little comment.
At 0-8, the Chargers figure to be sellers and eye the future. Widespread rumors put up against Harbaugh’s latest comment, though, keep the waters muddy at best.
All the leaguewide buzz says the Chargers will stand still.
At first, it was easy to suggest that the Chargers didn't want to tip their hand publicly or lose leverage. But reports started coming out that the Chargers’ stance on trades during talks behind the scenes were confusing other teams .
The only report that really made sense about the Chargers was them shooting down trade offers for big names like Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey . If they’re going to sell, it won’t be on foundational building blocks.
Harbaugh changed things during his first presser before the trade deadline.
Speaking with reporters, he hinted that general manager Joe Hortiz will indeed work the phones and keep an eye out for deals.
Harbaugh said Hortiz is “pursuing and active" before adding this: “If something makes sense that will make our team better, now or in the future, Joe Hortiz is going to be open and active in pursuing that."
This is, literally, the first time Harbaugh has given even a hint of the Chargers being open to anything, so it makes things at least a little interesting.
Is the commentary from Harbaugh aimed at easing the concern of fans, just saying the usual coach-speak or something else?
Trading away Khalil Mack makes all the sense in the world. He’s on an expiring contract, still productive and it would be nice to let him go compete for a title with a contender before he possibly retires.
The vibe the whole time on this subject has been that Mack himself doesn’t want to leave. And if the conversation is doing right by Mack , if he wants to stay with the Chargers and the offers on the table aren’t very good anyway, it probably makes sense to have him remain in town.
Here’s the other problem: The Chargers roster stinks .
These Chargers are 0-8 for a reason. Hortiz failed at building it out properly, especially in the offensive trenches. The skill positions are a mess. They have gaslit themselves into rostering late-round picks and even practice squad candidates in key depth roles while trying to contend now and keep plenty of cap space and draft picks for the future. It’s backfired.
The offers coming in for these non-core players (Herbert, McConkey, Alt, Slater, Hampton) aren’t going to be great. And the offers for iffy players with trade value (Henley, James, Tuipulotu) are going to be under proper value too, because the Chargers have zero leverage and other teams view them as a chance to get a discount.
Like any pro organization, the Chargers will pick up the phone and listen. But it’s total fiction to think anything meaningful actually happens when the team probably doesn’t even know if the entire coaching staff will be around next offseason.

title: Chargers Players Rising, Falling After Week 9 Loss, Impact on NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline a few short days away, the Los Angeles Chargers should be the obvious fire-sale franchise of the 2026 season, considering they are the worst team in the NFL, still being winless going into midseason.
The Chargers have continued with the storyline that they do not want to trade away players and want to see if they can turn things around; however, it has to get to a point where reality sets in, and the delusion of winning football games with this coaching staff and roster goes away.
All of this to say, who are some risers and fallers after Week 9, and who could be traded after these players either proved to be a keeper for the roster or an expendable asset?
The Chargers finally did it. They benched Cole Strange, the guard they overpaid for in the open free-agent market. This comes after Strange continued to get obliterated all game long, especially by the hands of the veteran defensive tackle, Sheldon Rankins.
Branson Taylor, finally coming back from injury and after a positive training camp, got the first nod. He looked good in his small stint. Then Alex Harkey subbed in for Taylor, likely starting the guard 'platooning' all over again.
While platooning is still a terrible strategy, both Harkey and Taylor played well, much better than the player they collectively replaced.
Genesis Smith is a fourth-round rookie who has flashed early in the season, even having a multi-interception game against Josh Allen and the Bills. Since then, he has been terrible in coverage, which was supposed to be his strength coming into the NFL.
Massive coverage busts, poor angles, bad tackling -- it has all plagued Smith. It seemed to manifest the most in this loss against the Texans, with CJ Stroud throwing for 384 yards. It should be noted that Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley were also awful, surely not helping Smith's case.
Marlowe Wax has always flashed when given the opportunity to play. More of the same occurred during Week 9 against the Texans, batting a ball in the air which allowed for Daiyan Henley to collect an interception.
Wax also had eight tackles, giving all the reason for the Bolts to play the young LB more and more, especially considering how poor the linebacker room has been.
Finally, everyone's favorite offensive lineman on the Chargers, Cole Strange. After a horrid first half, Strange was finally benched in favor of the aforementioned Taylor and Harkey. The offense still did not play well, but it was at least a band-aid on the bleeding wound that is this Mike McDaniel offensive unit.
With these risers and fallers, a few names emerge as possible trade-away candidates heading into Tuesday's deadline.
Daiyan Henley: Once a rising star, but has yet to see those 2024 heights. With Wax playing well, it would be smart for the Bolts to take what they can get from their poorly-performing LB who has really only offered vocal leadership this season.
Dalvin Tomlinson: While there was no mention on Tomlinson or those on the DL in this article, he deserved an honorable mention for his play against the run today. Tomlinson is 32 and deserves to contend. After his strong performance, sell high.
Donte Jackson: Another veteran DB who has underperformed this season. He has a strong resume as a DB and could be moved for a late Day 3 selection . The only issue is that the team is dealing with a plethora of injuries at the position and would need to find names off the street to fill their roster.

title: Time for Chargers to Have Uncomfortable Ladd McConkey Conversation After Latest Injury
full_text:
When it comes to the Los Angeles Chargers , it’s all eyes on whether they will be big sellers at the NFL trade deadline and the possible hot seats of Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel.
Don’t forget, unfortunately, the latest Justin Herbert injury that could cost the star quarterback time.
There are other issues, too, but there’s one to circle in red way down the list that deserves more attention than it’s getting right now: Ladd McConkey is hurt again .
The latest Ladd McConkey injury was one of the strangest yet.
McConkey wasn’t a major point of concern on the injury report all week, which in of itself is pretty rare now. But by the time the game kicked off, the Chargers had already ruled him "questionable" to return. Only reporting later attempted to clear the air: He was dealing with back spasms during pregame warmups.
So, the uncomfortable McConkey topic: He’s not reliable.
The Chargers are 0-8. When thinking about long-term building blocks, McConkey’s name should be right there next to guys like Herbert, Joe Alt, Omarion Hampton and Tuli Tuipulotu, to name a few.
McConkey is about to turn just 25 years old and is on a rookie contract. He should make that list. But frankly, he’s regressed statistically every single season since his rookie debut (82 catches, 1,149 yards, seven scores) and questions about his size (listed at 185 pounds, 6’0”) seem warranted after the injuries have piled up.
McConkey has a massive list of injuries, soft-tissue and otherwise, on the resume. In no special order, we’re talking about knee strains, calf strains, rib fractures, concussions, foot injuries and now this back issue.
Limited attendance here disrupts both McConkey and the Chargers’ offense. He played 73 percent of the snaps over 14 starts as a rookie. He played 78 percent over 12 starts last year. He’s started just three games in 2026 at 53 percent of the snaps.
There are obviously other major problems for the Chargers across the board. And there’s a conversation about the organization's training and approach to injury prevention worth having, too, because the injury rate in Los Angeles on an annual basis borders on preposterous.
But specifically with McConkey, it makes him unreliable. Quentin Johnston has drop issues and Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith haven’t fully emerged. McConkey should be the No. 1 and a critical piece.
Going into a draft where the Chargers might pick first and get Jeremiah Smith to pair with McConkey, that sounds good. But so did bringing McDaniel to Los Angeles to help Herbert.
Realistically, the Chargers have very few proper building blocks for three-plus years down the road right now. And things have hit a point with McConkey where it’s even worth questioning if he classifies as one of those.

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers Defense Breaks as Offense Watches Helplessly
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel tried a new approach against the Texans. McDaniel moved from on the field to the booth to call the game, the results were the same. The Chargers lost, again.
The Chargers' trainwreck of season continued in week nine against the Houston Texans. The final score of the game was 44-22; a final score that makes the game feel more competitive than it actually was. Los Angeles has now fallen to 0-8 on the season.
The Chargers offense continues to be unable to score and remains frustratingly inefficient. Despite being winless on the season, head coach Jim Harbaugh is not adjusting his coaching style, he maintains a conversative approach, opting for field goals instead of going for fourth-down attempts.
Los Angeles' defense has been the lone bright spot for the team this season. The defense has consistently put their best foot forward and gone to battle week in and week out despite the offense not holding up their end of the bargain. The defense was bound to have a bad day at the office and that day came this week against the Texans. Houston quarterback CJ Stroud appeared dialed in and carved up the Chargers defense. Even when the coverage was perfect, passes were still caught.
NICO COLLINS, ARE YOU KIDDING ME?!? 🤯 (via @HoustonTexans ) pic.twitter.com/zv7Zrgbuf0
There were several developments that happened before, during and after this beat down that are worth discussing for the Chargers. Let's dive into the biggest takeaways.
Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has dealt with every injury imaginable this season and his role in Mike McDaniel's offense has left him downrange for massive hits across the middle. He played only his second full game of 2026 in week eight afte coming off a bye. McConkey experienced back spasms in pregame warm ups in Week 9 and did not play a single snap against the Texans.
Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz brought in Cole Strange and gave him a low-level starters contract to be the Chargers new right guard after spending most of the season with Mike McDaniel and the Miami Dolphins in 2025. Everyone outside of the Chargers building suspected this may not go well.
It is not breaking news that the Cole Strange experiment has been awful. He has been the worst offensive lineman the Chargers have had on the field this season and the grades make that clear. Still, the Chargers rolled him out there every week but finally Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins took him behind the woodshed today, to the point where the broadcast was nearly laughing about how bad he was being beaten on a down to down basis.
The Chargers finally pulled him and rotated Branson Taylor and rookie Alex Harkey. Head coach Jim Harbaugh did say that Strange may have lost his starting job and they will look at it this week.
After 37 consecutive drives, the Chargers finally scored a touchdown as Quentin Johnston broke a tackle and broke free for a 57 yard catch and run. When asked about the streak ending, tight end Charlie Kolar had no idea it had been that many drives without a touchdown.
#Chargers TE Charlie Kolar had no idea the offensive did not score in 37 straight drives. 💀😅 “37!?” Kolar said. “I wish you never told me that.” @SportingTrib | #BoltUp pic.twitter.com/nlcpzub7TS
It appears breaking a bone now appears to be an annual tradition for Justin Herbert. Late in the third quarter Herbert stiffed armed away a would be sack and immediately looked down at his finger. In true Justin Herbert fashion, he did not come out of the game and actually finished the drive with the touchdown to Quentin Johnston.
Herbert went to the sideline and the blue medical tent and emerged with a glove with a massive temporary cast on his finger. The specific injury has not been announced but the broadcast did capture his finger pointing in an unnatural direction. Backup quarterback DJ Uiagalelei finished the game and threw his first career touchdown pass.
The Chargers are driving the NFL world mad with their apparent stance that they will not trade anyone. There is an argument that because the Chargers do not have high-value trade assets, the late Day 3 picks that they could get in return are not worth moving on from as they try to right the ship heading into 2027.
oh but remember, they don't want to make anyone feel discouraged!
It is worth noting that edge rusher Caleb Murphy who has mainly logged special teams snaps since he returned to the Chargers, did function as the fourth edge against the Texans despite Bud Dupree being active. Either Dupree has been demoted or Murphy may be getting a look in the event that Khalil Mack is moved before the trade deadline despite all the public statements that he will not be moved. Dupree has not logged snaps on defense since week five.
All eyes now shift to the Chargers front office ahead of the deadline. Will they still stand pat and move no one? Or will they move a player or two at the deadline?

title: Justin Herbert Injury: How Does Chargers QB’s Setback Impact NFL Trade Deadline?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have fallen to 0-8, already finding themselves in what we all thought was the worst possible situation for the franchise after their semi-successful 2024 and 2025 seasons. Unfortunately, in classic Chargers fashion, it got worse .
Justin Herbert suffered a finger injury , playing through the injury for a few plays, eventually moving to the blue medical tent once the offense was off the field. Once it was time for the offense to go back on the field, Herbert stayed back and found himself on the bench watching backup QB DJ Uiagalelei finish out the blowout loss at the hands of the Houston Texans.
While information has yet to be finalized on the exact injury Herbert has suffered, it seems that the consensus is a broken middle finger on his non-throwing hand. Herbert has played through broken fingers before, but it seems that the team may need time to consider if he should continue to play and risk more injury.
Now, with this hesitancy, this could very well change the Bolts' outlook on the NFL trade deadline, which is right around the corner, being marked as Nov. 10, 2026.
With the Bolts being 0-8, NFL teams were rightfully calling Los Angeles to ask about some of the team's players in hopes of hoping their own roster. The Chargers should be answering those calls and looking to build for their future, not for the 0-8 2026 Chargers.
Unfortunately, Joe Hortiz has seemingly been unwilling to move away from players, with reporters saying the Chargers "still have belief" prior to this Texans loss. Now, with another loss and their star QB injured, can they finally turn the other way and sell off assets?
Of course, only time will tell, but it was only logical when the team was 0-5; it is even more logical with the team being 0-8 and with an injured QB. To go full fire-sale mode, some names to look out for on the trade market:
Khalil Mack: The most spoken-about trade asset . He has mentioned he does not want to be traded, but it is worth mentioning that the veteran EDGE has plenty of value to other teams...if Mack were to change his mind.
Donte Jackson: Another veteran who could have some value for a team in need of a starting-caliber DB. Even with the Chargers having injuries piling up at the position, it could be smart to let young practice squad players play rather than letting Jackson play for no team-related upside.
Dalvin Tomlinson: One of the team's better run defenders could find his way on the market, as he is playing well, is healthy and is 32 years old. The Chargers have other options in Jamaree Caldwell and Nick Barrett who could take some snaps as the position.
Daiyan Henley: A young LB who had a 2024 season filled with promise. He had an interception against the Houston Texans, but he is obviously in need of a fresh start. He could possibly be valued highly around the league considering his age and history of strong play.

title: Where the Chargers Stand 48 Hours Before the  NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are officially at a crossroads. What was supposed to be a season of competing and building momentum has turned into something entirely different. At 0-8, the Chargers have reached a point where simply looking ahead to the next game isn’t enough.
Sunday’s game was another reminder of how much work remains for this team. Eight games into the season, the Bolts still cannot get into rhythm.
Now, general manager Joe Hortiz has to determine what makes the most sense for the organization moving forward. They don’t necessarily need to abandon everything they have been building, but continuing to approach the season as if a turnaround is right around the corner could be a mistake.
One of the biggest questions heading into Tuesday is whether they will seriously consider moving veteran players. I know they are firm on not dealing any of their guys whatsoever.
However, When a team is sitting at 0-8, the conversation surrounding potential trades naturally changes. Players who might have been considered untouchable earlier in the season could suddenly become part of a much larger discussion. With every loss more becomes possible.
Khalil Mack is an interesting name in that conversation. His experience and production make him valuable, especially to teams that believe they have a legitimate opportunity to compete this season.
There is also the question of what the Bolts could realistically receive in return. A trade only makes sense if the compensation matches the value of what the organization is giving up. Accumulating draft picks is important, but those selections eventually have to translate into players who can help change the direction of the franchise.
The same approach should apply to any other veteran who could generate interest around the league. Hortiz needs to evaluate the roster honestly rather than make decisions based solely on the disappointment of the current record.
Perhaps the most important part of this situation is what happens once Tuesday passes. The Chargers still have the remainder of the season to evaluate their roster, develop younger players and determine which areas require the most attention heading into the offseason.
There is no reason to make unnecessary moves simply because the season has gone poorly. However, there is also little reason to ignore opportunities that could improve the team beyond this year. The Chargers have reached a point where the remainder of the season should be about finding answers. Tuesday’s deadline gives the organization its first major opportunity to act on that reality.
Honestly, there's no salvaging the season. The question is whether the decisions made over the next 48 hours can help prevent another season like this one.
The Chargers are reportedly not trading players ahead of the deadline. Per ESPN, they do not want to send the message that they are quitting on the season. I'd argue keeping McDaniel without any adjustments sends a louder message of quitting than flipping expirings for picks. pic.twitter.com/1XxdAW8S7k
