title: Rams Trade Deadline Winners and Losers: Les Snead Fails Matthew Stafford
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams entered the NFL trade deadline desperately needing help at wide receiver. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on injured reserve, the Rams had an opportunity to make a move that could help save their season. Instead, the Rams stood pat with their roster as it was . Here are the biggest winners and losers from the Rams' trade deadline.
This is not the Les Snead that we are accustomed to seeing. The Snead that we’ve seen operate over the past several years would have made a move for a wide receiver, even if it wasn't for a big name. It’s hard to fathom how the offense could lose Puka Nacua for several weeks and the front office could look at the roster and come to the conclusion that it was enough. Not doing anything felt like the Rams are punting on the 2026 season.
There is not a bigger winner than Konata Mumpfield. He is now the top wide receiver on the depth chart and will get an opportunity to show what he can do in a larger role. It’s very clear that the coaching staff likes him in the offense. An argument can be made that Mumpfield hasn’t seen many opportunities because of Stafford’s comfort level with Nacua. Now is his chance to show what he’s capable of.
The Rams failed Matthew Stafford at the trade deadline. They don’t know how many more chances they’re going to get with Stafford and seem to be treating him like a bridge quarterback instead of one that can win them a Super Bowl. They didn't use one of their Day 2 draft picks on a wide receiver or address the position in free agency. In a hot wide receiver market, the Rams once again stood pat at the position and didn’t give Stafford any help. The Rams could have and should have done more for their quarterback.
It will be interesting to see if the Rams utilize CJ Daniels more or if he remains limited in his role. The Rams haven’t used the rookie wide receiver at all in the passing game and this will be his best chance to get involved. Daniels impressed throughout training camp and the preseason. With Adams and Nacua out, it's time to see what he can do.
How can the Rams look at Aaron Donald after this and say they did everything to try and win him one more ring? Donald came out of retirement this season, and it hasn’t gone the way that he expected, to say the least. It took nine weeks for him to finally play alongside Myles Garrett. The Rams owed it to Donald to make this season worth it for him by making a trade at the deadline. Instead, they did nothing.
Once the trade deadline had passed, the Rams announced the signing of Xavier Smith . Smith is back on the roster and presumably will resume his role in the offense and as the team’s primary punt returner. Had the Rams made a move, they may not have brought back Smith. By standing pat, the Rams are relying on a familiar face at the position.
It’s hard to see the Rams surviving the next four games without Puka Nacua and with Davante Adams not at 100 percent. They are entering a grueling part of their schedule in which they will face the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers. To make the playoffs, the Rams likely need to win at least two of those games. That’s a tall task as it stands. It’s going to take Matthew Stafford to play some of his best football of the season

title: Rams Place Another Wide Receiver on Injured Reserve, Bring Back Familiar Face in Xavier Smith
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams didn’t do anything at the trade deadline . However, once the deadline had passed, the team announced that Jordan Whittington had been placed on injured reserve and that it had signed wide receiver Xavier Smith in a corresponding move.
On Tuesday, head coach Sean McVay noted that Whittington had been dealing with some soreness in his back.With Whittington headed to injured reserve, his season is likely over as the Rams won’t have enough return designations to bring him back. Whittington had two catches for 12 yards on the season and was averaging 26.3 yards per kickoff return.
The Rams losing Whittington is another hit to the wide receiver position.They were already without Davante Adams, who has been on injured reserve, and then lost Puka Nacua as well . While Whittington doesn’t offer a lot in the passing game, he is arguably the best blocking wide receiver on the team and provides value on special teams.
Given the current injury situation at wide receiver, the Rams will be relying heavily on their wide receiver depth over the next month. With Nacua and Adams sidelined, players like Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels could take on larger roles. Losing Whittington only makes that situation more difficult.
Still, bringing back Smith is certainly an interesting choice. While Smith has experience in the offense, his size limits what he can offer as a receiver. The Rams previously cut Smith this season as they looked to make improvements at punt returner.
With the Rams needing depth at wide receiver and in need of a punt returner again, it’s possible they saw Smith as the best available option. After cutting Alex Bachman, the Rams had Kyren Williams returning punts against the Washington Commanders.
Smith will likely take Whittington’s place on kick returns and could go back to returning punts as well, despite his previous struggles in that role. It’s possible he could see snaps on offense as well, taking away from Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels.
The Rams opted not to make a move for a receiver at the trade deadline and instead signed Smith. While Smith provides some familiarity with the offense, it's difficult to see how he significantly improves a wide receiver group that was already lacking depth.
Over the last few weeks, the Rams have dealt with a handful of injuries at wide receiver and are running out of options. Smith at least provides someone with experience in the offense. With no outside help coming at the trade deadline, the Rams will have to find a way to make it work with what they have.

title: Grading the Rams NFL Trade Deadline: Was Doing Nothing the Right Decision?
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams found out that wide receiver Puka Nacua was likely to end up on injured reserve , their entire trade deadline plans changed. They went from a team content with waiting to get healthy to one that may need to make a move just to get by.
“I think you have to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up,” said head coach Sean McVay. “A lot of new things occur on a daily basis, so I would never rule it out.”
Despite the injuries that have put their championship hopes in jeopardy, the Rams still have reason to believe they can compete. Nacua will be out at least four weeks, but it will likely be more. When Nacua was out in 2024 with a PCL sprain, he was out for six weeks.
Davante Adams also remains on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury against the Arizona Cardinals. Adams was given a 6-to-10-week timeline with optimism that he could return on the shorter end of that. A six-week timeline would put Adams back following the Rams’ Week 12 matchup with the Packers. Even then, hamstring injuries can be difficult to return from.
Coming into the season, the Rams were seen as a team looking to compete for a Super Bowl. Had the Rams made a move at the trade deadline, it could have been seen as them trying to chase their losses. The Rams went to Vegas and bet the house on themselves to win it all. Each time they’ve won a hand, they’ve lost two more.
At this point, were the Rams better off walking away from the table and accepting their losses, or continuing to throw chips on the table when they had none to lose? Sitting at 5-4 and on the outside looking in at the postseason, it’s possible the Rams realized that the best-case scenario was a first- or second-round playoff exit rather than the championship run they were hoping for.
It makes sense that the Rams wouldn’t want to overpay for Brian Thomas Jr. or trade for an aging Keenan Allen. However, the Kansas City Chiefs traded for Josh Downs for a fourth- and fifth-round pick. That seems like a manageable price.
With that said, it’s hard to fathom this front office and coaching staff looking at a wide receiver depth chart of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, and Jordan Whittington and being content with that. Those four make Brandon Gibson, Tavon Austin, Austin Pettis, and Chris Givens look good.
The Rams may not make the playoffs, but doing nothing at the trade deadline makes it seem as though they’re waving the white flag. The team certainly won’t quit, but the front office has seemingly come to the conclusion that the roster is too hurt to do anything meaningful.
Again, it’s fair that the Rams wouldn’t want to overpay for a player like Thomas. However, with Downs going to the Chiefs for a fourth and fifth, that’s a deal the Rams could have done. One day after Puka Nacua went on injured reserve, the Rams did nothing to replace him. The Rams don’t know how many more swings they’re going to get with Matthew Stafford. Aaron Donald certainly deserved the Rams doing more at the trade deadline.It may be hyperbolic to call their inactivity a failure, but it was fair to expect more from this front office.

title: Rams Trade Rumors: Rashod Bateman Emerges as Last-Minute Wide Receiver Target
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are in the final hour of the trade deadline and have yet to make a move for a wide receiver. Earlier on Tuesday, it was reported that the Jacksonville Jaguars would not be trading Brian Thomas Jr. Additionally, the Indianapolis Colts sent wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers.
The Rams already had limited options at wide receiver heading into Tuesday's trade deadline. With Thomas and Downs no longer available, those options have become even more limited. With Thomas and Downs no longer available, that was especially the case.
However, with less than an hour remaining before the trade deadline, the Rams appear to still be working the phones. According to Pierce DeLuna of the 1st and Tuna Substack, One name the Rams are exploring is Baltimore Ravens' wide receiver Rashod Bateman.
Some smoke for #RamsHouse sources tell me. (God it feels weird saying that) https://t.co/0bXemGS6n8 pic.twitter.com/lhFyz8XSQe
A trade for Bateman would make a lot of sense for the Rams. He’s a reliable, experienced wide receiver and shouldn’t cost too much to acquire if the Ravens are looking to move him. The Ravens currently sit at 4-5 and have lost three straight games. Lamar Jackson could also be out for the season with a hand injury. Additionally, Lamar Jackson could be out for the season with a hand injury.
Bateman would only cost around $1.1 million against the cap for the Rams and fill an immediate need at wide receiver. He has 20 receptions for 294 yards this season. Bateman was productive in 2024, finishing with 756 yards and nine touchdowns. However, Bateman has struggled with injuries throughout his career, limiting some of his production.
Last offseason, the Ravens signed Bateman to a three-year extension worth $36.75 million. He’s currently in the first year of that extension and will count for $10.9 million against the cap next season. While he would provide a reliable, experienced option with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out, Bateman would also have a role in the offense when both players return.
Without Adams and Nacua, the Rams are in dire need of a wide receiver. As it stands, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Jordan Whittington are the only healthy wide receivers on the roster.
It’s still possible the Rams make a deal, but time is certainly running out. With Downs and Thomas no longer available, Bateman remains one of the few realistic options as the trade deadline approaches. However, as the trade deadline closes, wide receiver Rashod Bateman remains one name to watch.

title: Rams Would Make a Massive Mistake Trading Matthew Stafford to Vikings
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams found out wide receiver Puka Nacua would be out at least four weeks and likely headed to injured reserve, their injury-riddled season somehow got worse. Just as the Rams got Myles Garrett back and won their third consecutive game to improve to 5-4, they lost Puka Nacua for at least a month.
The Rams have simply been unable to catch a break when it comes to injuries. It’s been one after another, and just as they get one player back, another gets hurt. It’s been one step forward and two steps back all season.
With Nacua on injured reserve, it seems more likely that the Rams miss the playoffs than make them. They have a grueling part of the schedule coming up with the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers all back-to-back. If the Rams lose to the Packers and 49ers, they can essentially say goodbye to any playoff chance they had.
Despite the Rams facing a potentially lost season, it’s unlikely they become “sellers” at the trade deadline . Still, that won’t stop any potential speculation. On Monday night, following the Minnesota Vikings' loss to the Buffalo Bills, some started floating around the idea of the Rams trading Stafford.
As every second passes, I further believe the blockbuster trade that should happen tomorrow is Matthew Stafford to the Vikings. https://t.co/Tv8zV9JZkR
Stafford to the Vikings certainly makes sense. The Vikings have a Super Bowl caliber defense and Stafford has a history with Kevin O’Connell. He’d fit in seamlessly in that offense and has a history playing in the NFC North.
Following the Vikings’ loss to the Bills, it’s clear they have a need at quarterback. Kyler Murray hasn’t been the answer at quarterback before his injury. He currently ranks 26th in EPA per play. On Monday night, Carson Wentz was 8-for-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions. It’s hard for the Vikings to justify having a defense playing as well as theirs has and sticking to the status quo at quarterback.
From a source in the know: "Vikings going to get a QB now. Question of who. Daniel Jones, Geno Smith, Mac Jones, Kirk Cousins, TBD surprise, TBD huge surprise, but it will be someone."
At the same time, it’s hard to see how it makes sense from the Rams’ perspective. It’s true that they drafted Ty Simpson with the 13th overall pick, but he was always selected with the idea that he would sit and learn behind Stafford for at least a year, if not two.
Additionally, that would put the Rams in a tough spot with Stetson Bennett. The Rams held a quarterback competition in the summer between Simpson and Bennett. While both were pretty even in the preseason, the Rams listed Bennett as the backup quarterback. It would send a bad message to the locker room and Bennett if the Rams leapfrogged Bennett and elevated Simpson to the starting quarterback role after he’s been the emergency third-string quarterback all season.
Hear me out. The Rams trade Stafford to the Vikings. They probably aren’t Super Bowl bound anyways with all the offensive injuries + they used a first on Ty Simpson, so just commit. Get some picks. Stafford goes to a 6-2 team that’s only missing a QB.
The Rams have a development plan in place for Simpson, and that plan never included him starting as a rookie. In the current offense with both Nacua and Adams out, the Rams would essentially be setting him up to fail. Matthew Stafford has struggled enough as is.
That's a much different spot than if the Las Vegas Raiders were to trade Kirk Cousins. The Raiders have lost five of their last six games and were just happy to be competing. If they can get something for Cousins, it makes sense to move on to Fernando Mendoza.
While the playoffs may seem like a long shot right now, the Rams are 5-4. By trading Stafford, the Rams would be signaling that they are giving up on the season despite being above .500. That’s difficult to justify for a team that may believe it can stay alive through December and came into the season with Super Bowl aspirations. How do you explain that to Aaron Donald , who came out of retirement for this roster?
It may be tempting for the Rams if the Vikings were to offer at least one first-round pick in return. Still, that first-round pick likely ends up in the 20s, and the Rams are a team with good, young talent and the cap space to bring a lot of pieces back. The 2026 season is by no means the end of their window.
There’s a reason why the Rams have sacrificed picks in 2027 and not as many in 2028. The Rams have little incentive to move Stafford unless they're getting significant value back. Even then, Stafford may not want to move. If Stafford ends his career, it feels like he’d want to do it in Los Angeles despite trade rumors two years ago during contract negotiations.
The Rams have never been a team to give up on a season under Sean McVay, and it's hard to imagine that changing now. Trading Stafford to the Vikings may be fun to think about in theory, but making that move now would be a premature decision that could do more harm than good for both the current roster and Simpson’s development.

title: Rams Should Swing for the Fences With Garrett Wilson at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams approach the NFL trade deadline , they will be exploring their options at wide receiver. With Puka Nacua likely set to go on injured reserve and Davante Adams out as well, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels make Brandon Gibson, Tavon Austin, and Austin Pettis look good.
Heading into Tuesday’s deadline, there had been some speculation that the Rams could make a move for Jacksonville Jaguars’ wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. However, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler has reported that the team isn’t looking to move Thomas.
With Thomas unavailable, the options for the Rams at wide receiver are very limited . While Josh Downs could be available, he may no longer be a fit. Downs would have been a good WR2 or WR3 alongside Nacua and Adams, but he’s not a true WR1. He’s certainly an upgrade over what the Rams have, but the Rams would still be in a similar situation to the one they're in now.
The issue with the Rams’ wide receiver situation is that they don’t just need another complementary wide receiver. Players like Jauan Jennings or Jerry Jeudy make sense as complementary pieces. However, without Nacua and Adams , the Rams need a player who can be a featured piece of the offense.
Under Les Snead, the Rams have been no stranger to taking big swings. They are a team that has consistently swung for the fences with trades. Just this offseason, the Rams acquired All-Pro players in Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett. The Rams have made moves for players like Brandin Cooks, Marcus Peters, and Jalen Ramsey.
It’s very possible that the Rams simply stand pat and don’t chase their losses. In the end, that might be the smart thing to do. Still, at 5-4 and on a three-game winning streak, it wouldn’t be crazy for the Rams to believe that they can compete for a championship if they can keep their head above water until December.
Their options are certainly limited with Thomas no longer available. The Dallas Cowboys have also said that they have no plans to trade away George Pickens. If the Rams make a move on a wide receiver, it feels like it needs to be a big one. With that said, that type of trade may not be available.
Since McVay took over in 2017, the Rams have been able to take advantage of good players on bad teams with poor roster management. They traded for Dante Fowler and Ramsey from the Jaguars, both of whom were former first-round picks. The Rams did the same in a sense when they traded for Garrett this offseason.
If the Rams make a trade, that's the type of opportunity they should be targeting. One player who fits into that is wide receiver Garrett Wilson from the New York Jets. It seems unlikely that the Jets would trade Wilson. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported a few weeks ago that the Jets have told teams no on Wilson. Wilson has also said that he wants to be a Jet.
“New York has gotten calls on Wilson, whose frustration with a struggling offense was evident during last week’s loss to the Dolphins,” wrote Pelissero ahead of Week 8. “But the Jets’ answer to interested teams has been emphatic: Wilson is not, and will not be, available for trade.”
Since then, the Jets have lost two more games, extending their losing streak to four as they sit at 2-7. They may be a team with three first-round picks in April, but they are likely headed into a new regime at the end of the year. Aaron Glenn could be on the way out, leaving the Jets with another new head coach.
As much as the Jets may not want to trade Wilson, every player has a price. If the Rams gave the Jets their second-round pick in 2027 along with a first-round pick in 2028, would that get the conversation started? Wilson would give the Rams a young wide receiver option alongside Nacua to replace Adams and only cost $1.5 million against the salary cap for this season.
It’s certainly possible that any mention of a Wilson trade is simply internet fodder. Wilson is a special player and the Jets just extended him last July. He’s a player they should want to build around. At the same time, does it make sense for the Jets to commit $100 million to Wilson given their current situation? They don’t have a quarterback and their head coach looks to be on his way out.
The Rams have made it clear that they're all-in on winning a Super Bowl this season with the acquisitions of Garrett and McDuffie during the summer. At 5-4 and on a three-game winning streak, that could still happen even if injuries have put that in jeopardy.
Trading for Wilson would be expensive, but it would also give the Rams a legitimate chance to compete this season while setting themselves up for the future at wide receiver. It may take another aggressive move from Snead to convince the Jets to bite, but that's exactly the type of move he's built his reputation on making

title: Rams Week 9 Player Grades: Myles Garrett Shines, Matthew Stafford Struggles in Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won their third consecutive game on Sunday, defeating the Washington Commanders 20-13 to improve to 5-4. Myles Garrett's return provided a much-needed boost to the defense, which delivered one of its best performances of the season. However, Matthew Stafford and the offense remain inconsistent. Let's get into the Week 9 Player Grades.
The Rams have gotten average quarterback play from Matthew Stafford for most of the season, and Sunday was no different. Stafford missed throws that he typically makes and had another really bad interception. He finished with a -0.06 EPA per pass and 36.0 QBR. If the Rams are going to make a run in the second half of the season, they need Stafford to be better.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 103 yards on the ground. Corum scored a touchdown and Williams had an important conversion on fourth down on the opening drive. Williams added three receptions in the passing game as well, while Corum didn’t catch either of his two targets and got run through in pass protection.. Overall, the Rams’ running back duo played well.
We simply need to start grading the Rams’ wide receivers separately from Puka Nacua. Nacua played well, but this is a group project with one person doing all the work. Tutu Atwell dropped a pass on third down. Konata Mumpfield had two targets throughout the game and Jordan Whittington offers very little as a wide receiver. The Rams need to trade for a wide receiver.
The Rams were able to operate out of 13 personnel with Colby Parkinson healthy. However, until Terrance Ferguson returns from injury, the Rams’ tight ends don’t offer a lot in the passing game. Tyler Higbee had a drop and his route running left a lot to be desired. Given how Max Klare played last week, it’s fair to say he should get more opportunities.
For most of the season, the Rams have remained healthy on the offensive line. However, Steve Avila left Sunday’s game and Beaux Limmer was asked to step in. Limmer was fine, but the Rams will hope Avila is back in the lineup as soon as possible.
Myles Garrett returned for the Rams this week, and the entire defensive line benefited. Aaron Donald had his best game of the season. Ty Hamilton continues to play well in place of the injured Kobie Turner. As the Rams get healthy, the defensive line could be one of the biggest beneficiaries.
Over the last month, Omar Speights has played very good football. Because the Rams are perceived as being weaker at linebacker, Speights has flown under the radar despite playing like one of the better linebackers in the league. Nate Landman nearly created a turnover as well with the peanut punch.
Without Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, this group performed very well. Emmanuel Forbes was the best of the group on Sunday and has taken a step forward this season. He was targeted 10 times by the Commanders and had three pass breakups. Additionally, Kam Curl led the team in tackles.
Sunday was undoubtedly the best performance from the Rams’ special teams unit. Joshua Karty was effective on kickoffs, and Ethan Evans punted well. The bar was pretty low, but special teams played well against the Commanders.

title: LIVE: Rams NFL Trade Deadline Tracker — Trades, Rumors and Latest News
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has officially arrived, and the Los Angeles Rams could be a team to watch. After placing several key starters on injured reserve over the last few weeks, including wide receiver Puka Nacua on Monday, the Rams could look to add at the position on deadline day.
Throughout the Les Snead and Sean McVay era, the Rams have been one of the more aggressive teams when it comes to making trades. On Tuesday, the question will be whether the Rams feel like they can still compete at 5-4 despite all of the injuries.
The Rams could be considering Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman as the trade deadline nears a close. With the Ravens at 4-5 and Lamar Jackson possibly done for the year, they could look to move on from Bateman, who is just 27 and would cost $1.1 million.
Some smoke for #RamsHouse sources tell me. (God it feels weird saying that) https://t.co/0bXemGS6n8 pic.twitter.com/lhFyz8XSQe
The Jacksonville Jaguars are not planning to trade wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. With Thomas falling out of favor with the Jaguars over the last several weeks, there had been some speculation that the Jaguars would listen to offers for Thomas. With that said, the Jaguars seem to feel that Thomas provides more value on their roster at 6-2 than a potential future draft pick.
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
Prior to Monday, the Rams seemed content with their roster. The idea in the building seemed to be that players coming back from injury could be treated as in-season trade acquisitions. “What you look at is hopefully some of those trades will be guys getting back from injury that haven't played for us. That's the way that we look at it,” said head coach Sean McVay.
However, that has changed since Nacua went on injured reserve. McVay said on Tuesday that the team will look at all avenues and see what the team can come up with. With Jordan Whittington also injured, the Rams currently only have Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, and CJ Daniels available at wide receiver.
“I think you have to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up,” McVay said. “A lot of new things occur on a daily basis, so I would never rule it out.”
As much as the Rams may want to make a trade, there are some limiting factors with the cap space and draft capital that they have available. There are ways to make a deal work, but the Rams would have to get creative.
According to the NFLPA Public Salary Cap report, the Rams have around $248,600 in salary cap to work with. That makes a trade very difficult unless the other team is willing to take on a large portion of the salary or the Rams restructure a contract.
With that said, another significant obstacle to the Rams making a move will be their limited draft capital. The Rams don’t have a first- or third-round pick next year. Moving their second-round pick would mean not picking until the fourth round. They do have available picks in 2028, but the Rams may not be as willing to move those.
The Rams are in dire need of a wide receiver after Puka Nacua's injury. Here are a few names that have been rumored targets .
The Rams typically haven’t been active on trade deadline day, but that could change this year. At the 2018 NFL trade deadline, the Rams acquired edge rusher Dante Fowler. Fowler helped propel the Rams to the Super Bowl that year. Just ahead of the trade deadline in 2021, Snead traded for edge rusher Von Miller from the Denver Broncos.
In 2019, the Rams traded away cornerback Aqib Talib. The Rams made a similar move in 2024, trading away Tre White.

title: 3 Wide Receivers the Rams Must Target at NFL Trade Deadline After Puka Nacua Injury
full_text:
If the Los Angeles Rams were in need of a wide receiver last week, they will be desperate for one heading into Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least the next four weeks with a sprained PCL and MCL in his knee. Over the next four weeks, The Rams now enter another grueling stretch of their schedule. If they are going to remain competitive, trading for a wide receiver is a must. Here are three wide receivers the Rams should consider trading for ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
Prior to the Rams losing Puka Nacua, Brian Thomas Jr. may not have made the most sense . It was hard to see where he fit once Davante Adams returned from injury. However, with both Nacua and Adams out, the Rams need a player that has the ability to be a WR1. While Thomas hasn’t found success in Liam Coen’s offense, he has already shown that he can be a WR1. He had 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie and fits the wide receiver profile that has been successful with Stafford.
The question remains whether the Jaguars would trade Thomas. While they are set to listen to offers, they are still 6-2 and he has a role in their offense. He may have more value on their roster than a second or third-round pick. With Nacua out, the Rams also won’t have a ton of leverage in trade negotiations.
George Pickens is currently playing the 2026 season on the franchise tag. He hasn’t been happy with the Cowboys this season and was inactive last week with a nagging hamstring injury. Still, he has 39 receptions for 533 yards and two touchdowns. He’s at least a player the Rams would have to make a call on before the trade deadline on Tuesday.
Pickens would fit in well alongside Nacua and Adams when they return, but he would likely cost the most to acquire. It’s also hard to see the Cowboys moving on from him as they remain in the thick of the NFC East race.They have said they aren’t willing to move on from Pickens, but everybody has a price.
Bad franchises stay bad for a reason. They typically trade away good players and the Rams have taken advantage of that in the past. Like Pickens, Wilson may not be available, but he’s someone the Rams should at least call on ahead of the trade deadline. He’s the caliber of wide receiver that the Rams need while Nacua and Adams are sidelined with injuries. Wilson has 43 receptions for 527 yards this season.
Again, the biggest hurdle here is getting the Jets to bite. Wilson just signed a contract extension last offseason and is someone the Jets want to build around. The Jets already have three first-round picks, but only have one pick in the second round and are 2-7. The worst the Jets can do is say no, and Wilson is a player worth calling on.
With the Rams in need of an “X” receiver, a player like Ridley could make sense . He’s a veteran who could help the Rams get by over the next four weeks. While Downs was initially one of my favorite options on the trade market, he’s not a WR1. He would have fit perfectly alongside Adams and Nacua, but he’s not a standalone guy. If the Rams want a cheaper option, Dontayvion Wicks from the Eagles could be someone to watch.

title: Rams Lose Puka Nacua to Injured Reserve as Injury Nightmare Continues
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams just can’t catch a break when it comes to injuries this season. On Monday, the Rams announced that they will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua as he heads to injured reserve. According to Ian Rapoport, Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL late in the game against the Washington Commanders and will now be out for at least four weeks.
The #Rams are expected to place WR Puka Nacua on Injured Reserve with MCL and PCL sprains, plus turf toe, coach Sean McVay told reporters. pic.twitter.com/LLWLyGwVMy
With Nacua headed to injured reserve, the soonest he would be able to come back is for the Rams’ Week 14 game against the Dallas Cowboys. It’s unfortunate timing for the Rams as Nacua is now set to miss arguably the most important part of their schedule. He’ll at least miss the team’s games against the Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers.
Nacua got hurt on the second-to-last drive of the game against the Commanders. The Rams called a jet sweep to Nacua, who took a helmet to the knee. While the Rams were confident that Nacua didn’t tear his ACL, missing time always felt like a possibility.
All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A
Without Nacua, the Rams will now be down their top two wide receivers for the immediate future. Davante Adams was placed on injured reserve following the loss to the Arizona Cardinals. His timeline was 6-10 weeks, and the Rams hope to have him back closer to the 6-8 week range. Still, Adams will likely miss the next three to four games as well.
That leaves the Rams with Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington as their top three wide receivers . While the Rams were set to get Terrance Ferguson back last week, a last-minute hamstring injury during Friday’s practice likely sidelined him through the bye.
The Rams' decision not to add a wide receiver in the offseason remains a huge oversight. Adams was coming off of a hamstring injury and Nacua hasn’t played all 17 games since his rookie year. The chances of both staying healthy were low, especially with Nacua averaging 13 targets per game given his physical playstyle. Nacua had already missed time with a groin/hip injury early in the season.
Now, to be clear, that doesn’t necessarily mean that the Rams should have drafted a wide receiver with the 13th overall pick. If Ty Simpson works out, that was the right call. However, the Rams had opportunities to draft Antonio Williams over Max Klare in the second round. They also could have added veterans such as Keenan Allen or Stefon Diggs before training camp.
Nacua’s injury is the latest setback in what has been an injury-riddled season for the Rams. Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Myles Garrett, Jaylen Watson, Kobie Turner, and Aaron Donald are among players for the Rams who have missed multiple games due to injury. Adams, Nacua, Garrett, Turner, and Watson are players who have now been on injured reserve. The Rams simply can’t seem to catch a break.
With the trade deadline on Tuesday, the Rams still have time to find a solution at wide receiver to help navigate the next four weeks. At 5-4 and entering a critical part of the season, the Rams need to continue winning games if they’re going to make the playoffs in a very difficult NFC.

title: Inside Scoop: How the Kirk Cousins Trade Unfolded for the Raiders
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) made a move that is familiar on The Strip in this city, but not always common in the National Football League, as they moved all in on both the present and the future.
Kirk Cousins was brought to Las Vegas in order to be an example to the 2026 NFL Draft's number one overall pick, whom NFL executives ranked the best QB prospect of the last four years:  Fernando Mendoza.
Cousins and Mendoza quickly hit it off, and the relationship became not only that of two teammates, but two friends. Close friends.
From Monday night team bible studies to early morning review sessions, Cousins and Mendoza worked well together, and each day the relationship blossomed.
Credit the work ethic and attitude of Mendoza that won Cousins, and credit Cousins for showing a willing heart to offer anything he could to the man, waiting in the wings to take his temporary hold on his job.
Before we dig into the details of the trade, yesterday would not have happened without both men performing at their very best.
For just over two weeks, sources in the building have made it abundantly clear that Mendoza was ready. The impediment to his playing was that Cousins was performing at a career-rejuvenating high level.
Mendoza didn’t pout; he continued to work at a very high level to be ready.
A fact that wasn’t lost on Cousins. One of the fiercest competitors ever known, Cousins is also a realist. He knew exactly why he was brought in, and that was to warm the seat for Mendoza, who was ready.
The locker room knew it, and so did everyone else.
While Mendoza won’t be as ready this Sunday versus the Seahawks (5-4), he was as ready as could be, and then some.
The details of how this went down are amazing, and it should make all of Raider Nation proud.
I was told three weeks ago that the Raiders were going to ask an “exorbitant” price for Cousins. That came down, but not by much.
I can tell you that even as reports surfaced recently that allegedly people hadn’t called the Raiders, that is the typical spin of the NFL and the semantics of word salad that NFL executives love.
GM John Spytek didn’t say that in those words, but he did allude to it when talking about how it all unfolded.
“I don’t want to get too far into that, but really, this morning, Nolan [Teasley] and I spoke for a while, and we figured out kind of the framework of it, and if it made sense for both teams, and obviously we ultimately agreed that it did. But I talked to a lot of the guys around the league for a long time, but I would say this morning.”
I started reporting last week that Cousins, after Sunday’s game with the 40ers, could be got for a third .  I am NOT calling Spytek a liar, far from it.  But you can have calls in which no offers are made, and clearly everyone on the call knows the details.
I was reporting what NFL people were telling me, “They perceived.”
You can also never make a call, but take all of them.
As one NFL executive told me last night, “John is smart. He didn’t have to call anyone; he wasn’t shopping him. You have nice calls, and say hi, and you know who is a serious player and who is a bargain shopper. Cousins ain't a Dollar General guy; he was playing like Neiman Marcus, and when it was time, a team with a Neiman Marcus defense, and other weapons came calling.”
Spytek essentially said that, “I got a few phone calls, but one real one this morning.”
The point was that Spytek played this perfectly. Had he held on to Cousins, all was good. If he made the move, the Raiders got all of the efforts of Cousins, on and off the field, for essentially free thanks to Tom Delaney, who is one of the NFL's elite contract and salary cap brains, and picked up a third-round pick.
Spytek explained what he has seen in Mendoza that told him that he was ready when I asked, and he didn’t hold back.
“Well, I’m not in the meetings every day with him, but I hear all the reports about how well he does in there. But just to watch him go out and practice, and the level at which he operates the scout team, and the unselfishness and his ability to throw the football, and I think we’ve both seen him improve as a passer as well. So, again, he worked really hard and performed at a level in practice that was hard to ignore, impossible to ignore, and he put us in a position to make a really hard decision today.”
I asked Klint Kubiak the same question, and his answer, while echoing the sentiments of Spytek, offered even more analysis.
“Fernando [Mendoza] has everything we’ve asked him to do in practice. I think he’s exceeded those expectations, and we all know that live bullet Sunday is far different from practice. However, he showed us that he’s ready, not only physically but mentally. He’s up there studying right now like he would any other game. He puts a lot of work in. His teammates know how prepared he is. It’s not just lip service, but he has shown it on the practice field.”
The fact is that I wrote months ago what just happened. I told you all that Cousins would only be here a short time, but his impact would be felt for years with the development of Mendoza. Kubiak explained that very well.
“Work habits, preparation, ways to take care of your body, ways to connect with your teammates, progressions, blitzes to expect, things to expect from coordinators. We could go on and on, but there’s a lot more to playing the position than what your coaches tell you in your meeting room, and I think Kirk [Cousins] embodied all the right things there, how to prepare and how to be a professional, and really, when things aren’t going well, what buttons to push on your teammates and what questions to ask your coaches. It’s an endless list of all positive things.”
Spytek didn’t sugarcoat or bloviate about the move. The fact was that Mendoza was ready, and the deal benefited both the Raiders and Cousins.
“Well, we had to make a hard decision. And I mean, we’re all kind of staring the future in the face here with Fernando [Mendoza], and Kirk [Cousins] was very open with that when we got him. We had to basically decide do we want to go forward here over the last eight games, or do we want to take what Minnesota is offering right now? Ultimately, we decided to do that.”
Perhaps the most underrated Raider in the entire organization is Tom Delaney.  Universally respected around the NFL as a contract and salary cap genius, his masterful handling of the Cousins deal (mentioned above) got a great contract for Cousins and a remarkable deal for the Silver and Black. I asked Spytek about it.
“Yeah, it was a unique negotiation with Kirk [Cousins] last year, given his contract that he was coming off of in Atlanta and what we were trying to get accomplished as well, and we found a middle ground to make it work, where some of the compensation would be due next year had he finished today on our roster. That was something that we were thoughtful about, that we were willing to do because we felt like this is the kind of player we were signing, and he could bring what he brought to our organization. That was $10 million we were willing to pay, ownership was willing to pay, and then today things changed, and now that’s Minnesota’s contract now.”
Kubiak broke down the progress he has seen in his young QB, and the undeniable truths that proclaimed he was ready to take the next step.
“Yeah, well, every day he’s going against a live pass rush with Maxx [Crosby] and with Kwity Paye and Quay Walker and number 17 [Nakobe Dean] coming up the E gap, so he’s got a lot of game speed reps. I see him progress in his accuracy, in his total command of our system, his ability to get in and out of a huddle, operate two-minute drills, situational football. I think, just every aspect, like any rookie, you’ve seen growth. But his most important piece of production is his ability to throw a football accurately and make good decisions, and I’ve seen those two things really jump out.”
Kirk Cousins' 15 years in this league speak for themselves.…

title: Raiders Rookie, Sophomore Power Rankings: Growing Pains Continue
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders needed to get younger this offseason, and they did just that. Las Vegas added a wave of talented free agents and draft picks this offseason, most of whom were years younger than the players they were replacing on the roster. However, with that youth also came inexperience.
It was a trade-off the Raiders desperately needed to make across their roster. However, their past month of play has put the reality of that trade-off on display for four full quarters. This offseason, Las Vegas' front office decided to lean heavily on the young players on the roster.
Most of those players were added in the two most recent NFL Drafts, Las Vegas' first two drafts under general manager John Spytek. Their 4-5 record has both been aided and burdened by the talented but largely inexperienced wave of talent that Las Vegas is depending on.
Still, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak explained that even with that being the case, his team has taken an aggressive approach to improve throughout this season.
“I think one thing that I’m proud of is that we’re not talking about rebuilding. We’re talking about being in every game and winning every game. That’s how we treat it. We’re not looking at the future as coaches or players,” Kubiak said.
“You develop the future on the way, but every game we’re talking about winning that game. We are not satisfied with a rebuilding process, so that’s the mentality I want our players and coaches to have.”
Below are the power rankings for Las Vegas' rookie and second-year players who played enough to have an impact in Week 9.
Stukes' continued development is on display weekly. Sunday, against the 49ers, Stukes' interception helped keep the Raiders in the game. Stukes is proof that practice is valuable but not nearly as valuable as letting young players get on the field, for better or for worse.
Zuhn continued to look like arguably the team's best option at offensive guard. If the rookie can keep improving, that would be huge for a Raiders offense that has struggled to get going on the ground this season.
Assuming Zuhn is healthy and able to play this week, Las Vegas must keep him in the starting lineup to help further his development. So far, Zuhn looks like a solid addition to the offensive line for the second half of the season.
Jeanty continues to make an impact when he can. Although he led the team in rushing yards on Sunday, the team only ran for a total of 24 yards. However, Las Vegas stopped running the ball early in the second half after Kirk Cousins' interception that was returned for a touchdown.
Las Vegas' inability to run the ball well has more to do with its offensive line than anything else.
Entering the season, Las Vegas' defensive backfield was well known as the team's biggest weakness. The season's first nine games have confirmed as much, as the unit's overall youth stands out weekly. Although the Raiders have skilled players, they need more from those players.
Week 9 was another long outing for Las Vegas' group of young defensive backs. With the first half of the season in the books, Kubiak expressed his confidence in the position group following Sunday's loss.
“I do think Zeke [Hezekiah Masses] is doing some good stuff too. I know Zeke got beat on a touchdown, but I think we’ve got young guys that are playing good football that we’re going to keep playing all of them. Zeke and DP [Darien Porter] and Jermod [McCoy], and we’ll let the cream rise to the top and those guys will play more,” Kubiak said.
The Raiders only made one move at the trade deadline, and it was not to add a cornerback. This should make it clear how confident the Raiders' front office is in the group. Kubiak elaborated on the unit, noting that even rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy is coming along nicely.
“Jermod [McCoy], just a player that’s ascending. That’s making us play multiple DBs because he’s covering at a high level, he’s improving. Again, is a guy that we all didn’t know if he’s going to play football this year, and he’s not missing practice. He’s playing in games. He’s staying healthy. He’s progressing, getting better with reps," Kubiak said.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Pros and Cons of Raiders Turning To Fernando Mendoza Now
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick, subsequently triggering the beginning of the Fernando Mendoza era.
Moving the 38-year-old quarterback was always a possibility, but based on how the Raiders' season has unfolded in recent weeks and the Vikings' desperation for a reliable quarterback, this move had to happen. Not to mention, the Raiders received a third-round pick, which is incredible value for Cousins at this stage in his career.
Nevertheless, Mendoza is slated for his first career start in Week 10, and barring anything unforeseen, he is Las Vegas' starting quarterback moving forward. With that in mind, here are the pros and cons of the Raiders thrusting the No. 1 overall pick onto the field at this specific time.
If you look at the history of the NFL, especially in recent memory, sitting rookie quarterbacks for the season has proven beneficial for those players. For example, Patrick Mahomes and Jordan Love sat behind seasoned veterans - Alex Smith and Aaron Rodgers. Mahomes started the season finale, while Love learned from the bench for multiple seasons.
Sitting Mendoza for the entire season was the coaching staff's original plan, but as Las Vegas continued to lose games and the Vikings came to the table with an offer too good to turn down, the Raiders' hand was forced.
The writing has been on the wall for several weeks now, with Las Vegas losing four of its last five games . That said, Mendoza will now have eight weeks of on-field experience to provide film for himself and the coaching staff to assess. Assuming Mendoza stays healthy for the rest of the season, he'll have extensive experience heading into the 2027 season when the Raiders should have more pieces in place to support the franchise signal caller.
Mendoza won't be afforded an acclimation period. The Indiana product will make his debut on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, who arguably have the league's best defense. The Raiders follow that game with a two-game road slate against the Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns.
Ideally, a team wants to provide their incoming rookie quarterback with a soft-landing opponent. Based on the timing of the trade deadline, Las Vegas can't do that for Mendoza. It's important to note that if Mendoza struggles during this span, which is legitimately possible, Raider Nation shouldn't panic. Growing pains are part of the development process, and these upcoming opponents all have above-average defenses.

title: Kirk Cousins Delivers Heartfelt Message to Mendoza After Raiders Trade
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders weren't hyperactive during the 2026 NFL trade deadline, but they did make one significant move.
On Thursday, the Raiders agreed to trade quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. Las Vegas was not actively shopping Cousins, and we reported here that it would take a third-round pick to get him. That's exactly what Minnesota gave up.
This now paves the way for Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, to begin his tenure as the Raiders' franchise quarterback, while Cousins has a chance to chase a deep playoff run in Minnesota.
Cousins was brought to Las Vegas to serve as a mentor for Mendoza, as the franchise patiently waited before giving him the keys to the offense. As the Raiders' starter so far in 2026, the former Michigan State Spartan has been fantastic. Cousins currently ranks fifth in the NFL in passing yards (2,340) and second in passing touchdowns (20). The 15-year veteran has tallied a QBR of 62.8 and a completion percentage of 64.1%.
Simply put, Cousins did his job while in Las Vegas. Now, it's the former Indiana Hoosier's turn. However, on his way out, Cousins delivered a heartfelt message to the Raiders and wished Mendoza the best as he begins his journey as an NFL starting quarterback.
Following the deal that sent Cousins to Minnesota, Cousins posted a picture of himself and Mendoza on his Instagram story. The caption read, "Thank you Raider Nation! Go get 'em [Fernando Mendoza]."
It's a class act from a stand-up veteran in the National Football League who will now have an opportunity to chase a deep run in the playoffs with the Vikings. Back in Las Vegas, Mendoza takes the reins.
Everyone knew Mendoza would take over the quarterback position at some point, and that time has come. The rookie top pick's first start will come against the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks at home, who are 5-4 to begin the 2026 campaign.
The Raiders were patient, waiting for the right time and the right move to give Mendoza the opportunity to take over. At 4-5, following a 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the Raiders are not out of the playoff mix this season, which is already a success. However, the franchise is clearly looking toward the future. Get ready, Raider Nation. Your star rookie's time has arrived.

title: Raiders Trade Kirk Cousins to Vikings: Here Are the Details
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders have traded QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings.
As we first reported when Cousins was originally signed, the 15-year veteran was brought in to prepare Fernando Mendoza to become the starter and franchise QB, and the deal was structured to make him a fully tradable commodity.
We have reported for weeks that Cousins was available, and that it would take a third-round pick.
As we have been reporting, the Raiders were holding firm on a third-round pick, and that is exactly what the Vikings are giving up in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The Raiders essentially got all the benefits of Cousins, gained a third-round pick, and paid him essentially nothing, thanks to the creative genius of Tom Delaney, SVP of football administration.
The Raiders kept three QBs on the roster, as we have told you, because of this exact situation.
Aidan O’Connell will now be the backup to the new starter: the 2026 NFL Draft No. 1 overall pick and the youngster NFL executives ranked the best QB prospect in the last four years, Fernando Mendoza.
Coach Klint Kubiak recently spoke about what it would take for Mendoza to get his shot, and he didn’t mince words.
“Yeah, eventually Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football. We have a plan. We don’t have a timeline for that. Kirk [Cousins] is playing really well, and we’re in the hunt. It’s really important that we keep playing really well behind him and continue to develop Fernando, but Fernando is going to play at some point. It’s not going to be this week.”
Each week, Mendoza looks more ready and capable than the week before. He has a stronger arm and significantly better mobility than Cousins, and with the terrific example that Cousins provided, he is much more prepared for the role.
Raiders GM John Spytek made it clear the night he took the reigning Heisman Trophy winner that he loved him and staked the future of the franchise on him.
"Just a great person. Raised the right way, great family. He's about the right things, it's about his team, it's about winning, it's about doing the right thing, being accountable to the whole organization. It's very little to do with all the accolades he got after they won all those games. And he's really smart. He works really hard."
"This means a lot to him. And I don't that being the first overall pick and winning the Heisman and all the things that he's gotten will change him. I think that it'll actually make him work harder to prove that he's worth all that and then earn even more."
Mendoza played in October against the Patriots to get his first meaningful action of the season, and he spoke about the opportunity and what it means.
“It wasn't a great experience because of the overall outcome. I wanted to do my part any way I could help the team. I was called upon and I really appreciate all my teammates, especially some of the stars going out there, still having a fight to win and a fight and a fighting effort. So I really appreciate all those guys putting their best effort for that last drive.”
Mendoza will start this Sunday versus the defending Super Bowl Champions, the Seattle Seahawks, and a new era of Raiders football begins.
Hondo S. Carpenter Sr. is an award-winning sports journalist with decades of experience. He serves as the Senior Writer for NFL and College sports, and is the beat writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders. Additionally, he is the editor and publisher for several sites On SI. title: How Raiders Sticking To Plan in More Ways Than One
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' 2026 season has been interesting, to say the least. After winning three games all of last season, the Raiders started this season 3-0. As much as the Raiders improved, few could have guessed they'd get off to the start they did.
Las Vegas' hot start to the season put them in a position early to potentially contend for a Wild Card spot in the playoffs. Most things seemed to be going the Raiders' way during their three-game winning streak, but four losses in the past five weeks have quickly changed things.
The Raiders sit at 4-5 this season, with games against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos up next on the schedule. They have struggled against teams with winning records this season, making another multi-game losing streak a legitimate possibility.
Las Vegas' struggles, combined with one of the league's toughest schedules, have highlighted the remaining holes on their roster. Yet those holes remain after an offseason in which the Raiders added significant talent and invested heavily on both sides of the ball.
The roster holes Las Vegas still needs to fill have been debilitating, but not unexpected. Given that the Raiders are still technically in the hunt for a Wild Card spot, and that it is early in Klint Kubiak's tenure, the Raiders appear to be staying the course in several regards.
Over nine games, the Raiders have clearly aimed to stick as close to their plan as possible. During the Raiders' losing streak, Kubiak made it clear that Las Vegas would stick with Kirk Cousins as the team's starting quarterback.
Las Vegas' defense has struggled mightily this season, especially against the league's top competition. After weeks of subpar defensive play, Kubiak also vouched for defensive coordinator Rob Leonard.
Kubiak noted that instead of firing one of his coordinators after a mad dash to put together a new coaching staff and sweeping roster changes, he plans to look for ways to improve upon what the coaching staff has already begun building.
“No, I don’t. In fact, I see us doing the things we said we were going to do better. Stand behind Rob [Leonard]. Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players,” Kubiak said on Monday.
"And I think the world wants someone’s head on a platter every time things don’t go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason, to get a job done and develop players for the long haul, and that’s where we’re going.”
Kubiak elaborated on why he has confidence in Leonard and the defense, despite the unit's obvious struggles. Kubiak noted that the defense has played well in spurts, but has struggled to play well for an entire game against elite competition.
"Because I see it – not to interrupt you, sorry – I see it work, just not for four quarters. And I have belief. I have belief in the scheme we run. I have belief in the coaches that run it. I have belief in our play caller,” Kubiak said.
“I have belief in the players that execute. But as a group, as coaches and as players, it’s putting four quarters of football together. No matter who the opponent, you play a damn good offense in San Francisco, there’s got to be a happy medium somewhere between that first half and second half.”
Whether it is their plan at quarterback or along their coaching staff, it was apparent from the start that the Raiders had a well-thought-out plan. It is becoming more apparent weekly that, with less than half the season left, Las Vegas' front office and coaching staff will stick closely to that plan.
However, with the coaching staff and roster moves the Raiders' front office made this offseason, and the fact that the team is unquestionably better than they were last season, they have every right to take that approach. They could use more talent on the roster, but that will have to come later.
Until then, Las Vegas must trust the players and coaches they invested in heavily this offseason. The Raiders are right where they should be at this point in their rebuild.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: LIVE: Raiders NFL Trade Deadline Tracker: Trades, Rumors, Latest News
full_text:
Time is running out for the Las Vegas Raiders to pull off a trade ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Since the start of the season, Las Vegas' front office has taken a solid approach every step of the way. It will be interesting to see whether the Raiders are active ahead of the deadline.
The Raiders have no shortage of roster needs they could address via trade. Yet a trade may not be in the team's best interest right now. This will be a critical assessment and decision for Las Vegas' front office. The roster needs improvement, but not if it could derail its current trajectory.
Las Vegas must choose between making a playoff push this season or preparing for the future. What they decide to do, or not do, at the deadline could indicate which one of those options the front office ultimately ended up choosing.
The Raiders are in their first season under largely new leadership on and off the field. Las Vegas' solid offseason helped set the ship in the right direction, but the season's first nine games proved the Raiders' roster needs significantly more help.
Despite several blowout losses over the past few weeks to elite teams, Kubiak noted that the players in the locker room do not view the team as being in a rebuild. Las Vegas has approached every game more prepared to compete than it has in recent seasons.
“I think one thing that I’m proud of is that we’re not talking about rebuilding. We’re talking about being in every game and winning every game. That’s how we treat it. We’re not looking at the future as coaches or players,” Kubiak said on Monday.
“You develop the future on the way, but every game we’re talking about winning that game. We are not satisfied with a rebuilding process, so that’s the mentality I want our players and coaches to have.”
The Raiders' Week 9 loss to the San Francisco 49ers was the latest in a handful of losses that have made their impressive start to the season merely an afterthought. Las Vegas once again started slow,  heading into halftime down by double digits.
Las Vegas has been down by double digits at halftime in three of its past five games, including a nine-point deficit in its Week 8 win over the New York Jets. Although the Raiders have improved since last season, that team was the league's worst. This Raiders team has higher goals and expectations.
“Anytime you don’t accomplish the goal, you’re frustrated and you’re upset. I think the frustrating part of yesterday is just the way we started the game. Can’t start that slow. Can’t start that sluggish versus an elite team,” Kubiak said.
“In the NFL, every week things change. And right here we sit at 4-5 with half the season left, with everything in front of us. So, as a team, we’re focusing on the next game.”
Heading into the trade deadline , few rumors have surfaced about the team's plans to pull off a trade. The Raiders are not shopping Kirk Cousins. Few trade rumors surround Las Vegas because there are not many possible trade scenarios.
Although Maxx Crosby and Jackson Powers-Johnson are solid trade pieces , little has been rumored about either player ahead of the deadline. Things could change quickly, especially regarding a potential trade for Cousins or Crosby. Kubiak shared his thoughts on the situation.
“We’re talking all the time. That hasn’t changed. As the deadline approaches, things get more urgent, and we’ll continue to talk," Kubiak said.
"That’s the business that we’re in. That’s the business of football, and those guys are veterans. They’ve been around that, so you just keep working. There’s a lot of things that are out of your control."
The Raiders are trading QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick.
Trade: The Raiders are trading QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, per @rapsheet and me. pic.twitter.com/7Hxjt6TyR5
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: After Tough Road Loss, Raiders' Kubiak Still Maintains Belief
full_text:
After losing a game like the Las Vegas Raiders did to the San Francisco 49ers, there is always a great deal of frustration with the results.
The Raiders, nor any team, rarely win football games when they turn the ball over five times, including three interceptions from quarterback Kirk Cousins; star tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer each lost a fumble, while Las Vegas looked overwhelmed against the might of the 49ers' offense and defense.
Yet in defeat, head coach Klint Kubiak understands the process ahead and the mission for long-term success in Sin City.
Kubiak isn't shy about hiding his feelings about matters of the team. Right now, the Raiders do not have enough to compete with and beat the best teams in the league. Again, turnovers and slow starts have hurt them this season against the two best teams in the NFC West, among other opponents.
The biggest catalyst so far has been the defense, which is the worst in the NFL through nine games in multiple statistical categories. The Raiders spent a massive amount of money rebuilding the unit, and in most cases, changes would come.
Kubiak suggests otherwise, standing alongside defensive coordinator Rob Leonard in the process.
"In fact, I see us doing the things we said we were going to do better," Kubiak said. "Stand behind Rob [Leonard]. Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players. And I think the world wants someone’s head on a platter every time things don’t go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason, to get a job done and develop players for the long haul, and that’s where we’re going."
The Raiders have continued to show no signs of making major changes at the three levels of the defense. They are in a rebuild, committed to it, and steadfast in their approach.
Kubiak continued to explain that he sees the process working, but he also says they must put four quarters of football together, something they have struggled with all season long.
"Because I see it — not to interrupt you, sorry — I see it work, just not for four quarters," Kubiak said. "And I have belief. I have belief in the scheme we run. I have belief in the coaches that run it. I have belief in our play caller. I have belief in the players that execute."
"But as a group, as coaches and as players, it’s putting four quarters of football together. No matter who the opponent, you play a damn good offense in San Francisco, there’s got to be a happy medium somewhere between that first half and second half."
As the Raiders continue to find their footing in the second half of the season, Sunday was an example that, while things may look bad often throughout the year against quality opponents, the team continues to fight and put up a good fight against them while learning how to win in the process.

title: 3 Buzzer-Beater Moves Raiders Could Make at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are in an interesting spot with a 4-5 record heading into Week 10.
With the NFL trade deadline looming - Tuesday at 4:00 p.m. ET - the Raiders are one of the most intriguing teams to keep tabs on in the final hours before the window closes. With that in mind, here are a few moves general manager John Spytek could orchestrate.
After what transpired on Monday night, it further proved the obvious: the Vikings need to acquire a quarterback. Minnesota is 6-2 and would be a legitimate contender with a reliable signal caller. At this point, Cousins and Daniel Jones seem to be the most realistic options for the Vikings to consider.
Las Vegas is not shopping Cousins, but if the right offer comes to the table, you would have to think the front office would at least consider it. While I've been a proponent of sending Cousins elsewhere for draft capital, I don't think the Raiders should just give away the 38-year-old quarterback. If Minnesota shows its desperation and offers a second-round pick, that deal should happen.
While Las Vegas is on the precipice of the wild card, it's difficult to envision it reaching the postseason with the upcoming schedule. The Raiders face the Seahawks and Broncos in the next two weeks. It would be a tough pill to swallow and essentially punt on those aspirations, but this is the time to capitalize and sell Crosby at his highest value.
Over the last few years, we've seen Jerry Jones overpay for players at the trade deadline. The Cowboys owner has said multiple times this season that he's always looking to improve the team. It wouldn't shock me in the slightest if Dallas offers a first-round pick plus for the two-time All-Pro pass rusher. The Raiders need to look in the mirror and acknowledge that this roster is several pieces away from competing for the playoffs. Two weeks from now, the Raiders could be out of the conversation.
This hypothetical move makes sense for both scenarios: pushing for the playoffs or looking forward to 2027. While I've said the Raiders are multiple pieces away from a roster built to contend for a playoff spot, the playoffs are certainly not out of the question. On the other hand, acquiring Thomas Jr. could also provide Las Vegas with a legitimate wide receiver for the future.
Thomas just turned 24 in October and produced over 1,200 receiving yards in his rookie season. If the Raiders can land the 2024 first-round pick for a second- or third-round pick, Spytek should pull the trigger.
