title: Instant Grade: Eagles Trading Jordan Davis to Jaguars
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Jordan Davis certainly didn’t talk like he was a man about to be traded when he was one of the last players to leave the locker room on Sunday after the Eagles’ seventh straight loss .
He talked about the defense having a great week of practice, how they were challenged by defensive coordinator Vic Fangio to stop the run, and his plans for the bye week.
Less than 24 hours later, the Eagles have traded the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft to the Jacksonville Jaguars, per a report from ESPN ’s Adam Schefter. In exchange for the defensive tackle, the Eagles are getting quite a haul—the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 draft and a 2029 second-round pick.
pic.twitter.com/LoVwKERPqP
Asked for his perspective about the locker room potentially looking different when the team returns to work next week, Davis didn’t sound like he thought it would be him who wouldn’t be here.
“ I think it's something that we really don't think about,” he said. “Obviously, if somebody does come or leave, it does catch a lot of people by surprise. But for right now, we just all have been worried about playing the game, playing the game with integrity and just enjoying the moment.”
This is an A+ deal for the Eagles. Davis was popular among his teammates, but the draft capital was too steep for general manager Howie Roseman to say no to. It is similar to the trade in early October, when the GM traded center Cam Jurgens for a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round selection next year.
The Jags are loading up for a Super Bowl run.  Davis was the third defender acquired by the Jaguars, so the pick in next year’s first round could be the final one of the round if they win the Lombardi Trophy.
Still, as it stands right now, the Eagles have 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next three drafts:
On March 10, Davis signed a three-year contract extension with up to $78 million , with $65M  guaranteed. The deal was supposed to keep him in Philly through 2029. The Eagles will save $1.2 million on the salary cap, per overthecap.com. He exits town with nine career sacks and 15 QB hits.
Davis and Jalen Carter are close friends, so it will be interesting to see how Carter feels about the trade. It will also be interesting to see if the Eagles now turn their attention to signing Moro Ojomo .
It was reported that general manager Howie Roseman told trade suitors that Ojomo wasn’t available, that the Eagles wanted to re-sign him when his contract expires at the end of the year.
Davis was asked how he planned to spend his bye week.
“Rest, recover, keep working out, keep doing the things that help me become a better football player,” he said. “I think a lot of people, not just me, but a lot of people need rest on this team, and we can get their bodies back right and be grateful that bye week fell in the middle of the season.”
Now, Davis won’t get that rest. The 6-2 Jaguars play in Tennessee against the Titans on Sunday.

title: 3 Eagles Might Be Due for Bigger Roles After the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Trades are being announced across the NFL. It's only a matter of time before Philadelphia gets involved before Tuesday's deadline. The Eagles have lost seven straight games and sit at the bottom of the NFC East. They are lined up to be sellers, with several players available at the right price.
There's an obvious focus on who will no longer be wearing midnight green after Philly's bye week. It's important to put focus on who will be, too. Making a trade usually opens a spot for someone lower on the depth chart to take over. It's an intriguing development during a retooling campaign.
Here's a look at three Eagles who might be due for bigger roles following the NFL trade deadline.
General manager Howie Roseman shifted from the norm when he selected Eli Stowers in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The John Mackey Award winner was expected to make an immediate impact on Philadelphia's offense, but has been limited by injuries and blocked by Dallas Goedert.
Goedert could be moved at the deadline , considering he is 31 years old and playing on an expiring contract. That would give Stowers a chance to handle a steady role in an offense in need of change. It would also give the Eagles a window to evaluate whether the rookie can be trusted as a starter.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
Stowers logged 53 yards on three receptions in Week 8 (13 offensive snaps) and flashed solid blocking skills in Week 9 (seven offensive snaps). There's no time like the present to expand his route tree and depend on him to secure running lanes along the edge. Stowers is healthy and ready to roll .
There's no questioning defensive tackle Ty Robinson's potential. He has the strong frame (6'5", 288 lbs) needed to push back offensive linemen and an explosive first step that catches opponents off guard. The Eagles will never know whether that potential can turn into reality if he isn't on the field, though.
Robinson has served as the fifth option in the defensive tackle rotation since being drafted in 2025. That could change after Tuesday. The defensive tackle position is in high demand. The Eagles can capitalize by dealing Moro Ojomo or Byron Young, both of whom will be free agents next offseason .
Robinson was praised as a "wrecking ball" in college. The former Nebraska standout is violent at the line of scrimmage and always plays through the whistle. Robinson could be the spark Philly is missing in its disappointing run defense. The Eagles rank 24th in rushing yards allowed per game (126.1).
This selection is a bit more intricate than the other two. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt is already a reliable player on Philly's defense. However, his role has been reduced behind Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith lately. Hunt has played in fewer than 45% of the defensive snaps in each of his last four games.
Roseman could swing big by trading Smith at the deadline . He has posted five sacks in eight games and remains under contract in 2027. It'd be a move that brings back valuable draft capital for the Eagles. In that case, Hunt would become Greenard's counterpart, wreaking havoc in the backfield.
Hunt has tallied eight sacks, 12 tackles for a loss and 33 quarterback hits in 41 career games. The 25-year-old has shown versatility with six pass breakups and four forced fumbles. The final eight games of 2026 could go a long way toward determining whether Hunt is eventually signed to an extension.

title: McMullen: Joe Milton Isn’t to Blame After Eagles Set Him Up to Fail in Week 9
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — In the thick fog that settles over an organization after a seventh consecutive loss, the usual postgame noise quickly transformed into apathy in the shadow of the Eagles' 19-11 setback to the Giants on Sunday .
At 2-7, the Eagles are past the stage of searching for a spark and into the quieter territory of just trying to get through the remaining weeks of the 2026 season before rebooting in the offseason.
Into that haze walked Joe Milton, three weeks on the roster and making his first NFL start. He inadvertently said the quiet part out loud. ⁠
During a desperate final drive with seconds waning and no timeouts, Milton noted he trusted the embattled offensive line and loved the communication he was privy to despite the year-long issue with unaccounted-for pass rushers.
It was the kind of honesty only extemporaneous speech provides.
“I will learn y’all verbiage. I will,” Milton told his bodyguards. “That’s something that I put on myself to do for sure.”
Three weeks to absorb an offensive line’s language—the calls, the slides, the checks, the ‘who’s got the free runner’ signals—and the promise he would catch up.
That is not a quarterback complaining. That is a quarterback admitting the assignment was heavier than the preparation time allowed. ⁠
The play that made it obvious came from athletic rookie Arvell Reese, who came free on the right side, breezing by fellow freshman Markel Bell before nearly splitting Milton in two.
Milton never saw Reese, who separated the QB1 from his senses for a moment and the football.
Afterward, head coach Nick Sirianni did what he usually does when the film is going to be ugly . He said he was not going to assign fault.
Then he walked through the accountability coaching checklist: anytime a guy is free, look at the coaches first; ask whether everything possible was done to help the players; both coaching and execution matter; it starts with him; every product on the field is his responsibility. Yadda, yadda, yadda.
Sirianni’s monologue and Milton’s admission are not necessarily in conflict. They describe the same problem from different viewpoints.
Milton was signed off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. By the time he took the first snap against a Giants team that blitzes often and had the quickly ascending Reese, who finished with three sacks overall, Milton had a limited number of practices in the scheme under his belt.
The offensive line has been a problem all year for the Eagles. Protections have been a problem all year. Putting a new quarterback behind that line and asking him to diagnose, communicate, and correct in real time did not give Milton a chance.
It was testing whether the young signal caller could survive while still learning the language the line already speaks.
Sirianni is right that he owns the product. That ownership includes the decision to start Milton when the verbiage was still unfinished business. It includes the protection packages that left Reese with a free run. It includes the cumulative reality that seven sacks and a lost fumble on an unblocked blitz happened on the first start of a player who had just promised the line he would get their calls down.
Milton put the learning curve on himself, as professional quarterbacks do. The organization put him in the game before the curve was flat enough.
The Eagles did not hand Milton a functional offense and ask him to elevate it. They handed him a protection problem that has gone unsolved for weeks and told him the answer was on the field Sunday. He did what he could with what he had.
The result was what the setup predicted.

title: Riq Woolen Makes Trade Deadline Hopes Clear as His Eagles Future Remains Uncertain
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Riq Woolen doesn’t want to leave. The cornerback wants to see the season through with the Eagles, but that's out of his control.
Woolen has struggled in his first nine games with the Eagles, but he is still an attractive trade candidate for teams that believe they can challenge for the Super Bowl. Like, say, the Bears.
It’s up to general manager Howie Roseman to find a dance partner as the trade deadline arrives at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
“It sucks as a human when you don't know the unknown, but you wanna know the unknown, you know what I'm saying?” Woolen said after the Eagles lost for a seventh straight time, falling to the Giants on Sunday afternoon .
There are other players who could be ex-Eagles by the time the trade deadline comes, including Moro Ojomo, Dallas Goedert, and maybe Landon Dickerson.
Could there even be a blockbuster for Jalen Carter?
It’s hard to do one deal, let alone two. Soon enough, we will find out how many times Roseman hits the dance floor.
For his part, Woolen is trying to stay focused on playing football, leaving the heavy lifting to Roseman and his agent on what his immediate future could hold.
“I'm gonna just leave it to them, and whatever I have to do, I still gotta suit up and play football, and I still gotta be able to provide for my family,” he said.
Even if it means he could be traded to a contending team?
“I mean, if you woke up every day with your friends, some of your close friends, and y'all worked hard as hell every day, and you just up and disappear when stuff got hard or when you just up and disappear, then it'd seem kind of weird, especially when it's on you, you know?” Woolen said. “If it's up to Howie and the GM and my agent, then I'm gonna leave it to them. But me as a person, I've worked hard with these guys, and I'd love to be here and stay here with them.”

title: Eagles Stock Market: New QB, Same Old Story With Milton After Giants Loss
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—Another Sunday produced another loss that feels heavier than the final score.
The Eagles fell 19-11 to the Giants at Lincoln Financial Field, their seventh consecutive setback, and now sit at 2-7 heading into their bye week. Three weeks into his Philadelphia tenure, Joe Milton got the first NFL start, Saquon Barkley punched in an early score against his old team, and for a few minutes it looked like the offense might finally find a pulse.
Instead the second half turned into the same familiar grind: short drives, pressure, and a crowd that started leaving to beat the Olivia Rodrigo concert traffic that was looming across the street.
Here's our weekly Eagles' stock market:
The Eagles generated pressure, finished with five sacks, and made J.J. McCarthy uncomfortable before knocking him out for a short period with a hip injury. It wasn’t consistent all afternoon, but it was the clearest sign that the defensive front can still disrupt when it gets a chance. On a day short on bright spots, that was one of the few that actually pushed the other side backward.
Milton’s mobility gave the offense a different look. He picked up 64 rushing yards and converted the two-point conversion himself, creating a brief 8-6 lead. It wasn’t enough to sustain anything, but the mobility created a couple of positive plays that Tanner McKee, a pure pocket passer, hasn't produced in recent weeks. It's a small sample, but it was the one offensive wrinkle that didn’t immediately get stuffed.
In the same game Eagles punter Braden Mann had an 86-yard effort, the longest by an NFL player since the Giants' Rodney Williams' 90-yarder on Sept. 10, 2001 vs. Denver, the veteran also had one for minus-2 after mishandling a high snap from Rocco Underwood, and another for only 17.
There were no declarative statements about job security as the Eagles enter their bye week. Head coach Nick Sirianni is likely safe for now but scapegoat season could be ready to start earlier than expected with offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, offensive line coach Chris Kuper and run game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey all in some kind of peril.
"We'll talk," Sirianni said when asked if staff changes are on the table. "Obviously, right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything. I think we always think -- we'll do everything. I'll do anything I can to help this team win football games. Like I said, I'll look at myself internally first and then go from there.
"My job is to coach the players and to coach the coaches, and anything I can do to help this team win games, we'll do. Everything can always be on the table, but I don't think you change just to change because that's what your record says that -- you've got to look at what's really real and not react to anything else. Again, I just don't believe you just change just to change. If you have a strong reason to do things in anything, not just change, but in anything and you're convicted on it, that's how we'll go about our business."
Milton the passer faded quickly, finishing 18 of 34 for 169 yards, while being sacked seven times and losing a fumble. Once the Giants adjusted, the rocket arm never found a rhythm and the protection broke down. The early spark was extinguished and by the second half the stock was trading like every other recent Eagles quarterback outing.
"For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better [at] this week coming up for sure.”
The offense after the first quarter was the clearest underperformer. Three points the rest of the way, repeated three-and-outs, and no sustained drives once the Giants got a beat on the tortured offensive system.
"Obviously, none of us offensively have done a good enough job," Sirianni said when asked about the embattled Sean Mannion. "We're not going to sit here as coaches -- and it's not Sean, it's all of us and it starts with me. I think the correct question there to me is, 'Do you think you've done a good enough job?'
"Obviously, I haven't done a good enough job. We all have things that we've got to get better at and we've got to figure it out on offense. I mean, I think our defense is playing solid. I think they're doing really good things and it's hard to keep the game there. I think we've got some things that we're doing on special teams that have been really good, and then we can be more consistent in that particular case, but we have to figure it out on offense. That's coaches, that's players, that's everybody.
"So no, I haven't done a good enough job yet. The only way you grow in the midst of adversity is to get up, keep fighting, and work and stick together because you need everybody to do that. But adversity gives you opportunities for growth that steady times never would, but only if you do all those other things. We'll fight and we'll keep going."
Unaccounted for rushers remain a weekly staple and a drain on the Eagles' offense. Milton was under constant pressure, the pocket collapsed on multiple series, and the line never established a consistent ability to communicate.  The lack of protection turned what started as a manageable game into the same stalled effort that has defined the losing streak. Until the offensive line stabilizes, the rest of the offense will stay limited.

title: Former Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson Takes Shot at Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers moved on from former third-round draft pick Kaleb Johnson before the regular season began. After an uninspiring performance in training camp and the preseason, the team decided to cut ties with the second-year running back.
After that decision, the Steelers sent Johnson to the Green Bay Packers in exchange for a draft pick. It was an unceremonious end to his time in Pittsburgh, but it was clear he’d get a better shot at playing time in Green Bay.
With the Packers starting running back, Josh Jacobs, leaving their Week 9 contest with an injury, it allowed Johnson that chance. In response, he had a career game, posting 68 rushing yards on 14 carries and his first NFL touchdown.
After the game, Johnson shared some major love for his quarterback, Jordan Love. According to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman, Johnson has a clear preference when it comes to the two quarterbacks he’s played with, and it’s not Aaron Rodgers.
”I’ve had two good quarterbacks,” he said. “Aaron and him, but I like Jordan better.”
Kaleb Johnson on Jordan Love: "I’ve had two good quarterbacks, Aaron and him, but I like Jordan better."
While Johnson has had the privilege of playing with two good quarterbacks, he hasn’t had the luxury of being a good running back with two franchises.
During his time with the Steelers, he was a bust of a draft pick. Despite having a ton of talent and a hard-working attitude every day he was a member of the franchise, he couldn’t produce or build trust. In 10 games as a rookie, he carried the ball 28 times and posted just 69 yards. That was good for an average of 2.5 yards per carry and the longest run he broke off was a nine-yard rush.
The nail in the coffin came early into his rookie season. Being used as a kick returner, he fumbled an attempt and that cost him the rest of the 2025 campaign. From that point on, he was relegated to the bench or inactive on game day.
Meanwhile, the Steelers have found new life in their ground game thanks to Jaylen Warren. Heading into the 2025 season, there was a belief that Johnson could supplant Warren as the go-to back in Pittsburgh.
Fast forward one year later, and Warren is one of the best running backs in the NFL this season. He’s almost single-handedly leading the Steelers’ offense, exceeding 100 yards from scrimmage in five of the last six games and 704 total rushing yards through eight games.
It might sound harsh, but the Steelers don’t miss Johnson, even as he finds success in Green Bay.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Wanted Three WRs and Failed
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers did nothing at the NFL trade deadline . That wasn't the goal, but it's how it ended, and they didn't look good because of it.
Going into the deadline, the Steelers had two positions they were targeting: wide receiver and cornerback. Wideout was the frontrunner for an addition, while cornerback was more of a best-case-scenario outcome. If something worked out for both, great. If not, no big deal.
But they didn't walk away with anyone. That doesn't mean they didn't try, though.
General manager Omar Khan had his sights on three names as November 10 approached. Those names were Josh Downs, Brian Thomas Jr. and Calvin Ridley.
Ridley became an afterthought after an incident at the Nashville International Airport happened It over the weekend. Once that occurred, the Steelers pivoted, removing Ridley from their list and focusing on Downs and Thomas Jr.
Eventually, the Jacksonville Jaguars made it clear that they weren't dealing Thomas Jr., and the Kansas City Chiefs landed Josh Downs with fourth- and fifth-round picks.
And the Steelers left with nothing.
The Steelers have a decent wide receiver room when healthy, and they weren't going to make the over-the-top move to add to that room that they needed. WR1 couldn't happen with any of the options available via trade.
But depth could've been added, and it was needed for Pittsburgh. This team has already been hit with multiple injuries and have half the season left. Now, they need to hope they don't find themselves shorthanded once again.
If they do, they look like deadline losers, plain and simple.
Targeting three wide receivers and not walking away with anyone is a bad look. It shows that they were too narrow in on certain names, and truthfully, those names were so all over the place that they could have, and should have, pivoted.
Why only chase Ridley and not Jauan Jennings or Keenan Allen? Why only chase Thomas Jr. and not Quentin Johnston or Dontavion Wicks? And why not try to match the offer for Downs?
The names were too abundant to miss and yet the Steelers did. And don't get it wrong, not enough names got moved, but that doesn't mean they weren't available. Chances are, they were.
Pittsburgh watched plenty of other AFC contenders get better at the deadline while they didn't. Now, it's about hoping they're good enough to beat them.
Only time will tell, but leaving November 10 and heading into the back half of the season, the Steelers sure look like they failed.

title: What If Steelers Wait for Brandon Aiyuk?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have stayed quiet at the NFL trade deadline to this point. Maybe they'll stay quiet the entire time, not adding a name via trade and moving into the back half of their schedule without an addition.
Or maybe they wait for Brandon Aiyuk.
According to NFL insider Mike Florio, the San Francisco 49ers will likely release Aiyuk. Aiyuk was reinstated by the NFL this week after returning to the 49ers over the weekend. He passed his physical and, if released, would be available to sign with another team - if another team is interested.
There's no hiding Aiyuk's troubled past in the NFL. After signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers in 2024, Aiyuk played just seven games before suffering a torn ACL. He then didn't return to the team in 2025 as the two sides feuded throughout the summer.
He never returned until last week when he began working with the team to be reinstated.
We all watched the Steelers chase after Aiyuk during the 2024 summer, trying to land the wide receiver in a trade with the 49ers. They were close, but never finalized anything, pushing Aiyuk toward a deal with San Francisco and beginning what has felt like an endless loop of trying to find a veteran wideout in Pittsburgh.
So, what if they go after him now? If Aiyuk becomes available, why wouldn't the Steelers consider it? They still need veteran depth in their wide receiver room, have had interest in him before and wouldn't need to trade anything for him.
Instead, they'd be signing him to a vet minimum contract, and chances are, he'd start on their practice squad. Once brought up to speed, he's only 28 years old and who knows what he has left in the tank, but it could definitely be a lot.
If the Steelers like their wide receiver room , which they clearly do, why not consider a younger addition for depth? That's all they were looking for all along. And Aiyuk is very clearly the most exciting option with the most upside.
At one point, the hope that Pittsburgh would land Aiyuk felt like it lasted months, maybe years. It's been a while, but why not have that desire emerge again? It certainly makes sense for what they're looking for.
Great news for the Rams, the Seahawks and the Chiefs. https://t.co/h2afpBAsti
The Steelers are Super Bowl contenders in the AFC . They watched the Buffalo Bills, Denver Broncos and Jacksonville Jaguars make moves at the trade deadline. They didn't do anything to respond.
But that opportunity hasn't passed them by. Because if Aiyuk becomes available, they could consider a name with plenty of talent who could truly change the upside of this team in 2026.
A move that could could taken them to the next level. And one that comes without a big trade.
So, what if the Steelers wait for Brandon Aiyuk?

title: Another Trade Deadline With Nothing to Show for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were supposed to go for it ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. With quarterback Aaron Rodgers bidding farewell to the NFL after this season, plus a Super Bowl-caliber defense, it should have been enough to compel general manager Omar Khan to go get that missing piece.
Then the Steelers went 6-2, exiting their bye week at the top of the AFC North standings. Things are going swimmingly for head coach Mike McCarthy halfway through his first season with his hometown team. A trade felt imminent. The roster deserved a dose of positivity for the stretch run.
Yet in the most Steelers fashion ever, the team did nothing. Plenty of players were available, but instead of going all-in, Khan stood pat. Now we can say definitively that the key additions during the 2026 season are headlined by plucking a pair of defensive backs from other teams' practice squads and bringing back wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling after the Los Angeles Chargers released him. Another deadline passes with an unsatisfying conclusion, and at this point we are all fools for believing they would do anything other than what they always do at the deadline.
The Steelers' big move was staring us in the face all along. Following their Week 6 victory, they signed the recently released MVS to their practice squad. This marked his second time with the organization, following a five-game stint in Pittsburgh in 2025.
During those five games, quarterback Aaron Rodgers targeted MVS a total of 21 times, connecting for 10 receptions. That amounted to 80 yards and a touchdown, far from the type of game-changing production the offense needed.
This season hasn't been any different for the former 690-yard receiver with the Green Bay Packers. He appeared in three games with the Chargers at the beginning of the 2026 campaign, collecting just two receptions for 22 yards.
Despite all of that, he has the one thing that means more than talent or productivity in Pittsburgh: a connection with Rodgers and McCarthy. Thanks to their time together in Green Bay, Rodgers trusts him, and McCarthy believes in him.
The Steelers are at the top of the AFC North, and if they defeat the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10, they have a strong chance of winning the division for a second consecutive season. And they've gotten there without a strong passing game.
Despite that, their inaction at the deadline proves that they are not legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Compare it to the other top AFC teams - the Buffalo Bills and the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Steelers watched those contenders upgrade their rosters. The Bills added a starting safety, and the Jaguars added multiple pieces to their defense.
Meanwhile, the Steelers provided no roster upgrades. They didn't give their vulnerable secondary any depth reinforcements, and they didn't give Rodgers any better options to throw to.
But we shouldn't be surprised by this at all. The Steelers do nothing at the trade deadline, save for adding random parts like they are at the checkout line of a grocery store. It's a yearly occurrence. This year felt different, partly because so much has changed around the organization, but some things remain completely the same.

title: Steelers Trade Rumor Tracker: 2026 Deadline News & Updates
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline mere hours away at 4:00 p.m. EST, the clock is ticking for the Pittsburgh Steelers to swing any deals.
Sitting in a tie with the Cincinnati Bengals atop the AFC North at 6-2, with a matchup between the two sides on Sunday Night Football in order in Week 10, the Steelers have an incentive to go out and add to their roster.
Whether it's for a wide receiver , which has long felt like Pittsburgh's priority, or even for a cornerback, it's no sure thing that general manager Omar Khan will find a suitable deal out there.
Khan has made trades in three of his four trade deadlines as the Steelers' GM, with the most recent example coming last year when he sent a 2026 sixth-round pick to the New England Patriots for safety Kyle Dugger and a 2026 seventh-rounder.
While Pittsburgh is on a four-game win streak as it exits its Week 9 bye and gets ready to face the Bengals on the road in primetime, an upgrade somewhere across its roster could do wonders for the team as it looks to cement itself as a top contender in the AFC.
With that, let's take a look at the rumors surrounding the Steelers before the deadline arrives.
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer has reported that the Tennessee Titans are doing making moves and that wide receiver Calvin Ridley will remain with the team, meaning Pittsburgh will not be acquiring him.
With less than half an hour to go before the deadline passes, the Steelers lost out on yet another potential wide receiver target.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Indianapolis Colts have traded Josh Downs and a seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for a package including a fourth-rounder.
ESPN's Adam Schefter later confirmed that Kansas City would also be sending a fifth-round pick to Indianapolis as part of the deal.
BREAKING: The #Colts are trading WR Josh Downs to the #Chiefs for a package that includes a 4th-round pick, per sources. A new weapon for Patrick Mahomes. https://t.co/SepYaJPiA6 pic.twitter.com/Iod5l2hBav
Downs was arguably Pittsburgh's top target at the position and was connected to the team on multiple occasions, but the organization struck out in its pursuit of the 25-year-old.
According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts are trading wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
Trade! The Colts are sending six-time Pro Bowl WR Keenan Allen to the 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/tDt5H7HgId
Allen (who has 351 yards and a touchdown over eight games this season) was one of several veterans on expiring deals who were at least hypothetical targets for Pittsburgh, though the organization will now have to look elsewhere if he was on its radar.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Jacksonville Jaguars plan on holding onto wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. through today's trade deadline after acquiring Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux on November 9.
"The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources," Fowler wrote. "They have relayed that to interested teams.
"Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise."
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
Thomas Jr. was one of the top receivers involved in trade rumors over recent weeks given his dwindling role in Jacksonville.
The 2024 first-round pick, who had 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie, had been floated as a potential fit for Pittsburgh as it looks to upgrade its receiver room and generate more explosive plays in the passing game.
For now, though, it seems as though the Steelers won't have the opportunity to acquire him ahead of the deadline.
During an appearance on "The Aftermath" on November 9, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler stated that Pittsburgh "doesn't want to give up a lot of draft capital" in order to acquire a receiver while naming Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley as a player who might "make sense in that regard."
The Steelers have 18 picks between the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts, though their lack of a fourth-rounder in the first of those two years could hurt their pursuit of some of the top receivers on the trade block, such as Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts.
The names who could entice Pittsburgh at a cheaper price include Ridley and Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) now that Allen is heading to San Francisco.
In addition to their pursuit of a wide receiver, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on November 9 that the Steelers also want a cornerback.
My over/under on trades by tomorrow is 10.5, and I’m taking the over. Here’s everything I’ve heard on who’s buying and which positions they’re targeting after speaking with sources: pic.twitter.com/KbrHfUNVLo
Pittsburgh could use another option on the boundary alongside the likes of Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette after previously trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.
Riq Woolen (Philadelphia Eagles), Donte Jackson (Los Angeles Chargers) and Mike Sainristil (Washington Commanders) are among the top names to watch if the Steelers do go out and bring in a corner.

title: Steelers Lose WR Trade Target After Jaguars Decision
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- One of the Pittsburgh Steelers' top trade targets entering the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline was former Jacksonville Jaguars first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr.
Once a 1,100-yard receiver for the Jaguars, he now finds himself sliding down the depth chart, which made him a high-upside target for the Steelers to pursue. But as the final hours before the deadline passed, the Steelers received a disheartening update regarding Thomas.
According to a report from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Jaguars have communicated to interested teams that they will not be moving on from Thomas. Fowler provided the latest via his X account.
"The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline," he wrote. "Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise."
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
The Steelers and the Kansas City Chiefs were the two teams most frequently linked to Thomas Jr. But after this latest report from Fowler, no team should feel surprised.
The fact of the matter is that the Jaguars are one of the top teams in the AFC and the entire NFL right now. They have quarterbackTrevor Lawrence playing at the top of his game, and they just acquired multiple defensive upgrades: safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis.
When you are a top team contending for a Super Bowl, you don't sell off your talented players. Even if they are underperforming and sliding down the depth chart, the Jaguars have no reason or incentive to move on from a 24-year-old receiver with a history of producing.
If anything, the Jags should feel even more encouraged to get the old Thomas back as they push toward the postseason.
The Steelers can't waste time crying over this update, however. The organization needs to focus on the players who were always more realistic targets.
The top name continues to be Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher Josh Downs. In the final year of his rookie contract and wanting out of his current team, he's a quick receiver who can create separation against man-to-man coverage.
Another pair of names to keep on your radar are Philadelphia Eagles receivers Dontayvion Wicks and Hollywood Brown. Both are players who would bring talent and speed to Pittsburgh's receiver group, and they would cost far less to acquire than names like Downs or Thomas.
There are also multiple veteran names that fit the mold of Steelers previous acquisitions. Those players include the Indianapolis Colts' Keenan Allen, the Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley and Jauan Jennings of the Minnesota Vikings.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Every WR Steelers Can Potentially Land at Trade Deadline
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers might not do anything before the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline.
It's a sad, but possible reality for the Steelers. With names like Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson hopefully returning to the lineup soon, the Steelers might not feel compelled to add before the deadline expires.
Regardless, the franchise has been tied to nearly every available (and not so available) wide receiver in the NFL. With the deadline just hours away, here's a rundown of each wide receiver the Steelers have been interested in or linked to.
The two names that stand out as the most impactful ones to wind up in Pittsburgh are Indianapolis Colts' Josh Downs and Dontayvion Wicks of the Philadelphia Eagles.
Downs has been repeatedly linked to the Steelers, and he remains the name most are pining for.
Meanwhile, Wicks is a name that fills a ton of holes for the Steelers and is under contractual control for the 2027 season. Both names make sense as a deadline addition.
Many believe that Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars is a perfect change of scenery candidate. I'm not one of those people, but the intrigue is undeniable surrounding the former first-round pick.
Another former first-round pick, Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston, is also a name that could be on the move. He's a poor fit for what the Steelers need, but he's still on the trade block and it wouldn't be surprising to see him moved before the deadline passes.
One "Plan B" name to monitor as the minutes tick down is Hollywood Brown, another member of the Eagles. He's bene a productive receiver across multiple organizations, and now that he's healthy, he could provide that for a new team.
The Steelers wouldn't be the Steelers if they didn't look into a few uninspiring veteran names to add to the roster. Both Jauan Jennings and Keenan Allen are frequently tossed out names in trade rumors. The Steelers have been tied to both players in previous seasons, and here comes the carousel once again.
Recently, Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley popped up in trade rumors. A multiple-time 1,000-yard receiver, he's become an afterthought in the Tennessee offense. Combine that with his expensive contract and a recent incident off the field, and it's hard to see why the Steelers would pursue him to upgrade the offense.
The two best names on this list are also the most unrealistic. Both Ladd McConkey and DeVonta Smith provide what the Steelers are missing - a truly dependable top of the depth chart wideout.
It will cost a pretty penny to acquire either, and that's what will likely drive the Steelers away.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Should Call Eagles About Fire Sale Trades
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are working the phones, trying to land someone before the 4 p.m. ET trade deadline passes. Wide receiver and cornerback are the two positions to watch, and the Philadelphia Eagles may be the team to call for general manager Omar Khan.
The Eagles are sellers at the deadline. With 2026 essentially over, the team is moving some key pieces as they stack draft picks for 2027 and beyond. So far, they've traded Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, but that may just be the beginning as the 4 p.m. cutoff approaches.
For the Steelers, there are three names they can ask about - cornerback Tariq Woolen and wide receivers Marquise Brown and Dontayvion Wicks.
Pittsburgh's top priority is wide receiver, and Wicks and Brown fill that need. They don't want to spend a lot of draft capital acquiring anyone, and neither of these players will be expensive. They do want a separator who can help stretch the field on the outside, which both players are.
And while both can impact a team when called upon, neither is required to be a starter once they join the roster. Something Pittsburgh is keen on, looking to add depth instead of a "game-changer" at the deadline.
Wicks has tallied 19 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown this season and is signed through 2027 with a $4 million cap hit next year.
Brown, who battled an ankle injury earlier in the season, has only caught five passes for 63 yards. His contract ends at the end of 2026, making him more of a rental option.
Both would likely go for Day 3 draft picks.
As for Woolen, that's a bigger name who's still likely cheap. The 27-year-old has started all nine games for the Eagles and has eight passes defensed on the season. He's a player who would come to Pittsburgh with expectations of contributing in a larger role on defense, likely being the No. 3 behind Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamel Dean.
And that works. Daylen Everette has impressed during his rookie season, but the third-round pick still isn't a player the Steelers want on the field in larger chunks. What they'd prefer is another option behind their starters to add more veteran capability to their secondary.
If they're not looking to spend much but still want to add a bigger name, Wollen is the easy answer.
It's an easy call to make for Khan, who should be trying to take advantage of the Eagles' fire sale. If they want to stock up on draft picks, Wicks, Brown and Woolen are all easy options to move on from.
And they are perfect fits for what the Steelers are looking for at the trade deadline.

A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. title: Steelers Have Another Opportunity to Prove They're Real
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers don't have any time to catch their breath following their Week 9 bye.
Not only do the Steelers have to tend to business ahead of the November 10 trade deadline , but they also are preparing for a Sunday Night Football showdown on the road against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Bengals, much like Pittsburgh, have won four games in a row. The two teams are now tied atop the AFC North at 6-2 as a result, and this week's bout could very well end up dictating who takes the division crown by the end of the year.
While the Steelers came away with a 30-27 win over Cincinnati in Week 3, sweeping the season series will be much easier said than done considering they're heading into a hostile environment in primetime.
Just two years ago, Pittsburgh also made waves around the league with a 6-2 start before entering Week 15 with a 10-3 record after Russell Wilson won six of his first seven starts for the team upon returning midseason from a calf injury.
Then, the entire foundation crumbled. The Steelers finished the regular season on a four-game losing streak, squandering the AFC North in the process, and fell to the Baltimore Ravens in the Wild Card round of the playoffs.
Some parallels have been drawn between the 2024 team and this year's Pittsburgh squad, though that doesn't feel fair.
Not only do the Steelers have an entirely new coaching staff headed by Mike McCarthy, but their defense is playing at a truly elite level under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, as evidenced by the fact that they have allowed the seventh-fewest yards (305.6) and fourth-fewest points (18.0) points per game in addition to being tied for the third-most sacks in the league with 26.
The passing game is still a bit spotty at times and struggles to generate explosive plays, though Aaron Rodgers is playing about as well as he has in several years, while the offensive line is quickly becoming one of the NFL's more impressive units.
Jaylen Warren has been nothing short of spectacular too, with 998 yards and three touchdowns from scrimmage in what could potentially develop into an All-Pro type of season for the 28-year-old.
All of that is to say that this is the most complete team Pittsburgh has put on the field in quite some time, though this week's matchup with the Bengals is arguably its toughest test yet.
The Bengals are one of the league's hottest teams alongside Pittsburgh, and it's just about impossible to shut down their passing attack led by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Though the Steelers defeated Cincinnati in Week 3, Burrow still threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns.
The Bengals are averaging the second-most points per game (30.0) for a reason, and it all comes down to that aforementioned trio since they have what's essentially a nonexistent run game.
Cincinnati feels like a pretty solid matchup for the Steelers because of how well the latter's defense has performed, and Pittsburgh has only lost on the road to the Bengals three times since 2014, but coming away with a victory this week won't be easy.
If the Steelers do win, though, they'd be a game up on Cincinnati while owning a 3-1 record in the division and emerging as the favorites to win the AFC North for a second-straight season.
On the flip side, though, a Bengals victory could spell trouble for Pittsburgh since it would be a game back and move to 2-2 in the division.
These are the types of wins the Steelers need to pick up if they want to be considered legitimate contenders in the AFC. They've already proven they have what it takes to hand a loss to Cincinnati this year, and while repeating that outcome will take an all-around effort on the road, doing so would help prove that Pittsburgh is for real and here to stay this season.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Mike McCarthy Addresses Steelers Trade Deadline Urgency
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy isn't wasting too much of his time or energy worrying about the impending NFL trade deadline, nor has he ever really done so.
During his press conference as the Steelers return from their Week 9 bye and get set to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, McCarthy joked that he didn't even know when the trade deadline was for a large portion of his time as a head coach.
"I spent a decade in my life as a head coach, I didn't know when the hell the trade deadline was. I just knew it was somewhere around the middle of the season," McCarthy said.
McCarthy, who was originally asked if seeing other contending teams like the Jacksonville Jaguars be aggressive on the trade market could motivate Pittsburgh to make some moves, stated that his focus is on the players currently in the building and that he has confidence in the organization's brain trust to handle all of the deadline activity.
"I get it, everybody wants to improve their roster, and I have great confidence in [general manager] Omar [Khan] and [owner] Art [Rooney II] if there's something there, we'll do the right thing," McCarthy said. "But I think it's very important for me as the head coach to keep my eye on the target, and that's the 68-plus [players] that are in the building. So if we add someone that's gonna help us win, everybody would be for that... The most important thing is, I've always done this, I worry about the ones that are here. Coach the ones that are here and keep building what we got going. We have a lot of positive energy going right now, and we got a big-time game, Sunday Night Football in Cincinnati."
As has been the case for over a month at this point, all eyes are on the wide receiver market for the Steelers.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler stated that Pittsburgh "doesn't want to give up a lot of draft capital" for a receiver during an appearance on "The Aftermath" and mentioned Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley as a player who might "make sense in that regard."
The likes of Josh Downs (Indianapolis Colts) and Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars) have been connected to the Steelers over recent weeks, though if the organization really isn't comfortable paying up for players in that sort of tier, they might have to settle for someone like Ridley or Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) in exchange for a late Day 3 pick.
Cornerback is another position to watch for Pittsburgh, though it's been a bit quiet on that front over recent days, and the team's priority at the moment appears to be adding a receiver rather than supplementing their secondary.

title: Why the Seahawks Didn't Act in the Final Hours of the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks made a big trade during the regular season for the fourth consecutive year. The Seahawks traded for guard Quenton Nelson a few weeks before the NFL Trade Deadline was set to pass.  With the Seahawks being a fringe playoff team, there was some debate that the team would make one more move in the final hours of the Trade Deadline .
​The Seahawks’ front office decided to hang back and avoid any more trades while other teams bought for their chance to win now or sell for the future. Whether the front office made the wrong decision remains to be seen. Regardless, the Seahawks like their plan ahead of them with their roster and their future with their draft plans.
​There were reports in the weeks leading up to the Trade Deadline, after trading for Nelson, that the Seahawks were looking into upgrading the roster. There were reports on Tuesday that Seattle was looking for a legitimate No. 2 wide receiver . The Seahawks had every option to get traded players like wide receiver Caleb Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Other veterans could have been available, such as Cleveland's Jerry Jeudy or Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr.
​Ultimately, the Seahawks might be confident in their roster; this includes wide receiver. Among some of the biggest reasons for the sloppy first half of the season are the struggles from offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and the injuries on both sides of the field.
The Seahawks might have more plans for wide receiver Rashid Shaheed once he recovers from his knee injury. Two starters are also out along each of the offensive and defensive lines. Once injuries aren’t a factor, there is some stability.
​One of the biggest and most likely reasons for the Seahawks to avoid making more trades at the deadline is because they like the talent coming out of the 2027 NFL Draft. The Seahawks are likely going to have potentially 9-to-12 first-round picks due to compensatory picks from the departing players, coaches and front office personnel. There is a real conversation that the Seahawks avoided those trades in order to keep multiple picks.
​The Seahawks need the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft to draft a potential franchise edge rusher, a No. 2 receiver, some help at the offensive line, including a potential starting center and some depth along the defensive line. There might need to be a conversation about the Seahawks going for a franchise quarterback, with Sam Darnold struggling and having the final expensive year and Drew Lock set to be a free agent.
​General manager John Schneider makes excellent trades, as indicated by the four veteran trades. He also uses the draft to quickly reload and build for the future. The Seahawks can remain competitive now and in the future.

title: 3 Positions Seahawks Should Have Targeted at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks were quiet at the trade deadline , making their Oct. 27 deal to acquire guard Quenton Nelson their only move . It was rumored the Seahawks had interest in multiple other players, but they either backed off or were turned down in each of those potential deals.
With injuries piling up midseason, a few positions stood out as priorities for Seattle at the deadline. The Seahawks don't have any blatant holes, but there were some potential missed opportunities if they're hoping to bolster another Super Bowl run.
Here are three position groups the Seahawks could have tried to get better at before the trade deadline.
Even when Uchenna Nwosu is healthy, the Seahawks essentially only have three high-quality players to fill two spots. Nwosu has missed the last two games, and it's hurt Seattle's pass rush overall. Seattle totaled 17 sacks in its first seven games, but has just four over the last two since Nwosu has been out.
The Arizona Cardinals' Josh Sweat, Los Angeles Chargers' Khalil Mack and New York Jets' Will McDonald were all names floated around the league as potential trade options, and all would have made the Seahawks' defense better.
For now, the Seahawks will continue to rely more on Dante Fowler Jr. and Connor O'Toole as their options behind DeMarcus Lawrence and Derick Hall until Nwosu returns.
This isn't an absolute need, but Rashid Shaheed's absence has taken a slight dimension out of the Seahawks' offense. Shaheed has now missed two games in a row, making the Seahawks' top-3 receivers Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton.
The Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley and Indianapolis Colts' Josh Downs, among others, could have been depth options for the Seahawks, but they likely couldn't have justified the price of either player. Especially if Shaheed comes back soon, they would quickly fall to fourth on the depth chart.
In the short term, it would have been a win. However, in the long term, it wouldn't have made enough sense for the front office to pull the trigger. Most targets will continue to flow to Smith-Njigba anyways.
Trading for a running back would have been a premium move. Before this season, the Seahawks have had a ton of high-quality depth since 2022. That's what's been lacking this season, even with Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back healthy.
Charbonnet and Price can be a good duo, but they've both been injured. Acquiring a running back could have provided some insurance at the position that is better than George Holani or Emanuel Wilson.
Obviously, Jonathan Taylor would have been the swinging-for-the-fences type of move, but the Colts wouldn't let him go. And there's no solid evidence that the Seahawks were even still inquiring late in the trade cycle. However, it would have been a potential season-altering deal.

title: Why the Seahawks Didn't Trade for Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are sitting back as Jonathan Taylor stays put while the NFL trade deadline comes and goes.
The Seahawks were reportedly interested in trading for the Indianapolis Colts' star running back, but the team opted not to make the deal. Instead, they acquired Quenton Nelson in exchange for a third- and fifth-round pick. Here is why the Seahawks ultimately chose to move on:
The Seahawks were unwilling to negotiate a contract with Kenneth Walker III in free agency. Walker signed a $43 million contract over three years, while Taylor is on the books for a two-year, $44 million contract.
If the Seahawks were unwilling to pay Walker's contract, they certainly weren't going to do the same for Taylor. The team also has several other options in the running back room.
The main reason behind the Seahawks not making the Taylor trade is because they believe in Charbonnet and Price as a dynamic backfield that can get the job done.
Price is a first-round pick who is under team control for the next five seasons at a reasonable cost. Charbonnet, although he is a free agent at the end of the season, is someone they have relied on for the past four seasons.
Charbonnet recorded 77 yards on 16 carries in the team's Week 9 win against the Cardinals, which is a sign that he is slowly getting back in a groove after he tore his ACL during the team's Divisional Round matchup against the San Francisco 49ers back in January.
"Super happy for Zach," Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba said postgame via the team's website . "Everyone has seen the work and all the grit it takes for him to get back on the field. He played great today. We're going to need him throughout the remainder of the season. So, happy for him today."
The Seahawks are also excited to see what Price can do as he continues to grow in his first season.
"I thought he was decisive with his runs," Macdonald said of Price via the team's website.
"Sometimes he's the primary in some of those pass concepts. Sometimes he's kind of at the end of the progression and when the ball finds him, if you can make a guy miss, it's a great example. It doesn't have to be some extraordinary play to create explosives, but let's just be efficient with our decision making and get it in our player's hands and let him do the rest. So again, he's another example. I think he's just going to continue to get better now that he's kind of stacking weeks and he's getting healthier, that'll help us."
The Seahawks are investing a lot in Charbonnet and Price , and to throw all of that away for half of the season of Taylor would not be a wise investment.

title: Seahawks Are NFL Trade Deadline Winners After Kirk Cousins Deal
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are facing off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 , but they won't be facing off against quarterback Kirk Cousins.
The Raiders traded Cousins just hours before the deadline to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft , which opens the door for Fernando Mendoza to make his first career start.
Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick and reigning Heisman Trophy winner, now has the reins of the Raiders offense, but he won't have it easy facing off against the Seahawks in his first game.
This will mark the second straight week the Seahawks will face off against someone in their first start of the season. Gardner Minshew made his first start for the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9, and his team clearly struggled by only getting up by three points during the game. The Seahawks went on to win 17-3.
Mendoza was placed behind Cousins on the depth chart, and he could have moved on to the rookie at any point, but Las Vegas got a lot out of the veteran. The team started out 3-0, but they have won just one of their last six games, though Cousins was not the reason behind their struggles.
In nine games this season, Cousins threw for 2,340 yards with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He joins the Vikings, who are looking to lead them to the playoffs as a 6-2 team, but it doesn't affect the Seahawks current schedule since Minnesota does not play Seattle at any point this season.
With Mendoza under center for the Raiders, the Seahawks' chances of winning the game should greatly improve. A win would take them to 6-4 going into their Week 11 bye. The Seahawks can't underestimate the No. 1 overall pick, who will have a strong game plan formed by former Seattle offensive coordinator and now-Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, but they will likely smell blood in the water.
Mendoza will make his first start for the Raiders as they are set to host the Seahawks on Sunday at 1:05 pm PT inside Allegiant Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: NFL Playoff Picture Update Provides Hope for Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are creeping closer to the playoff picture after their 17-3 victory against the Arizona Cardinals.
While they may not be in the playoff picture after Week 9, they have a strong outlook as they enter the second half of the season. Here's a look at what the playoff picture looks like at the halfway point:
1. San Francisco 49ers, 7-1-0 (1st NFC West) 2. Chicago Bears, 7-2-0 (1st NFC North) 3. New York Giants, 5-2-1 (1st NFC East) 4. Carolina Panthers, 3-5-0 (1st NFC South) 5. Detroit Lions, 6-2-0 (Wild Card) 6. Minnesota Vikings, 6-2-0 (Wild Card) 7. Green Bay Packers, 6-3-0 (Wild Card) 8. Seattle Seahawks, 5-4-0 9. Los Angeles Rams, 5-4-0 10. Dallas Cowboys, 4-5-0 11. New Orleans Saints, 3-5-0 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 3-6-0 13. Atlanta Falcons, 3-6-0 14. Arizona Cardinals, 3-6-0 15. Washington Commanders, 2-5-1 16. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-7-0
The Seahawks are not in the same position they were in a year ago, as they have already racked up more losses this season than they had all of last year. In a competitive NFC playoff picture, that puts them on the outside looking in. That said, the second half of the season should provide many opportunities for the team to jump into the top seven, with a chance to return to the postseason.
As the weeks go by, their chances of winning the NFC West are becoming slimmer. The San Francisco 49ers are 2.5 games ahead of the Seahawks and hold the tiebreaker following their Week 5 win against Seattle at Lumen Field. This means the Seahawks are likely targeting a wild card spot, which is more attainable just one game behind the Green Bay Packers for the No. 7 seed.
The NFC North occupies four of the top seven spots in the NFC at the moment. All four of those teams have the strongest schedule difficulties left in the season, mainly because each team still has 3-4 divisional matchups left in the second half of the year.
The NFC North teams are bound to beat up on each other, which means at least one will likely fall by the wayside and miss the playoffs. Since the NFL adopted the 14-team playoff format which made it possible for all four teams to reach the postseason, it has not been accomplished. However, a third-place team has qualified for the playoffs, much like the 49ers did last year in the NFC West.
On top of that, the Los Angeles Rams are arguably their biggest competition in the NFC West, especially with two games in the final three weeks of the season on Seattle's schedule. The team just placed star wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve, which means the team is down another top target after Davante Adams went down a few weeks back.
The Seahawks will still have to execute themselves , but their outlook is promising given how the stock is dropping with other contenders alongside them.

title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Why Seahawks Are Down Despite Win vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back over .500 after a 17-3 victory against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 inside Lumen Field.
Their 5-4 record keeps them in the hunt for a playoff spot, but there are certainly causes for concern. Here's a look at where the Seahawks stand in power rankings across the internet.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 6
Conor Orr moved the Seahawks down six spots despite their win, which is more of a sign as to where the team stands with their quarterback situation than anything.
"It’s the Drew Lock show for Seattle once again," Orr wrote. "I think it’s time to revisit a Sam Darnold column we wrote at the beginning of the season. How soon before we have the conversation about Seattle’s QB situation?"
ESPN moved them back one more spot after going down three spaces last week, which shows that winning isn't everything when it comes to the power rankings.
The power rankings also highlight the team's Week 12 contest against the San Francisco 49ers, citing it as the most important game in the second half of the season.
Ranking: 11 | Last week: 9
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff worked together for The Athletic and says the Seahawks need to start stacking some wins as they go into the second half of the season.
"They’re still weathering the storm of Sam Darnold injuries (and now Drew Lock may have to play through an injury), but the defense remains a top-five group, and there’s hope for what the running game will become now that Jadarian Price is back. Still, they haven’t won consecutive games since the first two weeks of the season," The Athletic wrote.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 13
Bleacher Report contributor Moe Moton highlighted the team's inconsistencies on offense as the reason why they aren't higher, even though they take one step forward in the website's power rankings.
"Entering Week 10, Darnold is nursing quad and rib injuries, and Lock has an oblique injury. With so much uncertainty at quarterback and the passing game's recent limitations and inefficiencies, it's hard to feel confident about the Seahawks' short-term outlook," Moton wrote.
Ranking: 14 | Last week: 14
Pete Prisco has Seattle at No. 14 for the second straight week, but he thinks things could turn around in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
"They are fighting through quarterback injuries, but it looks like Drew Lock will play against the Raiders this week. The Raiders might be the perfect tonic to get the offense going," Prisco wrote.
No matter how good the Seahawks' defense is performing, the team will always be looked at for their quarterback situation. As long as Darnold is underperforming, the Seahawks will not be viewed as a true Super Bowl contender in the NFC.
This year, there are several teams in the NFC that have improved from a year ago, and the Seahawks aren't one of them. That said, if they can stack some wins in the second half of the season and stay healthy after their bye week, they should be a team nobody wants to face come playoff time.

title: Mike Macdonald Discusses Seahawks Plan at Quarterback
full_text:
After a 2025 season where the Seattle Seahawks were almost entirely without quarterback drama, 2026 has been the exact opposite.
As of this moment, both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock are nursing multiple injuries. A couple days ago, there was even a moment where it looked like Jalen Milroe was in line to start. So, where do things currently stand?
It was fairly clear days ago that Darnold was unlikely to be healed up in time for the Las Vegas Raiders game. Lock suffered an oblique injury during the Arizona Cardinals game on top of his elbow problem, so his status was initially unknown. However, according to Lock himself and head coach Mike Macdonald, he should be available this week.
After that, the Seahawks have their bye week, giving them extra time to sort things out. And yesterday afternoon during his typical Monday press conference, Macdonald indicated he believed that Darnold would be ready to play on the other side of that bye. He stopped short of making any promises, but it sure sounds like the starting job is going back to Darnold.
Assuming that is the case, then I can certainly understand the decision. Macdonald isn’t going to be in a hurry to ditch the quarterback that helped him win a Super Bowl just nine months ago, and Darnold’s play against Kansas City reminded everyone that high-level play is still within his abilities. But does that make it the right decision?
I’m not so sure. We have a pretty decent sample size, going back to last season , of Darnold being a below average quarterback with occasional flashes of greatness here and there. For the most part this season, he’s been downright bad. Lock has played a much more complimentary style of football that I think serves this team better.
Beyond my own personal beliefs about who the better option is right now, however, there’s another layer. Lock has started two games, both against the Arizona Cardinals, and gets a third start this week against the Las Vegas Raiders. Very poor defenses, the kind that any competent quarterback can produce against.
If Darnold comes back after the bye, he jumps right into a matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, who have one of the NFL’s better defenses. It’s a circumstance that does feel like something of a setup that makes Lock look better. It also continues something of a pattern to this season so far, where Darnold gets saddled with the harder matchups.
If Lock does well this week and Darnold struggles in Week 12, well, the discourse is only going to get hotter. Darnold does get the Dallas Cowboys the following week, at least, but even if Darnold gets his starting job back I find it hard to believe he has an infinitely long leash. This controversy isn’t going anywhere anytime soon, is what I’m getting at here.

title: Seahawks NFL Trade Deadline Primer: What to Watch
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and the other 31 NFL teams are going into a day like today with an objective.
Some want to make their rosters better for a playoff push. Others want to swap good players that don’t fit into their timeline for draft capital and cap savings. Not every team will be able to achieve their goals today, but the ones that do may determine who wins it all, so let’s run it down.
Officially, the NFL Trade Deadline is today at 1 p.m. PT. Any deals that teams want to make need to be completed by then. That being said, remember that it takes time for a trade to go from the NFL office to beat reporters, so a trade could still be revealed some time in the following hour or so. Often, trades are leaked before they’re finalized, so even this is unlikely.
Once the deadline passes, the only way for NFL teams to improve themselves is to sign players out of free agency, and even that has some restrictions. Today serves as a last call for any team that believes themselves to be ready for a title run but needs one last piece. The Seahawks have been very involved in the deadline each of the last three years.
Typically, trade deals are initially broken on X by the Adam Schefter’s, Ian Rapoport’s, and Tom Pelissero’s of the world. They put it out there, and it propagates out to ESPN and NFL Network. This page will cover any trades the Seahawks specifically are involved in, of course. One way or another, whatever happens will spread through the general public quickly.
Also expect to see plenty of buzz and implication as the minutes tick down towards the deadline, as teams often work towards trade deals that never get completed. Often, deadline day comes with at least a couple of stories about how Team X was very close to acquiring Player Y from Team Z, but just couldn’t quite get the compensation right.
There were a fair few trades yesterday, including three from the Jacksonville Jaguars, so there’s a chance that some of the fireworks have already launched. But the general sense is that there’s going to be a lot of action today, as there are many teams that need to take that one extra step towards true contention and others that need to strip down a bit more.
The Seahawks, specifically, are believed to be on the hunt for a wide receiver , so we’ve got that. There’s no guarantee they find one, of course, but I’d be very surprised if they weren’t also sniffing around for an edge rusher. They have draft picks to give up to be sure, but note they already expended some capital for Quenton Nelson, so the big move has been made.

title: Seahawks Week 9 Snap Counts: Charbonnet, Price Flip Roles
full_text:
Despite missing several key players, the Seattle Seahawks pulled out a home victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Seattle has now won 11 straight games against the Cardinals, dating back to 2022.
The absence of some starters let more players see the field, which is a good thing when the team can avoid a loss. That was apparent in the Seahawks’ total snaps on both offense and defense this week, with multiple backups getting their most extensive action of the season.
Here’s a look at how the Seahawks’ snap counts shook out in their win over the Cardinals.
* All snap count statistics are courtesy of Pro Football Reference
RG Anthony Bradford (67; 100%), LG Grey Zabel (67; 100%), C Jalen Sundell (67; 100%), RT Abe Lucas (67; 100%), LT Josh Jones (67; 100%), QB Drew Lock (67; 100%), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (51; 76%), WR Cooper Kupp (49; 73%), TE AJ Barner (48; 72%), WR Tory Horton (41; 61%), RB Zach Charbonnet (38; 57%), TE Eric Saubert (32; 48%), TE Nick Kallerup (27; 40%), RB Jadarian Price (24; 36%), FB Brady Russell (12; 18%), WR Montorie Foster Jr. (5; 7%), T Bobby Hart (3; 4%), Olu Oluwatimi (3; 4%), RB George Holani (2; 3%)
The running back split between Charbonnet and Price flipped against the Cardinals, as the former saw more snaps in his second game back from a torn ACL. Charbonnet carried or caught the ball on 44.7% of his snaps, while Price’s usage rate was about 54.2% when he was on the field. This is unsurprising, as Charbonnet is a better pass protector and was always going to retake the lead running back role.
Barner, Saubert and Kallerup all saw significant snaps, as the Seahawks ran heavy sets much of the game. That could continue now that the running back room is healthy and offensive coordinator Brian Fleury tries to establish Seattle’s run game.
The Seahawks’ offensive line, which featured backups Bradford and Jones, all played every snap. That will look much different once Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross return, as Zabel will go back to the left side of the line.
LB/DB Nick Emmanwori (53; 100%), S Julian Love (53; 100%), LB Ernest Jones IV (53; 100%), S Ty Okada (53; 100%), CB Devon Witherspoon (52; 98%), CB Josh Jobe (52; 98%), LB Drake Thomas (42; 79%), DL Byron Murphy II (40; 75%), OLB DeMarcus Lawrence (39; 74%), DL Jarran Reed (32; 60%), DL Rylie Mills (31; 58%), OLB Derick Hall (29; 55%), DL Mike Morris (17; 32%), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (12; 23%), OLB Dante Fowler Jr. (12; 23%), OLB Connor O’Toole (11; 21%), LB Patrick O’Connell (1; 2%), S Rodney Thomas II (1; 2%)
Emmanwori has been trending toward being an every-down player for multiple weeks, and he played that role against the Cardinals. Love, Jones and Okada have routinely played every snap when healthy, and that continued in Week 9. Emmanwori playing more drove down the amount of snaps that Drake Thomas played in this one.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald dug deep in his front-seven depth, playing nine different defensive linemen and edge rushers. That was to make up for the absence of Uchenna Nwosu, Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili.
Pritchett continues to get some opportunity, but his usage has fluctuated from game to game. He still remains the No. 3 cornerback behind Witherspoon and Jobe.

title: Seahawks in the Market for a Wide Receiver Trade, per Sources
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are not waving the white flag on the 2026 season, despite some clear setbacks. Per Jordan Schultz, John Schneider is on the prowl for a wide receiver, specifically to complement Jaxon Smith-Njigba . Let’s take a look at the circumstances the Seahawks face as they try to find such a trade, and then look at some candidates to acquire.
First, the report from Schultz specifically said they wanted someone to complement JSN, which presumably means they want someone with a different skillset. I’d focus on bigger receivers who can win 50/50 balls and make catches in the redzone. That removes players like Josh Downs, who is a nice enough player, but would be the smallest WR on this team.
Remember that the Seahawks have very little cap space, around $3-4 million, so unless they pull some other levers they can’t really trade for a veteran on a bigger contract. That would make Rashod Bateman a tough sell. Also, since Cooper Kupp is probably in his final season , the team should prioritize getting a younger, long-term player here anyway.
Let’s start with the 2-7 Jets. The big name right now is Garrett Wilson, but he would be extremely expensive and I don’t think we’d get the most out of him. I’d rather cast my gaze at Adonai Mitchell, a decently-sized receiver with a lot of talent who is still on his rookie deal and under contract through 2027. There are some problems, but he’s flashed plenty.
Quentin Johnston, if the Los Angeles Chargers ever want to join the party, would be fascinating to me. Despite his bad reputation, he had back-to-back 700 yard seasons recently, is still on his rookie deal, and has the size to contrast JSN. It would be a very fun reclamation project for someone that is very talented, and is a free agent in a few months if things don’t work out.
Finally, and this one is a sleeper, I’d take a look at DeVaughn Vele with the New Orleans Saints. The Saints are still in the thick of the division race, but they’re still a bad team, and they barely use Vele. It should be cheap, and Vele is one of the biggest receivers in football at 6’5. His rookie year in Denver was pretty solid, so there’s something here.
All this being said, I’m not convinced trading for a wide receiver is the right move unless Rashid Shaheed’s injury is long-term . You could argue making a trade for anyone is a questionable idea, with the team sitting at 5-4 and staring at a very challenging wide card race, but a receiver in particular gives me pause. In an offense like this, how much can a receiver help?
This Seahawks team, in theory, is a run-first team. When they throw it, they throw it to JSN constantly. That leaves very limited opportunities for other receivers. To my eyes, players like Shaheed and Tory Horton are getting open at a good rate, and not getting the ball. Any receiver you trade for could easily end up doing the same. But, if you insist, those are my targets.
